Chapter 25


.

“Let’s talk.”

Micheal and Shin both sat down. Shin crossed his fingers over each hand, interlocking them while sitting impassively. Micheal, on the other hand, slowly raised his right hand, pointing to his Spatial Ring as he sat down.

“If you’ll allow me.” Micheal asked, his eyes evenly meeting Aaron’s piercing gaze.

“Go ahead.” Aaron nodded.

A journal appeared as Micheal withdrew it from the Spatial Ring.

Micheal slowly opened that journal, flipping through several pages before stopping on one particular page, where a sketch of a vague, shadowy figure was drawn.

And it was here that Micheal immediately dropped a bombshell, catching both Jessica and Aaron completely off guard.

“I have reason to believe that we are currently trapped inside a Time Loop, by an incredibly dangerous, antagonistic entity that is targeting you for assassination.”

You could hear a pin drop, in the stunned silence that followed, as both Aaron and Jessica sat up, tensing.

A sheen of ice fluttered over Jessica’s body, shimmering up and down her form before disappearing as she stared at Micheal, transforming into the spitting image of pure focus.

Aaron took the revelation with a steady pause, his gaze unflinching as he stared down Micheal.

“Elaborate.” Any trace of mirth or frivolity had vanished, replaced by the steely willpower of the Commander of the Round Table.

And so, Micheal did.

Information was a tool, like any other. In the wrong hands, it could invoke devastating effects, bringing about the ruin of countless innocent lives. In the right hands, it could shape the destiny of an entire species, changing the world forevermore.

There were times when Micheal knew he would need to hide information, to keep secret what he knew, to prevent the future from changing.

The higher up you climbed, the more dangerous possessing knowledge of the future became. From beings with Abilities that spied on the contents of one’s mind, to entities that possessed esoteric powers that recorded every word ever uttered planet-wide, secrets became far less secret once you reached the Fifth Layer and beyond.

Even here, on the Third Layer, there existed Void Nobles like Duke Atlas that could scry the past, leaving no stone unturned.

However.

This was not one of those times.

Micheal had weighed the risks, and made his decision.

‘The Round Table needs to know.’

An hour passed, as Micheal and Aaron talked, deep in discussion.

From the existence of Jay sol Arget, to the strange powers Endwalkers possessed, to the startling knowledge that Vesper had passed on, informing them about the existence of a Time Loop.

He told them about Constantine.

He told them about Navir.

He informed Aaron on virtually every single threat he had information on, sharing his own estimations, guesses, and every string of information he possessed from his past life when it came to the foes they might face. He also alluded that his knowledge was related to seeing the future, without outright saying he had regressed.

Their discussion went on for hours more, to the point where food and drinks were brought in, serving lunch for the group, unabated. Shin and Jessica traded stories on the sideline, while Micheal and Aaron remained deep in discussion.

At times, Aaron would call in one of his aides, dispatching them on new orders as Micheal revealed more and more information. After the first 3 hours had passed, Aaron revealed to Micheal that he possessed a Bulsoar Truth Circle, an extraordinary Artifact ring that you couldn’t buy in the Shop, that allowed him to parse truth from lies, a big part of the reason why he was taking Micheal’s word so seriously.

“You’re saying that the Fifth Layer is an enormous tree?” Aaron tapped his fingers on the desk as he spoke.

“A Planetary Tree, with its own atmosphere, yes.”

Their discussion ranged from a variety of topics.

“Dragon Building Liquid? Alright, I’ve noted down the recipe, and will pass it down for testing.”

"Mana Breathing Methods? A whole journal of them?"

They found common ground, time and time again.

“I was hit by the same beams of light just a few days ago. You suspect it was this entity, this Endwalker, ambushing us at the start of the Loop?”

“Exactly. I also believe Bastien, the other human Grandmaster I mentioned, was targeted as well.”

“Alright. My men will put out feelers to try and find him.”

Finally, as the hours winded down, the topic of the immediate present came up.

“You want to set a trap.” Aaron locked eyes with Micheal, his deep voice rumbling as he tapped his fingers on his desk.

“We know that you will be targeted during the Founding Celebration.” Micheal nodded.

“If Vesper’s information is accurate, and we are trapped inside a Time Loop, we need to be proactive. We can’t allow the enemy to dictate our pace.” Micheal explained, turning over a page in the journal, where he detailed several sketches of plans he had come up with.

“We need to strike first, to diverge the Loop from its set course, and to adapt that plan as we go, to ensure Time remains diverging.”

Aaron nodded slowly.

Over the course of their conversation, Micheal had learned a great deal about the infamous Commander of the Round Table. There was only so much you could gleam from years old records, after all – talking in person let him really gather Aaron’s measure.

The White Knight was understandably cautious. As the leader of the largest organization of humans on the Third Layer, he was responsible for an enormous number of lives. He also was the man in charge of spearheading humanity’s standing as a whole, with pockets of outreach spread across the Third Layer, gathering up stray humans and funneling them into Axellion, where they could find safety in numbers.

However, Aaron didn’t let his caution hold him back from making decisive decisions. He showed a hardened expertise and carefully calculated approach that made it very clear why he was the man in charge.

“You’ve given me a lot to think about.” As their conversation finally drew to a close, Aaron shut the notebook Micheal had given him, storing it inside a Spatial Ring.

“If everything you’ve told me here today turns out to be true…” Aaron’s expression softened, ever so slightly.

“I do not know how to repay you.”

There was a quiet pause in the air as Aaron’s words settled.

“You have done more for us, for all mankind, than I can truly comprehend. What you’ve shared with us here today…” Aaron continued, his steady gaze matching Micheal’s own.

“You have changed the fate of the human race as a whole.”

Micheal felt a feeling rise in his chest, warmth spreading, bursting through his veins as Aaron’s words resonated within him.

For days, weeks, and months, close to a year now, he had toiled, throwing himself into incredibly dangerous scenarios, facing down daunting foes and grappling with incredibly stressful situations. Every day, every hour, every minute was spent on the mission.

Ever since he went back in time, the burdens of responsibility and duty had pressed down upon Micheal like a mountain.

The weight was crushing, yet he carried it nevertheless…

Because if he didn’t, then who would?

He didn’t do it for glory.

He didn’t do it for fame.

He did it because it needed to be done.

He lived every day, every decision holding himself to a standard only he knew, so that one day he could look back and stand proud of what he had done, what he had become.

And it was here, for the first time in a while, that he felt something that gave him pause.

Recognition.

True recognition, not only of his efforts, but also proof that he was making a difference.

It was nice.

To see that his struggles, his hard work, all the hardships and pain he had suffered through were finally paying off.

He couldn’t help but to don a small, fierce smile, despite the dire situation they faced.

“Well, there is one thing I’d like to ask for, a small favor that I hope you’ll allow.” He wouldn’t take any Artifacts or other reward from the Round Table, not when they were still in the midst of establishing themselves.

“Anything.” Aaron nodded back instantly.

Micheal’s eyes twinkled as he turned his head, motioning towards Jessica, who was lounging back on the couch.

“I recently made some advancements in my Grandmastery, and could use some practice to help adjust to the changes.” As he spoke, Jessica blinked, her lidded gaze narrowing as she returned his gaze with one of her own.

There were still a few hours left in the day, before he had dinner with the Duke.

“Down for a quick spar?”

Jessica Wiles grinned, standing up.

“Say less.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Woah, this place is sick.”

Micheal ignored Shin as he stepped forward, his eyes narrowing.

‘Divine Scan.’ He took this opportunity to scan one of the attendants that Aaron had assigned to follow them while they were on Camelot 2.0’s grounds.

.

MANA: D+ (Growth Rate: Common or higher)

Path Notes: A Vampiric Human that walks a solitary path. Traces of the Path of the Sword are present.

.

He had just entered into an enormous ‘Black Room’ inside Camelot 2.0. After Jessica had agreed to his sparring request, Micheal, Shin, and Jessica had set off through a maze of hallways, traversing the compound until they reached this specific doorway.

This room here was incredibly unique, a magical space created by a human that possessed the Limited ‘Liminal Expansion’ Ability, an Ability that had been bought out during the First Wave. This rare Ability let the user transform a room, becoming much larger and more sturdy on the inside, expanding Space itself.

This particular room had originally been an underground wine cellar, and was converted into a secret training room that stretched more than a thousand meters across and wide, and more than 50 meters tall, a towering edifice where members of the Round Table could practice their Abilities in secret, away from prying eyes. The sheer scale of the expanded room made it very clear why this Limited Ability had been bought out entirely early on.

‘No need to alarm the natives while we train.’ For the average members of the Round Table, there wasn’t any real issue training in the open air courtyards above.

It was only when it came to the stronger Knights, whose Abilities and Stats stood far above the norm, that issues might crop up.

‘Even the regular rank and file have undergone training.’ Micheal nodded approvingly as he dismissed the Stats page.

A C- in STR was actually quite high, at least compared to regular humans, who normally possessed F tier Strength. It meant this person likely had a number of Abilities that focused on enhancing their physical prowess. Their C- in Regeneration was probably related to their Vampiric Type.

Their Growth Ratings, however, were what Micheal normally expected to see when he scanned a human. Without a Physique or a special Type that enhanced your Growth Ratings, most humans had painfully weak Growth Ratings.

It was just a fact of nature, given the incredibly low energy levels present on Earth, where concepts like Ki or Magic were things of fantasy.

The only standout here was their Rare Growth Rating in Strength, likely influenced by the Abilities they had purchased.

‘How about you two?’ Micheal’s eyes gleamed as he turned his focus forward, looking out across the expansive Black Room.

There, in a closed arena off to his right, a pair of Knights were locked in the middle of an intense duel.

Micheal recognized both of them, unsurprisingly.

The Knights of the Round Table were functionally celebrities in the eyes of humanity, at least in the first timeline.

Gabriel Ferreira, the Brazilian ‘Solar Knight,’ was currently throwing globes of incandescent golden fire at Si Hae-Won, the South Korean ‘Thousand Shadows Knight.’

Gabriel made a huge figure, standing a few inches over seven feet, geared in a set of fully-plated metal armor, save for his bare hands, which glowed with golden light. Bright yellow energy flowed out of the armor’s hinges as he activated his Abilities, launching out small explosions of raw, energized fire.

‘Divine Scan.’

.

.

‘Impressive.’ Two Heroic Growth Ratings put Gabriel well above the average.

Even Micheal, after all the efforts and transformations he had undergone, had only just barely obtained a single Heroic Growth Rating, after obtaining the Body of a Grandmaster.

‘How about you?’ He activated his Eyes of the Deep Ability, turning his focus towards Si Hae-Won.

The Korean cut a dainty figure, dancing between mirages of shadows as she avoided the globes of bright fire, laughing as she moved. She was also geared up in full metal plate, wielding a pair of black sabers.

‘Divine Scan.’

‘It’s a shame we lost her to Sion.’ She never made it to Humanity’s Last Army, instead dying on the Fifth Layer, during Sion Swordsoul's infamous ‘Human Hunt.’

‘And I think Gabriel died to Navir?’ Micheal forced himself to unclench his fists.

It would be different, this time around.

“Over here!” A bubbly yell caught Micheal’s attention as he walked forward, Shin following close behind.

The Black Room was split up into more than a dozen different arena-like sections, with large wooden posts marking off specific areas, designated for training and practice. The black stone that made up the floor, roof, and walls was strangely ubiquitous, a side-effect of the Room Expansion Ability’s power at work.

In the section just off to the left of the room’s entrance, Jessica Wiles now stood, following a thin trail of ice that led all the way to the entrance.

‘She’s fast.’ Blink and you’d miss it. Her ability to instantaneously form an ice trail, and then traverse along it, was incredibly potent.

.

.

‘I knew she becomes strong in the future, but to think, even now…’ Many people’s Growth Ratings weren’t public record in the first timeline, information of those still living often kept secret.

Legendary Tier.

That ranked her talent, when it came to anything related to Regeneration, in the single highest Tier across all of existence. It meant she had the potential to become as close to unkillable as physically possible.

‘S Rank too.’ The difference between an A Rank and S Rank stat was far more significant than the difference between B Rank and A Rank stats.

A Rank stats could be considered the upper limits of ‘normal’ beings. Powerful, yes, but not absurdly so.

S Rank stats, on the other hand, were the domain of the truly powerful, creatures whose abilities defied all rhyme and reason. S Rank stats were incredibly hard to achieve.

“Are you ready now, or do you need to warm up?”

Micheal’s thoughts were interrupted as Jessica smiled and flicked a snowflake at him. The magically hardened ice blurred through the air, streaking towards Micheal’s face at bullet-speed.

Instinctively, Micheal lashed out with his right hand, catching the snowflake in a split second. He studied the small shard of ice before tossing it to the side, and answering Jessica’s grin with one of his own.

“I’m good to go.” Micheal bent his knees slightly, superhuman strength charging before he leapt forward, flinging himself more than a dozen meters into the air.

Two Life Orbs appeared, hidden in his Cloud Stepping Shoes, and slowed his descent until he touched down, standing in the middle of the arena around a dozen meters away from the Glacial Knight.

“Let’s do this.”

.

Chapter 26


.

Micheal entered the Realm of Intent.

The world around him became overlaid in an instant, ephemeral copies of everything in his vision lining up. It was still a strange sight, one that he knew he needed to get used to.

Lightshorn appeared in his hand, the Blood-Refined Mithril blade gleaming as stark white Grandmaster Sword Energy emblazoned alongside its length.

“Wow!”

Across from him, Jessica Wiles smiled, her head tilted slightly to the left as she stared at Micheal’s sword.

“You really are a Grandmaster. You must be super talented!” As she spoke, she slammed her two fists together.

Immediately, a small shockwave blasted through the air as golden Master Tier Fist Energy erupted over her fists. The impact also sent several small snowflakes fluttering into the air, where they slowly began to float down.

“I worked hard.” Micheal didn’t bother trying to correct her.

From her perspective, he must look like a Second Waver who obtained Grandmastery in just a few short years. It was only natural to think someone like that was incredibly talented, on par with a genius like Bastien. If she knew he was actually a Fourth Waver, the misconception would only deepen.

‘Her Mastery is pretty solid.’ Micheal noted, eyeing the depth of the golden Master Tier Fist Energy Jessica wielded.

All the Weapon Mastery Energies were inherently linked together, on a Conceptual level – while he might not be a Grandmaster of the Fist, he could still accurately judge the depth of a Fist Master’s Mastery, just based on his own experience.

‘Right. She hasn’t been Cursed yet.’

In the original timeline, Jessica Wiles suffered from an incurable Curse, a terrible thing wrought by the hands of Ashroth, the nigh unkillable Titled Deity of The Yil.

‘I still have time before he becomes a problem.’

Ashroth climbed up the Layers at a steady pace before eventually deciding to stop on the Sixth Layer, and set up camp, sometime between the Fifth and Sixth Waves. Once there, the Titled Deity went on countless incursions out of boredom, causing an uncountable number of deaths. This ancient monstrosity truly epitomized the dangers of giving any entity absolute power – he abused his power, constantly, repeatedly, without a care for the suffering he spread.

It was humanity’s eternal misfortune that Ashroth’s path crossed with humanity numerous times. The Titled Deity’s actions heavily impacted the number of First Wave humans that remained alive by the time Micheal joined Humanity’s Last Army.

“Don’t even think about holding back, ya hear me?” Jessica interrupted Micheal’s thoughts, snapping him back to the present.

“I know I might look cute and breakable.” She grinned lopsidedly, before her eyes flashed blue and a wave of blue fire swallowed her entire form.

“But I can bounce back from even lethal attacks, so let’s go all out!” The flames slowly faded, revealing her untouched form.

Micheal nodded slightly. She had S Rank Regeneration, after all – who was he to argue with that?

“In that case, I hope you won’t hold back either.” Micheal slowly raised his sword, holding it out in front of him.

“I likewise, can recover from lethal injuries.” He didn’t plan on disclosing the specifics of his Life Orbs, unless truly necessary, just out of habit. Information security was always relevant.

Jessica returned his nod with a serious one of her own.

And then…

The fight was on.

Micheal’s eyes narrowed as a trail of ice appeared in his future vision, running along the ground right up to his feet. With a thought, his Life Orbs lifted him up, hovering a few inches into the air.

A split second later, the ice trail manifested in reality, spiking into existence in a fraction of a second. The sharp ice was a deep, dark blue, blending in with the black stone floor below. A small flurry of snowflakes fluttered off it, floating in the air around him.

‘Fast.’ Even with his precognition, it was still difficult to track the movement of the ice.

Abruptly, a phantom spear of blue blasted free from the icy trail, ghostily passing through Micheal as it pierced his chest.

Micheal smoothly sidestepped in mid-air, using his Life Orbs to counteract his balance, as he avoided the attack before it even began.

A tiny moment later, the spears of ice erupted forth from the ground, spiking through the air where Micheal had just been, following the trail of its ghostly predecessor.

‘1.63 seconds.’ Micheal’s perfect memory let him narrow down the exact amount of time lag between his future sight and the attack.

Instinctively, Micheal knew that this timeframe could change – it would fluctuate based on a number of factors. How strong his Soul was, how clear his grasp of the Realm of Intent was, how focused he was in the moment.

A phantom image of Jessica abruptly appeared, fist poised to slam into his face, barely an inch away from Micheal.

Micheal jerked back, raising Lightshorn out in front of him.

The phantom image shifted subtly, just a tiny fraction of a second after he moved, reacting to Micheal’s new position.

The phantom merged with the real Jessica as she vanished from her original position, and almost instantly reappeared, her golden fists slamming into Micheal’s blade.

A shockwave shattered the air as the two opposing energies collided.

“Wow, that’s really annoying, huh?” Jessica grinned as she locked eyes with Micheal, a flood of golden light clashing with the stark white energy on Micheal’s sword.

Micheal’s eyes narrowed.

‘Is she freezing her Fist Energy?’ His Sword Energy’s superior cutting force pushed her Fist Energy back, but at a much slower rate than he had expected.

‘A Conceptual Power? An Ability?’ Something had to be boosting it.

“You knew where I was going before I moved! Cool!” Jessica laughed out loud.

‘Her reaction speed is insane.’ Micheal leapt backwards, dodging several jutting spikes of ice as they tried to impale him from below.

Jessica Wiles, before she was weakened by Ashroth’s Curse, specialized in two specific types of combat – extreme, close range hand-to-hand, and large area denial and control.

‘She reacted to my new position, adjusting her manifestation point in less than a tenth of a second.’ Micheal’s analytical mind kicked into overdrive as he processed everything in his vision.

‘Am I thinking faster?’ The thought struck him as he landed and slid on the ground, his mind racing.

The Realm of Intent’s precognition had an effect not only on his senses, but also on his thoughts, in a way he couldn’t quite qualify. It was as if his mind was processing information from the future, feeding into his instincts on a subconscious level.

‘I need to get used to this.’

A phantom ice trail and a phantom image of Jessica appeared once more, just inches from Micheal’s face.

Instantly, Micheal dropped a Temporal Bubble on the image’s location, slowing down the flow of time.

In the same moment, he chanted out loud,

“S’vol Reize.” Micheal cast the 2nd Circle Spell, Mana Blade.

“I’ve always wanted to fight a Grandmaster!” Jessica yelled as she manifested once more, this time her fists clashing with a newly formed Mana Blade, setting off an explosion of energy as Grandmaster Sword Energy met Master Tier Fist Energy in a brilliant cascade of light.

And it was here that something unexpected happened.

The Brand of Janus pulsed in Micheal’s Soul as he created a Temporal Bubble, touching upon the River of Time.

That pulse created a Temporal Resonance, spreading throughout his Soul.

This resonance was an incredibly faint thing, to the point where it was virtually undetectable most of the time. Normally, the resonance would spread and then fade, as Micheal released the Time Bubble and moved on.

However…

In this moment, while Micheal was grasping onto the Realm of Intent, his Soul existed in an excited state, directly tapping into the Cognitive Sea, giving him a direct connection to the River of Time.

As the resonance spread throughout his Soul…

For the first time ever, Micheal felt it.

The world around him slowed to a crawl.

‘What?’

Micheal blinked as he felt his pulse throb, staring at a world moving in slow motion.

A bright, golden explosion of energy was mid-explosion just a meter away, as Jessica’s Fist Energy collided with his Mana Blade. The clashing particles of energy shot out in a flurry of colors, tracing bizarre patterns in the air as they fluctuated aimlessly.

‘What is this?’

The Temporal Bubble in front of him felt alive, in a way he had never noticed before. He could feel the ebb and flow of time, the tiny adjustments to reality that altered the flow of the River of Time in this specific area, at a level and depth he had never experienced.

Adrenaline pulsed in his veins as he realized he was experiencing something akin to Enlightenment, an opportunity he needed to grasp now or forever lose.

‘I need to… control it…’ Micheal stretched his hand out towards the Time Bubble, as he tried to grasp ahold of this fleeting sensation.

The resonance of Time fluttered, just out of reach as his Soul tried to lock onto it…

Until it hit his Mana Circles.

Anchored in the Conceptual Powers of Infinity and Eternity, his Echoes of the Eternal Mana Circles latched onto the Temporal Resonance like a thirsting man lost in the desert finding water.

His Mana Circles cast his Soul aglow with power as they seized upon the Temporal Resonance…

And Micheal gained control.

Micheal looked at the Temporal Bubble, as if seeing it for the first time.

Its shape and design was crude, artificially cut into a round circle, by a Soul that lacked the expertise and understanding to do more. What had seemed perfect and smooth before now looked jagged and unrefined, hastily cobbled together.

With a single thought, the Time Bubble shifted.

Jessica’s eyes narrowed as she dashed forward, blasting the floating Mana Blade away. Spikes of ice formed on her fist as she lunged forward, her right fist aimed right for Micheal’s head.

And then…

Micheal moved, unnaturally quickly, as he slipped around her fist, dodging the attack in one almost eerie motion.

“Woah!” Jessica dived and rolled, throwing up a wall of ice as she spun around, sliding along the ground.

“Freaky!”

Micheal floated, his Life Orbs keeping him up a few inches off the ground with Lightshorn in hand, as he stared at the icy wall.

‘It worked.’

In that tense moment, he had changed the entire shape of the Temporal Bubble, to the point where it no longer resembled a bubble, but rather, a large, fifteen meters wide section of the world that he designated, slowed down in time.

‘I was unaffected.’

His newfound prowess let him slow down the flow of Time for everything in that area… except himself.

Like a swan dancing upon a river, Micheal’s Mana Circles burned as his Soul shifted the currents of the River of Time, setting its course while letting him swim freely.

‘Incredible.’ Micheal’s perfect memory let him grasp every single minor step he took, immortalizing the technique and maintaining his understanding all in one fell swoop.

With a flick of his wrist, Lightshorn bisected the frozen wall, a slice of raw, Grandmaster Sword Energy shattering it like it didn’t exist.

Micheal flew over the broken wall, landing upon a boulder-sized chunk of blue ice.

“Not bad.” Micheal grinned as he looked down at Jessica, who was eyeing him with narrowed eyes.

“Hmph. Let’s see how you handle this!” Jessica threw herself forward, and their duel began again.

A dozen exchanges went by as sword met fist, ice clashing with metal, in a grand display of Weapon Mastery prowess.

Time and time again, Micheal reshaped his Temporal Bubbles, using his newfound understanding to manipulate them in a way more favorable to himself.

The minutes slipped away as Micheal adapted to controlling the Realm of Intent, rapidly mastering the power almost like it was second nature.

He wasn’t sure if it was luck, talent, or just the confluence of circumstances, with the Brand of Janus and his Eternal Mana Circles working in his favor, but he found it easier and easier to maintain the Realm of Intent as the spar went on.

“Woah, that one almost got me.” Micheal uttered as he knelt down, narrowly dodging an enormous fist of ice that whistled over his head. He slid around as he knelt down, using his Life Orbs to find his balance as he smoothly stood back up, Lightshorn held out in front of him.

“No it didn’t.” Jessica came to a stop, sweat dripping down her face as she glared at Micheal in consternation.

“I haven’t even come close to hitting you.” She pursed her lips.

It was true – even as he experimented with his newfound Time Zones, as he cheekily decided to call them, it rapidly became apparent how powerful a combo this was.

The ability to see the future was one thing – the ability to slow down Time for everyone else near you raised Micheal’s already fast reaction speed to a purely unnatural level.

‘My Mana Circles aren’t strong enough.’ The only problem, he found, was that his two Mana Circles weren't cutting it, not to handle this kind of output.

His Soul was more than strong enough, with the Brand of Janus and the Realm of Intent providing crucial links to stabilize this Ability, but his Mana Circles lacked the depth he needed to take full advantage of this newfound power.

‘I’ll need to commit to growing them, as soon as possible.’ He made a mental promise, adding it to the list of things to work on.

“Alright, if close combat ain’t enough…” Jessica abruptly vanished, reappearing almost a hundred meters in the distance as she traversed along the frozen ground.

By this point in the duel, the entire arena had been covered in a heavy sheen of ice. Micheal had been forced to use his Cloud Stepping Shoes and Life Orbs to stay afloat just to avoid giving the Glacial Knight a huge advantage.

“Try not to die!” Micheal’s future sight abruptly transformed.

“Glacial Domain…” His supernaturally strong senses heard her whisper, the words carrying in the still air as Jessica knelt down and slammed her hands into the ground.

“Ice Age.”

The world turned blue.

Micheal’s eyes blazed with energy as he imbued his entire body with Sword Energy, shredding parts of his clothes in his haste to encase his entire body.

Not even a split second later, he was fully encased in a world of frozen ice.

It was a stark transformation, happening so quickly that, if not for his future sight, he wasn’t sure he would’ve been able to react. The cold was incredibly biting, sapping at his will and strength far more than anything else Jessica had thrown at him.

“Shatter.” Micheal muttered as he swept his arms out, flaring his Ki.

The sheer raw cutting power of his Grandmaster Sword Energy ruptured the ice around him in a giant, explosive shockwave as he burst free, freeing himself in one glorious leap. The Sword Energy had helped shield him from the freezing cold, preventing what would otherwise have completely frozen his blood, muscles, and bones in an instant.

It would’ve almost certainly killed anyone else.

“Wow.” As Micheal flew up through the air, his enhanced strength sending him flying high in the sky, he activated his Cloud Stepping Shoes, jumping off the air as he surveyed the arena around him.

In what had once been a large, empty arena, now stood an enormous iceberg, easily 50 meters tall, towering upwards out behind him at an angle. It was a sight to see, a massive edifice of blue and white, all jagged edges and rough lines.

“You’re fine even after that? Geez, you really don’t go down easy, huh?”

The Glacial Knight’s voice carried as she manifested, appearing half made of ice and half flesh as she rose from the peak of the huge glacier, grinning at Micheal.

“I try not to.” Micheal returned her smile with a mischievous one of his own.

Before the pair of them could do anything else, however…

“Oi! Jessica! What did we say about freezing the arenas!” Gabriel Ferreira, the Solar Knight, yelled angrily from the sidelines. Yellow flames glowed around his figure as he leapt towards them landing on the edge of the giant iceberg in a flash of golden light.

Jessica’s Ice Age technique had spread past their arena and bled into the surrounding areas, coating the general vicinity in a thick layer of ice. The brunt of the attack had been aimed at Micheal, but even the outside portions were still powerful enough to form a layer of ice at least a foot thick for hundreds of meters.

“Oops! Sorry, Gabe!” Jessica tilted her head slightly to the left as she stepped fully free of the ice, her body transforming back to normal flesh.

Si Hae-Won, the South Korean ‘Thousand Shadows Knight’ morphed into existence, appearing from one of the shadowy edges near the top of the glacier.

“Don’t listen to him, Jess. He’s just mad he can’t land a hit.” The Thousand Shadows Knight giggled as she took off her helmet, revealing pale white skin, dark brown eyes, and tied-up black hair. She looked to be in her mid 20s.

“Not my fault you like to scamper in the shadows like a rat, Hae-Won.” Gabriel bit back as he took off his helmet, revealing a bronzed face with green eyes and brown hair, a man in his late 20s.

Micheal released the Realm of Intent as he watched Shin teleport into existence, appearing beside him. It was good to know that his future sight could also predict true teleportation.

“Bro… that was sick.” Shin held out a fist, which Micheal swiftly bumped back,

“Good job out there.” Micheal grinned as he accepted the compliment.

“Thanks.”

“Oh hey,” The Solar Knight grunted as he stepped forward, acknowledging Micheal and Shin’s existence with a nod.

“This the pair Yama was talking about?” He turned towards Jessica.

“It is! We were sparring!” She stepped up to introduce them.

“Gabe, Hae-Won, meet Micheal and Shin.” She smiled winningly, before turning towards the duo.

“Micheal and Shin, meet Gabe and Hae-Won!” She clapped her hands together.

“Well met.” Micheal nodded while Shin waved.

“I heard about your fight with the Apex. Yama mentioned you provided crucial aid.” Gabriel stared at Micheal intensely as he continued,

“Good job. We need all the help we can get up here.”

Si Hae-Won, in the background, returned Shin’s wave with one of her own.

“We just did what we felt was right.” Micheal returned with a slight nod.

Gabriel grunted in response, vaguely approvingly.

“And on that note.” Micheal considered the time that had passed, making a decision as he realized the spar had lasted longer than anticipated.

“I think we’ll call it here.” He turned towards Jessica, who looked back expectantly.

“I’d love to spar more, but…” Micheal continued, his eyes narrowing.

“We’ve got an appointment with the Duke for dinner, and we can’t afford to be late!”

.

Chapter 27


.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

An unknown amount of time later, on the Second Layer…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Shuck.

Shuck.

Shuck.

Prime carefully peeled back layer after layer as he shucked a large red fruit, removing its thick fleshy skin. The fruit was a strange thing, as big as a bowling ball, and glowing a deep, dark red, with a large, green stem that struck out at an odd angle from its roof.

“You’re cheating, aren’t you?”

Yvvtal’s rough, gravelly voice echoed in the dark air as he grumbled, glaring at Prime.

The former Toren was a sight to see, wearing the body of a pale human with the Celestial Silverback Type. He had the rough features of a large, muscular human male, with thick gray fur peeking out under the edges of the black leather garments he wore. In his hands was a large green knife, and a similar glowing red fruit.

“Of course not.” Prime lied without missing a beat, blonde curls of hair shifting as he wiped his brow.

He absolutely was cheating, stopping time to ensure each cut was perfectly performed.

“Geh. You humans are so frail.” Yvvtal snorted, with a shake of his head as he resumed slicing.

“Alas. That’s a curse you will have to bear.” Prime chuckled as he continued shucking.

Yvvtal’s Spirit Body had hardened, solidifying around his current form. This was both good and bad for the former Toren. The good was that his body no longer rejected his Soul, and he had fully returned to a life among the living. The bad was that if this body died, then he died with it.

The former Toren also had to get used to living as an entirely different species – a Human, specifically, a Human with the Celestial Silverback Type.

It was an interesting phenomenon. Despite possessing a human body, Yvvtal was unable to access the Shop. Clearly, the strange, magical Shop must have its origin tied to the human Soul.

“Why those foolish Dragons made such an impudent test I have no idea.” The Fallen Deity grumbled as he continued to peel back fruit.

Prime only chuckled, pausing as he considered his current circumstances.

The duo were currently resting inside the Tomb of Hapthos, one of the Twelve Tombs, within an eerie underground pavilion filled with fruit trees. Above them, a fake blue sky spread out, chiseled into the roof more than 15 meters high. Small crystals were set into the roof, glowing with golden light at intervals, evenly spread out.

The Twelve Tombs were a series of ancient Inheritances left behind by the Blue Drakes many hundreds of years ago, here on the Second Layer.

These Inheritances had remained sealed off, locked away from even the most fervent of Byren Martial Artists… until humanity got to them.

‘It is most curious.’ Prime thought as he continued handling the knife, pausing time every now and then to get the angle just right.

The golden hue of Master Tier Sword Energy flickered on his knife, showcasing Prime’s newfound advancement.

True to his word, or at least, Micheal’s Recorded Clone’s word, the teachings the man had offered had been incredibly poignant. The Life Orb Master was incredibly skilled when it came to Sword Energy, far and beyond Prime’s own level.

It was purely thanks to his direct, guided teachings, inside Tallanoran’s Inheritance, that Prime had finally advanced into becoming a Master.

This advancement had proven enormously useful, especially here on the Second Layer.

The native Byrens were a martially inclined species – they respected strength, and Weapon Mastery was seen as the peak of their culture. Becoming a Master had opened doors for Prime, making his journeys through the Ancient World significantly easier.

‘The Blue Drakes have a complex history.’

This was the second Tomb of the Twelve Tombs he had managed to infiltrate, though he was still in the midst of unravelling its mysteries.

The first, the Tomb of Iguel, had required a long and complicated string of specific puzzles that he had needed to solve in order to gain entry. Prime had lost count of the number of days he had spent frozen in time, whiling away at the First Tomb’s tests.

‘I had to learn an entirely new language.’ Learning how to read the tongue the Blue Drakes left behind had taken a herculean effort, for it was a dead language, held secret by their kind till the bitter end.

The automatic translation feature that came with the Shop was something Prime had taken for granted, he’d realized, once he stumbled upon the First Tomb. It translated all verbal communication, letting humans make free contact with the alien species of the 7 Layers without issue… but written communication was an entirely separate matter, only working for Earth-based languages.

‘Yet, the reward was worth it.’ Among other things, he was now able to independently verify at least some of the information Micheal had given him, learning more about the ancient history of the Dark Wraiths, the Blue Drakes… and the Torens.

‘Orion.’ The name evoked powerful emotions.

Fighting against Orion Thunderfist had felt akin to fighting a force of nature.

The ancient warrior was incredibly skilled, to a point where it was truly, genuinely impressive. He was the single most dangerous entity Prime had ever encountered.

And yet, the fact that Orion was now a Titled Deity was even more shocking.

The thought stuck with Prime, to the point where he frowned and came to a halt.

The world flickered as Prime froze time, activating his World Matrix Type Ability.

Prime calmly set his knife and half-shucked Dragonfruit aside, before tapping on his Spatial Ring, and bringing out the journal Micheal had passed off to him, turning to a specific page.

In the background, Yvvtal sat frozen mid shuck, angrily glaring daggers at the fruit in his hand.

This particular test was understandably frustrating – Blue Drakes possessed a special characteristic, according to the records Prime had obtained from the first Tomb: when they bathed themselves in their own Draconic Flame, their entire musculature underwent a series of temporary enhancements.

These enhancements allowed the Dragons to manipulate not only their claws, but their entire bodies, with incredible precision. This test was meant for a Blue Drake to pass, by perfectly shucking the native Dragonfruits that were a common part of a Blue Drake’s diet.

It was a surprisingly difficult test to pass, especially for those unable to read the Borandi instructions, the name for the written language Blue Drake’s used when they transformed into their humanoid-ish bipedal forms.

“How am I going to face any of you, when I could not defeat Orion alone…” Prime muttered as he stared down the open journal, to a list titled 'The Five Calamities.'

Jay sol Arget.

Sion Swordsoul.

Bosmond Jingleton.

Ashroth.

‘…’ He gazed at the final name with a hint of trepidation.

Navir.

This list alone had changed his entire mindset.

Petty things like emotional grudges no longer seemed that important, not in the face of the horrors that humanity was set to encounter.

A lesser man might shy away. They might say ‘Why should this be my responsibility? I just want to survive,’ and indeed, even Prime felt tempted, once he realized the full scale of the difficulties ahead of him. The future, as it currently stood, seemed almost hopeless.

However.

‘I made my choice long ago.’

Step by step.

Moment by moment.

No matter how long it took.

He would continue to walk forward.

This was the path he chose and…

He would not give up.

A few seconds passed as Prime pondered in silence. Those seconds passed into minutes as time stretched on, frozen in a world that only moved when he allowed it.

Finally, Prime sighed.

“How indeed.”

Prime flipped through a few pages in the journal, settling on a page near the back.

.

—- Nameless Mana Breathing Method used by Typhon, a Transcendent Dragon —-

Rank: SSS+

Effects: Allows specialization in either the development of Mana Circles or of a Mana Heart, or both. Vastly strengthens Mana density and capacity, greatly enhances the user’s body, and grants unique properties to one’s blood.

Successful practice of this Mana Breathing Method shifts a creature’s body into a state of constant evolution and growth that only ceases with death.

Successful practice of this Mana Breathing Method to Completion grants its user the ability to transform into a Dragon.

Note: Only a Dragon, the descendants of a Dragon, or a being in possession of Draconic Blood can practice this Mana Breathing Method.

.

This Mana Breathing Method paved the way forward, in his eyes. It was his answer to the question of how he could possibly face what was to come.

‘Once I finish with this Tomb, I’ll begin a Ki Transferal.’ It was a decision he had made after he achieved Mastery, as he began to plan for the long term.

Ki was a simple energy, easy to cultivate, without requiring any expansive Breathing Methods or rituals - though the danger of Heart Trials proved a daunting aspect to some. Cultivating a Mana Breathing Method was often seen as carrying less risk.

Therein, however, lay the problem.

As Prime learned more about Mana Breathing Methods, and the countless years of research and development that had established them, he had made up his mind about his future goals.

If Prime had the luxury of many, many years to work with, he might have considered maintaining his Ki Cultivation. The slow, steady progression was a powerful balm, enhancing his body and Soul at a core level over time. The Heart Trials were manageable, and the simplicity of Ki made it incredibly versatile as an energy source.

Alas, the future came all too quickly – should he tarry too long, countless humans that had climbed on ahead would fall to evils they could not defend against.

He could not allow that.

He owed it, not just to himself, but to those who had believed in him, and the mission he carried.

Prime flipped through a few more pages, landing on one page in particular, near the middle of the journal.

Mana and Ki were incompatible within the same body… however, because of the simplistic nature of Ki, it was possible to convert one’s Ki into Mana.

Outlined in this journal was an entire methodology describing, in great detail, an incredibly dangerous process that let one convert Ki into Mana, a technique humanity wouldn't discover for many years.

The process required a fully fleshed out Mana Breathing Method, and a very strong control of one’s Ki. It was also impossible to revert – Ki could transform into Mana, thanks to its simple nature, but Mana could not transform into Ki.

According to Micheal's future sight, most humans would rather simply disperse their Ki if they were opting to switch over to a Mana Breathing Method - Ki Transferals were dangerous and experimental, coming with a load of restrictions and burdens that they placed on one's body.

Taking this path meant forever giving up on Ki Cultivation. Once you accepted a Mana Heart into your body, it was virtually impossible to cultivate Ki. The two opposing energies would clash and destroy one’s body from the inside out.

‘A Ki Transferal requires minute perfection in every breath.’ A single misstep could prove fatal… but Prime wasn’t particularly worried.

His ability to pause time meant he could take every single step at a steady, measured pace, turning what was normally a dangerous and unfeasible process into something relatively safe.

Prime ruminated for a few minutes, taking his time as he enjoyed the solitude and quiet here in his own private world.

It was one of the perks of his World Matrix Type Ability – if he ever found his patience tested by Yvvtal’s incessant grumbling, he could simply freeze time to blow off steam. It made him appear far more sociable than he really was.

‘Telekinetic Push.’ Prime activated an Ability in his frozen world, causing the Dragonfruit to float up off the ground and into the air in front of him.

“I suppose I should focus on the present.” He nodded to himself as he grabbed the fruit in one hand, while holding the journal in the other.

Prime flipped to a page, near the back of the journal Micheal had given him.

The List of Legends.

A collection of the most powerful Artifacts humanity ever observed, at some point in the future, according to Micheal's future sight.

Prime’s gaze scrolled down the list, his eyes narrowing as he passed over the Artifact ranked 6th – the Crown of the Angel King.

A few ranks down, however, his scrolling stopped, landing on the Artifact ranked 8th.

Ignister – the Skysplitter Axe.

This Legendary Artifact, according to the notes in the journal, was supposed to show up on the Fifth Layer several years from now – it was an incredibly powerful Artifact that exponentially enhanced the power of any swing made with it. For it to have obtained Legendary status based off that alone meant it was an Artifact of true, enormous power.

An image of each Artifact had been inscribed into the journal, in exacting detail, as if transferred perfectly from memory.

And in that image of Ignister, the Skysplitter Axe…

A series of runes ran along the heft of the Artifact, glowing with orange light.

Runes that Prime now recognized, thanks to the countless days he had slaved away, learning an entire dead language from scratch.

‘A Borandi cipher.’

He had paused time for more than a month in order to break this very code.

‘Makatesh’ gu Guiven Wyrn tol vn Shosh.’

Prime stood up, calmly placing the journal back in his Spatial Ring out of habit.

He then began to walk forward.

He passed by Yvvtal, frozen mid-shuck, and soon found himself near the edge of his awareness, before a large, black door, hewn out of some mystical crystal substance he didn’t recognize. It was set into the dark grey stone walls, all lined with tens of thousands of Borandi glpyhs. A bowl was carved into the door, the place where there Dragonfruits were tested and, in every one of their previous attempts, had been rejected.

This Inheritance, like all of the Twelve Tombs, was heavily enchanted, covered in layer after layer of magical restrictions crafted with the inherent magical knowledge of the Blue Drake species. According to local Byren sources, attempting to damage the Inheritance would set off layers of dangerous defense mechanisms that would bathe entire forces in waves of immolating fire, annihilating any intruder. Local Byren Sects had tried for centuries to crack the magic on these Inheritances, all to no avail.

However…

Prime slowly began to stretch his arms, as he brought out a fine metal sword and one of his Memory Journals, one of the rare few Artifacts that actually had a use-case, here in his world of frozen time.

He left the Dragonfruit floating in the air behind him.

‘If I can’t brute force my way through this test…’ Even with his perfectly aimed cuts, he was having trouble reconstructing exactly what the test sought. There appeared to be some hidden aspect of the test he was unaware of, perhaps something only a real Blue Drake would know.

‘I simply have to understand how it functions.’ Prime set his Memory Journal to the side, leaving it floating in the air around half a meter away from him.

Golden energy lit up Prime’s blade as he began to hack and saw away at the door. While the Sword Energy couldn’t interact freely like it would in real time, the powerful cutting force was still useful as an enhancer to his weapon’s sharpness.

Slowly, bit by bit, Prime began to hack his way through the magically sealed walls.

Each bit of progress he made was incredibly small, thanks to the absurd enchantments shielding the Inheritance. The sheer redundant forces blocking all invasion were truly a spectacle to see, the strange, inherent Magic of the Blue Drakes at work.

His measured progress came in the form of millimeters, stab after stab, cut after cut.

Yet, because the world was frozen in time, no alarms went off, no fire came to wash the world in death, no traps were sprung. The walls simply gave way, bit by little bit.

Seconds turned to minutes, minutes turned to hours.

Eventually, after nearly 2 hours of dedicated effort…

A glint of blue light flashed free.

Prime’s eyes narrowed as he stared at the fruit of his labors.

A small, crudely bored hole, pierced fully through the side of the thick stone wall. On the other side of the hole, he could just barely make out several large, glowing blue glyphs.

With a grunt, Prime leveraged his sword into the hole. He moved carefully, sliding the tip of the blade along the edge.

Another 20 minutes of effort went into widening the damaged section, until, in one rough motion, Prime ripped out a huge chunk of the wall.

The bits of stone floated in the air just a few inches from his face, hovering. Prime pushed them out of the way, peering now into the bowels of the enchanted wall.

With his left hand, he snatched up his Memory Journal, his lips pursing as he eyed the results.

Inside the wall were hundreds of complex, glowing Borandi glyphs, all corded along several rope-like lines of glowing purple crystal.

‘Does it travel along the entire wall?’ Prime began to decipher the inner workings, copying down everything he saw into his Memory Journal.

‘I’ll need to uncover the entire wall.’ He took the realization with a steady pause as he turned to gaze at the entirety of the nearly 50 meters wide underground pavilion.

It was an enormous undertaking, requiring a truly unfathomable amount of effort, yet if his estimation was correct…

Prime began to smile.

He had found a method to cheat his way through this test.

“Makatesh’ gu Guiven Wyrn tol vn Shosh.” He repeated the line that was inscribed into the heft of the Skysplitter Axe.

‘Entombed, herein lies the Heart of the Twelve.’

Before he left to climb up to the Third Layer…

Prime had a mystery to solve.

.

Chapter 28


.

Breathe in.

Breathe out.

‘Calm.’

Breathe in.

Breathe out.

Micheal’s Ki fluctuated as he meditated, the warm energy flowing through his veins as he completed a cycle, circulating his Ki.

He was back in the guest quarters Vesper had provided them, after returning from his meeting with the Round Table. Shin was in the other room, both getting ready for the feast the Duke had invited them to.

'It's been a good day.' He'd successfully forged ties that he would need to rely on in the coming days while also informing Aaron of the threats they faced. Overall, he'd made some very important progress.

‘I’ve reached Mid Sky Tier.’ He flexed the depth of his Ki, letting the energy coil about him.

Obtaining the Body of a Grandmaster had accelerated his growth, helping him push forward, to recovering the strength from his previous life. The burgeoning energy felt incredibly comfortable as it flowed, passively enhancing his body.

This was an area where his future knowledge really shined.

Retreading the same path he had already stepped once was far, far easier than cultivating blindly.

‘The latent energy in the air is so much more dense.’ If he played his cards correctly, using every Artifact and trick in the book, he might be able to break into Lord Tier in a matter of weeks.

It was an absurd speed of cultivation, made possible only because Micheal had already obtained King Tier Ki in his first life. When you took that, and combined it with the multiple transformations he had undergone thanks to his Grandmastery, and general improvements to his Physique...

That experience provided the crucial links his body and Soul needed as it developed.

Any other person trying to cultivate at this speed would risk serious injury, to both their body and their Soul, and likely death. It was a feat only a Regressor could manage.

‘I need to keep pushing, for more.’ His eyes gleamed.

‘I should aim for the highest Tier.’

Mortal.

Earth.

Sky.

Lord.

King.

Emperor.

God.

The Tiers of Ki were separated by a stark hierarchy.

As one advanced their Ki, not only would their body grow, but so would their Soul.

‘The higher Tiers of Ki are insanely powerful.’

It was what set Ki apart from Mana, and a big reason why, even after learning he was talented when it came to controlling Mana, he made the decision to keep his Ki, opting only to form Mana Circles, and not a Mana Heart.

The sheer, raw power offered by the highest Tiers of Ki was simply incredible.

Mana Hearts, forged by complex Mana Breathing Methods, could grant any number of powerful, esoteric effects. This was a region where Mana really shined, the sheer complexity and depth therein was mind-boggling.

However…

When it came to raw output, Ki stood above and beyond the rest.

‘I got a taste of that with King Tier.’ His cultivation had been hard earned, obtained by using multitudes of Artifacts, Abilities, and really anything he could get his hands on in his first life.

By no means had he cultivated perfectly – in his first life, he’d lacked the expertise and knowledge he now possessed. His path to obtaining King Tier Ki was a shaky thing patchily held together by a stubborn body and Soul that refused to give up, and a hodgepodge of Abilities that supported him.

‘My Ironblood Body Type is probably the only reason I managed to hit King Tier in one piece.’ The Type Ability he had obtained in his first life had provided the bedrock upon which his Ki was built.

‘That, and Talos Mind Power.’

Micheal opened up the Shop, scrolling over until he found the Ability.

.

— - Talos Mind Power — -

Talos Mind Power grants the user a spiritually enhanced mind, greatly enhancing concentration and empowering one’s spirit, as well as enhancing one’s memory.

.

For a pricey 4,100,000 Points, it was this Ability that allowed him, a human with no privileged knowledge or experience, to obtain not only King Tier Ki but also achieve Grandmastery in his first life.

However…

‘I’m running out of Ability slots.’

It was one of the both upsides and downsides that came with obtaining Abilities or powers on your own – the Shop would adapt any power you obtained to suit your body and Soul, but in doing so, it would take up an Ability slot.

Micheal was under no illusions that his Eternal Mana Circles would’ve formed as smoothly and safely as they had, had they not been adapted through his Ability slots. The same applied for his Temporal Bubble Ability.

‘My Eyes of the Deep are an incredibly versatile tool.’ It would let him scan his enemies, to understand what kind of threat he was facing, as well as identify any Deities he might face up against. They could also be used to grasp the inner working of most Artifacts, an aspect Micheal had largely ignored up to this point.

This was the Ability he was most open to dropping, should he find an alternative way to maintain a perfect memory.

'Perhaps I could merge it with Talos Mind Power?' It was possible to merge similar Abilities, freeing up a slot, but there was no guarantee that these two powers would prove compatible.

‘Temporal Bubble is an Ability I’m only now beginning to advance.’ He was certain that if he mastered his newfound control of Time, he would be able to evolve this Ability into something greater.

The rest of his Abilities were not up for debate.

‘I need to plan for the long term, for my ultimate goal.’ Micheal nodded to himself, as he scrolled through the Shop, before landing on the one Ability he wanted, above all others, to obtain in the long-run.

.

—-Abilities—-

Thunder Legs Type - 860,400 (4/5)

Armageddon Matrix Type - 25,250,000 (0/3)

Golden Shield Warrior Type - 500,000 (9/10)

Eldritch Snarer Type - 235,000 (5/5)

Red Orc Type - 88,000 (9,000/9,000)

Fire Weaver Type - 23,000 (1,200/1,200)

Void Ripper Type - 40,000 (10/10)

Shock Geniton Type - 1,800,500 (2/2)

Black Mace Type - 12,000 (330/330)

Quickstep Type - 280,000 (18/18)

Frozen Warrior Type - 70,000 (250/250)

Armor Force - 92,000 (30/30)

Healing Aura - 65,000 (800/800)

Immemorial Vision - 212,000 (14/25)

White Mane Clone - 74,000 (50/50)

Impact Release - 45,000 (20/20)

Guiding Light - 22,800,000 (0/1) Expand - 65,000 (10/10)

Electric Touch - 80,000 (250/250)

Ocean Clone - 260,000 (35/35)

… (37/41 page)

.

‘A lot of the Abilities have been bought out since I last checked.’ He noted. The Fourth Wave had seen a billion humans arrive on the First Layer – the rate at which Limited Abilities were being bought out had rapidly increased.

However, one Ability in particular on this list, remained unpurchased.

.

Guiding Light - 22,800,000 (0/1)

.

He pulled up the Ability’s description.

.

— - Guiding Light — -

The user will be Guided by The Light.

.

‘I need to save room to buy this Ability, at all costs.’ He stared at the rather bare-bones description, recalling memories from the first timeline as he sat, lost in thought.

This was one of the single most powerful Abilities listed in the Shop, and one of the options he was considering, for his final Ability slot.

Guiding Light was an Ability infamously bought by a human named Maximillian Frost. Presumably, that wasn’t his real name, but rather, a moniker he took up.

Maximillian was a serial killer.

In order to fund this incredibly expensive Ability, sometime around the end of the Fifth Wave, Maximillian would go on to kill thousands of people, a sizable fraction of which were his own fellow humans, just trying to survive.

And once he obtained this Ability…

Micheal closed the screen with a dark look.

The crimes he committed were unspeakable, not just on his fellow man, but on all the other species he encountered.

For every Jessica Wiles, every Aaron Bartram, every Yama that humanity possessed, heroes who put it all on the line for mankind, there always seemed to exist grim counterparts, like Maximillian Frost, who stood for nothing more than their own selfish desires and greed.

‘If only he had used that power to help humanity.’ There was so much potential lost, all because of the actions of one man.

Guiding Light was an Ability that, according to Dark Void’s research records, tapped into a ‘Conceptual Entity’ known only as ‘The Light.’

Everything Dark Void knew about this Ability was based on data obtained after Maximillian was eventually killed by the Titled Deity Navir, and their own observations of the many, many crimes perpetrated by the rogue human.

It was an Ability that let its user obtain ‘guidance’ on a Conceptual level.

Maximillian would ask his Ability how to accomplish a certain goal, and in turn, would be not only shown every step necessary to accomplish that goal, but guided through those steps.

He could ask his Ability ‘How do I kill this person while remaining undetected?’ and it would immediately begin guiding him, step by step, through the exact process he would need to follow to achieve that goal.

This ‘guiding’ process let the Ability assume automatic, perfect control, something Maximillian could disengage at any point in time, wherein the Ability actively controlled his body to follow the exact steps it outlined.

This Ability’s potential was almost limitless.

Maximillian used it to perform incredible acts, from murdering powerful individuals in full public view and escaping entirely unharmed, to robbing even the most closely guarded treasures from powerful rulers, to far darker deeds, crimes that violated the basic tenets of humanity.

When you could achieve almost any goal with complete assuredness, it was easy to see how a man of Maximillian’s disrepute could abuse such a power.

The Light’s ability to analyze, scan, and predict was simply unmatched, on every level. This was an Ability that was almost impossible to defend against, at its very core.

Maximillian Frost grew to immense infamy because of this, until he met his eventual demise at the hands of Navir.

‘How did he die to Navir? Does his Title interfere with the functions of the Ability?’ It was a mystery that remained unsolved, at least by the time Micheal died in his first life.

‘Regardless. I should begin planning for this now.’ The Points Wall on the Third Layer was measured in the low millions. It was only once he reached the Fourth Layer that he would stand a chance at obtaining this Ability, assuming his Soul was strong enough - and even then, he almost certainly would have to climb to the Fifth Layer, if he wanted to find opportunities to gain enough Points.

‘Obtaining this Ability would be incredibly helpful.’ It might be his ticket to the future, to combatting the monsters humanity was destined to face, and even beyond that, to solving the mystery that was the Final Layer.

Even if he didn't personally obtain it, he at least needed to prevent Maximillian Frost from getting it.

Micheal’s eyes twitched open as Shin teleported into the room, interrupting his thoughts.

Shin was dressed sharply, in the Void Noble’s equivalent of a green jacket, suit, and tie, a set of clothes that Vesper had gifted them out of pity. He had on a pair of fine dark boots, and long, silken black pants, dressed to the nines.

It was a similar outfit to what Micheal was wearing, except his own jacket was a colored light blue, matching his eyes. Colorful, flashy outfits were all the rage in Void Noble fashion, at least at this point in time.

“Yo – you ready to go? One of Vesper’s maids is at the door.” Shin spun around, his jacket twirling in the air as he teleported sporadically around the room.

“That fancy Noble chick is totally crushing on you, bro.” Shin offered his decidedly unsolicited opinion.

“Have you seen how she looks at you?”

“…I’m all set.” Micheal stood up, straightening his jacket with a nod as he ignored Shin’s remarks.

“Let’s go.” He walked over towards the door, pausing before he opened it as he looked back at Shin with a grin.

“It’s show time.”

Shin grinned back.

“Time to meet the family!”

.
