Chapter 29


.

“You look marvelous!”

Vesper von Atlas smiled as she accepted the compliment.

“Aww, thank you, Shin! You look quite handsome, yourself!”

The trio were currently standing in a large foyer, one of several just outside the Grand Hall of Castle Atlas.

The Grand Hall was the single largest room in Castle Atlas, an enormous chamber with towering stone walls and a massive, stained-glass roof. The sheer scale of this room served to show off the opulence and wealth of the Atlas Duchy, with magically reinforced pillars and Spellbound stones lining the walls.

The ballroom had several entrances from which guests could enter, like the foyer they were currently in.

Even the foyer, itself, was finely decorated, like all the rooms Micheal had seen. Beautiful paintings, lush curtains, fine cabinets and chairs.

“And Micheal, I must say…” Vesper’s pink eyes danced as she tapped a fan against her cheek,

“You look simply ravishing.” She said as she eyed his blue suit.

Micheal stared the Void Noble dead in the eye, before bowing his head slightly.

“Thank you, milady.” Micheal’s bow followed courtly procedure to a T.

Vesper giggled in response, snapping her fan shut. She was dressed in a slim, dark red dress that fit her form, showing off her figure. A slightly lighter red shawl was looped around her shoulders, covering her exposed back.

“You’ll do quite well.” She nodded her head, before turning her gaze towards Shin.

“You, however.” She ‘tsked,’ tilting her head slightly to the side.

“He’ll follow my lead.” Micheal nodded his head towards Shin. Shin nodded back.

‘I gave him a crash course on Void Noble etiquette, but…’ Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he watched Shin awkwardly bow as one of Vesper’s maids approached him, offering him a drink.

‘Whatever. We’re Foreigners in their eyes, anyway.’ It shouldn’t matter too much.

And, even if it did, Micheal would handle it. He’d sooner die then leave his closest friend out to these wolves.

For, the battleground of many Void Nobles was fought in the feasts, the ballrooms and the dance halls, where status could tumble and fall for even the slightest of reasons.

Of course, for Void Nobles with significant power, like Duke Atlas it was a different matter – but Void Nobles of that status were the standouts, not the majority.

A few moments passed as they waited idly. Micheal took that time to glance around, keeping a sharp eye out for anything odd. He activated his Eyes of the Deep, constantly scanning randomly.

‘Even if I can’t consciously perceive Jay sol Arget, my Divine Scan should still pick him up.’ He just had to be careful not to let his scan land on people that would notice.

The door to the Grand Hall opened, letting in a wash of music, voices, and light, and out exited a male attendant, dressed in a dark black suit. While it was currently in fashion for Void Nobles to wear lively or colorful outfits, darker clothes were reserved for the maids and attendants serving them.

“They’re ready for you, milady.” The attendant bowed towards Vesper, before motioning inside.

“Excellent.” Vesper’s eyes narrowed as she began to walk forward, followed by one of her maids.

“Come on, boys.” She waved at Micheal and Shin as she strode forward imperiously.

The duo exchanged glances before falling in line, walking slightly behind her.

As Micheal stepped through the doorway, he found himself in a world that had transformed.

Loud, up-beat music colored the air, while warm lights flashed in the stained glass ceiling above. A subtle hum undercut the music, as more than a hundred and fifty Void Nobles, dressed in fanciful outfits, conversed, spread across the large room. Stepping in-between the Void Nobles were dozens of servants, maids, and attendants, carrying platters of food and drinks.

‘Is that…?’ Micheal’s eyes were drawn to the center of the room.

There, the skeleton of a huge Void Predator stood, a massive, hulking frame that had been preserved. The famous ‘Bloven Predator,’ the first Void Predator the Duke ever killed, several decades ago, before he had succeeded his father, Duke Teron von Atlas.

Around the skeleton was a large, relatively open dance arena, where several Void Noble couples currently danced, gliding gracefully around the floor. On one side, just beyond the arena, was the orchestra, a group of 14 Void Natives, performing with a variety of string instruments and drums.

On the outer edges beyond the dance arena sat dozens of large tables, complete with plates and silverware.

And, at the end of the Grand Ballroom sat one, large rectangular table where, at the very end, rested a large, imposing throne: the seat of Duke Atlas.

“Announcing, the ninth daughter of Duke Atlas, Lady Vesper von Atlas, and guests!” As they walked inside, the attendant that had let them in raised his voice and announced their arrival.

Because Vesper was only a minor daughter of the Duke, they weren’t given a larger announcement, which came with entering through the main entrance hall, a privilege reserved for more important Void Nobles.

Still, the words caused several heads to turn in the crowd. In particular, Micheal’s eyes narrowed as a pair of male Void Nobles began to immediately walk towards them, as well as an attendant that walked up and offered them a set of drinks.

“We still have around 20 minutes until father announces the start of the Feast.” Vesper guided them forward as they moved towards the side of the room, taking a glass of wine that was proffered.

“You should expect to be called to the Main Table, as guests of honor.” Micheal and Shin took a glass as well, eyeing the red liquid.

Before he could reply, the two male Void Natives, one a Noble and the other an attendant, reached them.

“Ah, dear sister, what a pleasant sight you make!” The speaker was a heavy-set Void Noble, with dark blue hair and placid, gray eyes. Micheal could see a vague resemblance in the man’s face with Vesper, likely one of her brothers.

“Gaivel.” Vesper turned towards the Noble, her gaze tightening so slightly that Micheal only caught it because he possessed supernaturally enhanced senses.

“This is Gaivel von Atlas, my father’s youngest son.” Vesper introduced the man, before waving towards Micheal and Shin.

“And this is Micheal and Shin, the two heroes who helped fight off the Apex.” She gave them both a winning smile.

“Oho? Well met.” Gaivel nodded vaguely at the duo before turning away, his gaze returning back to Vesper.

“Gahaha, it’s good to see you, Ves! You spend too much time, cooped up reading old Spellbooks.” As he spoke, his gaze drifted up and down, eyeing the cleavage her dress showed off.

“Us youngest ought to stick together.” He reached out, attempting to pat her on the shoulder.

With a loud ‘thwuck’ Vesper snapped her fan forward, knocking his arm away, as she giggled playfully.

“Aww Gaivel, I couldn’t think of something ever less delightful.” She said sweetly, her tone mixing with her confusing choice of words, causing Gaivel to smile back, none-the-wiser.

‘How unsightly.’

Micheal had heard rumors of the boorish nature of many Void Nobles, but never seen it first-hand.

‘Divine Scan.’

While the Noble was distracted, he took this opportunity to scan him.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Ivari Voidling

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

END: D (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

REG: D+ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or higher)

SOUL: D (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

MANA: D+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

Path Notes: An Ivari Voidling that walks a solitary Path. Traces of the Path of the Sword are present.

.

‘Pathetic.’ Despite possessing Growth Ratings far surpassing the average human, including even a Heroic Growth Rating in Mana, the Void Nobles stats ranged solely in the D Rank.

The term ‘Ivari Voidling’ was how the Divine Scan classified Void Nobles. The exact origin of the term itself wasn’t something Micheal was familiar with.

“Until next time.” Vesper smiled and turned, leaving her brother sputtering behind as she guided them across the Grand Hall.

As they walked through the Hall, Vesper smiled politely, occasionally exchanging words with several other Void Nobles. Micheal and Shin were, more or less, completely ignored, a fate the duo were absolutely fine with.

“The Rose of Axellion, huh?” Shin commented as they left one exchange, bringing up a compliment one of the Nobles had paid Vesper.

Shin moved to nudge her in the side with his elbow, before Micheal’s hand lashed out and stopped him, rolling his eyes at the obvious breach in decorum. Shin smiled sheepishly in response.

Vesper giggled at the interplay.

“If only more of my brethren acted like you, Shin.” The comment made Micheal’s mouth twitch.

He swore, Shin could befriend a stone wall if he truly felt like it. It was one of his best friend’s greatest qualities, his disarming nature and ease at which he treated life, making him a veritable social magnet.

“Oh, how I yearn for the day I’ll get to murder them all.” Vesper’s words were a quiet whisper, yet again only caught by Micheal’s superhuman senses.

‘Ah. Right. There it is.’ He was vividly reminded of the fact that Vesper von Atlas was a violent psychopath, though he was beginning to understand why.

She had acted so friendly around them, to the point where it was almost easy to forget.

“My brothers are all rather brutish, as are my uncles, and my cousins. Even my aunts.” Vesper continued without missing a beat.

“I have a poor opinion of my family.”

Notably, she didn’t mention her father – whether that was because her feelings for him were different, or rather out of an abundance of caution, Micheal felt it was probably the latter, given what he knew.

It was unwise to chatter loosely about an Archmage in the heart of his territory.

Out of the corner of his eye, Micheal spotted a familiar figure. The male Void Noble was leaning against the wooden railings that separated the dance arena from the rest of the Grand Hall, chatting up a young, beautiful female Void Noble wearing a pale blue slip of a dress.

‘Dunkore Salm!’ Micheal would’ve recognized this particular Wizard from anywhere – after all, he was one of the Wizards who helped craft his Iron Strings Gauntlet, an upgraded version of his Silk Strider Gloves.

‘Divine Scan.’ Micheal took advantage of the Wizard’s distractedness to launch a Divine Scan.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Kantor-Ivari Voidling

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: D+ (Growth Rate: Common or higher)

END: D+ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or lower)

REG: C- (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

SOUL: B+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

MANA: B+ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

Path Notes: A Kantor-Ivari Voidling that walks a cluttered path. Traces of the Path of Space and the Path of the Traveler are present.

.

The first thing he noted was the race listed – ‘Kantor-Ivari Voidling.’

It was a race that didn’t exist.

‘His disguise is strong enough to fool my Divine Eyes, at least partially.’ It was an impressive feat of Magic.

For: Dunkore was a dimensional wanderer, a traveling Wizard obsessed with the concept of ‘Parallel Worlds.’

His actual race, according to the records Dark Void had of the oddball Wizard, was known as a ‘Hantolile.’ A species of shapeshifters.

‘The Path of the Traveler.’ It was a Conceptual Power Micheal had never heard of, and likely the reason why Dunkore, a 4th Circle Wizard, was capable of something as complex as Dimensional Travel.

‘His Soul is roughly as strong as mine.’ The disguised Wizard possessed an unusually powerful Soul, something Micheal attributed to the man’s powerful Heroic Growth Rating.

‘Being exposed to the In-Between probably helps toughen up the Soul.’ It was a good theory, anyway.

“Yes, you humans have made a great addition to the dancing scene.”

Micheal’s focus returned as he listened to a rather unexpected tidbit, brought by one of the many female Void Nobles that had come to greet Vesper. Vesper was unexpectedly popular.

“I believe they’re called ‘violins’?” The female Void Noble, a woman named ‘Arella’ wearing a golden dress, gushed out loud, giving Micheal and Shin a friendly nod.

Micheal almost did a doubletake, only his strength of will preventing the break in decorum, as his eyes flicked to the side.

Sure enough, the orchestra was playing an ensemble of string instruments, some unique to the Third Layer, but others very clearly human in origin: a violin and a cello.

‘Only in Axellion, huh?’ It was very clear how strong humanity’s influence had grown here, all thanks to the Round Table’s efforts.

‘In fact, there’s no other race present here, except us humans.’ As Micheal scanned the room, he noticed that not even the Round Table had a representative here tonight.

‘Aaron’s power probably still makes him nervous.’

He did notice two other humans, however – the first was a middle-aged man dressed in the getup of the Purgatory Church. It was the first sign of the Church Micheal had seen on the Third Layer thus far. The second was another human talking to the representative, dressed in a grey suit, with his back towards them.

‘The schism with Dark Void should be happening around now – or maybe it’s already happened.’ Micheal’s eyes narrowed.

He needed to make contact with Dark Void.

And it was just as Micheal had this thought, that a series of horns echoed out loud, interrupting the conversation and silencing the room.

With a loud boom, the main entrance doors to the Grand Hall swung open, and in marched a series of Void Nobles, led by an intimidating figure Micheal couldn’t help but to recognize.

“Announcing, Duke Armon von Atlas, Guardian of Axellion, Protector of the Realm, Archmage of the Gyven Tower, and Hero of Stone!”

The Duke was dressed in a full, dark black suit – at odds with Void Noble fashion, and what would be considered ‘old fashioned’ – yet he cut an intimidating figure nevertheless. The heavyset Wizard moved with a sense of deadly grace, the sheer Aura about him crushing all in his presence.

‘An Archmage.’ Micheal gazed at the powerful Void Noble, feeling his pulse quicken, ever so slightly.

Even in the higher Layers, an Archmage would be considered a being of real power.

“Announcing, Beareth von Atlas, Firstborn of Duke Atlas! Announcing, Contrasz von Atlas, Secondborn of Duke Atlas!” Following the Duke were his two oldest sons.

Beareth von Atlas was a large, muscular man with a friendly smile on his face, waving to several Void Nobles as he walked in. He carried himself with an air that almost seemed to be imitating his father’s deadly grace, though not quite matching it.

Contrasz von Atlas, on the other hand, was a slightly shorter, but just as muscular warrior, a stern frown on his face as he walked forward, following his father.

“Good evening, my loyal subjects, guests, and family! Today, let us announce the 32nd Hyval Feast of this year, the Year of the Dolkai!” The Duke’s voice boomed out as he walked forward, a confident smile on his face. His words were met with a series of cheers, Nobles all around raising drinks in the air.

The Dolkai was a type of bird, native to the Third Layer, similar to large crow. Well, a magical crow that could spit blobs of shadow.

As Micheal watched the Duke walk forward and begin to greet several of the visiting Void Nobles, some family, some visiting from other City-States, he realized he had an opportunity here.

‘I could manage a Divine Scan of the Duke.’ It would be valuable intelligence to possess, as long as he could minimize any risk.

He slowly broke off from Vesper and Shin, making up an excuse about grabbing a drink as he took a few steps deeper into the crowd. He carefully positioned himself next to several Void Nobles on the far side of the Grand Hall, putting more than a dozen figures between himself and the Duke.

Then, while the Duke was distracted with his greetings, and only when Micheal felt his position was just right…

‘Divine Scan.’

He activated his Eyes of the Deep Ability.

Micheal didn’t immediately duck away after completing the scan.

Rather, he carefully whiled around, picking up a drink and casually turning to walk back towards Vesper and Shin. He didn’t make any suspicious movements and moved as if completely unrelated to the scan at hand.

He smiled and waved at Shin as he saw his best friend talking animatedly with Arella.

Out of the corner of his eyes, only after he was nearly reunited with his group, only then did he dare to look at the Duke.

‘It worked.’

The Duke was glancing at the various Void Nobles Micheal had positioned in-between himself and the Duke with a frown. He never once glanced Micheal’s way.

Eventually, the Duke turned back around and continued his conversations, an easy smile returning to his face.

Micheal took that time to read the Divine Scan’s results.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Ivari Voidling

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: B- (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

END: B (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

REG: C- (Growth Rate: Uncommon or lower)

SOUL: A+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

MANA: S++ (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

Path Notes: An Ivari Voidling that walks a cluttered path. Strong traces of the Path of Space, and traces of the Path of the Sword and the Path of Time are present.

.

‘Wow.’ Micheal stared at the stats, seeing the single highest grades he had witnessed since returning to life.

‘S++ Ranked Mana.’

Once you reached S Rank, Stats were divided into S-, S, S+, S++.

This highlighted the sheer difference in power between S Rank and SS Rank.

The difference between SS Rank and SSS Rank was even more vast.

‘He has two Heroic Growth Ratings.’ It really went to show how rare Mythical and Legendary Growth Ratings were, that even a powerful Archmage and ruling Void Noble lacked a Mythical Growth Rating. Not that Heroic Growth Ratings were poor, by any means.

‘An A+ Rated Soul.’ Despite not being S Rank, an A+ Ranked Soul was still an incredibly impressive Stat, given how difficult it was to raise one’s Soul Stat.

“Oh dear.” Vesper nudged Micheal with her fan.

“Yes, milady?” Micheal bowed his head slightly, to which Vesper crinkled her eyes.

“My Grandmaster, it seems father has taken a liking to you.” Vesper whispered quietly in Micheal’s ear, her hot breath flowing down his neck.

Micheal eyed her slightly askance.

“Get ready to move.”

And it was here where something unexpected happened.

The other human talking to the representative of the Purgatory Church turned around.

Like Micheal had guessed, he wasn’t someone from the Round Table…

Micheal knew this, because he recognized this human.

‘No way.’ He forced himself not to stare at the man, as his mind reeled in shock.

Because, standing right there before him…

Was none other than ‘The Invincible’ Kim Jiwoon, a legendary human from Micheal’s first life, and also the most famous user of the Life Orb Master Ability.

Before he could give the man’s presence here any more thought, his attention was drawn towards the end of the room, as Duke Atlas’ booming voice cut through the air once again.

“Now, let me call to the table, our two guests of honor, two Humans that stood for Axellion in her time of need!” The Duke’s words caused everyone in the Hall to freeze and turn, dozens of eyes piercing through Micheal and Shin as they realized that they were just two Foreigner nobodies.

“Their direct actions helped to stall out the Apex until my, and Commander Aaron of the Round Table’s, timely arrival!”

The Duke notably left out any mention of Vesper and Yama.

“Please, come forth and be welcome!” The Duke’s eyes sharpened as he stared at Micheal, a mix of genuine curiosity and measured awareness.

“Micheal Care and Shin Hopefell!”

.

Chapter 30


.

“You honor us, your Grace.” Micheal bowed deeply, pulling Shin down with him, while crossing one arm over his chest. Shin matched Micheal’s movements, his crash-course in Noble decorum not going in vain.

Duke Armon chuckled as he gestured.

“Please, be seated.” Micheal and Shin stepped forward, taking a pair of seats near the head of the table, directly to the left of the Duke’s own throne. All around them, dozens of Void Nobles moved to their seats, whether at the Table of Honor, or the lower tables.

Behind the Duke’s throne, Micheal noticed the figure of a Void Noble, standing in the background. The Noble’s eyes were piercing, constantly flickering about the room.

‘Tywel Kathos.’ The Chief Steward of the Atlas Duchy.

‘And its Spymaster.’ A fact humanity only learned many years later.

“It is Axellion’s honor to host a Grandmaster here in my court, moreso a Grandmaster who rose to the occasion and aided my people.” Duke Armon’s voice boomed as he spoke, giving Micheal a slight, but genuine, nod of appreciation.

A hush of quiet whispers broke out as it was revealed that Micheal was a Grandmaster – none of the nobles present had dared go even in the vicinity of the Apex, and information about his Abilities had yet to spread…

Until now.

Immediately, every eye in the court turned towards Micheal, reevaluating his entire existence.

For, if there was one thing consistent above all others about Void Nobles, it was this:

They respected power.

Real, true and tangible power.

You could be a terrible villain, but if you possessed enough power, here on the Third Layer, you’d be worshiped as a Hero all the same.

“Now, let us feast!” The Duke raised a glass and a round of cheers rang out as the feast officially began.

The music took up a lively tune as platter upon platter of food was ushered out, carried in by servants and maids alike.

Huge plates full of steaming ribs, slathered in red sauce. Fatty, ‘Perchu’ Chickens, grilled to perfection. Fine, golden bread covered in warm honey and butter. Sweet fruits native to the Third Layer alone, coated in their own unique version of sugar, ‘vera.’

Some of these ingredients were distinctly human – in particular, while the Third Layer had equivalents for wheat and butter, there were no bees native to the Shattered Plane.

‘They must have Humans supplying them honey, via the Shop.’ It was one of the many ways humanity could leverage the mystical Shop, using it to their advantage. Food bought from the Shop disappeared after roughly 30 minutes if it wasn't consumed, but there were several food-related Abilities that could be purchased that didn't have that same limit.

Some common items or foods on Earth were considered luxuries here on the 7 Layers.

Micheal and Shin both began to take part, Shin grabbing a whole handful of ribs and some fruit, while Micheal stuck to the Perchu.

The fatty grilled bird brought back memories of the first timeline, where he’d fought for years in a Knight Company, here on the Third. Perchu was considered a rare delicacy.

“I’ve heard a detailed breakdown of your efforts, young Micheal.”

The Archmage's voice was low as he spoke, not carrying across the room like previously, as he caught Micheal’s attention with a smile.

“Your courage is commendable. You and young Shin will be richly rewarded, come the Founding Celebration.” The prefix ‘young’ was a common way for older Void Nobles to refer to younger individuals that they viewed in a positive light.

Micheal bowed his head, donning a warm smile that he absolutely didn’t feel.

“I only did what I felt was right. You’ve welcomed humanity into your walls, it’s only proper and just that mankind stands with the people of Axellion.”

“Gahaha, now that’s what I like to hear!” Across from the table, Beareth von Atlas chuckled as he slapped his hand down on the table.

“If only all the Foreigners we encountered felt the same.” The Firstborn of the Duke shook his head.

“Indeed. Humanity has proven to be a race of honor.” Contrasz von Atlas cut in, sitting directly to Beareth’s right.

“My Knights would welcome a talent such as yourself, Foreigner or not.” Contrasz continued, his eyes boring into Micheal.

“Now, now, let’s not get ahead of ourselves.” Beareth chuckled as he slammed a hand down on his brother’s shoulder.

The Duke, in the meanwhile, finely sliced apart a large, meaty steak, content with letting his First and Secondborn take over the conversation.

‘Ah.’ Micheal had a sudden realization, though he didn’t let it show on his face.

‘They’re interested in me, individually.’ Suddenly, all of this made sense.

It was a bad habit, Micheal had, of comparing himself to the most powerful of foes and allies alike. It was a habit of necessity, as he prepared for what was to come…

But he also needed to recognize his own worth.

He was a powerful Grandmaster, which, here on the Third Layer, was a rarity. Even in the higher Layers, those who had mastered a Conceptual Power to a depth akin with ‘Grandmastery’ were rare indeed.

Purely by himself, he represented a very significant level of combat power, on par with an entire elite Knight Company packed down into a single body.

In the eyes of these Void Nobles…

He was a walking weapon of mass destruction.

He watched quietly as the two brothers bickered, his face impassive.

By no means was he willing to intercede within a dispute between potential Heirs.

Shin, in the meanwhile…

“They play ball under the islands?!’ His best friend gaped as he casually spoke across the table to the Duke’s Thirdborn, a thin, reedy Void Noble named Kasos von Atlas.

Kasos wasn’t considered in contention for heir due to his middling personal strength, and had thus turned his focus to trade. Micheal vaguely remembered that he had founded a trading company, bringing in large amounts of wealth to Axellion, transporting human-spawned goods all across the Third Layer.

“Yes, yes.” Kasos nodded, his eyes beaming as he spoke with passion.

The one other thing Micheal knew about the Thirdborn was that he was an Underball fanatic.

“The match between the Skyriders and Axellion’s own Stone Giants is happening a few days before the Celebration! In honor of the Stormbringer's demise, Father has doubled the prizes!” He went on excitedly.

“I have a whole set of First Tier tickets, I’ll see to it you and your friend each get a pair, Shin.” He smiled back at Shin.

“That’s awesome! Thanks so much!” Shin grinned back, giving the Void Noble a thumbs up.

“Think nothing of it. Underball is something everyone should enjoy!”

‘How the…’ Micheal minutely shook his head.

If he didn’t know better, he’d swear Shin possessed a Conceptual Power related to Friendship.

“It sounds like a sick sport!!” Shin replied.

Underball was the most popular spectator sport, here on the Third Layer. It was a dangerous mix of soccer and lacrosse, with the use of powerful Abilities or Spells completely legal as long as they didn’t try to maim or kill other players.

The game was played on the underside of a large cluster of floating islands, where complex gravity nets had been set up in accords with the Underball League’s regulations. Spectators watched through a series of Magic Screens, or, if they were rich or had connections, through specially designed Void Ships with a front row view of the action.

‘Good job, Shin!’ It couldn’t hurt, making a good impression on the Duke’s more influential family members.

It also didn’t pass by Micheal’s notice how here, at the head of the Table of Honor, there wasn’t a woman present, not until you got a half dozen chairs down.

‘…’ He pushed the unpleasant observation aside, focusing back on the present.

The feast went on, as it ever did.

Fine foods were eaten, backroom deals struck, allies and enemies alike meeting on the battlefield of Nobility.

There were performances, Void Natives juggling bolts of energy, a troupe that put on a dance performance intermixed with Ice Magic, and even, of all things, a human juggling act.

As the feast began to die down, and Void Nobles began to get up, many moving off to the dance floor, Micheal finally found the opportunity to broach a topic with the Duke, just before the man was about to stand up, after both the Duke’s First and Secondborn had already left.

“Another Human Grandmaster?”

“Yes, Bastien Amiot. Have you heard of him, perchance?”

Duke Atlas tapped his finger on the table exactly twice.

In the background, the Duke’s Spymaster made a slight, imperceptible motion that only someone with Micheal’s senses and awareness could have noticed.

Immediately, the Duke gave a slight nod.

“I believe so. He’s active near the Inner Sea.”

Micheal resisted the urge to give any reaction, maintaining perfect decorum as he bowed his head slightly.

“He’s a fellow Grandmaster I have immense respect for, and one who has recently gone missing. If possible, I humbly would request any information you may have on the matter.”

The Duke titled his head slightly, before giving Micheal a slight nod as he got to his feet.

“I’ll look into it. You’ll have a response before the Founding Celebration.”

'Success!' The Duke clearly wanted to win him over, and Micheal absolutely took advantage of that. It was for a good cause too, so he didn't even feel guilty.

The Duke immediately set off, his eyes flickering briefly as he noted that Micheal gave a slight bow in response, following proper Void Noble etiquette, before walking down the table and offering his hand to one of his Wives, halfway down the Table of Honor.

‘If nothing else, at least he won’t see me as a savage.’ He thought as he watched the Duke lead his Second Wife to the dance floor.

Shin, in the meantime, had left the Table of Honor, and rejoined Vesper on the other side of the Grand Hall, after giving Micheal room to talk to the Duke privately.

“The hero of the hour!”

Just as Micheal was getting up, a man’s voice caught his attention. Micheal turned his head, seeing a familiar figure.

Kim Jiwoon gave Micheal a friendly wave as he walked up to the now empty head of the Table of Honor.

“I heard-“ Kim Jiwoon paused, whatever he had been about to say dying in his mouth.

For… the moment the two of them locked gazes…

Both of their eyes widened as they felt a resonance, through their very Souls, a recognition on an almost instinctive level…

For just the briefest moment, the Life Orbs hidden within each of them pulsed, recognizing the presence of other Life Orbs.

Kim Jiwoon’s mouth fell open, before he instantly recovered, a charming smile reappearing on his face. His eyes, however, took on a different light, a more serious demeanor.

“I hear the gardens are lovely this hour, a real treat for us lowly humans. Quiet, too.” He waved towards one of the exits with a lopsided grin.

“Shall we?”

Micheal slowly stood up, his eyes narrowing as he stared at the man, whose famous legend and feats were part of what inspired him to become a Life Orb Master, here in the second timeline.

“Yeah.” Micheal grunted, in a rare moment of humor, his expression deadpan,

"I'm down to stare at some plants."

.

Chapter 31


.

The night air was cool and crisp as the duo exited the Grand Hall, moving down a hallway into a large, open air courtyard. Here, strings of white lights were setup along a large, walled garden. A few guards stood, at the entrance and exit to the garden, while an attendant passed through, carrying trays of drinks.

The colorful, flowery garden stood at odds with the pitch-black sky of the Third Layer, contrasting in a rather artful way.

Kim Jiwoon eyed the man that had followed him into the garden, a slight smile on his face as he observed the man.

A measured pace. A confident, but calm gait. Posture that suggests control.

‘He moves with decorum.’ He walked like he belonged, here in the court of a Void Noble, on a world like no other.

‘He’s quiet.’

Incredible body control. Inclined head, forward shoulders. No signs of wariness or uncertainty.

‘He’s confident he could take me, if it came to a fight.’ That, or the man had a will of steel.

Perhaps both.

‘No scent. Ki Cultivation likely at least Sky Tier.’

One of the odder facets of Ki – the stronger your energy, the less of a scent you gave off. It was a fact few people knew, and yet fewer would pay attention to.

Kim Jiwoon knew.

Kim Jiwoon paid attention.

These highly-skilled observations weren’t the result of any analyzing Abilities or powers, nor Artifacts or outside tools…

But rather, they were a display of the sheer, almost unnatural observational prowess Kim Jiwoon possessed.

It was a fact lost to history in the first timeline, and one of the greatest secrets behind the legend of the ‘Invincible’ Kim Jiwoon.

Back on Earth, in the right circles…

Kim Jiwoon was infamous.

The Divine Hunting Dog.

A high-level consultant for Interpol.

A valued adviser who helped the South Korean National Intelligence Service (NIS) track down terrorists and serial killers alike.

Before his life changed forever with the advent of the 7 Layers…

Kim Jiwoon was one of Earth’s greatest detectives.

He noticed things.

‘He’s strong.’ Kim Jiwoon thought as he came to a stop, in an unassuming area in the middle of the outdoor garden. Large, extravagant bushes blocked the lines of sight of any guards or attendants, while a few glowing stones lit the area, in a warm, orange hue.

It wasn’t just the fact that this man was a Grandmaster.

It was the way he carried himself.

The way he walked.

The way he met Kim Jiwoon’s gaze, his eyes an ocean of implacable calm.

‘It’s like I’m standing before that man again.’

Jiwoon pushed the uncomfortable memory away.

The so called ‘Black Dragon’ of China had already moved on to the Fourth Layer.

There was no point dwelling on past unpleasantness.

Kim Jiwoon waited, standing still for a few moments as he eyed his fellow Life Orb Master.

Micheal stared back, his eyes narrowing.

Finally, just as Kim Jiwoon felt Micheal’s posture shift ever so slightly, indicating that he was about to speak…

Kim Jiwoon held up a hand, stopping him, before fishing out a small pocket watch from his vest. This pocket watch was finely made, crafted from pure silver, covered in precise carvings and finely hewn symbols. An arm’s-length silver chain dropped off the watch, swaying gently in the cool night air.

The Korean Life Orb Master tapped on the Artifact watch, activating its effects.

A small, translucent bubble appeared, spreading to wrap around both Micheal and Kim Jiwoon. Instantly, all noise from the outside world was cut off, giving the duo a semblance of privacy.

“Handy things, these Silence Watches. Picked em’ up in the City-State of Eyrion, over to the East.” Kim Jiwoon smiled as he tapped on the Artifact, storing it back in his coat pocket.

Of course, he could’ve activated his Silence Watch at the start, instead of waiting to interrupt Micheal.

That act was a small, petty gesture, but Micheal’s reaction to it would tell him a great deal about himself.

Irritation? Annoyance? Anger? A short temper?

…

Micheal simply nodded back, his face a brick wall for all the reaction he gave off.

‘He’s patient.’

It was a trait all-too-rarely found, at least in Kim Jiwoon’s recent encounters.

Quietly, Kim Jiwoon’s estimation of Micheal rose.

“You’re well-travelled.” The Grandmaster’s voice broke the quiet tension that had settled between them.

“Oh, I’ve been around, quite a bit.” Kim Jiwoon smirked.

“For Life Orb Masters like us, the Third Layer’s floating islands are practically speedways.”

For a tiny fraction of a second, the Grandmaster’s eyes flickered. It was so small a reaction, that it was almost imperceptible, corralled by an iron will – only someone as perceptive as Jiwoon would've noticed.

‘Why did that statement take him by surprise?’

“So.” Kim Jiwoon held up a hand, confirming what both of them already knew.

A small, blue Life Orb appeared, floating in mid-air.

Micheal responded by raising his own hand, unveiling an identical looking Life Orb.

“Kim Jiwoon.” Jiwoon held out his hand, vanishing the Life Orb as he reabsorbed it back into his body.

“Micheal Care.” The Grandmaster shook his hand – a firm grip, not overpowering, but not ostentatious or overbearing either.

“We can talk freely here, but only for a few minutes.” Jiwoon’s eyes flickered as he scanned his surroundings.

He’d picked their current position by calculating the angles at which the guards could see, as well as the movement patterns of the attendants and maids serving guests here at Castle Atlas.

Privacy was a rare treasure, quickly fleeting, during such an event.

“You’re the first Life Orb Master I’ve met.” The Grandmaster’s words confirmed Jiwoon’s suspicions.

‘He’s new.’

Likely, the man had focused only on raising his Sword Mastery for years, and only relatively recently obtained his Life Orb Mastery Ability. While most other humans Jiwoon had met had selected a Type Ability early on, locking themselves out of Life Orb Mastery, it wasn’t unheard of to have staved that choice off for later.

Becoming a Grandmaster, in and of itself, was an incredible feat – it wasn’t something that could be achieved without an enormous amount of dedication.

“You are the second!” Kim Jiwoon smiled back, his thoughts rapid-firing, shielded behind a mask of geniality.

‘He helped fight off an Apex when he had no reason to.’ Jiwoon considered everything he had observed and now knew about Micheal.

‘First I need to figure out… is he related to the anomaly I'm investigating?’

Jiwoon looked off to the side, casually, as if scanning his surroundings. It was a brief flicker of movement, a gesture that wouldn’t look suspicious or alarming.

That gesture broke his line of sight for his right eye and Micheal.

In that tiny, transition period, where his right eye could not be seen…

Kim Jiwoon activated his Eye of Liberation.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

‘There.’

Micheal forced himself to not react as he felt a slight, almost imperceptible change in the flow of Time through his Eternal Mana Circles, just as Kim Jiwoon glanced off to the side.

‘He’s using it.’

The Eye of Liberation.

Kim Jiwoon, nicknamed ‘The Invincible,’ was one of many figures to have a profile made about them by Dark Void.

In total, the profiles Dark Void made numbered in the tens of thousands, a huge, enormous record of all individuals ‘of power’ that Dark Void had observed and traced. It was one of many great undertakings the huge research collective underwent, in their efforts to ensure the survival of the human race.

In the end times of his first life, Micheal spent countless hours scouring over these profiles, searching for a way forward, a path, anything he could use to improve.

His supernatural perfect memory let him recall exactly what he read back then, pulling up the initial summary.

.

Name: Kim Jiwoon (alias: The Invincible)

Status: Unknown (Last seen on the Sixth Layer, presumed deceased)

Confirmed Shop Abilities: Life Orb Master, Eye of Liberation, King Tier Ki, Shockwave Tapper

Suspected Shop Abilities: Ceaseless Mind

Confirmed non-Shop Abilities: Wound Transmission, Illusion Creation, Flight

.

The profile also went on into a more detailed breakdown about Kim Jiwoon, reporting his known fighting style and activities, a combat rating and Artifacts he possessed, as well as speculation about his disappearance on the Sixth Layer.

What Micheal focused on, however, was what he knew about one of Kim Jiwoon’s main Abilities.

The Eye of Liberation, a powerful Limited Ability that cost 2,210,840 Points, was fully bought out by the time Micheal arrived in the 7 Layers, with a stock of only 5 in the Shop.

It was this powerful Ability, synergizing with Life Orb Mastery’s incredible regenerative prowess, that let Kim Jiwoon gain the title ‘The Invincible.’

‘Would opening the Realm of Intent interfere?’ Micheal pondered briefly, as Kim Jiwoon turned back towards Micheal with a smile.

For…

The Eye of Liberation was one of the extremely few precognitive Abilities that could be purchased in the Shop.

.

—-Eye of Liberation —-

The Eye of Liberation draws upon the Veil, simulating the future, at a steep cost to the user’s vitality.

.

’27.3 seconds.’

That was what Dark Void had recorded in the profile, a fact revealed by Kim Jiwoon himself on the Fifth Layer.

The Eye of Liberation allowed Jiwoon to simulate an accurate, precise rendition of the next 27.3 seconds of the future, conveying that information to Jiwoon in an instant.

As far as precognitive powers went, this was one of the single most powerful precognitive Abilities Micheal knew of.

Even within the Realm of Intent, Micheal could barely grasp a few seconds of insight into the future… to simulate an entire 27.3 seconds was far and beyond what he was capable of.

However.

Therein lied the difference between their two powersets.

Micheal’s Realm of Intent was a constant, ongoing gaze into the future, while Jiwoon’s Eye of Liberation gave him a one-time glimpse, every time he activated it.

In addition, every time Jiwoon activated the Ability, his vitality sapped away.

Of course, Jiwoon circumvented this downside entirely through the use of his Life Orbs, an ideal synergy that Micheal would freely admit he was jealous of – had this Limited Ability not been bought out, it absolutely would’ve been one of Micheal’s goals for the Third Layer.

Nevertheless…

“It’s always neat to see a fellow Life Orb user.” Kim Jiwoon continued smoothly, not at all acting as if he had just seen what the next 27.3 seconds of the future should have entailed.

“There aren’t that many of us, but we make it count!” He nodded towards Micheal.

“Are you, by chance, new to the Ability? I know a few Life Orb Master slots got restocked in the Shop after the last Wave.”

Micheal paused for a moment. Just as he was about to reply…

He felt another, tiny, almost-imperceptible alteration to the flow of Time.

‘Again?’ Micheal resisted the urge to Divine Scan Jiwoon in return, knowing the man was probably skilled enough to notice.

“I’ve had it for a few months, but I’m still getting used to it.” Micheal held up his left hand, sending a stray blue orb floating in and out of his skin, whipping around.

Technically, he'd spent 7 long years practicing with his Life Orbs inside the First Gate of the Soul King's Inheritance. However, that time-accelerated Gate, while valuable as a training tool, didn't quite translate over in reality one-to-one.

Due to the lack of latent energy in the air, controlling his Life Orbs inside the Gate felt somewhat different from controlling them outside the Gate.

Still, just by dint of the sheer time he'd spent training, he'd managed to fine-tune his control over his Life Orbs there and mastered the application of Mana and refined his control over Magic, gaining his Second Mana Circle.

“It’s part of why I agreed to talk.” He continued, gesturing towards Jiwoon.

“I was hoping we could trade tips on our mutual Ability.” His intentions were genuine. Jiwoon, as a First Waver, had years of expertise when it came to his Life Orb Mastery.

“That’s not a bad idea. Us Life Orb Masters ought to stick together.” Kim Jiwoon’s right eye flickered.

‘Again.’

Another small change in the flow of Time.

‘How do I combat this?’ Micheal resisted the urge to frown, not wanting to give away any sign that he could detect Kim Jiwoon’s Ability usage.

For, few beings were anywhere near as in-tune to the River of Time as Micheal was.

‘Is he asking me different questions in the future, and changing them?’

It was one of the more frustrating aspects of Kim Jiwoon’s Eye of Liberation.

For all Micheal knew, Jiwoon might’ve even tried to murder him in one timeline, just to gauge him and his reactions. It was just speculation, but that was absolutely how Micheal would’ve taken advantage of the Ability if he had it, so he couldn’t discount the idea.

And if that was the case… Micheal mentally committed himself to going all out, without any restraints whatsoever, should Jiwoon attack him.

“Are you aware of the under-cling force Life Orbs posses?” Kim Jiwoon asked, getting straight to the point.

“You’re referring to what lets us hover on the Orbs?” Micheal replied.

“Yes. And the 10 meters rule?” The Korean raised an eyebrow.

Micheal nodded back.

“The Orbs can only fly within 10 meters of a stable surface. I figured that one out.” Micheal returned.

“Good, you’ve got the basics down. That's solid progress.” Jiwoon remarked, his words firm and confident.

‘Again. That’s the fourth time.’ Micheal noted, once again forcing himself to not react as he felt the flow of Time shift.

‘This is tricky. I need to be measured in my responses.’

Any sensitive or potentially dangerous questions Jiwoon might ask, he probably was asking in the futures he simulated. Micheal felt his paranoia rise at the thought.

'What an irritating Ability.' He had to give it to the Korean Life Orb Master - he definitely lived up to his legend.

“How about rotational flight?” Jiwoon queried.

Micheal paused.

“Rotational… flight?”

What?

“Yes. Using the under-cling force to get around the 10 meters rule. Have you…?” Jiwoon raised another eyebrow in silent question.

Micheal shook his head.

“No. I haven’t figured that one out.” He admitted as he leaned forward slightly, his interest ignited.

‘Is there a way to fly with my Life Orbs that I don’t know?’ Micheal thought, tamping down the hint of excitement that rose at the prospects of learning something new about one of his core Abilities.

“Yes, it’s-“ Jiwoon abruptly turned his head to the left, his eyes narrowing.

Micheal followed his gaze, where…

Nothing, just the path through the garden, along several bushes and sets of flowers.

A second and a half later, however…

Kim Jiwoon deactivated his Silence Watch, just as one of Duke Atlas’ attendants walked around the corner. The attendant paused once he noticed the two humans staring at him, before bowing politely and continuing to walk along the path.

“I’m afraid our free time seems to be up.” Kim Jiwoon’s eyes quirked as he nodded down the path.

“So it would seem.” Micheal returned.

From the direction the attendant had appeared, stumbled a few clearly drunk Void Noble youths. The sounds of chatter and merriment spread throughout the garden as more guests from the feast exited the Grand Hall, signaling the final hours of the feast.

“Are you free, tomorrow, say noon? A friend of mine owns a private courtyard, where I’d be more than happy to finish comparing tips.” Kim Jiwooon held out his right hand, giving Micheal a winning smile.

‘We don’t have any set plans tomorrow.’ Micheal made a judgement call. Anything he could draw on to advance his skills was worth at least seeking out.

“I am. What’s the address?” Micheal grasped Jiwoon’s hand in his own, shaking it firmly.

In that same moment…

One final shift in Time occurred and…

Micheal just barely heard Kim Jiwoon wince, his eyes crinkling, before immediately being replaced with a smile. The movement was so quick that Micheal would’ve missed it, had he not been paying close attention.

“Excellent! The address is…” Jiwoon rambled on as if nothing had occurred, giving the location and details on how to get there.

Soon, their conversation finished, and the duo parted ways, Jiwoon leaving the garden to rejoin his friend, while Micheal set off to join back up with Shin and Vesper.

As Micheal watched the other Life Orb Master leave the garden, his eyes narrowed.

‘I wonder what that was about?’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

‘What the hell…’

Once he was clear of the garden, and the line-of-sight of that Grandmaster, Jiwoon rubbed his throat, a rueful expression coloring his face.

“With his bare hands, really?” He muttered as he ducked down a hallway, headed back towards the Grand Hall. His heart throbbed in his chest, begging for the succor of a Life Orb after drawing so heavily upon the Veil. He held off, however, eager to vacate the premises.

‘Who just does that?!’

In that final moment, Kim Jiwoon had used his Eye of Liberation to simulate a future where he decided to peek at Micheal’s combat potential. Seeing was believing, after all!

In that future, the moment they shook hands, Kim Jiwoon used that moment to attack Micheal, activating his Shockwave Tapper Ability to create a powerful shockwave with Micheal’s hand at the epicenter.

As one Life Orb Master to another, such an injury should be easily recoverable – how Micheal reacted should’ve given him more information on the kind of man he was.

However…

What he didn’t expect was that, in a tiny, split fraction of a second after he made his move…

Micheal’s other free hand shot upward in a blur of Sword Energy and…

He ripped Kim Jiwoon’s throat out with his bare hands.

It was a brutal movement so quick and instantaneous that it caught Jiwoon completely off guard.

‘Geez, the man’s on a hair trigger.’ Jiwoon thought as he touched his throat again, holding back a wince at the memory.

‘Definitely… yeah, let’s play nice.’

He had yet to die by getting his throat ripped out in this life and...

He planned on keeping it that way.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

5 days remained until the Founding Celebration.

.

Chapter 32


.

Dawn, on the Third Layer, was a calm affair.

The grim, black sky lightened a few shades, to a turgid dark gray, bringing light to the floating islands that populated this strange, shattered world.

Far in the sky above Axellion, a few clouds gathered, clustering as they drifted overhead.

Shin pondered as he stared at the largest cloud, a big white clump shaped vaguely like a lumpy donut.

“It’s quiet, up here.”

He spoke to himself as he hovered, thousands of meters above Axellion, floating with the help of the Neo-Levitation Bracers Micheal had given him.

A small clump from another cloud drifted aimlessly in front of Shin, blocking his view.

With a thought, Shin teleported downward and adjusted his Bracers, letting gravity send him floating through a small opening in the clouds. Small bits of water vapor stained his leather garments as he hovered, dripping down off him to the city below.

‘It’s nice.’ He thought to himself.

He quite enjoyed the quiet solemnity of the early dawn.

Here, he was lost in a world all to himself.

It reminded him, inadvertently, of the many, many days he spent inside the First Gate, within the Soul King’s Inheritance.

Shin sighed.

‘Man, am I weird?’

He’d almost found himself missing the solitude of the First Gate.

A place where all he needed to worry about was training, facing off against the Shadow Seekers, practicing his teleportation, his Expand Ability…

Those days, he reflected, had impacted him far more than he realized.

It was hard, being on his own for so long… but it was fulfilling.

It was peaceful, in an odd sense.

Here, back in the real world, danger seemed to rear its ugly head at every corner.

Life down below was chaotic, non-stop, and always changing.

‘No, I’m not weird.’ Shin came to his own conclusion, after thinking it through.

‘That’s just life. Life is weird.’ He nodded to himself.

Vesper had introduced him to numerous Void Nobles after Micheal left. Interacting with the gray-skinned natives of the Third Layer had been a mixed bag. Most of the Nobles were clearly more interested in Micheal than him, which was a fact he was just fine with. The few that did bother talking to him had been dismissive, focused more on Vesper.

Still, at the end of the day, it was a lot of fun.

It was like he went back in time to 1600s Europe, except a Europe that was now inhabited by aliens.

It was a unique experience, and that in itself made it worth dealing with.

‘Enjoying solitude does not make me weird.’ Shin nodded again.

‘And even if it does…’

He smiled.

‘So what? I do what I want and like what I like.’

In that moment, as Shin reaffirmed his own existence, he felt something in himself solidify.

Strength flowed within him, power flooding his veins as he floated in the air.

Innately, in the core of his Soul, Shin felt his connection to the Conceptual Power of Strength deepen, advancing to a higher level.

‘What?’ He froze, taken aback.

Shin stretched out his right hand, feeling the power of Strength rush into him, more easily than it had before.

He had taken a step forward, one step closer to attaining Mastery in Strength.

It was a culmination of growth, the time he spent training in the First Gate, the months he had survived here on the First and Second Layer, all the battles he had been through, the feats he had achieved…

Not just physical Strength, but something deeper, something more.

Emotional Strength. Mental Strength. Spiritual Strength.

His entire person, as a whole, had grown.

Shin’s eyes widened as he realized this, feeling the Conceptual Power pulse within him.

To embody the very Concept of Strength was no easy thing.

There was a reason it chased away all other sources of power.

To be Strong took Strength of all kinds.

And today…

He had grown Stronger.

He wasn’t Strong. Not yet.

But he was on the path to Strength.

And that thought made Shin laugh out loud.

“One step at a time.” He grinned as he teleported, buzzing through the holes in the clouds.

A few minutes passed as he let the power of Strength fade.

And, just before he was about to teleport down, to start the day…

“Oh? Is that you Shin?”

A familiar voice caught his attention as Shin floated up above a snake-shaped patch of clouds.

Shin looked up as he saw another figure, floating about two dozen meters away, flying between clouds.

“We meet again.” Aaron Bartram, Commander of the Knights of the Round Table, remarked as he gave Shin a wave.

“Fancy seeing you up here!”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Breathe in. Breathe out.

Micheal meditated, focused on his Mana Circles.

He desperately needed to form his Third Mana Circle to take advantage of his new Abilities, and there was no time like the present.

The Eternal Mana Circles seemed to blur into existence, arcane symbols flashing within his Soul at an impossible rate. All 412 lines of the Echoes of the Eternal Magic Imprint glowed along the length of the Mana Circle, giving it an otherworldly sheen.

There were two main obstacles to forming a new Mana Circle.

The first: control.

There was only one being in existence, as far as Micheal knew, that was born with an innate mastery of Mana.

Dragons.

For every other Race, controlling Mana was inherently unnatural. It was a skill that had to be learned, trained, and refined as one grew, not something that any being apart from Dragons were born with.

Micheal’s years of experience controlling Ki gave him a strong baseline when it came to handling Mana, but that experience alone wasn’t enough.

However…

7 years.

That was how long he’d spent inside Tallanoran’s First Gate.

While reality inside the Gate didn’t quite reflect back onto the real world, Micheal had managed, with his unwavering focus, to practice handling his Mana, every single day, of every week, of every month, of every year that went by.

It was thanks to that, and that alone, that made his current control of his Mana incredibly precise.

The cool energy pulsed with his will, moving exactly as he demanded it.

And now, he was showing the results of the long years of practice.

‘Form.’

The second obstacle to forming a new Mana Circle was energy.

Mana Circles didn’t just form out of nothing – coalescing one required intense focus, absorbing the latent energy of the world, and making it your own. Here, on the Third Layer, the air was thick with power, far more so than the Second Layer, and vastly more than the First Layer.

Spread out on the ground, in a circle around Micheal, was a cluster of blue crystals.

Mana Crystals, given to him by Vesper at his request.

These were a unique byproduct found not only here on the Third Layer, but also on the higher Layers, where the native energy levels were high enough to support their generation.

Technically, what was held within these blue rocks was not actually Mana, despite their namesake.

Rather, these crystals were quite similar to the Helion Treasures found on the Second Layer – rocks that had absorbed enormous amounts of natural energy, which was easily converted into Mana. Latent, pure, unrefined, condensed down into stone and cast away across tens of thousands of floating islands.

They got their namesake simply from the fact that Mana was the predominant form of energy usage here on the Third Layer, and on the higher Layers.

Mana Ore deposits, as the unrefined version of Mana Crystals were known, were spread out across the Third Layer, held as strategic interests by various Void Noble factions. These deposits, similar to how Magic Herbs reappeared on the Second Layer, restocked themselves over time, absorbing energy from the air and condensing back into existence.

‘It’s good to have rich friends.’ Micheal thought as he began to chant the 412 lines of the Echoes of the Eternal Magic Imprint.

“Aeygio myphor ol lamme eonan shieuo, naguil mino eephren melusik.”

As Micheal chanted, the circle of blue Mana Crystals glowed brighter, energy rising off them, and flowing into him.

“Morfin melusik ol lamme, partuk nupal caraf bent du reade.”

One of the benefits of having already formed two Mana Circles, was that Micheal had already experienced saying all 412 lines perfectly twice. Well, technically, only once, as his Second Mana Circle, he formed through a mental expression of the Magic Imprint.

That time, however, was after an immense amount of practice within the First Gate – this time around, as he formed a Third Circle, he’d decided to say the chant out loud, in part because he was forming it so quickly after his Second Circle.

Making such immense changes to the landscape of his Soul, back to back, was bound to be dangerous, and he was taking all the precautions he could. His room was layered with protective Wards and Artifacts he’d set up. Shin had offered to stand guard, but Micheal had waved him off – his best friend had apparently hit it off with Aaron by coincidence up in the sky this morning, and was now off training on the Round Table’s grounds, getting used to his new Conceptual Power.

“Aeugio ol lamme forstwo, shadoiw coufa belko mon eephron.”

As he enunciated line after line, repeating everything once again, his mind drifted.

The differences between the Second and Third Layer were intriguing, not just in Mana Crystals, but in the wildlife as well.

It was a unique view and an example of divergence in evolution.

On the Second Layer, native animals developed Spirit Crystals from the latent energy in the air.

Here on the Third Layer, where the energy was thicker, the native wildlife evolved to absorb that energy directly into their bodies, empowering them as a whole. The Energy Heart of a Void Predator was the closest thing, structurally, to a Spirit Crystal, and even that was still quite different.

If not for the constant, omnipresent horror of being ripped away from Earth and thrust into danger, exploring the wonders of the 7 Layers might’ve actually been enjoyable.

“Antori nivor, eephon aigo tu monlew. Fallo mon tor aiygo meluski.”

The minutes slipped by as Micheal chanted, absorbing more and more Mana into his Soul.

Bit by bit, he could feel his third Mana Circle coalescing, straining his Soul as it burned into existence. As it formed, however, it felt harder and harder to control, something Micheal hadn’t felt with his previous Circles.

“Thundra chronos uldon mon vultur ol eterna mu infinit.”

Finally, after what felt like forever, Micheal’s eyes glowed blue as he said the final line.

A flux of blue energy swarmed into existence as the Mana Crystals surrounding Micheal began to shatter, one final wave of Mana rushing into his Soul, as his Third Mana Circle formed.

And…

Micheal frowned.

His Third Mana Circle had successfully formed… but it was… wobbling?

Sweat poured down his brow as Micheal concentrated, sending his focus inwards.

He could feel his first two Eternal Mana Circles, flowing with energy deep within.

His third, however…

His eyes narrowed as he felt it shift back and forth.

It was there, successfully formed, that was beyond doubt… but it wasn’t entirely stable, he recognized. The lines of energy swarmed back and forth, like a ship rocking at sea during a storm.

Tentatively, he tried drawing on the Mana Circle.

Mana did beam off it, but the energy response was sluggish.

‘Damn.’ He rubbed his forehead as he sighed.

‘At least it safely formed.’

Native Mana users formed their Mana Circles across a number of years for good reason.

Forming Mana Circles in such quick succession was incredibly dangerous, and could bring about numerous side effects, of which, this was one of them.

‘An Unstable Circle.’ He’d read about this condition.

‘I’ll need to slow down for a bit.’ The Circle itself was still useable, but its instability would take, at minimum, weeks to stabilize – and that was only because Micheal possessed a heavily refined control of Mana, thanks to his many years of practice inside Tallanoran’s Inheritance, and his own experience with Ki.

A regular person might take months, or even years, to rectify an Unstable Circle – if they managed to form it at all. Many normal Wizards would’ve fractured their Mana Circle during the Imprint process, as they struggled to control the destabilizing Mana flow.

Micheal had brute forced his way through that process unknowingly, simply by dint of his iron-clad willpower and precise control, something few could mimic.

Slowly, Micheal let out a breath he hadn’t realized he had been holding as he stood up, wiping the sweat off his forehead. He glanced towards a wooden clock set in the corner of his room, noting the time.

About half an hour shy of noon.

‘About as long as I expected.’ He nodded as he brought out a towel, and wiped himself clean.

More than enough time to make his meeting.

He looked down at the mess he had made on the floor, shattered crystals and dust staining the ground in a circle, before shaking his head with a sigh.

“First, let’s clean this up.” His eyes glowed as he began to cast a First Circle Spell, gathering a small circle of wind, to pull the dust and crystal bits into a pile.

Then, after he finished…

It was time to see what Kim Jiwoon was all about.

.

Chapter 33


.

Alone, in the heart of the Imperial City…

The God-Emperor of Kalos wept.

“Syraphine.”

Kyvenval’s deep voice rasped, hands trembling.

“How far, we came, yet to lose you now.”

The red-skinned Kalosian cut a tragic figure as he knelt down before a small, clear-faced coffin.

“Rage. My heart bursts, yet I find no succor.”

Kyvenval drew his six-finger hands across the coffin, staring down at his fallen love.

His instincts screamed at him, to lash out in violence, in blood, in war.

Yet, Kyvenval took a deep breath, and exhaled.

‘I am one with the Sky. The Sky is one with me. I will not be controlled.’ He repeated this mantra as he stared down his dead wife, his emotions cast askew.

It was an odd chant, yet one that made sense, given the history of Kalos.

For, the Kalosians were an artificial species.

Forged in the Flesh Vats by their creators, they were an entire species created for one purpose, and one purpose only:

War.

Slowly, Kyvenval stood up, his hands steadying as he rose.

“My heart. I will not falter.” The loss cut deep, yet he held strong.

For he was Kyvenval.

The Conqueror.

The Uniter.

God-Emperor of Kalos.

And…

Heir to the First Celestial.

“…”

“You…” Kyvenval towered over the coffin, his muscular, 8 ft 4 inches (2.54m) form rising up.

“You will be avenged.” As he spoke that promise into existence, the air around him crackled, Mana fluctuating off of him, his Perfected Mana Heart exuding raw power.

Slowly, Kyvenval reached up, touching the clean white bandages that wrapped around his eyes, shielding them from view.

“Your killer will behold the Eyes of God.” His words fractured the air as he left the Mourning Room, the doors trembling as they sealed behind him.

Kalosian guards, clad in white mail, trembled before his rage as he stalked forward.

The Imperial City was lost in a foreign world, beset by foreign killers.

He did not know what the symbol carved into his love meant. A calling card? A false flag? A trap?

He did not know.

But he would find out.

And then…

I W I L L F I N D Y O U.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Micheal ducked through the streets of Axellion, making his way towards the courtyard Kim Jiwoon had directed.

The streets were lively, now, as noon approached, bustling with activity.

Merchants accompanied great hovering caravans, floating a few inches off the ground, pulled by teams of Void Natives haulers or directed with bulky, sail-shaped Artifacts known as a Forward Driver, a relatively new advancement in Artifact creation that was slowly driving Void Native haulers out of a job. Hawkers hawked their wares in-between alleys, while everyday workers went about their tasks, moving from place to place.

Micheal kept his dark hood raised as he moved through the streets, avoiding eye contact for the most part.

‘Is that a Glycen?’ It wasn’t only Void Natives that he spotted as he traversed Axellion.

While their numbers were low, he began to spot members of the other Races that had been Chosen, climbing up to the Third Layer.

Humans might be the most populous Chosen species residing in Axellion, but that didn’t mean they were the only ones.

In particular, he spotted a pair of Glycen – green skinned, feathered, and winged humanoids that stood roughly 4 and a half feet tall (1.37m). The duo were arguing in broken speech with a merchant in front of a clothing shop, something about a purchase over fine silken garments.

Glycen were one of the more fortunate species to reach the Third Layer – they were natively capable of flight, meaning the interspersed floating island-nature of the Third Layer wasn’t particularly challenging.

Their larger, beaked mouth and sharp, hooked nose stood out as one of the stranger appearing of the many humanoid races – even now, the Void Natives in the street gave the duo a wide berth.

‘Still… there’s barely any around.’ Micheal noted as he walked on by.

Down another street, and he finally exited the commercial district, passing by two other individuals from separate Chosen species.

A large male Ugthor, a tall, lumbering one eyed humanoid with pasty white skin, and a female Cricken, a rather unsettling boney humanoid with thin, reedy skin, and a long, leathery face.

The Ugthor he passed was walking down the street the opposite way, while the Cricken was clad in armor, standing guard beside a large, floating wagon.

‘This brings back memories.’

Back in the first timeline, on the Fifth Layer, that accursed World Tree, he’d met a Cricken Swordmaster, in an off-shoot bar in the Upper Roots.

‘Gyle.’ A ghost of a smile wormed its way onto his face as he glanced back at the boney humanoid, recalling the name of the other Cricken.

Crickens, despite looking like a stiff breeze would knock them over, had bones denser than solid steel. They were a matriarchal species, and Gyle, a male Swordmaster, was an odd sort – he was friendly, loud, obnoxious, and an all-around great guy, at least, for the one night of drunken revelry that Micheal knew him.

Micheal had only recently forged his Mastery at the time, and Gyle had been all too willing to compare notes, a rare showing of generosity that said a lot about Gyle’s character.

It was one of the few fond memories he had of the Fifth Layer that stuck with him, despite lasting only a single night.

Soon, Micheal’s trip down memory lane ended, however, as he reached his destination.

A small, out-of-the-way courtyard, situated in a quiet district on the outskirts of Axellion.

The front gate was a mix of wood and metal, hinged to a wall built out of plain, dark gray bricks.

Micheal walked up to the door and, just as he was about to knock on the knocker attached to it…

The door swung open.

‘Very dramatic.’ Micheal held back a snort as he walked through the entrance, entering the main area of the small, 10 meters wide stone courtyard.

“Ah, the man of the hour, right on time!” Kim Jiwoon’s voice boomed out as he stood in the courtyard, apparently waiting for Micheal.

Standing next to Kim Jiwoon was another man, one Micheal instantly recognized.

‘Ah, it’s him.’ It was none other than the member of the Purgatory Church that also participated in the 32nd Hyval Feast.

The middle-aged man had dark skin, of African origin, and a pensive smile on his face. He was tall, about an inch above Micheal’s height, and looked to be extremely fit despite his age, his gray robes doing little to hide his athleticism.

Kim Jiwoon caught Micheal’s gaze, and waved him off with a smile.

“Oh, don’t mind him – Jabari’s a friend who’s helping me investigate a few things. I trust him with my life, and every secret I possess.” Jiwoon explained as Micheal walked forward, the door shutting behind him.

“Greetings.” Jabari nodded.

Micheal nodded back.

“You’re a member of the Purgatory Church?” Until the Nirvana Saint climbed up to this Layer and seized control, he held little trust for the fledgling organization.

“Of sorts. It’s… complicated.” Jabari shrugged, his smile never dipping.

“Oh? I’ve heard there’s been some turmoil recently, within the Church.” Micheal pressed, raising an eyebrow as he took a shot in the dark.

“You’re unusually well informed.” Jabari returned, his eyes narrowing.

Micheal stared him down, his face a mask of implacable calm.

After a tense moment, Jabari chuckled.

“You needn’t worry. I am no longer affiliated with the Church. You could say I’ve… branched out.”

Micheal’s heart stilled.

‘He’s with Dark Void.’

Micheal had met many members of the decentralized, research collective in his first life, and they all had one thing in common – they were oddballs, men and women who dedicated their lives to exploring the unknown, ensuring the spread of information, and working towards the survival of the Human Race.

‘Through him, I can contact Marco, and share what I know.’ One of his overriding goals, ever since he went back in time – to make contact with Dark Void.

Specifically, with Marco Barone, an Italian scientist famous back on Earth for the Nobel Prize he won in Physics for proving the existence of Tachyochrono Particles.

Marco was the mastermind behind Dark Void, and the former Director of the Dark Void Research Branch, back when it was still an arm of the Purgatory Church. Before he was killed by the Titled Deity Bosmond Jingleton on the Fifth Layer, Marco pioneered Dark Void’s efforts at decentralization and coordination, aided largely in part by the Limited Ability he had purchased from the Shop – Envious Touch.

It was a classic case of thinking outside the box, using an Ability not as it was intended, but working around constraints to create something useful.

Envious Touch was an Ability that let Marco materialize an invisible hand within 2.8 meters of anyone he had previously touched – anyone, as long as they were within the same dimension. It was an incredible Ability, just when you considered the space-shattering connotations that came with manifesting something on the other side of a planet from someone else.

The intent of the Ability was very clear – it could be used to steal anything on someone’s person. When the floating hand demanifested, anything it was holding was transported to Marco.

However… what Marco figured out, in his brilliance, was that he could force his Ability to function backwards.

He could first manifest the floating hand next to himself, put something in that hand, and then shift it to someone else, through a clever use of self-hypnosis, getting around the constraints of his Ability.

This was one of the ways Dark Void managed to maintain its decentralization, passing along information disks, journal results, studies, and whatever else needed to be shared, regardless of the distance between its members.

Micheal snapped back to the present, however, as the conversation continued.

“That’s right! He’s a fine fellow, trustworthy to the teeth.” Kim Jiwoon broke in, cutting the tension apart with a disarming smile as he stepped forward.

“Jabari has personally helped me develop my Life Orbs, and understand the underlining mechanics that make them work.” Jiwoon held up his hand, pulling out a pair of blue Life Orbs.

Micheal simply nodded back.

If there was one thing that stood the test of time, it was the authenticity of the members of Dark Void – they truly represented some of the best of humanity. In the first timeline, there were no incidents of a traitor or betrayal within their members, history that would almost certainly have been made public, given the group’s ideals.

“So, where were we?” Kim Jiwoon’s smiled widened as he stepped forward, until he was just a few feet away from Micheal.

“Rotational force.” Micheal replied, carefully paying attention, in the background, to see if Jiwoon activated his Eye of Liberation.

“Ah, yes!” Jiwoon clapped his hands together.

“First, we need to talk energy density, and its affects on Life Orb’s inherent undercling force…”

Micheal leaned forward, unable to resist a hint of excitement as he listened to the Korean Life Orb Master.

It was time for this old dog to learn a few new tricks.

.
