Chapter 34


.

“I call it rotational force.”

Kim Jiwoon motioned towards his two floating Life Orbs.

The two Life Orbs slowly drifted together, floating in mid-air. Micheal watched intently as the Orbs made contact, his eyes never leaving them.

Gradually, the two Life Orbs began to spin in opposite directions.

Internally, Micheal held back a frown.

‘I tried this already.’

Inside Tallanoran’s First Gate, in the countless days he spent practicing, his perfect memory let him recall several days he had spent experimenting with his Life Orbs.

Still, Micheal watched patiently as the two Life Orbs began to spin, grinding against each other. A soft, ‘whirring’ sound echoed out as the Orbs began to pick up speed, glowing with blue light.

‘Exactly the same.’ He nodded along.

“Once they pick up enough force…” Kim Jiwoon raised a hand, accelerating the Orbs…

And it was here that Micheal came to a pause, eyes widening, as he watched a shower of blue sparks began to ricochet off the Life Orbs.

‘What?!’

With a flicker of will, two Life Orbs formed in front of Micheal. He controlled the Orbs, bringing them together, just like Kim Jiwoon had, and setting them to spinning.

And, sure enough, a flurry of blue sparks rained down on the ground as the Life Orbs began to glow, grinding against each other.

“Here on the Third Layer, the energy in the air is much heavier.” Those words sent a shock through Micheal’s system as his mind instantly grasped the connotations.

‘There was no energy inside the First Gate!’ Immediately, he realized why his attempt inside Tallanoran’s Inheritance had seen different results.

It was one of the side-effects of Tallanoran’s time-accelerated First Gate – not only were Conceptual Powers nigh impossible to perceive, there also wasn’t any energy in the air that should exist on the Second Layer.

‘That’s the difference.’ He realized as he studied the sparks intensely.

The Life Orbs were grinding against the background energy itself, somehow, a reaction from the two floating Orbs spinning against each other at a high velocity.

“These two Life Orbs form an engine, and…” Kim Jiwoon casually floated upward, two additional Life Orbs appearing under his feet as he began to fly.

“These two Orbs serve as my wings.”

Micheal watched as Kim Jiwoon flew upward, exceeding the 10 meters rule as he rose freely.

‘Flight. Actual flight.’ Micheal spawned another 2 Life Orbs at his feet, holding only 2 more in reserve - with his current advanced Soul stat, he could control up to 6 individual Life Orbs, fully restocked now.

Slowly, Micheal began to rise up into the air. As he crossed 10 meters, he felt a shift in his Orbs, a sort of drift as the anchor the Life Orbs used to float changed.

‘Those sparks.’ For whatever reason, the sparks his other two Life Orbs were grinding into existence counted, very briefly, as solid ground.

He stared at the blue sparks, watching as they faded and were instantly replaced, creating a continuous chain of energy that counted as ‘ground’ here two dozens meters up in the air.

‘Incredible.’ It was an advancement he had never considered, one that opened up a ton of possibilities.

Having the ability to fly without relying on costly or energy-intensive Artifacts was a huge boon, not just here on the Third Layer, but also on the Fifth Layer, and even in certain parts of the multi-Dimensional shifting mess that was the Sixth Layer.

It was a power that would never stop being useful.

“Wow, you picked that up incredibly fast.” Kim Jiwoon flew over next to Micheal, staring at his Orbs in shock.

“I’ve… had a lot of practice, controlling the Orbs. I just didn’t know.” His training in the First Gate allowed him to innately sense and freely control his Life Orb’s location, speed, and acceleration.

‘What else might there be that I haven’t considered?’ As the thought struck him, he decided to return the favor.

“Are you aware of how Life Orbs can be used to anchor Spells?” He waved his hand as he chanted, “Gravton Konen.” The 1st Circle Spell – Concentrate Gravity. It was the most basic manipulation of gravity, a Spell that was relatively easy to cast thanks to his connection to the Conceptual Power of Space he gained through Kyrui’s Inheritance.

Immediately, Micheal felt a pull from the Orb as it hovered, its gravity switching to pull in anything near it.

“No, no I was not.” Kim Jiwoon stared at the Orb, his eyes narrowing.

Micheal felt a flurry of activity in the background as the flow of Time shifted.

“Fascinating.” The Korean Life Orb Master swirled around in the air, ducking in and out of the Orb’s gravitational pull.

He then turned to Micheal.

“You’re a Wizard, too? That’s some work ethic, man.” He gave Micheal a thumbs up.

“I try.” Micheal held back a snort.

Kim Jiwoon looked away for a split second and…

The flow of Time shifted once more. Then again. And again. And again.

Four times, all in rapid succession.

Micheal forced himself not to freeze, his gaze never wavering as he stared down his fellow Life Orb Master.

Abruptly, Kim Jiwoon looked back at him and let out a sigh.

“Why don’t we drop down? I’ve got something else to share with you.” He motioned back towards the ground.

Micheal simply nodded, acquiescing with the man’s request.

‘What did he see?’ Curiosity burned in him.

‘Is there a way for me to stretch the Realm of Intent to look farther into the future?’ It was somewhat maddening, being at the mercy of another precognitive.

‘This must be how everyone else feels, dealing with me.’ The thought struck him.

Given how much knowledge he had of the future… it was an amusing observation.

The duo returned to the ground of the courtyard, where Jabari was now sitting on one from a set of fine wooden chairs, pulled from thin air. Or, more likely, a Spatial Ring.

“Thanks, Jab.” Jiwoon nodded at the Dark Void scientist, who simply nodded back, as Jiwoon sat down on one of the chairs and motioned Micheal towards the other.

Micheal sat down, his thoughts pensive.

‘This seems serious.’

“Is there another technique with our Life Orbs I might not be aware of?” Micheal broke the tension, asking first.

“There is, but… hmm.” Jiwoon tapped the fingers of his right hand along his upper thigh, staring at Micheal intently.

Another shift in the flow of Time.

Jiwoon exhaled again, before rubbing his eyes.

“Micheal, what are your goals in this life?”

The Korean asked him point blank.

Micheal didn’t hesitate.

“I’m going to ensure the survival of the human race, and uncover the mystery behind the 7 Layers. To fix the hell that humanity has been thrust into.”

It was a grand ambition, and yet, Micheal wasn’t done.

“And, if I can…” He spoke words that had burned themselves into his heart, so many years ago.

“I will grow strong, strong enough to face whatever being is responsible.” Blood pounded in Micheal’s ears as he finished, the mission he had assigned himself, dedicated his very life to, bared for all to see.

He wasn’t just doing this for himself. Not just for his family. Not just for his friends.

But for all mankind.

They had been wronged.

Untold suffering, endless loss of life.

Live or die, in his deepest heart of hearts, Micheal couldn’t help but to rage at the circumstances forced upon all mankind.

One day, at a time yet to come…

"There will be Justice." He spoke without meaning too, passion overcoming him.

‘Calm.’ He exhaled, forcing himself to calm down.

Hot blood would fix nothing. Only in control would he find success, a bitter lesson learned through years of hardship in the first timeline.

There was a quiet moment where Kim Jiwoon sat still, staring at Micheal, completely transfixed.

It was as if the man was looking at a ghost, his eyes widened as he looked on.

That moment passed, and Kim Jiwoon gathered himself.

Now, however, as he looked at Micheal, there was a different look in his eye, one Micheal couldn’t quite place.

“Alright. Alright, we’re doing this.” Kim Jiwoon nodded to himself, before leaning forward.

“I mentioned that I met another Life Orb Master before you, right?”

Micheal nodded back in response.

“We met on the First Layer, in the big ol’ Cluster of towers, you know the ones in the middle, with the exit to the Second Layer downstairs?” Kim Jiwoon motioned.

“The Main Cluster.” Micheal returned.

“Is that what they’re calling it now?” Reminding Micheal, once again, that he was talking to a First Waver, one of the first humans to arrive on the First Layer, trailblazing ahead of the rest of humanity.

“Yeah, anyway. His name was Henry, from the island of New Zealand. A great guy. We shared everything we knew about our respective Life Orbs, and their interactions.” Jiwoon smiled briefly, before that smile died.

“And one day, when we were still exploring that big, central Cluster, we met it. A reminder, that our new lives are fraught with horror.” Jiwoon sighed.

“A Monster Class Morenkai.”

Micheal held back a wince.

“It was a freakish thing, with an ominous red Aura that was impossible to miss. It was just me and Henry at the time, a pair of sorry fools that didn’t know better. We treated it like we had the other Abnormals we faced before.” He rubbed his eyes.

"Our Life Orbs made us cocky. We should've fled on sight." He sighed again.

“It ripped us apart. Limb from limb.” He went on, staring dead into Micheal’s eyes.

“Henry died that day. But in his last breath, he gave me a gift, showing me something I otherwise never would’ve learned.” Jiwoon held up his right hand, palm open, sending a Life Orb out to hover just an inch above it.

“Tell me, Micheal, have you ever consciously shattered a Life Orb while on death’s door…” Jiwoon motioned towards the Orb.

“While also making skin contact with another living being?”

Micheal blinked.

“Skin contact?” His mind jumped backwards, reviewing every single use of his Life Orbs. From the First Layer to the Second to here on the Third.

“I…” He frowned,

“No.” Oddly enough, that situation had never occurred.

Jiwoon nodded back.

“It’s a rare enough scenario that I wouldn’t expect you to.” He leaned back in his chair.

“I trust you, Micheal. It’s silly, saying such a thing despite knowing you for so short a time.” Jiwoon chuckled to himself.

‘Uh huh. I’m sure your liberal use of the Eye of Liberation has nothing to do with that.’ Micheal kept the thought to himself.

“I trust you to not abuse this aspect of our mutual Ability.”

And it was here that Micheal’s mind flashed back, to the list of Abilities written down by Dark Void’s profile of Kim Jiwoon – and the powers he possessed.

.

Name: Kim Jiwoon (alias: The Invincible)

Status: Unknown (Last seen on the Sixth Layer, presumed deceased) Confirmed Shop Abilities: Life Orb Master, Eye of Liberation, King Tier Ki, Shockwave Tapper Suspected Shop Abilities: Ceaseless Mind

Confirmed non-Shop Abilities: Wound Transmission, Illusion Creation, Flight .

“It’s something I like to call…

“Wound Transmission.” Kim Jiwoon’s eyes gleamed,

“The ability to, when shattering a Life Orb, instead of healing your injuries…” Jiwoon’s Life Orb twisted around his hand in a tight circle, “You copy them, and share them with someone else.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“I need you to give Marco these journals.”

The hours were winding down, after Micheal and Jiwoon finished talking, sharing their experiences with Life Orbs, giving advice, tips, and even a bit of light sparring.

It was after their meeting wrapped up that Micheal stepped off to talk with their curious observer, a scientist who was rapidly writing down notes, immortalizing the progress Micheal and Jiwoon had made in their comprehension of the Life Orb Mastery Ability.

“How do you know that name?” Jabari hissed as he looked up from his notes.

The man’s entire demeanor shifted, his entire body tensing as he glared at Micheal, his friendly gaze nowhere to be seen. Micheal vaguely sensed energy gathering within the man, as he prepared to flee or fight.

Slowly, Micheal shifted his free hand in a series of gestures, causing the robed man to freeze, his eyes widening.

“Marco Barone. Director of Dark Void.” Micheal answered.

“You- you aren’t a part of- how?! I don’t -!” The man looked at Micheal’s hand as he stuttered, before he began his own set of gestures, the answer protocol ironed into him.

These two different series of hand signs were something Micheal knew, once more, thanks to the obsessive research he’d done in his first life - the early established protocol for Dark Void members to confirm each other, established in their first year of formation, something Micheal’s perfect memory recall let him drudge up.

Once more, he blessed his decision to obtain a perfect memory – without that, he never would’ve remembered this extremely useful tidbit.

“I’m a Seer, and I have information that must be shared.” Micheal emphasized, tapping on the set of notebooks as he stared at Jabari.

“Can I count on you?”

The middle-aged scientist stared back at Micheal for a few seconds, his eyes crinkling…

Before he slowly began to nod.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

And so, thus ended one hectic day, as Time marched ever onward, to fate unknown.

And now…

Only 4 days remained, until the Founding Celebration.

.

Chapter 35


.

An explosion of red stained the air, shockwaves spreading as a hurricane of blood whipped about, covering almost half of the Round Table’s secret, space-expanded Training Hall.

“Vector Wall: Null.”

Aaron Bartram ducked as he wrought a hardened wall of nothingness into existence, blocking the torrent of blood. The searing winds of blood had a powerful, red Aura that clashed against his Vector Wall, each drop of blood slamming down like a hammer.

“Vector Field: Expel.” With a twist of his hands and willpower, he shifted the vector plane, slamming away the hurricane of blood.

The numbers came easier to him now more than ever, calculation after calculation boosted by the Mana flowing in his veins, as he activated his newly forged Mana Body – the first stage in forming a Mana Heart.

A small silver coin materialized out of thin air as he withdrew it from his Spatial Ring.

Then, in one casual motion…

“Vector: Mach 2.”

Like a bullet, the silver coin blasted out of his hand and shot through the air, slamming into a figure hidden in the midst of the storm of blood, knocking them back and sending them flying.

“You’re going to need more than that, if you want to take me down, Felix!” Aaron grinned as he called out to the third Vice-Commander of the Round Table he was sparring with, Felix Seranno.

‘This Mana Breathing Method is perfect.’ It had come to him at the perfect time.

Aaron had connected to his Conceptual Power on the First Layer. As a result, he never felt pressed to take up Ki Cultivation, opting to keep his Ability slots open as he climbed the Layers. Most humans picked up Ki early on, given how easy it was to purchase in the Shop, and its ubiquitous nature on the Second Layer.

After Aaron took on a leadership role, he’d committed to waiting before taking on Ki, simply out of an abundance of caution.

‘Heart Trials can kill you.’ He didn’t fear the Heart Trials, but… there were so many people depending on him, it was a risk he opted not to press, not when he already possessed immense personal power in the form of his Conceptual Power.

However… as they climbed up the Layers, the Round Table had gradually come to the conclusion that the rising energy density in the background of each Layer meant each of their members needed to obtain some sort of internal energy technique.

And so, that was how the Round Table found themselves on the Third Layer, presently.

Before Micheal’s arrival, one of their chief concerns in negotiating with Duke Atlas was to obtain a high quality set of Mana Breathing Methods.

And now…

Aaron had just that.

.

—- True King Mana Breathing Method —-

Rank: SSS

Effects: A Mana Breathing Method created by the Transcendent King Augorian Doom, found on the Sixth Layer, after his death to the Titled Deity Navir. Can specialize in either the development of Mana Circles or of a Mana Heart, or both. Greatly strengthens Mana density and capacity, enhances the user’s body, and grants unique properties to one’s Mana. Enhances the user’s willpower. Enhances the user’s regenerative properties.

Note: This Mana Breathing Method requires an unbreakable will. Requires an exceptionally strong Soul to operate. Practicing this Mana Breathing Method will modify one’s Physique over time.

.

Vector was a jealous mistress – it was impossible for him to form Mana Circles of any kind, lest he give up on his Conceptual Power – a Mana Heart, however, was completely viable.

‘I’m not sure if my will is truly unbreakable but…’ Aaron reflected on his past.

Arriving on the First Layer, meeting Jess, his first encounter with a Morenkai. The journey to the Main Cluster, gathering comrades, facing down Monster Class Morenkai, reaching the Second Layer, encountering Byren Martial Artists and Magic Beasts, before finally reaching the Third Layer, where they faced down Void Predators while juggling Void Noble relations, and where they finally set down roots, cementing the Round Table's existence.

‘I will not falter.’

Previously, he had been working to create a vanguard for mankind’s effort here on the Third Layer, like the Syndicates that formed on the Second Layer.

That way, he could advance with the Round Table to the Fourth Layer without any worries.

Now, however…

“Vector.” His right hand tapped on his chest,

“Forward.” Instantly, he shot forward, blasting through the torrent of blood like it didn’t exist, breaking the sound barrier, before stopping exactly where he calculated, 2.8 meters to the right of Felix. The jarring movement whipped up a storm of wind, blowing away the haze of blood.

Despite the unnatural start and stop of his motion, his body rested perfectly at ease, his connection to the Conceptual Power shielding him from the harmful affects of such sudden acceleration and deceleration.

The instant he arrived, however, Aaron blinked as two blood red blades slammed into the invisible Vector Field he held, shrouding his entire body as the wind buffeted around them.

“Tch.” Felix’s blood-red eyes gleamed as he leapt backwards, glaring at Aaron.

“You rely on your shields too much, bro.” The High Vampire’s voice betrayed his youth as he backflipped through the air, sending down bolt after bolt of blood red energy.

Aaron ignored the Blood Bolts as they slammed ineffectively against his Vector Field.

“Well, why wouldn’t I?” Aaron smiled as he watched his third Vice-Commander begin to gather up his Blood Energy, creating a truly massive sphere of power.

Felix was slightly below average height for his age, with stark white hair and blood-red eyes, side-effects of his Vampiric Type. He was the youngest of Aaron’s Vice-Commanders, at only 16 years of age, yet his power was inarguable.

‘I still can’t believe he Evolved his Type naturally.’ If he had to take into account every member of the Round Table… Felix Seranno was inarguably the single most talented individual.

Felix was only 12 years old, a few days shy of 13, when he was Chosen from his home in Mexico City during the First Wave.

And now…

Felix Seranno also happened to be the only High Vampire present on the Third Layer.

The High Vampire Type cost 11,350,000 Points in the Shop – obtaining it through the Shop on the Third Layer was impossible.

Instead, Felix had bought the Lesser Vampire Type for 16,000 Points on the First Layer.

From there, the future Vice-Commander had obsessed over his new Type, mastering every aspect of his Ability – Seranno could be said to be one of the utmost talented Vampires, of all Humans that chose the Vampire Type, across the entire 7 Layers.

Not only did he natively evolve his Lesser Vampire Type into the full Vampire Type, just 4 months back, here on the Third Layer, he managed to evolve further, upgrading his Type Ability to where it stood now.

A High Vampire.

‘I need to take this seriously.’ Aaron’s eyes gleamed as he sized up the nearly 20 meters large globe of Blood Energy that Felix had created.

If he was careless now, this attack might break beyond the boundaries of the Training Hall.

Ever since that decisive meeting with Micheal, a fire had been lit in Aaron’s heart.

‘We need to be ready.’ The horrors listed in the journal Micheal had given him, the sheer knowledge of what was to come…

Aaron had done the math, and it wasn’t pretty.

And it was here, just as the two were about to clash in a bout of epic proportions…

Both of them froze as their heightened senses caught the arrival of one of Aaron’s personal attendants, bursting into the Training Hall.

Aaron’s gaze flickered.

They weren’t to be disturbed, unless it was something important. He trusted his men to use their best judgement, which meant…

The globe of energy gradually began to disappear as Aaron flew over towards the entrance of the Training Hall.

“Report.” He ordered.

“Commander, there’s a pair of men that are requesting a high-priority meeting, two Humans we haven’t seen before.”

Aaron Bartram frowned as he waved for the attendant, a portly male dressed in the gray leathers marked with the symbol of the Round Table, to continue.

“He said you’d recognize their names.” The portly attendant continued,

“Lux and Rex.”

‘Them.’ Immediately, Aaron felt his pulse spike.

Lux, and his companion, Rex.

A pair of those ‘Seeded’ by Constantine Lancaster, a man Micheal had devoted three entire pages to in the journal he gave Aaron.

Lux had also been given his own half page.

“I see.” Aaron grunted, his gaze pensive.

“Felix, you’re with me.” The powerful First Wave Vampire nodded as he landed down on the ground next to Aaron, his Blood Energy orb fully absorbed, as he gave Aaron a curious look.

“Let’s see what the man has to say.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Wow, this place is fancy too.” Shin remarked as the pair walked up on a grand building, near the center of Axellion.

“It’s one of the nicer ones.” Micheal agreed.

The duo stood outside the Inner Sea Mages association, a grand pavilion constructed quite close to Castle Atlas. It was a large, towering mansion, one of the tallest buildings in Axellion, carved from pitch black stone, belying the colorful nature of most other buildings common to Axellion.

“Let’s head in.” Shin nodded as the duo stepped forward, heading towards the entrance, a set of large, black marble doors.

He had been informed by a runner sent to his guest quarters earlier this morning that Duke Atlas had set aside a large commission to reward both him and Shin for their efforts in stalling Barsoth, preventing the Apex Void Predator from savaging Axellion.

Micheal had opted to use that reward here, to commission a pair of Artifacts at the Inner Sea Mages association, a place he was very familiar with from his first life.

As they entered, they were greeted with a huge entrance hall. Great arching stone platforms held up the ceiling, where a series of beautiful, shifting paintings coated the roof, displaying Void Ships sailing across the Empty Sea. The famous Bellal Expedition Voyage, an exploration mission that was famous here in Axellion.

Below the fancy paintings was a large front desk, attended by a female Void Native dressed in a black dress, wearing a pin with the insignia of the Inner Seas Mages association, a lightning bolt above a ship cresting an outline of waves.

“Welcome to the Inner Seas Mages association, how can I help you?” The front desk clerk greeted them politely while leaning back in her chair, which was already a huge plus in Micheal’s books, and really showed the influence the Round Table had, that non-Void Natives were greeted at all, here in Axellion.

“I’m here to commission a couple of Artifacts, with the personal counsel and commission of Duke Atlas.” That got the front desk clerk to sit up, her entire body freezing as she stared at them.

“Of course! We are honored that you chose us.” She immediately began to sort through a series of ledgers as she leaned forward.

“Is there a specific craftsman you have in mind? I can share their availabilities and customizations.” She spoke like a salesperson, continuing,

“I have a few I can recommend!”

‘A few that likely bribed her.’ He knew how it worked down here.

“That’s fine, I already have a Wizard in mind.” Micheal smiled.

“I’d like to request two commissions from Dunkore Salm.”

.

Chapter 36


.

Within the bowels of the Inner Seas Mages Association, two Humans and a disguised Void Noble sat around a large black table. The room housing the table was large, cluttered with bookshelves and books on all ends, lit by two glowing orange crystals, set like torches on the walls.

“A Melding Plate Arm, you called it?” Dunkore stared at the metallic object in wonder, the Wizard’s eyes glowing with Mana as he peered into the Artifact, aided by the Tier 3 Spell ‘Keen Manasight.’

The elongated metal Artifact was masterfully crafted, a close-knit marvel of Magical Engineering, finely forged with incredible precision. Its magical network possessed lines that would interact seamlessly with flesh, while also allowing the integration and absorption of stronger metals.

‘It reminds me of the Masterclass Artifacts crafted by Rugal Stronghammer, though simpler in nature.’ Rugal Stronghammer was the Forge Chief of the Stronghammer Clan, among the Dwruden, the sole sapient inhabitants of Dimension 237.

The Dwruden as a race were predisposed to the art of Artifact creation. Much of Dunkore’s own skills in Artifact creation had been learned in the three decades he spent, laboring away in Dimension 237. Time well spent, in his opinion, even if the brutish humanoids made for lousy intellectual debate.

‘Gah.’ Dunkore frowned, barely holding himself back from swearing out loud.

To think, he, a Traveler of the Conclave, would find himself trapped in a Dimension, unable to return to the Conclave due to binding chains of warped Time, sealing off the In-Between…

Truly, his life had taken a turn for the worse, ever since he found himself here in what he tentatively named Dimension 1742b.

“Yes. My friend here,” The Grandmaster spoke, motioning towards the arm Dunkore was examining.

“He has the power to Expand an object to a great size, while maintaining its physical properties.” The golden-haired Human nodded.

‘Strange, but not unheard of.’

The Trillyons of Dimension 551 could do something similar. Gigantism, they called it.

“I see. I think I comprehend what you’re requesting.” Dunkore nodded as he examined the Artifact a little closer, tracing its internal energy lines.

‘It wasn’t built for the application of Gigantism, but if I reinforce its structural integrity along these lines, infusing it with a dense metal like Durallion or Adamantyne, while redirecting its runes...’ He nodded again, finally feeling a hint of excitement.

With Duke Atlas writ to fund, this would be a worthy Artifact modification indeed. And, given that he’d be working closely on the Artifact, he’d also be able to note down its exact design parameters, making for a worthy addition to the Akashic Archives of the Conclave.

“I can complete this request.” Dunkore looked up, donning an affable smile. In the long, 70 years he’d spent Traveling the Planes, he’d long since grown used to adapting the body language of various bipeds.

“In how long?” The Grandmaster asked back, his voice admirably measured.

‘Scary fellow.’ He hid it well, but any Grandmaster of something as brutal as the Sword was bound to be a violent savage.

When Dunkore learned the very same Human Grandmaster that had fought that lumbering abomination was requesting his commission, he’d had half a mind to up and abandon Axellion as a whole.

In all his travels, it was freakish beings like him, Masters who had honed their senses to an absurd degree, that were most capable of detecting Travelers like himself. And, when outed, his kind were often found unwelcome. Few races were capable of comprehending how great the Conclave’s mission to gather all knowledge was, and often responded with violence to guard their secrets.

“This arm?” Dunkore gave it some amount of serious thought.

“I can finish it before the day ends.” While the changes he made would be complex, Dunkore prided himself on his knowledge when it came to Artifact refinement and creation, especially in this barren Dimension.

Few beings could match his expertise in that matter. The changes they wanted were, for him, a relatively simple matter, if very expensive.

“With the Duke’s writ here, even the price of modifications to this Artifact leaves you with plenty of room.” He decided to be honest when it came to matters dealing with the scary Grandmaster. No need to make powerful enemies, not when he was trapped in this Dimension for the foreseeable future.

“At least- hmm. I still have funds to create 2 Artifacts, entirely from scratch.” He subtly gave them a hint, hoping to wring this writ for everything it was worth.

‘An opportunity to work with resources like this doesn’t come often.’

“2 more?” The Grandmaster pondered as he stared down the Dimension Traveler.

His friend nudged him in the side with his elbow.

“I don’t need anything fancy - what if we get something for ol’ Sofa, for when she climbs up here?” The blonde Human offered.

The Grandmaster’s face shifted in what was a ghost of a smile, before he turned his maddeningly calm gaze back towards Dunkore.

“Alright. How familiar are you with the Conceptual Power of the Storm?” The way the Human phrased the term was slightly odd, but Dunkore grasped his meaning clearly.

The Way of the Storm. One of the many Ways, just like the Way of the Traveler he dedicated his Soul to.

“I’m aware of its existence.” Dimension 991 housed an entire world assailed by massive storms, non-stop, on a planetary scale. The Rymbods that called that hellscape home professed to be the foremost experts of the Way of the Storm – not that Dunkore would know. He only knew of the Dimension in passing through the Conclave’s Akashic Archives.

‘I’m not fool enough, to visit such a dangerous Plane.’ He inwardly complimented himself.

‘Then again, I did get myself trapped here.’ Dunkore resisted the urge to gnash his teeth.

The Grandmaster went on to describe, but of course, a sword attuned to the Conceptual Storm. An Artifact that would allow a user of that harsh Conceptual Power to, theoretically, deepen their connection, while providing a bridge of sorts that was hardy and durable.

The man spoke of concepts and design details that were surprisingly in-depth, ideas and knowledge that were far beyond the purview of a mere savage, to the point where Dunkore leaned forward, looking at him with new eyes.

‘These Humans are no simple race.’ The concepts he spoke of were something he’d only be aware of if he came from a highly educated background, one where countless individuals had dedicated themselves to the research of Artifact creation, and shared that knowledge freely.

Dunkore found himself subtly impressed, and forced himself to reassess the Grandmaster.

Scary, yes, but perhaps not so savage.

“I can work on that tonight as well. I’ll have a prototype ready tomorrow, but will need to check again then, before I can give a final date.” He had never attempted creating an Artifact quite like this before, but it should be well within his skill to make, especially with a budget this vast.

“For your final Artifact?” Dunkore nodded again, this time with a genuine smile on his face.

Finally, something to break up the dull monotony that had overcome his stay, ever since he found himself trapped.

“I have an idea for a gauntlet.” The Grand-, no, Micheal, as Dunkore mentally corrected himself, now deciding the Human was worthy of him acknowledging at least his name, brought out a journal from his Spatial Ring, tearing a page out of it.

“A gauntlet where metal strings could extend here, you see…?” He pointed to the design blueprints, showcasing a detailed sketch.

He also brought out another Artifact from his Spatial Ring, a set of ‘Silk Strider Gloves’ which immediately Dunkore noticed had served as the inspiration for Micheal’s new design.

“But rather than use normal strings…” Micheal’s blue eyes gleamed as he smiled at Dunkore.

“I want something similar to the sword I requested. An Artifact that would bolster a connection to a Conceptual Power, or rather, a pair of Conceptual Powers.”

Micheal pointed to a series of runes outlining each metallic line,

“Strings linking together Space and Time.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“There is beauty, in the violence of nature.”

At the center of the Empty Sea raged a never-ending hurricane of epic proportions.

Great, towering walls of white stretched for hundreds of miles, guided by currents of energy and power. It was a huge, massive formation of clouds and thunder, the likes of which were not seen anywhere else on the Third Layer.

For, this was not just a normal storm.

No…

This was the Highstorm.

An eternal hurricane that acted as a stabilizing force upon the Shattered Plane, hiding a Nexus of pulsing, white energy in its Eye, where torrents of wind clashed with raw power, in a beautiful display of the power of nature.

Standing atop a chunk of floating rock, high, high in the sky, stood a tall, lanky Void Noble. The man was fit and healthy, but not overly muscular, garbed in a well-made dark red toga, draped over one shoulder somewhat similar to those worn by the Greeks of Earth, but with clear differences, as he also wore a full set of red pants. His feet were clad in simple brown sandals, and on his head rested a small, golden laurel crown.

On his back was strapped a long wooden sheath, long enough to hide a spear or stave, shrouded in black wood.

Here stood Eon, the King of Heroes.

“Soothing, in its own way.” Eon muttered as he studied the Nexus at the center of the Eye.

The huge, pulsing globe of energy, spanning easily 100 meters across and tall, fluctuated in a myriad of colors.

After a long moment’s study, he finally turned away.

“Perhaps it was nothing.” He shook his head.

He’d spent the last several years here, off and on, in meditation and study, pondering how he might advance his Dream, here in this strange world. A few days ago, he’d noticed a slight change in the Nexus, lines of Time that had taken him aback.

However…

Now, as he gazed at it…

Every time he looked, he found nothing wrong. No matter how he turned his gaze, how he modified the Dream, how he studied the Nexus, he found no slights or signs of malevolence.

Truly, he concluded, nothing had changed in the fabric of Time here on the Shattered Plane.

After all…

The only other possible explanation was that another being had accounted for his every method of observation, his every application of the Dream, and his every attempt at comprehension, coincidentally blocking or shying away from every attempt, including powers none on this Plane even knew he possessed.

And, well…

What were the odds of that?

Eon snorted to himself.

“I grow paranoid in my old age.” He chuckled quietly, for…

Eon had a secret that no one knew.

Not Micheal, with his knowledge of the future.

Not Jay sol Arget, in his mire of Looped Time.

Not even Dark Void, in the first timeline, ever discovered what lay hidden.

For...

Yes, Eon was a Void Noble, native to this plane of existence…

But in his Soul, he was also something else, something more, something… greater.

A Perpetual.

Every sapient creature, in all the many worlds that made up reality in the greater Dimensional Sea, from Dimension to Dimension spread across the In-Between, in all these realms, every sapient creature shared one thing in common.

They possessed a Soul – a vestige of energy, connected to them and them alone, ephemeral as the wind dancing across the sky.

When a normal being died, their Soul passed on to whatever afterlife may or may not exist, not even Eon knew for certain.

When a Perpetual died, however…

Their Souls fled their home Dimension, and were reborn, maintaining their memories, in another, as they gained new life once more.

Eon, the Perpetual, smiled as he turned away from the Nexus.

“Hmm. It’s nearly time.” The air around Eon began to distort as he warped space around him, traversing through the world at great speed.

“Sylee…” His former friend and now deceased ally, Sylee Atlas, had a nephew that was hosting a grand party, celebrating a hundred years of stability, in the seat of the Atlas Duchy - or something along those lines. Eon hadn't really paid attention to the smaller details.

Regardless, he'd made up his mind. In remembrance of one of the true friends he had made, here in his 53rd life, he would attend that Founding Celebration and raise a drink to the memories they made, hunting down Apexes before illness took her.

“To Axellion, I go.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

3 Days remained until the Founding Celebration.

Chapter 37


.

“Let’s get ready to rumbleeeee!”

A wave of cheers broke out as the official Underball League Playoff match between Axellion’s Stone Giants and Tannathone’s Skyriders began.

“Goooo Giants!”

“Boulder strong!”

“Rock them!”

“Go New York!”

Micheal elbowed Shin in the side for his last cheer.

“What, we gotta rep the Giants too, ya know?” Shin grinned back at Micheal shamelessly, before bopping him on the head with his metal nub.

Micheal shook his head as he gave Shin a side-eye.

Shin had detached his Melding Plate Arm, removing almost all of the Artifact except for its central base, which connected to his arm's nerve endings, and left it with Dunkore overnight to get upgraded. They would pick it up tomorrow morning, after giving the Wizard time to test the modifications and ensure everything was peachy.

“You’re not even from-“

The rest of Micheal’s response was lost as another wave of cheers swept through the crowd, deafening them as the game intensified.

‘Why am I here..?’ Micheal held back a sigh as he took in his surroundings.

He was seated, alongside Shin, in the First Tier Stands – a floating island perched below Axellion, with a clear view of the Underball Field. Their ‘First Tier Stands’ were actually just one of many private rooms, secured for just the two of them, complete with a couch, a couple of chairs, and a table, walled off on the sides and back. They even had complimentary fruit and drinks, served on a platter.

Dozens upon dozens of other floating islands circled the underside of Axellion, artificially moved through the use of Gravity Magic. Some were filled with normal stands packed to the brim, while others were filled with private viewing rooms or larger, more open pavilions. Besides those floating islands, hundreds upon hundreds of Void Ships could be seen, hovering in space as people watched the games unfold from their own vessels.

Underball, as the namesake implied, was played on the underside of the enormous floating islands that made up the Third Layer. In this case, there was an entire section of rock leveled off under Axellion that was used as the official Underball Field.

The fact that the Demarcation Line for the Void was only a few hundred meters below them was part of the excitement.

An explosion of energy shook the air as figures darted forward, flying through the void on small wooden boards – officially called Underboards, they were, expensive hoverboard-like Artifacts.

Each team had 12 members, utilizing Mana Hearts or Mana Circles to their advantage as the scrimmage began.

‘…I don’t think I ever got tickets this good, in my first life.’ Micheal watched as one of the team members of the Stone Giants, geared in gray uniforms emblazoned with a giant stone sword, raced into the middle and picked up the ‘Underball’ – where the sport got its name.

A glowing blue ball that hovered in the air until it was captured. The Stone Giant player fast-chanted a Tier One Fireball, colliding it with the Underball and sending it streaking across the underside of Axellion, towards a Mana Knight from the Stone Giant’s team that had rushed ahead.

The Stone Giant’s teammates quickly swarmed in tow, clashes of energy breaking out as the other team began to obstruct them. It was a grand display of sporting spirit and athletic ability, as the athletes flew through the air and fought for the ball.

It was a mix of gladiatorial combat and soccer, but flying in the air, where the ground was above you, if such a sport could be imagined.

‘At least Shin is having fun.’ Micheal noted as he eyed his best friend, whose eyes were jumping from Underrider to Underrider, the official name for Underball League players.

Shin had pitched this as an opportunity to destress and check out the local sights, and Micheal had decided to go through with it. Both of them had been under a tremendous amount of pressure recently, and taking breaks like this was important, to keep them both in peak condition.

Shin didn’t have the backdrop of an entire timeline’s worth of experience to draw on, after all. And, with both the Duke's agents and the Round Tables' men out searching for the Sundering Swordmaster, there was little else Micheal could do, in the present moment.

'Hurry up and wait.' He was reminded of a saying from back on Earth.

As another wave of cheers swarmed the crowd, Micheal tapped on his Spatial Ring, withdrawing a thick burgundy book.

This was a Spellbook, gifted to him by Vesper at his request.

Now that he had formed his Third Circle, however unstable it might be, it was important that he fleshed out the Spells he could cast. There were gaps in his knowledge when it came to Magic, since it had never been a priority for him in the first timeline.

It was kinda funny, after he thought about it – he knew more about the intricacies of Artifact Creation and Magic Engineering, than he did about the actual Language of Magic and the Spells of higher Circles.

It made a certain amount of sense – Artifacts had been a part of his daily life, and something he was always researching, while he had nothing to do with Magic in his first life.

‘…is she really allowed to give me something like this?’ He thought as he perused the Spellbook.

Spell after Spell was revealed, all dealing with the intricacies of manipulating the ebb and flow of Gravity, what her House specialized in. The more Micheal read, the more certain he was that this was definitely not a text Vesper was allowed to share.

The strange female Void Noble had proven herself to be nothing but helpful, despite Micheal’s prior trepidations. He almost felt bad for how cautious he was around her, but logic dictated that needs must - he couldn't just ignore what he knew about her from the first timeline.

A few minutes slipped by before Micheal glanced up again. Despite focusing on reading, he was also splitting his focus, multitasking as he maintained a constant awareness of his surroundings. Doing that was somewhat draining, but well… what else could he do, when he knew Jay sol Arget was after them?

Such was life.

“Yoo, bro, look at that!” Shin nudged Micheal as he looked away from the Spellbook.

A brilliant clash of blue light shook the air as a pair of Underriders flipped upside down onto the underside of Axellion, their feet landing firmly on the stone, as the duo fought for the ball.

“They’re like Spiderman!” The two Mana Heart users sprinted along the underside of the floating island, running upside down in a brilliant display of athletic control.

‘Right, I almost forgot about that.’

All Underriders wore special shoe Artifacts colloquially known as ‘Clingers’ that allowed them to defy gravity and run or stand along the underside of the floating island.

“Brilliant!” Shin cheered as the home team Underrider managed to flip past the defender, whipping around his Underboard as he flew past and threw the Underball into a large, glowing green net.

“Scoooooooooreeeeee 1 for the Stone Giants!” The announcer’s voice echoed as a wave of cheers broke out across the various floating islands and Void Ships.

Micheal snorted as he shook his head.

‘Well…’ It was a strange experience to be back, watching an Underball game again, but Micheal couldn’t help but to relax, just a bit.

As the crowds cheers washed over him, and the lights of the arena flashed by, he felt some of the tightly coiled stress that served as a constant presence inside him seem to… settle, ever so slightly.

It didn’t go away, nothing could truly change the burdens he faced…

But times like this, it did make it a little easier.

“Wooooo! Get em, Ser Grogsworth!” Shin yelled, cheering on the Stone Giants Team Captain.

Micheal smiled.

‘Maybe this isn’t so bad after all.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

On the opposite side of the Third Layer, far to the northeast, sat the quiet City-State of Ibrasia.

This City-State was considered relatively quaint – ruled by Baron Charg von Auras and guarded by the Baron’s father, the Hero of Black Fire, Sven von Auras, it was among the most peaceful of City-States, situated out-of-the-way near the Outer Ringlands.

Despite the recent onset of Chosen species climbing up the Layers, Ibrasia was at peace – unlike the Red Line to the west, new arrivals were allowed entry to Ibrasia, flourishing whole new lines of trade for the otherwise somewhat poor province.

Here, inside a small, non-descript stone house in the middle-class region of Ibrasia, stood a human, pacing back and forth inside a small study. The man had short black hair and a gruff, black beard, dressed in a simple set of black pants and a dark gray vest and black undershirt. Various books lined the bookshelves on the walls of this room, countless papers and notes stashed almost haphazardly. A small, golden lightbulb lit the room at an angle, spreading shadows in an almost haunting manner.

“The patterns, the lines, a ripple in Time.”

This human was disheveled, his eyes bloodshot as he turned to stare at his desk.

Lying there was a set of journals, sprawled open, full of small, clean, detailed English writing, alongside a few other odds and ends.

Marco Barone, Founder and Director of Dark Void, slammed his hand down on the desk, rattling the wood. A collection of Artifact rings sparkled on his hand as the metal bit into his flesh, drawing blood.

“Think.” Marco shoved the desk to the side and sat down on the ground, intensely focused.

With but a thought, one of the notebooks flew through the air and landed down on the ground before him, picked up by an invisible hand.

Marco turned through the notebook, flipping through it.

He didn’t focus on the many pages of incredible information, the veritable font of knowledge that Marco knew would evolve the very core of Dark Void as he knew it, propelling his fellow researchers years into the future.

No, what he focused on was a note, hastily scribbled and added to these journals.

A note that detailed a fact that changed everything.

“A Time Loop. It all makes sense now.”

Marco’s eyes bled blue light as he sat there, energy rushing around him.

Finally, the pieces to the puzzle he had only recently discovered began to unfold.

A question that had dominated his mind, ever since one of his Spatial-Temporal Readings went askew, just a few days ago.

It was the type of thing no normal person would ever notice, or even think to monitor, as difficult as it was to monitor something as abstract as the Flow of Time.

For, Marco was as far from ‘normal’ as a human could be.

Because…in every sense of the word…

Marco Barone was a genius.

He graduated from high school at the age of 6, from college at the age of 9, and earned his first Doctorate when he was only 13 years old. He founded his own company at the age of 15 and won a Nobel Prize in Physics the day before he turned 20.

And now, here on the Third Layer, more than 3 and a half years after being Chosen…

Talos Mind Power. Bright Soul. Cerebral Split. Erudite of Crossed Stars Type.

More than half of his Ability slots were specialized with a singular focus:

Marco wanted to understand.

Why had the world changed? What was different? What caused this? How did Magic work? Why did Abilities work? How did Conceptual Powers function? Exist? What was the Shop?

And it was precisely that drive to comprehend his new reality, that saw him to this point here.

“Envious Touch.” Marco’s words were a bare whisper as a dozen pages of paper appeared in his left hand.

Like a man possessed, he slammed down on the paper, pen moving so quickly that it became a blur as he wrote out orders.

“Assemble a team, immediately, for an emergency recall.”

His hands moved up and down, writing line after line.

“Antwon, Mei, reform the Wavelength Squad on the shores of the Empty Sea, coordinates…”

His breathing grew ragged as he trembled, focused utterly in the moment.

“Jabari, act as a gathering point. Axellion is the key, we must be bold.”

“Envious Touch.” A flurry of papers vanished as Marco twisted the activation of his Ability, letting him transport his orders across the vastness of Space.

Finally, Marco looked up, his bloodshot eyes staring at what was about to fall off his desk.

A chess board, with its pieces scattered about haphazardly. The black king stood precariously above the white knight, caught in the corner’s edge, while the whole board teetered off the side of his desk, perched to fall away at a moment’s notice.

“Time, precious time.” Marco whispered, his eyes glowing with blue light.

“A plot within a plot. A key within a key.” He muttered,

No one else across the entire Third Layer spotted it… but here, shrouded in the shadows…

Thanks to a set of journals, and a note hastily scribbled…

Marco Barone saw.

Marco Barone knew.

“We must hurry, before it is too late.”

They were not ready for this, they were not prepared, yet Time waits for no man.

Dark Void sprung into action.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

2 Days remained until the Founding Celebration.

.

Chapter 38


.

Micheal embraced the Realm of Intent.

Here, alone in the heavily Warded room provided by Vesper, he felt more than saw an outline of the world around him overlay itself, a second copy, peeking forward into the future.

He was sitting down on the ground with his legs crossed, dressed in a simple set of black pants and a dark gray shirt. In front of him was a small wooden stand, upon which an earthen brown vase sat, recently purchased from the Shop.

Micheal shut his eyes, however, as he ignored the outside world, looking inward.

His mind remained centered, in meditation as he gradually brought the state of his Soul into his awareness.

It was a delicate process, though one made significantly easier by his Eternal Mana Circles. The Mana Circles acted like a beacon, making him instinctively able to reach out and sense his Soul.

‘One, two… three.’ He felt at his third Mana Circle, sensing the shivering instability in its foundations – the Circle was becoming more stable over time, but it was an ongoing process that would take several weeks, at minimum.

Micheal stretched his senses further.

While he maintained the Realm of Intent, his Soul existed in an excited state, directly tapping into the Cognitive Sea, giving him a direct connection to the River of Time.

Micheal used that connection to zero in on a faint, almost imperceptible mark upon his Soul.

‘There you are.’

The Brand of Janus.

With his Soul enhanced by the Realm of Intent, Micheal could directly feel the bridge the Brand formed, dipping into the ebb and flow of Time.

It was a strange, esoteric mark, an image of power that defied comprehension.

He cast his mind back to what he knew about the Brand.

It was a Brand upon reality, rediscovered and recreated by Yvvtal, back when he was still alive and experimenting with the ‘Divine Language’ – a tongue that allowed Deities to manipulate their Divine Energy. It wasn’t clear how the Toren race came into contact with the Divine Language, at least not as far as Micheal knew – only that they did, and that they would go on to, at some point later, Ascend and become Deities themselves.

Through the Brand, Micheal felt strands of Time drift by, as the present became the past, and the future became the present. Yvvtal believed the Brand was originally created by a Titled Deity known as Janus, who altered the fabric of existence itself, leaving a mark for all Time to see.

‘There.’ His eyes glowed beneath his eyelids as he shifted his perspective of the Brand.

Diametrically separate, yet intrinsically linked, guided by the sensations he felt inside Kyrui’s Inheritance…

Micheal reached out to the Concept of Space.

For the briefest second, the air around Micheal trembled as he felt a bridge form along the Brand of Janus, just like it did when he connected to the Concept of Time. The currents of Space felt different from the flow of Time, more solid, more tangible, confined to the building blocks of reality around him.

Sweat poured down his brow as he zeroed in, his heart pounding. This was an incredibly high-level, esoteric process that took up an enormous amount of concentration, willpower, and focus. Connecting his Soul to such abstract, foreign Concepts was incredibly difficult, even with everything he had going in his favor.

Slowly, Micheal raised his right hand, reaching out to the wellspring of Space around him, and…

His eyes opened and he pulled.

His future sight overlaid with double vision as he watched the process unfold out in front of him.

With a faint shriek, the clay vase sitting on the stand in front of him fractured, a dozen cracked lines forming as the fabric of space it stood upon… twisted.

“Woah.” Micheal snatched his hand back as he felt the fabric of space snap back to normal, a rush of air sweeping past him and stirring the room about.

He grinned.

‘Progress.’ He resisted the urge to pump his fist like Shin.

Finally, he had managed to form, however faint, a connection to the Concept of Space.

‘If not for Kyrui…’ He bowed his head slightly, in honor of the fallen warrior.

The dead Dark Wraith’s Inheritance had proven incredibly pivotal, letting him touch upon the Concept of Space and find it almost familiar, rapidly speeding up the time it took for him to form a stable connection through the Brand.

He had read the guides, left behind by other humans recounting their interactions with Conceptual Powers, spread by Dark Void – but there was no replacement for actually feeling the sensation that a Conceptual Power brought to your Soul.

Micheal exhaled a long, deep breath, staring down at his hands. A set of hard, thick calluses had formed, from his daily practice with Lightshorn and his training in general.

He traced a finger over the lines of that callus, his thoughts turning inward.

The path of the Sword was closed off to him, at least for now.

He had come to peace with that fact.

Becoming a Grandmaster with his talent was a miracle in its own right, possible only due to the numerous Abilities, efforts, and circumstances Micheal worked with in his first life.

Progressing beyond that had felt akin to running into a brick wall.

It simply wasn’t in the cards, and…

That was fine.

‘You play with the hand you’re dealt.’ He couldn’t control something as abstract as talent…

But what he could control was his mindset, his attitude, and his focus.

With but a thought, a wave of Sword Energy enshrouded his hand. The violent, prickly energy wrapped around his fingers, cutting through the air with deadly intent. He stared at the fluctuating energy, giving it a moment’s study.

“I may not be able to progress you, but my efforts will not go to waste.” He clenched his fist, strands of energy pulsating as he once more reached out for the Concept of Space.

The air rippled once more as he strained, relying on the Brand of Janus to ease his pull upon the Concept. The power came to him, this time, slightly easier.

The air trembled as space itself twisted for a split second.

In that moment, as it twisted, Micheal flicked his hand forward.

His eyes glowed as his Soul strained, the Realm of Intent letting him adjust his movements ahead of time, to perfect the strike.

A tiny slice of Grandmaster Sword Energy shot out from his hand and… it curved and split along the twist in Space, rotating in on itself. The deadly energy entered a whirlwind of destruction as it clashed against itself, creating a small, miniature tornado of rippling white energy.

The impact, despite using only a miniscule amount of Sword Energy, detonated loudly in the room, creating an enormous gust of wind that blew Micheal back a step. The pillows and cover on his bed went flying, while several paintings shuddered back and forth, almost knocked off the wall.

“Woah there.” Micheal abruptly released the Realm of Intent, rubbing his forehead as he felt a small spike of pain.

‘My connection is still too weak.’ His attempt fell apart in the end.

He was still far from displaying the Mastery of Space that Kyrui had shown, in his final duel against Sion Swordsoul.

‘But progress is progress.’

Step by step, Micheal continued to move forward.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Shin stretched out his newly upgraded Melding Plate Arm, grinning as he felt the Artifact seamlessly reach out. He was back in the room Vesper had provided them, after another day spent training with the Round Table.

“Hup!” He twisted the arm around him, feeling it coil along his lower back.

He then pulled it back out and in front of him, admiring its new look.

A line of runes had been implanted, marching up and down the arm, carved in with faintly glowing blue ink.

‘Sick.’

That Wizard dude, Dunkore, had really outdone himself – this was the first of the Artifacts the Wizard had finished his work on, needing one last day before he finished the others.

There was a whole world of difference, just in how the arm felt, as Shin raised it back and forth, feeling the hardened metal shift like it was actual flesh.

“Expand.”

His arm bulged outward as Shin drew upon his Concept of Strength, his body running flush with warmth.

“Yeah.” Shin twisted the arm back and forth. It moved smoothly despite being enlarged, perfectly following his intentions. His shoulder and ab muscles flexed as he steadied himself, drawing on the Concept of Strength as he held the hulking metal appendage upright.

After a second, he released his Expand Ability, letting the arm shrink back down to normal size.

“It works like a charm!”

He didn’t quite know how to put it into words, but if before, the Artifact had felt like something he stuck to his body to resemble an arm, now it truly felt like he actually had a real arm again. The sensitivity, the control, it was on another level.

‘Dang, this feels good.’ He teleported himself down to the ground, before planting his arm firmly and then pushing himself up, doing a one-handed handstand.

“It’s almost like I have you back, eh?” He patted his newly-upgraded left arm. His left arm didn’t reply, but Shin didn’t let that bother him, simply smiling as he flipped, landing back on his feet.

“Shop.”

Shin opened the Shop menu, turning through the various Ability pages.

“I think Micheal was right.” Shin muttered, as he landed on one page in particular.

.

—-Abilities—-

Hypoxic Touch – 782,219 (11/15)

Shockwave Tapper – 1,800,500 (8/8)

Moonlit Flicker – 7,104,622 (1/10)

Elemental Companion – 2,008,150 (21/172)

Manifold Clone - 3,786,411 (13/15)

Power Flow - 175,000 – (1,138/44,008)

Death Parade – 3,803,442 (2/7)

Soul Imprint – 4,109,005 (0/25)

Fitzgolem Shield Type – 1,998,000 (2/6,000)

Phintowinter Excel Type – 3,944,006 (1/25)

Liminal Expansion – 1,823,995 (12/12)

Obsidian Arms – 988,100 (12/4,002)

Helion Ray Type – 2,887,236 (2/11)

Frozen Starfire Type – 3,228,980 (2/4)

Ogre of Ten Thousand Arms Type – 7,871,225 (0/2)

Induction Shield Aura – 891,912 (31/690)

Blackout Reign – 1,080,400 (3/25)

Awakened Goliath Type – 19,408,250 (0/1)

Erratic Sight – 782,000 (21/308)

Twisted Step – 1,480,295 (4/72)

… (40/41 page)

.

“The next Ability I should work towards…” The blonde-haired human tapped his chin, a thoughtful look in his eye.

.

Manifold Clone - 3,786,411 (13/15)

.

“Manifold Clone.” Shin stared down his choice.

According to Micheal’s future sight, Clone Abilities were some of the most lucrative powers, bought out from their Limited supply in the Shop early on. After all, when compared to the myriad of other complex or confusing superpowers, the usecase for a ‘Clone’ was clearcut and simple. A Clone Ability granted the user a very clear advantage, immediately.

However…

“We’re still early enough that not all Clone Abilities are gone.” Shin recalled the exact words Micheal had told him, when he asked for advice on his next Ability choice.

Because of his unique Conceptual Power, what Micheal had described as a ‘Closed’ Conceptual Power, more than half the Shop was filled with Abilities that were useless to him. Any Ability that needed a source of energy, like Ki or Mana, wouldn’t work for him, now that he was a Devotee of Strength, as he liked to put it. It sounded cool.

Manifold Clones, however, were one of the Abilities that didn’t rely on something like Ki or Mana – an upside in Shin’s eyes that was also part of the reason why Micheal suspected the Ability hadn’t already been bought out, like most Clone Abilities had.

.

—-Manifold Clone—-

A Manifold Clone splits away its users strength to form a semi-independent Clone, dissolving and transferring its memories upon its demise.

.

The Ability description wasn’t too specific, but Micheal had come in clutch, once more, explaining how the Ability worked for Shin. His best friend was truly GOATed.

The way it worked was simple – he split off a portion of his overall strength, the stats of his body, and created a Clone based on that. The Clone would be identical to him in every way, even possessing its own recreation of his upgraded Melding Plate Arm. It would also have its own temporary consciousness, based on him. His own mini-me.

It was only when the Clone died that its memories would transfer to him, a neat feature that not all Clone Abilities possessed.

This Clone also only split away portions of his body’s raw stats – things like Ki or Mana weren’t carried over at all, which, for Shin, didn’t matter.

This was one of the more unique types of Clone Abilities, and another reason why it hadn’t been bought out yet.

“…I really can do it.” Shin stared at the Ability description, eyeing the Points total as he committed himself.

This was it. The next Ability he was going to work towards, farming up Points as quickly as he could, until he could buy it.

“My own Shadow Clone Jutsu.” He grinned, his eyes shining.

He punched the air with his newly upgraded metal arm, jumping in excitement.

“Let’s go!”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

1 day remained until the Founding Celebration.

Chapter 39


.

“He left.”

“What?” Micheal leaned forward, for once, taken completely by surprise.

He was down in Aaron’s office, back at Camelot 2.0, the headquarters of the Round Table.

Even now, just after dawn, Axellion had become a hive of activity – today was the last and final day before the Founding Celebration. Foreign Nobles, dignitaries, merchants, Knight Commanders, a veritable deluge of visitors had begun arriving, setting the city to swarming. Great fleets of Void Ships lined the horizons, bringing along caravan after caravan, teeming with Void Natives.

Just outside Camelot 2.0, cheers and revelry leaked in through the windows as a huge parade proceeded down Axellion’s main streets, heralding the arrival of the Third Layer’s biggest celebrity – Eon, the King of Heroes.

With the ominous future just ahead of them, Micheal and Shin had come to visit the Round Table early, coordinating for what was yet to come.

Shin was out training with Jessica Wiles again, in the Round Table’s space-expanded secret training grounds. Jessica’s ability to instantaneously transport herself through ice was close enough to Shin’s teleportation that the duo had taken to swapping notes, comparing their combat styles and giving each other tips over the past few days.

“As far as we can tell…” Aaron flipped over a page of vellum, reading through several scribbled reports. The Commander of the Round Table was dressed in a casual long-sleeved white shirt and a pair of gray pants, reclining in his office’s plush chair.

“Bastien Amiot took one of his surviving disciples with him and left the Third Layer, working together with one of the refugees brought here by the Purgatory Church that had a nearby exit point and wanted out.”

The Purgatory Church also had a branch setup in Axellion, though not one Micheal had deigned to visit. Until the Nirvana Saint climbed up and took control, the organization lacked effective leadership. Their current headquarters on the Third Layer was hundreds of miles to the east, at the direct southernmost point of the Empty Sea.

“He left one day before you arrived.”

Micheal rubbed his forehead.

“That doesn’t- alright.” He frowned, uncharacteristically stumbling over his words as his mind raced.

‘I definitely saw a Grandmaster attack Barsoth.’ As a fellow Grandmaster, it was impossible for him to mistake Grandmaster Sword Energy for anything other than what it was.

“Thanks to you, we’ve managed to establish a line of communication with Dark Void. They haven’t gotten back to us, yet, about Bastien, but I’m certain their findings will be the same.” Aaron continued.

Micheal hadn’t skimped out on the details when it came to sharing his future knowledge with the Round Table. He’d given Aaron and Dark Void almost everything he possibly knew, every morsel they could devour and use to mankind’s advantage.

“He’s no longer present on the Third Layer.”

“And you’re certain of this?” Micheal queried.

Aaron nodded as he tapped on the pages of vellum on his desk.

“As certain as we can be. Duke Atlas sent us these records last night, coordinating with us after you gave him your request.” He raised one of the pages, turning it over.

“I assume you’ll probably find a similar copy placed back at your guest room when you return.”

“We know he was present, here in the city, but he definitely left one day before you arrived – he was seen leaving the Western Gate. We also believe he successfully left this Layer and moved on to the Fourth Layer.” Aaron placed the vellum back down on his desk as he continued,

“Bastien left a Life Link Artifact, a Soul Compass, with the Purgatory Church, in case his last missing disciple showed up.”

Life Link Artifacts – there were a few different types, from Guardian Bracelets to Everliving Candles, they were esoteric Artifacts that could bond to the Soul of any individual, with a singular purpose – if that person should die, the Artifact would react. Everliving Candles would blow out, Guardian Bracelets would shatter, the range of effects varied.

A Soul Compass was similar – once bonded, it would point in an individual’s direction no matter how far away that person was, only breaking its hold if the user died or removed the esoteric ‘Connection Mark’ that was placed upon their Soul.

“It took some finagling, but we managed to convince the Branch Leader to let one of our members look at the Compass. It’s still active, so he’s alive, but it’s stuck pointing straight up, with no shifting no matter how its moved.” Aaron pointed towards the ceiling.

Micheal simply nodded back, slowly. Corruption in the Church was just par for the course, until the Nirvana Saint arrived.

That was the exact response the Compass would give if Bastien had moved on to a higher Layer – if he was dead, the Compass would’ve broken its connection.

“That’s all I have for you.”

Micheal rubbed his forehead, holding back a sigh.

‘As long as he’s still alive, I guess it’s fine.’ He would simply have to adjust his plans. He’d seek Bastien out once he arrived on the Fifth Layer, down in the Roots of the massive Planetary Tree.

“Thanks, Aaron – I appreciate it.” He did. The Round Table leader had gone above and beyond his expectations.

“It’s nothing, not compared to how you’ve helped us.” Aaron waved it off as he continued, folding his hands together as he looked at Micheal.

“I wanted to inform you – that pair you spoke of, Lux and Rex.” Micheal’s eyes flickered as he registered the names.

“They came to us, seeking something similar – they wanted to coordinate ahead of time, for tomorrow. They’ve offered a line of aid, not just themselves, but also from the man they represent.” Aaron continued,

“Constantine’s forces.” Micheal’s eyes narrowed.

“Precisely.” Aaron nodded.

There was a tense moment, before Micheal broke the silence.

“You accepted.”

“I did.” Aaron added,

“Better the devil you know, than the devil you don’t. I think they’re dangerous, but I also think it’s in our best interests to work together for this.”

Micheal slowly nodded back.

“Hard times make for hard decisions.” He understood the logic – humanity was facing a crisis, now was not the time to be divided.

“We’ve also elected not to inform Duke Atlas, not after what you shared with us.” Aaron went on.

Micheal grunted his assent.

According to Vesper, in previous Loops conveying foreknowledge of the impending attack to Duke Atlas turns the Archmage into a paranoid mess.

Foreigners were already viewed with suspicion, the fact that they knew about an impending attack on his city ahead of time would, in her opinion, convince the Duke that they were in some way related to the attack.

Showing foreknowledge of an impending attack upon Axellion would almost certainly turn the Duke against them.

And…

Micheal held back a grimace.

In the first place… Jay sol Arget was here because of humanity.

If Duke Atlas learned that… then all of the efforts humanity had made, establishing a foothold here, would go to waste. It was a callous truth that he couldn’t help but acknowledge.

‘We’ll deal with it when it comes up.’ The fact that they were trapped in Time Loop complicated everything, to the point where Micheal forced himself to prioritize what mattered most to him – humanity’s survival. Everything else came after.

“Finally…” Aaron turned

“Lux also left a message for you - 'Goodbye, I'll leave it where we met'.”

‘What?’ Micheal’s eyes narrowed, thinking back to their last conversation.

‘Leave what?’

It was a question he’d have to find the answer to later, as Aaron and Micheal got down to the nitty-gritty, discussing force positioning, relay points, and battle strategies, planning for the day to come. Micheal’s vast experience when it came to combat in the 7 Layers shined as he and Aaron dived into a back-and-forth.

Minutes turned to hours as time slipped by, where plans within plans were formed, backup plans considered, and emergency options taken into account.

Just like that, morning and afternoon turned to evening.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“It fits.” Micheal sat up upon the roof of one of Castle Atlas’ lower towers, adjusting his new Raidon Gauntlet. He had gotten permission to be up here thanks to Vesper, a place where he could be outside and find some measure of peace and quiet, as evening turned to night in Axellion proper.

The newly forged Artifact was crafted from a mixture of conductive metals, an enchanted alloy that could transfer Ki or Mana with almost 0% loss of energy. It was adjustable, fitting either hand quite well, with thin layers of overlapping black metal covered in dark red magical glyphs. It had an almost scale-like quality, each piece individually bending as he moved his hand back and forth.

‘I can feel a connection.’ He drew on his Mana Circles, forming a connection with the Raidon Gauntlet to his Soul. He felt that connection strengthen and then snap into place, giving him a more active control over the Artifact.

‘Just in time.’ Micheal smiled.

After his hours long talk with Aaron, Micheal had left to pickup the set of Artifacts he’d commissioned from Dunkore. He had Sophia’s gift in his Spatial Ring now, while he tried on the gauntlet Dunkore had made for him.

‘Let’s try it out, just a little.’ He didn’t have the time to fully field test the Artifact, but testing it now was better than nothing.

Micheal embraced the Realm of Intent.

Immediately, the world was overlayed with a second vision of itself.

Micheal felt his connections to Space and Time both strengthen, the two Conceptual Powers operating like opposite sides of the same coin.

‘It’s there.’ Dunkore had delivered on his promise.

Micheal activated the Artifact.

Immediately, five invisible trails of energy shot forward a few meters. Micheal concentrated as he felt the invisible lines of power extend outward, floating in the air.

With a conscious thought, Micheal drew upon his connection to Space and…

He twisted his hand.

Space warped.

His view of Axellion twisted, for a split second, into a mashed up, whirlpool, the lights of the city blurring together in a swirling vortex, guided by five distinct lines of invisible energy.

A storm of air shot out as Micheal released his control, space snapping back together in one violent jerking motion.

He grinned, stretching his fingers inside the gauntlet as he stared down at it. Affecting empty Space was far easier than affecting Space occupied by someone or something, but it was still an achievement, an advancement in his control, nonetheless.

The Artifact acted as an amplifier, like a Wizard’s Stave or Wand, a focal point he could use to leverage his connections to his Conceptual Powers.

“He’s outdone himself.” Micheal muttered as he released the Realm of Intent.

The Artifact had incredibly steep control requirements – in the first place, if you didn’t have a connection with both the Concept of Space and the Concept of Time, it would be useless to you. Manipulating those Concepts through the Gauntlet wasn’t exactly easy either – Micheal had to fight against Space’s natural tendency to hold still, and Time’s tendency to maintain a stable flow.

The gauntlet amplified the power of his connections, but the actual process of controlling that increased power was entirely reliant on Micheal’s finesse.

It was here that his many, many years of manipulating dangerous Sword Energy came into play. While his experience as a Grandmaster of the Sword couldn’t translate entirely one-to-one, it still left him at a sizable advantage.

“Really well done.” Micheal commented as he tapped on the Artifact, storing it in his Spatial Ring.

If everything went to plan, and they managed to put this Time Loop behind them while remaining in one piece, Micheal planned on setting Dunkore up with Dark Void – in the first timeline, the inquisitive Dimensional Traveler eventually entered into a partnership with Dark Void, here on the Third Layer, though to what exact extent Micheal didn’t know.

It was the least he could do, to help the stranded Wizard.

He let out a long sigh as his thoughts turned outward, gazing down at the city lights.

Axellion bustled, even now, so late at night, as more and more visitors arrived, preparing for the Founding Celebration tomorrow.

Here up on his tower, however…

At night, there was an omni-present darkness to the Third Layer. It was part of what made Void Predators so deadly – their ability to blend into the darkness as if they didn’t exist.

Here, alone on his tower, Micheal felt a sense of kinship with that darkness, as he found solitude in its repose.

Tomorrow, his fate was uncertain.

He didn’t know what the future would hold for him, how their battle with Jay sol Arget would go, and the machinations the vengeful Titled Deity had wrought.

Like the darkness of the night, the relentless flow of time was everywhere and inevitable.

He couldn’t change that final truth any more than he could create a new Sun, here on the Shattered Plane.

Micheal slowly got to his feet, feeling a sense of serenity wash over him.

Tomorrow, everything would come to a head.

He’d prepared what could be prepared, planned for what could be planned, and now, all that was left was to wait.

Dawn would come, and…

He would be ready.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The hours drifted by, like a ship cast along a river, swaying gently in the night breeze.

Soon, dawn came to Axellion, as Void Nobles, Natives, and Foreign races alike woke to start the day.

The Founding Celebration had come upon them.

And in those early dawn hours…

No one noticed as a vague figure slipped in through Axellion’s Northern Gate.

.
