Chapter 40


.

Trumpets bellowed in fury, glorious chimes ringing through the air in a grand symphony of noise. Great explosions of False Fire lit up the dark sky of the Shattered Plane, fluttering in colorful patterns that spread out upon the air, a thousand lines of harmless energy burning up in a display of wealth and power.

Up in his private office, a large room covered wall-to-wall with bookshelves, Duke Armon von Atlas smiled.

“And so it begins.” The powerful Archmage relished in the moment, feeling the pulse of Mana thrum within his Soul as the trumpets blazed on, announcing the start of the Founding Celebration.

Armon was dressed in full regalia, donning a resplendent golden robe woven from thin strands of enchanted metal, finely enjeweled gloves covered in Glyphs, and the austere Dark Prism Cape, an ancient Artifact cape passed down through House Atlas’ history. On his feet, he had on a set of boots that had been hewn from the spine of a Void Predator, enchanted and further refined with Mana-conductive metals.

In his right hand, he held the Erebo Staff, a stave that had the insignia of a shattered globe at its highest point, with several small celestial bodies orbiting around the globe. Smaller orbs of mana circled those celestial bodies, giving it an ethereal appearance.

The Duke was a veritable walking arsenal, a display of the raw power and wealth that House Atlas was able to project.

As Duke Atlas strode through his office, his eyes gleaming as he tapped into the Wards shrouding Axellion.

This was his moment. His triumph.

‘One of the Eight here in Axellion, dead, on the eve of the Founding Celebration.’ The fact that a Human had been the one to kill Barsoth didn’t diminish this fact.

If anything, it proved the resilience and capabilities of House Atlas, to have such a powerful subject acting at his behest.

For 1375 years, House Atlas had stood the test of time. From the Dawn of the Shattering, to the Stumbling Ages, to now, the Era of Heroes - an unbroken legacy that none could diminish. Pride swelled in Duke Armon’s chest, the weight of his ancestry pressed upon his shoulders and finding him not lacking.

“Arundath.” He cast a casual Spell, a slight movement-enhancing technique as he took a single step forward, bounding across his large office in an instant.

Six Mana Circles hummed quietly within his Soul, borne from the Endless Fall Mana Breathing Method, a Mana Breathing Method refined over a thousand years of tradition.

His Six Mana Circles had reached a stage known as Full Unification, granting him dominion over Mana.

Armon made use of this as he opened the side-door to his office, stepping out onto a large balcony.

With a casual thought, he manipulated the raw Mana in the air around him, combining it with his movement Spell, and he flew.

Unlike many feasts and parties, which were held in fancy ballrooms or private castle halls, the Founding Celebration was held outside, on a massive, open-air pavilion – a pavilion that normally did not exist.

For, in a grand display of Gravity Magic that House Atlas was famous for, the center of Axellion had been expanded, the very bedrock of the floating island shifting to form a massive, open landscape at least a mile wide, shaped like an oval.

A series of grand stone pillars had been set up, circling the pavilion in patterns, creating the Outer Pavillion which held the masses, and the Inner Pavillion, which held House Atlas’ invited guests. Lavish tables had been setup, adorned with fruits, meats, and cheeses of all kinds. House Atlas had spared no expense, not when they were flourishing as never before, with the glut of trade provided by those odd Human Foreigners.

A rumble of cheers broke out as he hovered over the Inner Pavillion, Magic highlighting him high up in the sky.

An Archmage could never make too subtle an entrance, after all.

With a smile, Duke Atlas waved to his people as he began to descend, the ebb and flow of gravity dancing to his tune as he lowered himself to the ground.

He ignored the announcers pronouncing his arrival as he landed atop a raised two-tiered dais, the ceremonial Atlas Platform, his eyes steady as he took in his surroundings.

Standing on the lower level were those he trusted most - his Chief Steward, Tywel Kathos, his first wife and his Firstborn Beareth von Atlas and his Knights, his favored disciple Sebastian Lomon and a faceless servant, his second wife and his Secondborn Contrasz von Atlas and his Knights, and the rest of his extended family, his younger sons and daughters alike.

Beyond them, on the ground floor, sat all the guests, invited Void Nobles and bannermen, those sworn to him, those who professed themselves rivals, and those who simply held power enough to not be ignored.

Duke Atlas’ eyes gleamed as he relished the moment once more.

It was time.

He stepped forward, his chest raised as his voice boomed out,

“Today, on the 275th Founding Celebration, we welcome the tides of victory!”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“He looks angry.” Shin whispered as he nudged Micheal with his elbow.

The Founding Celebration had officially kicked off. Micheal and Shin were both seated within the Inner Pavillion, thanks to their invitations from the Duke.

The Inner Pavillion was setup in a large semi-circle, all facing the raised dais that housed the Duke and his closest allies/family. Stepping down from the dais was more than five dozen spread out large tables, where those invited by House Atlas sat.

From foreign dignitaries to wealthy merchants to skilled Wizards to powerful Knight Commanders, it was a huge collaboration, and, when you looked at the thousands of tables that made up the Outer Pavillion that was open to the public…

It truly was a scene worthy of being called the greatest celebration Axellion ever threw.

Micheal glanced to the side, in the direction Shin had pointed him.

Vesper had helped them select their seating, positioning them at the same table that the Round Table was seated at – a table just slightly off center to the dais, indicating how great the esteem in which the Duke held the Round Table. Aaron Bartram and all three of his Vice-Commanders sat across from Micheal, alongside a good dozen of the actual Knights. Micheal recognized most of them, eyeing legends, men and women whose tales etched themselves into mankind’s history in the first timeline.

Beyond them, however, at the large table neighboring theirs, and the most central table – here, Micheal recognized a few familiar faces, Void Nobles who possessed some measure of fame in his first life. In particular, four figures stood out: Allmaster – the Many Faced Hero, Lord of the Helianor Principality to the North, Kyrog – the Hero of Thunder, Lord of the Kabul City-State to the South-East, Veryn Aliceon – Vice-Master of the Gyven Tower, and…

The figure Shin was pointing to: Eon – the King of Heroes.

The rest of the table was half empty, seats reserved for the Duke and his family, once they finished the opening ceremony.

Micheal eyed the legendary figure. Eon was dressed in a dark red toga bearing a golden crown upon his well-trimmed head of white hair. His red eyes practically radiated anger as he sat there, tapping two fingers on the table.

‘He looks positively fuming.’ Micheal frowned, wondering what had set the powerful Void Noble off. Could it be…?

‘Look alive.’ As the thought struck him, he split his awareness while entering the Realm of Intent.

The world was overlaid with a second copy as his eyes flickered scanning his surroundings.

According to Vesper, the ‘Unseen One’ always appeared, here at the Founding Celebration.

This was the key moment, to finding the solution they needed to break out of this Time Loop. The one place they knew Jay sol Arget would show up at.

Vesper’s past selves hadn’t conveyed anything more specific – according to her, the impending arrival of Kyvenval, the God-Emperor of Talos, proves incredibly disorienting.

While he couldn’t be certain, Micheal had a few guesses he had shared – Kyvenval famously possessed multiple Legendary Artifacts.

The Duke finished his opening speech, rousing another wave of cheers. Up on the Dais, Vesper caught Micheal and Shin's gaze and sent them a small wave, grinning cheekily.

Servants began to filter out, passing through the lines of guards separating the Outer Pavillion from the Inner Pavillion, while carrying large trays of drinks or specialty snacks.

“At least the food is good.” Shin commented as he took a bite of a large, meaty sausage, though only after Micheal confirmed it wasn’t poisoned.

An orchestra began to play in the background as the festivities moved forward.

The Duke began to descend from his dais, followed by his family and closest aides.

Micheal caught eyes with Aaron, who gave him a slow nod.

If everything went to plan, the attack should come in roughly fifteen minutes, after the opening feast was well into motion.

However…

Just as the Duke took his final step down from the stairs leading up to the highest dais…

The first sign that something was wrong came in the form of a loud ringing in his ears.

As one, everyone seated in the Inner Pavilion clutched at their ears. A loud, piercing whine screeched into the air, causing servants and Nobles alike to flinch.

The Duke’s eyes blazed with blue Mana as he raised his Erebo Staff, circles of complex Magic Glyphs forming around him.

And then…

“Paradigm Tilt.”

A deep, hate-filled voice spat, cutting through the ringing noise like a knife through butter and…

The world turned sideways.

“Shin!” Micheal lurched forward and grabbed Shin and-

A series of sonic booms shook the air as the duo teleported away.

“What-“ Shin didn’t have time to speak as Micheal whipped Lightshorn forward from his Spatial Ring, Grandmaster Sword Energy flaring as he cut forward.

A shockwave split apart before it slammed into the duo, blasting around them as it sent tables, food, servants, and guests flying. A second shockwave quickly followed, once again sliced apart by Micheal thanks to his future sight.

“What the-?” Shin let his sentence die off as he activated his Neo-Levitation Bracers, letting him float in mid-air.

In the same moment, Micheal brought out two Life Orbs and turned his body perpendicular with the ground, for…

Up was no longer up.

Rather, up was now what had originally been to their left, while down was behind them, what had originally been to their right. Gravity hadn’t just shifted – it was turned over entirely on its side.

The effects of such a change could be seen immediately, as the remaining tables began to slide down the now wall that was the Inner Pavillion. Various guests either clung to the pillars of stone that had been sealed into the ground, or fell, hurtling through the air as gravity sent them flailing.

“It’s him, Kyvenval!” Micheal yelled as a series of explosions shook the air, keeping an arm on Shin.

The Crown of the Angel King appeared on Micheal's head as he prepped it, ready to activate it on a hair-trigger. Likewise, his Raidon Gauntlet appeared on his left hand, settling into place, and he kept a mental track of his Scythe of Chains, ready to deploy it.

‘This isn’t what Vesper told us!’ Something had changed - the attack came early.

“He’s using the World Box!” Micheal yelled as he began to soar forward, scaling up

The World Box – one of the Legendary Artifacts known to be in the possession of Kyvenval, God-Emperor of Talos.

It was an Artifact quite literally out of legend, supposedly created by a dying Celestial God, that allowed Kyvenval to manifest a sort of Domain, in which he could alter certain fundamental forces like gravity for a wide region.

Many, if not most, of House Atlas’ Magic Wards were bound and created using Gravity Magic – the World Box’s Gravity Domain overrode those Wards at a base, fundamental level.

Micheal’s eyes glowed as he tried to parse what he was seeing. A cloud of obliterated stone dust had formed a haze in the air, further lowering visibility.

‘There!’ A glowing cube of energy walls had formed, about a hundred meters away, serving as the agreed-upon rally point for the Round Table. Several of the Knights, including all three Vice-Commanders were staging there, earlier than they had planned. Neither Dark Void nor Constantine's forces were present yet, upstaged by the early attack.

‘Where’s Aaron?!’ Micheal tapped into the River of Time, creating an accelerated pocket of Time for himself and Shin, slowing down the world around them - his Raidon Gauntlet amplified this bubble, further slowing down the outside world.

‘He’s with the Duke.’ The White Knight had shot forward, and was helping Duke Atlas stand. The powerful Archmage was hovering unsteadily in the air, bleeding from his ears and nose - he had taken the brunt of the explosion Kyvenval had led with, surviving only through the sheer power of the Defensive Artifacts he wore, after his Wards were invalidated.

Micheal’s gaze flickered, scanning behind the Duke.

Half the Duke’s family had been flung off as the world upheaved itself. Those that remained, however, either possessed a control of Gravity Magic, or Artifacts that could stabilize them. The Duke’s Spymaster, his Firstborn, his Secondborn, and Vesper-

A quiet, ripping sound echoed, barely audible through the cacophony of chaos.

In that tiny, frantic moment…

A bloody, broken hole was brutally punched through Vesper’s chest by…

By…

By…

By…

Nothing.

“NO!” A hoarse scream echoed.

Not from Micheal, but from Shin.

Shin’s body swelled, the Concept of Strength flowing within him, as he watched in slow motion as the light began to fade from Vesper’s eyes.

They had only known each other briefly, just for a few days. But that was enough, in Shin’s eyes, to form a bond – a real bond of friendship, for all their differences, for all the strangeness that was Vesper von Atlas, past-seeing Time-Loop revealing Wizard noble girl.

In that moment…

All he saw was a friend in need.

And so…

Shin acted.

The power to teleport was practically ingrained within Shin by this point in his life, a lived experience that had altered him down to his very core.

He moved instantaneously, acting on instincts that were now a fundamental aspect of his nature.

The world transformed, overlaid with a million translucent lines of energy, as he began to teleport.

And it was here, as he rocketed forward along those lines, instinctively knowing which ones led to Vesper’s location…

Shin saw something he had never seen before.

The lines that bound reality, luminous and ethereal, visible every time he activated his Warping Phaser Type Ability to teleport always looked the same. They had a strange consistency that never shifted, a feeling to them that he couldn’t quite put into words as he travelled along them.

However…

Right now, in this tiny, fragile moment as he teleported from one place to another…

Shin came upon something new.

A set of lines that were practically enveloping Vesper’s location and then… stretched back.

It was an incredibly odd sight that left him at a loss for words. Incomprehensible, the lines existed alongside the normal translucent lines, but also stretched backwards, as if they existed alongside a different plane of existence, an axis parallel to reality.

And in that moment, as Shin reached forward and began to finish his teleportation…

Shin made a decision that would change his life forever.

Shin reached the end of the line that would teleport him to Vesper’s location and…

Instead of just travelling along this line and finishing his teleport… Shin exerted his will, and did something he didn’t know he was capable of.

His Warping Phaser Type Ability pulsed within his Soul as he flexed the line he was on, causing it to warp back, stretching to match the lines that had enveloped Vesper.

And… as a result…

Shin teleported into the Background.

.

Chapter 41


.

“Ves!”

Strength filled Shin’s body as he teleported into existence, appearing right beside the injured Void Noble and-The world was strange. Colors appeared less vibrant, faded, in a way Shin couldn’t quite describe. The scents of the world felt muted, less existent, while the air felt odd, heavier, pressing down upon him.

And the wind…

It whistled, ominously, oddly, a faint, keening cry echoing in the air.

The wind continued to whistle oddly in Shin’s ears as he grabbed ahold of Vesper, stuffing the highest quality Healing Pills he had into her mouth. Around him, he was vaguely aware of Vesper’s family members turning in horror, screams erupting. Their words, however, came out somewhat muffled, as if yelling from a distance.

Vesper’s body remained slumped, the light fled from her eyes, as the gaping hole in her chest continued to bleed, unabated.

She was dead.

“Heavens, this feels good.”

A voice cut through the strange wind as Shin’s head snapped up, his breathing turned ragged as his hands trembled.

Standing roughly half a dozen meters away was-

‘What?!’

Shin’s thoughts were interrupted as two enormous roars shook the air, and a pair of hulking, Apex Void Predators shimmered into existence.

The massive creatures appeared just above the ground, falling as they shook free from enormous chains of blue energy, the gravity-tilted zone sending them sailing towards the now ruins of the Inner Pavillion and-The world transformed again, a wave of golden light encompassing Shin and everyone around him.

Shin blinked.

Abruptly, Shin found himself holding Vesper’s corpse, while standing in the middle of an enormous field of wheat. The sky overhead was blue, like that of earth – in the distance, he saw rolling hills, all filled with the same fields of golden wheat, spreading endlessly outwards like a plague, until they reached an outer edge of great, towering gray mountains.

“Ah yes, we’re in the Dream now.” Standing roughly half a dozen meters away, was…

A man, almost human-like in appearance.

He had plain brown hair, pale, pasty white skin. He wore a set of plain brown pants and a basic gray shirt. His face was plain and nondescript – a small nose, thin eyes, a weak chin. If not for the tight oval shape of his pupils, he could be mistaken for an extremely pale human.

“Such a queer power, this Eon doth profess.”

Shin recognized the speaker, matching the description Micheal had told him.

It was…

Him.

The architect of all this misery and suffering.

One of the Five Calamities that ruined Humanity.

A Titled Deity.

Jay sol Arget.

Shin slowly lowered Vesper’s corpse, controlling his breathing like Micheal had taught him. His heart raced inside him, rage boiling over to hatred as he stared down Vesper’s killer.

His eyes flickered, once to the left and once to the right.

Micheal was nowhere to be seen.

The guests, Vesper’s family, everyone that had been just right beside them… they were all gone.

Even those two enormous Apex Void Predators were gone, vanished, nowhere to be seen.

It was just him and Jay sol Arget, holding Vesper’s corpse amidst an endless field of wheat.

“Where are we?” Shin asked, not expecting a response as he tried to control himself.

‘Think.’ What would Micheal do?

Micheal wouldn’t let his anger control him.

Jay sol Arget chuckled as he turned to glance at Shin.

In that movement, Shin noticed something odd – faint particles of… something… were drifting off the Endwalker, floating up into the sky and dissipating.

“You again.” Jay sol Arget’s voice was flat as he flicked his wrists, wiping away a few drops of Vesper’s blood.

“Shin. Shin. Shin.” The Endwalker quirked an eyebrow, clapping his hands together as he stared Shin down with a smile.

Shin stared back impassively, refusing to give him a reaction, no matter how unsettled he felt.

“You know, all these years, I never answered any of your questions.” The Titled Deity paused, rubbing his chin.

“Everytime we met, always the questions, always me ignoring you, always the violence.” Jay sol Arget shook his head.

“It’s nice, now that this is all over, to finally avail myself to something different.”

‘Keep him talking.’ Shin’s heart pounded in his chest as he listened to the monster speak.

“Years?” He frowned, thinking back to what Vesper told them, “This is the 74th Loop, no? That’s a long time, sure, but not years.”

“Oh, you already knew about the Loop? And 74? Ah yes. Right.” The Endwalker glanced towards Vesper’s body.

“I suppose that’s around the time I stopped killing that annoying Farseer at the dawn of every Loop.”

Shin felt a sinking feeling in the pit of his stomach as he listened to the Titled Deity talk.

“This truly is freeing, Shin. You have no idea how long – well, let me think.” Jay sol Arget casually wiped some of Vesper’s blood onto his forehead as he ran his fingers through his hair.

“14,784.” The Endwalker grinned widely.

“14,784…” Shin repeated, feeling numb as the realization hit him.

“That’s how many Loops I’ve suffered through, and I have to say…” Jay sol Arget shook his head.

“Quite frankly, I’m just glad it’s over.”

Shock hit Shin’s system as the words settled, realizing the import of what Jay sol Arget claimed.

‘I need to tell Micheal.’

Abruptly, the fields of wheat they were standing in shook. Shin flinched as he knelt down, keeping Vesper’s body close as the ground trembled.

“Where are we?” Shin repeated his earlier question, clenching his upgraded Melding Plate Arm fist.

Jay sol Arget smirked, his gaze turning upward.

“The Dream – or, well, the Background of the Dream.” He chuckled, “You teleported into the Background, and then were encompassed by the Dream.”

Shin asked the Deity what that meant and…

To his surprise, Jay sol Arget answered him.

Shin had teleported into the Background.

A Conceptual Power made manifest, the Background was a surreal plane of existence that intersected reality one-to-one, and the plane of existence that all Endwalkers naturally dwelled within.

It was a unique Concept, a power that could not be Mastered, nor controlled – it simply was. A Concept manifested into existence.

A world that existed behind reality – and the reason why beings like Jay sol Arget were nigh impossible to notice, hovering in a realm that wasn’t quite the same reality as everyone else.

“And the Dream?” Shin asked.

Jay sol Arget swept his hands out, stretching them wide as he gestured towards the fields of wheat.

“A false world, wrought into existence by the being known as Eon. Magnificent, in its own way.”

The Endwalker reached down and grabbed one of the stalks of wheat, ripping it free from the earth as he examined it.

Around them, the world began to shake again. Small cracks began to form, high above in the rich blue sky.

“The Dream is an obscure Conceptual Power that Eon has Mastered just a half-step shy of Supremacy. Quite impressive for a lesser species.” Jay sol Arget raised the stalk of wheat up above him, before dropping it and watching it fall.

Quietly, more and more particles began to drift off the Endwalker’s form.

‘Is he dying?’

“Why are you telling me all of this?!” Shin couldn’t help but to ask, frustration overwhelming him.

Jay sol Arget turned his gaze back to Shin.

He casually waved his right hand.

A blue blur of energy shot out, rupturing the ground and scattering a large clump of wheat into the air, while a lump of dirt formed, smushed together by the attack.

Jay sol Arget walked over to that lump of dirt and sat down.

“You know, you’re quite hard to kill.” Jay sol Arget folded his hands together while resting his elbows on his knees.

He then rested his chin on his folded hands, giving Shin a small nod.

“You, Aaron, and that rat bastard Bastien.”

“No matter what I did. No matter how hard I tried, how well I planned…” Jay sol Arget let out a long sigh.

“I could never kill all three of you in the same Loop.”

The sky above them warped, its hues shifting from blue to a deep red. The mountains in the far background began to shake and tremble, some of them splitting apart, erupting in great rending arcs of molten magma.

“You always seemed to adapt. To be ready. To be prepared after one of you died, always changing, always different, always… annoyingly impossible.” Jay sol Arget oval pupils narrowed as he gazed at Shin, grumbling, “After 10,000 Loops of failure, I was forced to change. My time was running short.” The Titled Deity continued, “But I couldn’t just give up. Failure was not an option.” His voice dropped, “So I decided to watch, to learn, and to find a different way to win.” Jay sol Arget leaned back on his clump of dirt, staring up at the fractured sky.

“I derived my own Clone technique, using Paradox-Time Energy, by watching the Knight known as Yama – and I spread them out, across the Third Layer… always watching.”

“I learned about you. About Aaron. About Bastien. And most importantly, as it turned out…” Jay sol Arget turned his gaze back to Shin.

“I learned about your comrade, Micheal. The Seer.” Jay sol Arget spat out Micheal’s name, his voice layered deep with emotion, before resting back again with a sigh.

“He was the problem, but a damnedly hard problem to solve.” The Titled Deity shook his head.

“I never did manage to kill him, even on the Loops where I focused solely on that. He’s a right paranoid bastard, that Seer is.” Jay sol Arget chuckled.

“Killing you only seemed to make him fight harder. He never broke, and believe me, did I try.” He shook his head again.

Shin had to resist the urge to teleport, then and there, and slam his fist into Jay sol Arget’s cocky face, as he listened to the Deity’s infuriating tone.

“So, why am I telling you all this, like a village tale villain, revealing his evil plan?” The Titled Deity slumped back as particles began to swarm off his body in a storm. Bits and pieces of gray energy began to dissipate, peeling back and away from his face.

“That’s simple.” Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clone held his hand up, watching as it began to dissipate into dust.

“All this death, this destruction, this glorious chaos.” The Titled Deity’s grin widened into a rictus.

“This was just a distraction.”

The words sent Shin rocking back on his feet.

“What?” He sputtered, trying to come up with a response.

‘A distraction?’

“Oh, look at you, even now, planning to run off to tell your comrade.” Jay sol Arget grinned as his Clone’s body began to fall apart.

“How unfortunate… because…” Jay sol Arget rasped out,

“None of this matters.” The Titled Deity managed one final sentence, “I’ve already won.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Meanwhile…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

‘The Apexes are here!’

In that moment, just after Shin teleported to rescue Vesper…

Two huge Apex Void Predators appeared and immediately began to fall towards them.

Micheal activated the Crown of the Angel King.

Immediately, a rush of power filled him, energy enhancing his body, Ki, and Soul-Micheal blinked as a wave of golden light embraced him and the world transformed.

Before he could get his bearings, a wave of energy slammed into him as a loud voice yelled, booming in the air, “EON. I'LL. KILL. YOU!”

Micheal held Lightshorn out before him as, just a dozen meters away, two blurred forms began to clash amidst a field of golden wheat.

.

Chapter 42


.

One bad day.

There was a sentiment, that all it took for a good man to fall, was one bad day.

Kyvenval, the God-Emperor of Kalos, was not an unreasonable man.

He was a Kalosian – an artificial species, whose creators, the Celestials, had long since abandoned them.

Borne to a world constantly at war, as Kalosian Clans clashed against each other on a yearly basis, Kyvenval lived the life of a typical Kalosian. He was a blacksmith by trade, forging iron and copper into metalworks fit for a warrior.

While their ancestors were forged in the Flesh Vats, Kyvenval himself was a ‘Natural-Born,’ borne to a father and a mother, raised right in the small-time village of Kant. He mastered his craft, day by day, and lived his life loyal to those who did right by him.

When the Lord’s Tax came, he paid his share. When his Apprenticeship was completed, his manhood proven, he found himself a lover – Syraphine, his childhood crush. The village of Kant celebrated, as a union was formed, between man and woman, heralding the future.

The chaos, the wars, that was Lord’s business and, as a Journeyman Blacksmith, Kyvenval’s life was good.

It wasn’t until, one day, in the midst of his journey from youth to adulthood, that he stumbled upon something that changed his life forevermore.

An Inheritance.

A tomb, discovered by happenstance, one day, as he dug through a rocky cave, in search of rare ores to further his craft.

The Lordly Tomb of the First Celestials.

Kyvenval wasn’t some blessed hero, born with knowledge or shouldering a vast destiny…

Nor was he an arrogant noble filled with delusions of grandeur or a clever snake, seeking to fool others to better himself.

He was but a man, simple and of solid character, who came upon that which should have stayed hidden.

For, in that Lordly Tomb, laid the treasures of those who came before them.

Four Legendary Artifacts.

From the First Celestial, Aikos - the Eyes of God, whose gaze turns matter to crystal.

From the Second Celestial, Gyntor – the World Box, which bends the laws of nature.

From the Third Celestial, Kleator – the Imperial City, a world unto itself that defies space.

And… from the Fourth Celestial…

Janus.

He obtained the Twilight Ring, to walk upon the River of Time.

These Artifacts changed the trajectory of Kyvenval’s life.

He gained power, great and vast, and so he did what any man of his character would.

He wrought the wrongs of the world as he came across them, and stayed true to his beliefs. Those that challenged him fell, turned to crystal by the Eyes of God, crushed by the gravity of the World Box, or struck down in the Twilight World.

For 38 years, Kyvenval stayed true and strong.

He united the warring Clans, unifying the people of Kalos, one Clan at a time.

The Uniter, they called him.

The Conqueror, those less favorable, named him.

Yet, none could argue – under his reign, justice was dispensed, and…

The World of Kalos was at peace.

And then…

It happened.

People began to disappear.

A great storm overtook Kalos as 1 million of its inhabitants vanished, teleported away from their homes, kidnapped by forces outside Kyvenval’s control.

Among those that were Chosen was Lleyta, his sole-daughter, borne from a union between himself and his lover Syraphine.

The God-Emperor was enraged.

For 38 years, Kyvenval had reigned supreme – none had challenged him, for he possessed power that defied comprehension, Legendary Artifacts that bent the very rules of existence.

Yet now, his citizens were kidnapped under his very eyes, his own daughter taken against her will.

The Imperial City set to work, the best and brightest of Kalos scouring the world to understand what had happened. ‘Foul Magik’ was suspected, the Magic of Old, powers wielded by the Celestials that had inhabited their world long ago – yet Kyvenval found himself at a standstill.

Kalosians, as an artificial species, were incapable of using Magic.

Kalosian bodies were strong, durable, with naturally borne Mana Bodies that evolved into their own Mana Hearts simply by growing up.

That quirk of their own physiology, however, rent them incapable of forming a Mana Circle, forever barred from exploring the deeper mysteries of Magic.

And it was here, in the midst of storied debate, as the God-Emperor sought to unveil the mysteries behind his vanished citizens…

Kvyvenval, alongside his lover, was Chosen in the Second Wave.

Kyvenval’s First Layer was a massive expanse of sand, inhabited by monstrous ‘Sand Wyrms’ that preyed upon his people, scattered throughout various oases.

And so, the God-Emperor of Kalos tamed the First Layer, slaying every Sand Wyrm, and rescuing those Kalosians Chosen before him, gathering them within the empty Imperial City, to safe-guard them as he climbed the Layers, in search for his missing daughter.

Kyvenval’s Second Layer was far stranger – a world full of molten, magma seas, interspersed with islands of ice and earth. It was here, Kyvenval learned, that his people were not the only ones subjected to this cosmic kidnapping – other races, other worlds, millions of innocents had been captured, teleported away, in some sort of sick, twisted game.

The God-Emperor of Kalos' rage delved ever deeper.

And so it came to be, here on the Third Layer, that Kyvenval arrived.

The Shattered Plane – a strange realm full of floating islands hovering above an endless black Void.

One bad day.

It started with a murder.

Syraphine – his lover, the one who stayed true to him from humble beginnings to the crown that now burdened his head.

Overcome with grief, he vowed vengeance, seeking to understand not just why but how her death came to be.

He set off on a journey, to hunt down the one whose mark was left – Eon, the King of Heroes.

And he found the man – in a large City-State far to the South, known as Axellion.

And it was here that everything fell apart.

In his eagerness to confront Eon, to demand answers…

Kyvenval made a mistake.

An accident – pure happenstance, a coincidence so jarring, so unnatural that it never should’ve happened.

Yet… it did.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Just moments ago…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Kyvenval activated the World Box, using its control of gravity to allow himself to float high up in the air.

The God-Emperor of Kalos was a sore sight – his hands trembling, his face drawn and tired, the death of Syraphine hitting him incredibly hard.

‘I will have answers.’ The rage that boiled in his veins threatened to overwhelm all reason, as he pushed away at the shrine of grief that constantly hollowed out his heart, ignoring the faceless man floating next to him.

“Paradigm Tilt.” Kyvenval spat as he commanded gravity to shift and distort, intent on confronting Eon here and now, ignoring whatever celebration seemed to be ongoing.

Then, out of an abundance of caution…

Kyvenval ripped off his bandages, exposing the Eyes of God. The Artifacts, two solid black obsidian orbs that had replaced his own eyes, were always passively on, granting him a constant area of vision – their true power, however, came when he activated the Artifact directly.

‘A show of force is necessary.’ Had his lover’s brutal slaughter not been so fresh on his mind, perhaps he would have adopted a less confrontational approach.

Now, however, it was all he could do to restrain himself as he activated the Eyes of God, intent on crystallizing merely an arm-And then it happened.

A mistake that should never have occurred.

In that split second that Kyvenval activated the Eyes of God, he looked forward and…

The necklace that housed the Imperial City flipped up, obstructing his vision.

It was an impossible coincidence.

The Legendary Artifact was bonded to him, constantly under his control – he could manipulate its location telekinetically, keeping it permanently pressed to his chest, under a dozen protective seals. It should’ve been impossible for it to fly free.

Yet, somehow, in that tense moment, as his focus slipped elsewhere…

The Artifact appeared in his line of sight.

And his world froze, time itself slowing down as he activated his Twilight Ring, yet it was too late.

His heart plummeted to his stomach.

He stared at the Imperial City, the small, pea-sized Artifact that housed the millions of Kalosians he had rescued from the First and Second Layers…

Turned to crystal by the Eyes of God.

In his exhausted state, Kyvenval tried to rationalize the movement, and yet...

He was alone.

It was his fault.

It had to be.

The last string of rationality holding him together broke and…

One bad day.

The God-Emperor of Kalos lost himself to rage.

.

Chapter 43


.

For all his might, power, and wisdom, built up over dozens of reincarnations…

Even the King of Heroes was vulnerable to a surprise attack.

In a thousandth of a second, the instant Eon felt his very flesh betray him, transforming into pure, translucent crystal…

Eon opened the Dream.

“Do not fear the Reaper,

He walks in Fields of Gold.”

The mantra echoed in the air, Words of Power changing the very essence of reality itself as the Dream descended, Conceptual prowess borne from multiple lifetimes of dedication and study.

Eon crashed down on a field of wheat, grunting as a wave of pain slammed into him. A small crater formed as he landed, sending up juts of dirt and wheat, fluttering into the sky. The air tasted sweet, the scent of Harvold Wheat, native to a reality in one of Eon’s past lives.

He heaved as he knelt down on one knee, his mind delirious, for…

The left half of the powerful Void Noble’s body was entirely transformed into crystal, from the toes of his left foot to the left half of his skull. The rocky substance was translucent, glimmering with light, and incredibly eerie to the eye.

‘Is this how I go in this life?’

All around Eon, the world of the Dream spread out, as he felt his consciousness waver. Grand fields of golden wheat, backlit by mountains far in the distance, holding up a beautiful blue sky.

‘No.’

He refused.

“Do not fear the Reaper,

The Righteous and the Bold.”

As one, Eon felt the core essence behind the Dream warp and change, the rules binding it manipulated by the Words of Power he uttered, commanding its form.

His mind stabilized, and the pain lessened.

The damage was irreversible… but here, in the distorted reality of the Dream…

Anything was possible.

Slowly, Eon got to his feet, his breath regained and his back straightened.

He turned to examine his left arm, slowly raising it and flexing the strange crystal. The odd stones gleamed in the sunlight of the Dream, shimmering in mesmerizing patterns.

Had this been normal reality, back on the Shattered Plane, the arm wouldn’t have moved – muscles, tendons, his very veins had all been wrought into crystalline rock, at a microscopic level. It was a horrific transmutation, warping flesh into stone.

In the Dream, however…

“For now, I live.” Eon spat the words out as he stared down at his Spatial Ring.

The storage device where he kept much of his treasures had been on his left hand – it was now ruined like the rest of his left half, turned to useless crystal.

The sky shook, the air around Eon set to trembling as a massive gust of wind whipped up.

‘He’s breaking in.’ Eon felt more than saw the presence of his attacker as he fractured through the layers of the Dream, heading towards his location.

The powerful invader clearly radiated great power, openly and outwardly pulsing with the Conceptual Power of Time – he was either a Supreme Master of Time, or, far more likely…

He possessed an Artifact created by a Titled Deity.

There could be no other reasonable explanation.

‘False Gods whose arrogance knows no bounds.’ Eon had clashed with their kind before, in his previous lives.

Either way, it was enough to let his attacker breakthrough into the Dream.

“Tricky.” Eon frowned as he tapped the left half of his head, feeling the odd, now crystal texture.

He didn’t question why he was being attacked, nor the scale, nor the reason… because it didn’t matter.

He didn’t have much time left.

Eon spat out a shard of crystal, coated in blood.

He didn’t fear death.

He had lived, died, and lived again more times than he cared to count – death was a familiar friend to all Perpetuals.

However…

He absolutely loathed the thought of losing to someone who relied on one of them, the False Gods that called themselves Deities.

Eon stretched his will out to the Dream, feeling its contours and inhabitants.

He had been forced to burst out the Dream in one giant swell, inadvertently dragging in hundreds of others into this fake reality.

‘How do I avoid losing?’

Eon pondered, as time seemed to stretch – in fact, it quite literally did stretch, distorting as Eon finely manipulated the Dream, in-between the Lines, to give himself more time to think, considering the present. Time worked oddly in the Dream - for some, entire conversations were held, while for others, not even a second had yet to pass.

‘I can’t reshape it.’

He was already 4 Lines deep into the Dream and only barely still standing.

It was a rule known to all those who dared touch upon the Dream – the more Lines you wrought of the Words of Power, the closer you came to losing control, turning the Dream into a Nightmare.

Eon’s normal limit was 10 Lines, but in his current state, he put that limit lower, down to 8.

‘What do I have to work with?’ He tossed the useless Spatial Ring aside, discarding it. The Artifact crumbled at his touch, small crystals flashing as they fell apart and landed amidst the golden wheat.

The first line of a Dream Mantra was the most important – it wrought cohesiveness to the Dream, giving it a central theme that tied the Conceptual Power together.

‘Do not fear the Reaper.’

This line set the stage, making it harder for any within the Dream to die - not impossible, just more difficult.

It was because of this that Eon hadn’t already passed away, with half his brain turned to crystal.

The second line of the Dream Mantra was just as important, building the setting and background, to create the bedrock of this reality.

‘He walks in Fields of Gold.’

Fields of wheat, scenes from a world he once knew.

‘Do not fear the Reaper.’

The third line repeated the first, a pattern that must be maintained for the Dream to remain stable.

The fourth line…

‘The Righteous and the Bold.’

Those who considered themselves both righteous and bold, would now find themselves hale and hearty, the Dream itself granting them more strength, more power, more control.

In Eon’s case, his crystalline half acted like it was flesh again – even the half of his skull and brain returned to normal function – it was an impossibility, and yet… in the Dream, anything was possible.

Of course, this had the side-effect of boosting the power of anyone else in the Dream who considered themselves both righteous and bold…

‘But a beggar does not get to pick who shares his table.’ It was an old saying from his second-to-last life, that of a Knight Royal in the Kingdom of Tabash.

And-

The sky burst.

The Dream expanded and then closed instantly, shifting around its inhabitants and-Eon stood face to face with his attacker.

‘A Foreigner.’ He used the term his fellow Void Nobles used to describe the various species of Dimensional Travelers that were somehow forced into this Dimension, an odd mystery in its own right. He had yet to encounter this particular species in any of his previous lives.

A tall, red-skinned bipedal sapient, with eyes of black obsidian. Mana wreathed around this warrior like a furnace, boiling into the air itself, raw power that only a Perfected Mana Heart could produce. On the man’s chest was a small, crystalized necklace.

Others, too, had been brought near Eon, thanks to his attacker’s action, drawing in those nearby to the center of the Dream.

Eon’s awareness took in the entire scene in a fraction of a second, a skill grasped over a thousand years of practice.

7 humans. 5 Void Nobles and a plain servant.

“EON. I'LL. KILL. YOU!” The red-skinned sapient screa-

And then he moved.

'I recognize that langu-'

The impact slammed into Eon’s chest, sending out a small shockwave as he rocketed backwards. Eon felt his ribs fracture, crystal and bone alike splitting as he was blasted away.

And then-

Another impact, smashed down and crushed against the earth. Wheat and stone ruptured as the blow sent out a second shockwave and-

‘He’s-‘

Smash.

‘-too-’

Crash.

‘-fast.’

Guided by instincts and intuition built up over thousands of years, Eon stopped thinking and, instead, acted.

“Do not fear the Reaper,

As Mountains Shake and Rend.”

It didn’t matter that his jaw had shattered, leaving him unable to speak – the Dream worked all the same.

In the background, far away, the mountains that made up the walls of the Dream began to crack. Great streaks of red fractured the sky above as the Dream shook, railing against the constraints of reality.

As he was blown backwards yet again by another powerful impact so quick he was unable to spot it, Eon’s body hardened, his injuries scrambling to heal, as he had once more used 2 more Lines of the Dream to-It didn’t matter.

Blow after blow, shockwave after shockwave, Eon was attacked at a speed that was simply impossible for him to react to. The Dream fought against his injuries, his body gaining the toughness of a mountain, yet what use was strength when he could not fight back?

And so-

Eon flared his Soul.

The pressure slammed down like a meteor as Eon brought the full force of his Soul to bear.

A Soul that had lived through millennia, weathered and aged, built up across lifetime after lifetime.

A tremendous Aura burst out from Eon in that moment, a well of spiritual pressure that sent out a physical shockwave, blasting the air around them.

And, as a result, for just a moment... the attacks stopped.

The wall of spiritual pressure had slammed into Kyvenval, stunning him.

'I will not-' Eon's thoughts were cut off as-

Another impact knocked him back even farther.

Kyvenval was a Speedster - not only did he attack at a tremendous speed...

He also recovered at that same speed.

And then- it happened.

A glacier, a beautiful blue wall of ice, morphed into existence out of nowhere, separating Eon from his attacker in an instant.

A brief respite, yet all the more galling, for…

It came not through his own efforts, but from those around him.

‘Humans.’ His pride dug at him, yet he couldn’t help but be grateful.

His body was a ruin, yet he still clung to life, the Dream rebuilding him with every second he managed to scrape by.

It was an incredible feat, to bring a Perpetual like him to his knees, yet the only emotion Eon felt was overwhelming rage - emotions he controlled, through millennia of practice, and dismissed.

And it was here, as his right eye managed the desperate second it needed to regenerate, that he saw his defenders.

A human boy, not even full grown, holding two blades of red blood.

A human woman, shrouded in ice, pulsating with so much life she was almost blinding to look at.

And…

A man, human, clad in white armor, with a fluttering red cape.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

It all came down to this.

In that moment, as the Dream enveloped him, Micheal felt the rush of power run through him as the Crown of the Angel King filled his body with pure, raw energy. He felt like he could take on a Titan with the-The world around Micheal rapidly began to slow down as he lay witness to the future.

The River of Time throbbed in the background of Micheal’s Soul as he held on to the Realm of Intent, gazing upon the world that was yet to come.

Kyvenval clashing with Eon, at inhuman speeds, moving so fast even in Micheal’s future vision, his form was distorted.

‘This is strange.’ Micheal realized as he gazed farther and farther ahead.

Through some confluence of factors, the Crown and his Gauntlet, the unreality of the Dream, his own Mastery of the Realm of Intent, and his connection to the Brand of Janus, Micheal’s future sight was gazing beyond what it usually could.

From 2 seconds to 3, from 3 to 4, and from 4 to 5.

And then he saw it.

In those 5 seconds.

Vice-Commander Felix Seranno.

Vice-Commander Jessica Wiles.

And…

Aaron Bartram, the White Knight himself.

They put themselves between Kyvenval and Eon.

And it was here that Micheal realized the insidiousness of Jay sol Arget.

‘This is the trap.’ His mind processed thoughts at a speed unimaginable, his Gauntlet glowing unhealthily as he accelerated his connection to the River of Time.

The Round Table didn’t have to act here – they could have abandoned Eon, left him for dead and retreated. Only 2 of their Vice-Commanders were present, Yama unaccounted for, alongside most of their support troops.

But they did act.

Fighting not just for mankind, but for justice.

They were the best of us.

In the future Micheal saw…

He watched Kyvenval tear out Jessica Wiles’ throat.

She began to regenerat- and then, Kyvenval atomized her, dragging his hands across her corpse at super-speed so fast it blurred Micheal’s vision.

In the future he saw…

Felix Serrano’s body glowed crimson, a dozen silver runes appearing on his arms and legs as he moved at a speed even Micheal was unable to match, desperate to rescue Jessi-Kyvenval killed him all the same, his body shattered into pieces like it was made of clay.

In the future he saw…

Aaron Bartram blurred forward, yet even he was too late.

As he embraced what was left of his comrades-

His arms began to turn to crystal.

Micheal’s vision blurred as he made a decision.

4 seconds remained.

He decided to be bold.

‘How do I win?’

A thousand thoughts rose up, plans made and discarded, as he sought the only solution possible.

‘I need to move at his speed.’ It was the only way.

Blood began to drip down from Micheal’s nose as he enthralled himself even deeper within the Realm of Intent, And…

He saw it.

3 seconds.

As deep as his connection was now, to the River of Time…

He saw the warped, terribly warped, stream of Time that propelled Kyvenval forward, the power that gave him such tremendous speed. It was an incomprehensible sight, a shroud of warped Time that defied reason, pulsating from a ring he wore on his right hand.

It was similar to Micheal’s own Time Zones, fields of accelerated time, but wrought to a level Micheal could barely comprehend, no longer a Zone, but rather, a Stream.

2 seconds.

‘I can’t match that but-‘ His Mana Circles could never withstand that burden but-It was an idea borne from desperation.

He didn’t need to match Kyvenval’s accelerated Time distortion – he just needed to connect his Time Zone to Kyvenval's Stream, and then cling on, like a passenger sneaking aboard.

‘If he just stands still…’

The thought struck him and…

As an enormous glacier of ice shot forward, and exactly 0.87 seconds before Kyvenval began his killing spree…

Micheal activated the Scythe of Chains.

‘An Artifact that can ‘chain’ any being in place for 0.5 seconds.’

And…

Like a leech, Micheal latched on to Kyvenval’s Timestream.

.

Chapter 44


.

Wind that was not wind.

Words to describe what Micheal felt came and went as he took a step forward. He tried to store the Scythe of Chains in his Spatial Ring, but found he was unable to activate the Artifact.

All around him, the world stood still.

A huge glacier stretched out, hundreds of meters long. It was a beautiful construct, jagged blue ice spiking upwards at an angle, cut through a field of golden wheat. Small bits of ice broke off from the glacier, hovering still in the air, gleaming with blue light.

Micheal took another step forward. And then another. He dropped the Scythe of Chains, both hands on Lightshorn as he zeroed in.

Another step.

The wind that was not wind blew at him fiercely, like a hurricane, a storm constantly trying to blow him away. It was omnipresent, shackling his every movement, his every motion. He had to fight to move forward, each step a battle in its own right, the wind not only washing over his physical form, but also over his Soul.

His plan, a desperate gambit built off logic and experience, had worked.

Micheal’s Mana Circles burned, working overtime as Micheal felt his connection to the River of Time move at a snail’s pace, sluggish, almost entirely still. The Time Zone he had raised had merged, converging with something far beyond his own control.

To the right of the glacier stood those he had seen in his vision - the Round Table and Eon.

Vice-Commander Felix Seranno was crouched and mid-slide, frozen in motion with his hands splayed out, blood-red eyes ducked behind a few frozen stalks of wheat, hovering in mid-air. His mouth was open in a fierce grin, showcasing two Vampiric teeth, both edged downwards on the left and right side of his teeth.

Vice-Commander Jessica Wiles was mid-jump, just after emerging from the enormous glacier of ice. Her face was a mix of emotions, eyes drawn tight as she twisted, fierce and ready for the fight. Only her torso was fully flesh, her legs still made of the same ice from the glacier she was jumping free of, mid-transformation.

Further to the right was Aaron Bartram himself, the White Knight, clad in his resplendent white armor and red cape.

He hovered, his hands outstretched, floating barely an inch above the ground, putting himself between the glacier and a crumpled figure lying on the ground…

Eon.

In that fragile moment, as time stood still…

‘Divine Scan.’

Micheal activated his Eyes of the Deep, scanning everyone present.

.

.

He was well-rounded, talented, and incredibly dedicated to growing ever stronger, with a powerful High-Vampire Type backing him up.

He skipped over Jessica Wiles’ screen, having already scanned her once before, and moved down to Aaron’s.

.

.

The rest of Aaron’s stats were a result of his reliance on his Conceptual Power, his other Abilities and training, and the fact that Aaron had only recently started cultivating a Mana Breathing Method.

Micheal scanned Eon.

SOUL: SSS- (Growth Rate: Mythical or lower)

MANA: S++ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or higher)

Path Notes: An Ivari Voidling that walks a solitary Path. Extraordinary traces of the Path of the Dream are present.

.

'What?!'

There were no records of what Eon’s stats were, not that Micheal knew of, in the first timeline.

What it revealed now, however, was…

Impossible.

‘An SSS- rated Soul?’ That stat alone almost made Micheal freeze.

That was…

Absurd.

He knew Eon, the King of Heroes, was a legendarily powerful warrior but…

An SSS- stat in Soul should not have been possible.

Micheal stared at the results, his mind processing what he was looking at.

Eon possessed tremendous raw stats, cultivated through countless years of training and effort. He had delved deep into Mana Heart Cultivation, attaining prowess that rivaled Duke Atlas, an incredibly powerful Archmage who had achieved 6 Mana Circles.

His Growth Rates, however…

‘This doesn’t make any sense.’

A Mythical or lower Growth Rate in Soul was a tremendous boon, but the rest of the King of Heroes’ Growth Rates were oddly middling.

‘Even with a Mythical or lower Soul Growth Rate…’

It still didn’t make any sense.

To grow one’s Soul stat was hard.

Had Eon possessed a Legendary Soul Growth Rate, maybe Micheal could’ve rationalized his tremendous Soul stat. Maybe.

But…

He didn’t.

Mythical or lower was certainly a mighty Soul Growth Rate, any Mythical Growth Rating was insane in its own right but-

‘Whatever.’ Micheal cut himself off, refusing to let himself get distracted.

He discarded the thought for now, filing it away as a mystery for another day as he took another step forward and-Micheal resisted the urge to flinch as a small explosion rocked the air, hollowing out a large hole in the enormous glacier of ice.

The explosion itself was oddly stilted, and the chunks of ice that flew free slowing to a crawl before stopping, frozen in the air, as…

Kyvenval, the God-Emperor of Kalos, broke through the glacier.

‘Divine Scan.’

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Kalosian

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: S (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

END: S- (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

REG: B- (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

SOUL: C- (Growth Rate: Common or lower) MANA: S++ (Growth Rate: Heroic or higher)

Path Notes: -

.

‘He has no Path Notes?’ The Kalosian’s Growth Rates were strangely homogeneous, identical across the board, except for Soul.

His Soul stat was oddly low – his physical stats, however, and his Mana, were both tremendous.

The red-skinned Kalosian let out a harsh, disjointed keen as he stumbled forward, smacking a floating shard of ice out of his path. He let out a snarl as he saw the humans in his path and-He began to stalk towards them.

‘Move.’ The thought struck Micheal as he tried to leap forward.

The wind that was not wind, however, slammed against him, hindering his every movement.

‘Is this… Time?’

Micheal’s senses spread outward.

The constant wind, the gale-force that was blowing against him over and over…

As Micheal frantically studied it, fighting forward with every bit of willpower he had, he felt a hint of familiarity.

It was an echo from the River of Time, or at least, the force of that River, trying to reassert itself back to the natural order – the Winds of Time.

The Flow of Time was akin to a universal constant – by natural law, Time would move towards that constant at all times.

Micheal’s current state was unnatural, an aberration of Time that defied reason.

As Micheal managed to lurch several steps forward, his Eyes of the Deep Ability scan touched upon Kyvenval’s ring.

‘His ring is the source!’ The thought spread though his mind like lightning.

Right now, his Time Zone had merged with the stream of Time Kyvenval had raised – a stream because it was incredibly unstable, a Timestream of accelerated Time far beyond what should be possible – and it was all thanks to the Artifact Kyvenval wore on his right hand.

The Twilight Ring – the name of the Artifact came to Micheal intuitively, after he scanned it.

Kyvenval was known to possess multiple Legendary Artifacts, but the source of his speed, the power that let him become a Speedster, was never public knowledge.

With that ring on his hand, Kyvenval was able to shrug off the Winds of Time that sought to slow him, gaining monstrous power.

And now, thanks to that, the Time Zones Micheal had created acted as a shroud, linking up with Kyvenval’s ring, and allowing him to move within Kyvenval’s Timestream. This came at a cost – he no longer had control of his own Time Zones, as they moved at the pace Kyvenval dictated – a fact the God-Emperor, in his rage, failed to notice.

‘Move!’ Micheal’s Life Orbs emerged behind him and instantly began to push him forward. His Life Orbs carried that same shroud, pushing back against the Winds of Time.

Here, in this ultra-accelerated world, it was all he could do to hold on.

Casting a Spell was impossible, his Mana Circles were searing his Soul just by staying in this temporal stream. Likewise, when he tried to draw up some Grandmaster Sword Energy, the response he felt back was incredibly sluggish – it would take what felt like hours for the energy to form. Even the Realm of Intent had stopped functioning, unable to pull up any vision of the future.

‘I don’t have time.’

Micheal focused in and-

The red-skinned Kalosian snarled as he lunged forward, reaching with his left hand for the Glacial Knight’s throat and...

Kyvenval missed.

A pair of Life Orbs shot forward and around, gently nudging Jessica back as she was encompassed, however briefly, by Micheal’s protective shroud, letting him shift her position without killing her.

Kyvenval’s hand missed her throat by an inch, just barely averting the future Micheal had seen, as he pulled her away.

“I’ll. KILL. YOU.”

The Kalosian snarled as he raised his right arm forward and-It collided with Lightshorn.

‘Strong.’

Micheal was currently empowered by the Crown of the Angel King, but here, even after having latched onto Kyvenval’s Timestream, his strength was heavily restricted as the Winds of Time hampered his movements.

So, when Kyvenval’s right arm smashed into Lightshorn as Micheal finally arrived in-person…

Micheal felt his left arm break as the sword went flying, shooting off to the side several meters before rapidly slowing down, and then freezing in mid-air as it escaped Micheal’s influence.

‘I can’t fight that.’ The difference in stats was simply too much.

The God-Emperor screamed something incomprehensible again.

He then punched forward, a right uppercut aimed directly for Micheal’s jaw.

Micheal ducked backwards, using his Life Orbs to further propel himself, just out of the way of the attack, leading Kyvenval away from the vulnerable Round Table members, still frozen in time.

Another punch, another near miss.

‘I can’t keep this up.’ Micheal ignored the pain he felt as a bone in his right shoulder cracked from one of his Life Orbs colliding harshly with it, just barely pulling him out of the way from another massive punch.

Any single blow was enough to pulverize Micheal – Kyvenval, like Micheal, couldn’t activate his other Artifacts, not while he was accelerated so far in Time – but the sheer difference in stats between the two of them gave the Kalosian a huge advantage.

Micheal’s eyes latched on to the Twilight Ring as Kyvenval’s fist slid past him and…

An idea struck.

Another mad punch, a wild lunge, a brutal elbow-turned uppercut.

Every impact he dodged, every near miss he forced through battered at his body – if he used a Life Orb to heal, he risked interrupting his connection with the Crown of the Angel King, the only thing remotely keeping him in the fight right now.

‘Not yet…’ Micheal thought as he continued to dodge, his eyes practically spinning as he identified Kyvenval’s fighting style.

Even lost to anger as he currently was, the God-Emperor fought in a clear, regimented hand-to-hand style, clearly well trained and disciplined. His punches were hard, aimed at vital locations and difficult to dodge.

‘There!’ Finally, he found his moment.

The God-Emperor stepped back ever so slightly, telegraphing a powerful blow to the chest he’d tried several times before.

He punched forward and…

Micheal didn’t dodge this time, his hands trembling as he instead latched on, grabbing Kyvenval’s arm.

Like a wrecking ball, Kyvenval punched a hole straight through the left side of Micheal’s chest.

The impact was brutal, accompanied by a crushing wave of pain that slammed into Micheal's mind and tried to force him into shock.

In a single blow, Micheal felt his heart, his left lung, several ribs, and part of his spine vanish, obliterated in a single attack. The God-Emperor’s strength was monstrous, an unstoppable attack that blew away anything in its path.

And… in that same moment…

Micheal grinned, his smile a bloody rictus.

‘Got you.’

A Life Orb shattered.

There were rules, Kim Jiwoon had taught him, when it came to copying your injuries and sharing them with your opponent.

The first rule: the injuries you copied couldn’t be caused by yourself.

Kim Jiwoon didn’t have an explanation for why this was the case – it was simply a function of how the Ability worked – it couldn’t copy injuries that were self-inflicted, the Ability somehow able to filter through what was and what wasn’t through means unknown – with less complex injuries having a higher transfer rate. A broken bone was far easier to transfer compared to a missing body part.

Pain rocked Micheal’s mind, a familiar companion he’d felt all too often these days, as he felt his connection to his Raidon Gauntlet begin to sever, his shattered spine losing control of his arms.

While Micheal couldn’t cause the injuries himself…

There was nothing to stop him from using injuries inflicted upon him by others.

In that moment, just before his connection to the River of Time began to waver…

‘Wound Transmission.’

Micheal copied his shattered spine, and shared it with Kyvenval.

And herein lied the second rule.

Kyvenval’s head twitched as his body trembled, a powerful force slamming into it.

The injuries shared via Wound Transmission weren’t necessarily permanent.

It was a matter of willpower.

The Life Energy imbued within the Life Orb was imbued into whomever you targeted – that Life Energy was used to recreate the wounds Micheal currently had, reflected in a similar manner to his target depending on their physiology…

And that same energy could be usurped, repurposed, and used to revert those copied injuries – once the Life Energy left Micheal’s Life Orb, it came down to a matter of will.

Micheal’s will of iron slammed into Kyvenval’s wall of rage and…

He cut through it.

For a brief moment, the technique took root.

Kyvenval’s spine fractured.

The God-Emperor of Kalos froze, his head twitching, as he lost control of his arms and legs.

Almost instantly, the God-Emperor’s rage fought back, the willpower of an Emperor crushing Micheal’s own line of will and expelling it from his body. It was natural, after all – in your own body, one’s own will was inherently stronger, the advantage of the defender, and this attack wasn't a true clash of wills - it was only a fraction of Micheal's intent, a quick, violent jab instead of a sustained clash.

As Kyvenval regained control, the Life Energy from the shattered Life Orb shifted, beginning to heal the injuries it had inflicted.

However, in that brief window of time Micheal had managed to scrounge up…

Kyvenval’s connection to the Twilight Ring was severed.

The world around Micheal abruptly shifted, the Winds of Time finally blowing over him as reality asserted itself and…

The Flow of Time returned to normal.

A thousand things seemed to happen all at once.

Screams, flashes of energy, fields of wheat and a sky that was falling.

Micheal ignored it all, however, as he felt the energy boost from the Crown of the Angel King begin to flee from him, his body quite literally failing as his head tilted to the side…

And it was here, as his body began to slump, that Micheal pulled a trick he’d seen someone else do before.

He stared down Kyenval’s crowned head and…

He shut his right eye.

The eyelid went from wide open… to swinging down shut in an instant…

A motion that qualified as a ‘swing.’

And in that motion…

A small line of white Grandmaster Sword Energy shot forth.

That energy shredded his eyelid as it emerged, blinding him in that eye, but it rocketed forward all the same and…

Kyvenval was caught unprepared.

A blade of light cut forth and…

Micheal decapitated the God-Emperor of Kalos.

.
