Chapter 45


.

Felix Serrano blinked, his instincts screaming at him as the world shifted.

It’d been nearly 4 years, just a few months shy, since he had given up part of his humanity.

All around him, he felt the world in blood.

He sensed the blood flowing in Eon’s bedraggled form, slowly regenerating a half dozen meters behind him. He knew Jessica was 1.4 meters on his right, jumping free from her glacier, by the blood flowing through her upper half. He felt Aaron’s presence, exactly 3.6 meters behind him at an angle, his right hand raised with his palm out, hovering in front of Eon. He sensed several Void Nobles and someone else off in a clump, two members of the Round Table’s Forward Support Team roughly 18.6 and 14.2 meters to his right, the Seer, Micheal, 11.3 meters to his left, and…

Kyvenval, on the other side of this glacier, standing still for a brief moment. 9.8 meters.

He called this power his ‘Blood Sense.’

It wasn’t an Ability, but rather, an aspect of his type – a High Vampire.

All living beings possessed blood, of some kind, and because of that…

Nothing with blood could escape his senses.

And that was why…

His instincts screamed at him, as two of those sources moved, at such speed he was incapable of noticing.

In one moment, he was preparing himself to intercept their attacker, the alien God-Emperor of Kalos.

In the next…

The Seer who had reshaped the Round Table’s future, Micheal, appeared in front of them, his body slumping in the hands of-

A flash of white-

And Kyvenval, the powerful enemy they had prepared so much for, fell to the ground with a thump, his head tumbling free from his body as he collapsed on the ground.

Dead.

The Beast inside him screamed at him to attack, the pride of a High Vampire roaring at him to humble those not of his Brood, for daring to stand in his way.

Felix forced the Beast down, maintaining his Blood Blades as he slowly stood up. Behind him, he sensed Jessica spin around, her fists raised before freezing up, stunned by Micheal’s arrival.

Felix’s eyes flickered to the left and right. He didn’t let himself freeze. He was on a hair-trigger, right now, ready to cut down anything that even remotely seemed like a threat to his new family. As one of the strongest members of the Round Table, he took this responsibility extremely seriously.

While he might not be related to them by blood, the Round Table was his home, and he would defend them till the bitter end.

After a moment, however, he slowly relented – the threat was contained. Or, well, this part of the threat was contained – the schemer behind this was still at large.

His eyes narrowed as he studied Micheal, briefly, before giving him a slight nod.

‘This guy’s alright.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

.

—-Points Notification—-

Points Obtained: 376,204

.

Clarity settled into Micheal’s mind as he blinked, healing energy restoring his body to its peak condition.

‘That’s 2 down.’ He kept the Crown of the Angel King on his head, ready to activate it again at a moment’s notice - his usage of the Artifact had been relatively brief, leaving it with enough power to activate again.

4 blue Life Orbs resonated, floating into existence before reabsorbing back within his Soul - his remaining Life Orb count.

“Well. Good job.“ Felix Serrano commented after standing up, two blood-red swords in hand, as he gave Micheal a small nod.

“Mike what-“ Jessica began, but was interrupted as,

“He’s dead.” Micheal cut her off as he dashed off to the side, Ki-enhanced muscles flexing as he slid down on to one knee.

With a grunt, he stood back up, picking up Lightshorn from where it’d been blown away in one smooth motion.

Whatever Jessica was going to reply with was cut off again as the two other members of the Round Table, from one of their support teams, ran forward and knelt down near Eon. The nearby Void Nobles, all guests invited by Duke Atlas, looked around in confusion, while a servant broke off and began to walk towards Kyvenval’s dead body.

“On me, Knights.” Aaron’s voice cut through the air, a commanding presence that immediately took control of the scene. The air around Aaron trembled as a series of yellow energy shields sprung into existence, a Defensive Artifact activating to shield not Aaron, but Eon’s downed figure behind him.

Micheal held back a wince as he tried to cast a Spell, a minor telekinesis Spell that would pick up the Scythe of Chains and bring it to him. His Mana Circles burned as he cancelled the action – his merger with Kyvenval’s Timestream had overworked his Circles, to the point where his Soul itself felt tender.

Instead, he moved, in a half-sprint, half-leap, and picked it up like a normal person, storing it in his now functioning Spatial Ring. He also stored his Raidon Gauntlet, the Artifact useless to him while his Soul was in its current state.

By the time he returned to the God-Emperor’s corpse, Aaron had managed to prop Eon up – the King of Heroes was a sorry sight, half his body turned to a strange, white-ish almost translucent crystal, and the other half coated in blood, his clothes mostly ruined.

‘Better safe than sorry.’ After rearming himself, Micheal knelt down next to Kyvenval’s corpse, placing his hand on the dead God-Emperor’s chest and-

He stored it, and everything on the God-Emperor’s headless body, inside his Spatial Ring.

Now, all that was left was…

Micheal paused, flicking away a stalk of wheat that was poking his leg.

He was forgetting something.

‘What?’ Something was strange-

He didn’t think.

He acted.

Just like he’d been doing this entire time, ever since he arrived on the Third Layer, met Vesper, and learned that Jay sol Arget was hunting him inside a Time Loop.

A bag of flour exploded in his hands, dusting the world around him in a cloud of white.

This was the 13th time he’d done this.

Four times on the premises of Castle Atlas, five while traversing Axellion in public, two times while visiting the Round Table, once while he was leaving the Inner Seas Mages Association.

The flour rushed out into the air in a massive wave, coating everything within several meters of Micheal in a layer of white.

It was the best countermeasure he could drum up, to scan his immediate area, and confirm whether or not an Endwalker was within his presence.

Was it stressful, maintaining his guard at all times, all hours, always keeping a mental line ready to throw and explode a pouch of flour?

Yes, yes it was.

The previous 12 times he’d thrown out flour had all shown to be false alarms. Paranoia that crept up on him, seeing things in shadows that weren’t there, movements in the dark that turned out to be nothing.

A normal person might be embarrassed by the scene he caused, over and over, to the point where even Vesper’s servants were giving him odd looks.

But Micheal knew he was in a Time Loop.

And that changed things.

‘Either always be on guard or…’

‘Die.’

Those were his options.

The concept of embarrassment didn’t even cross his mind at this point.

And it was thanks to this…

As the cloud of white flour spread out, the fine particles staining the air as they shifted through the stalks of wheat, coating part of the icy wall of the glacier that Jessica had raised in a white film and-

A humanoid shaped gap appeared, a shape of a figure holding something, vaguely like a bowling ball, where there was no flour.

The actual gap itself was completely unremarkable, with nothing of interest or note. Just a pale man holding a head, nothing out of the ordinary.

It was this absence of flour around it, however, that drew Micheal’s attention.

And it was here that he attacked.

Lightshorn cut forward in an instant, the Realm of Intent settling upon Micheal’s shoulders despite his Soul’s protests as a slice of Grandmaster Sword Energy shredded the air.

And Micheal blinked, again, as Kyvenval’s head flopped on the ground, appearing out of nowhere, accompanied by…

A fleshy, pale hand.

“He’s here!” Micheal shouted, adrenaline spiking as he activated the Crown of the Angel King for a second time, once more filling his body with a rush of raw power. The Artifact burned on his skull, the rush of energy from activating it twice in quick succession threatening to give him a blinding headache.

And it was here, as Micheal prepared to rush forward…

Shin teleported into existence right next to Micheal.

A decade of life spent climbing the Layers with Shin was the only reason why Micheal didn’t lash out at the abrupt interruption, as high-strung as he currently was, instinctively recognizing his best friend.

Shin grabbed Micheal’s arm, the duo communicating without speaking and-

Reality shifted as Micheal and Shin teleported into the Background.

The world was strange. Colors appeared less vibrant, faded, the air heavier, and the wind-

It whistled, ominously, oddly, a faint, keening cry echoing in the air.

“Shin-“ Micheal began, but was interrupted immediately.

“He’s a Clone!” Shin yelled out loud.

Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he zeroed in on the pale figure that had appeared, about half a dozen meters away, right in front of him. The pale humanoid was crouched down, its left now-handless stump clutched to its chest, while its right hand rested atop Kyvenval’s decapitated head.

“We’re in the Background right now, a weird space that is also reality, but slightly behind it at the same time, occupying both spaces at once. It’s where Endwalkers exist and why we can’t focus on them.” Shin’s mouth moved at a thousand miles a second as he explained,

“We’re on Loop number 14,784, not 74! He says this is all a distraction!” Shin went on, explaining everything he’d learned.

‘A Clone?’ Micheal parsed through to the most relevant information instantly and-

He activated his Eyes of the Deep to scan the pale figure.

His Ability failed.

“Wait!” Shin’s grip tightened on Micheal’s shoulder, stopping him from dashing forward.

“The only thing keeping you here in the Background is me. If you let go of me, you’ll immediately drop down back to normal reality.” Shin panted as he finished speaking, his eyes taut.

Slowly, while Shin was speaking, the pale figure had stood back up, raising Kyvenval’s head and admiring it with his remaining hand.

Then…

Jay sol Arget frowned as he lowered the God-Emperor’s head and met Micheal’s gaze.

“Micheal. How… unpleasant it is, to see you again.”

Micheal discarded impulsive emotions like anger or rage as a strange sense of serenity swept over him.

“Jay sol Arget.” He returned, his voice placid and calm.

Finally, he had found the architect of all this misery.

As Micheal studied the Endwalker, he zeroed in on the flakes of light that were drifting off the creature’s body. Just like Shin had said, bits of the Endwalker were slowly drifting away. His Divine Scan failing had confirmed it.

This wasn’t Jay sol Arget’s main body – this was a Clone.

“You know, it took me nearly 300 Loops to figure out the proper way to energize this thing, and make use of these dreadful eyes.” The Titled Deity’s frown eased as it hoisted up Kyvenval’s head once again, motioning with it casually.

Micheal tensed, keeping one hand on Shin’s arm. He kept the Realm of Intent open, giving himself forewarning for anything Jay sol Arget tried to pull.

“Be ready to teleport near him.” He hissed, his eyes never leaving Kyvenval's head.

The Endwalker chuckled.

“Oh, you needn't be so dramatic.”

In an almost too casual motion, the Titled Deity threw the head of the God Emperor to the side, sending it rolling across several flattened stalks of wheat.

“It never worked out in my favor, unfortunately. Hmm.” Jay sol Arget’s Clone shook his head as he glared at Micheal.

“I don’t think I’ll talk to-“

A massive spear of blood obliterated the Endwalker where he stood, his body splattering into pieces as it rocketed past, powerful red Blood Energy sizzling through the air. A gust of wind followed the spear, whipping past them and setting the air to a gale.

Micheal’s head jerked to the side, his eyes locking on to the attacker.

There, Felix Serrano stood, silver runes glowing up and down his body as several spears of Blood Energy hovered, floating in the air next to him.

"I felt- Kyvenval's blood reappear..." Felix muttered, just barely audible.

“Shin, take us out!” Micheal spoke over him.

Shin didn’t need any more encouragement, warping them both back to regular reality.

“Micheal! Shin!” Jessica Wiles appeared in an instant, a trail of ice coalesced behind her. The Vice-Commander had her arms raised, half formed with ice as she stalked forward.

“Are you alright?! You two vanished!”

“We’re fine.” Micheal answered as he slowly lowered his sword.

“All good here!” Shin yelled slightly too loudly, his breathing hard as he looked around.

The group of Void Nobles had stumbled back in a panic, their numbers swelling as more denizens in the Dream had gathered in their vicinity. Several more Knights of the Round Table were even now rushing forward, forming a defensive perimeter at Aaron’s location. A loud din of voices echoed as Nobles, Knights, and humans all spoke, some asking questions, some giving orders, and some yelling demands.

The sky above them shook again, the world of the Dream set to trembling.

“We need to-“ Before Micheal could finish speaking, he was interrupted.

“Wait!” A voice cut through the chaos as Micheal knelt down, storing Kyvenval's head in his Spatial Ring.

Eon, the King of Heroes, had shakily gotten to his feet.

Aaron Bartram stood next to him, right hand still raised, now holding a small, metal orb.

Micheal met gazes with the White Knight. The Commander of the Round Table gave him a grateful nod.

“I can feel the world shifting, outside the Dream.” Eon’s voice rasped, his bloodshot eye twitching as he looked towards the red sky.

“Something… something terrible has happened.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

All across the Third Layer, a change had overtaken the Shattered Plane, spreading from the center of the Empty Sea.

From the City-State of Ibrasia to the Northeast, to the Red Line of the Northwest, to the Lektplor Collective to the Southeast, to the City State of Axellion in the Southwest.

From every floating island that circled the Empty Sea, from the farthest reaches of the Outering Ringlands to the closest isles of the Inner Ring.

For a brief moment in time, every single island seemed to shudder as they floated above the yawning Void, an invisible wave of energy sweeping through them all in an instant.

And then that wave was gone, and…

The world stood still.

The moment passed.

And…

Slowly, inch-by-inch…

Every single floating island across the Third Layer began to sink, falling towards the dark, endless Void.

.

Chapter 46


.

“The Dream is collapsing.”

Eon’s words rasped out of his throat as the world around them shuddered.

The sky was a deep, dark red, full of black cracks and lines that twisted ominously. In the background, the distant mountains had shifted into volcanoes, spewing up magma and smoke, in a cacophony of destruction. The fields of wheat they were in still stood, but the ground beneath them had set to trembling.

“Steady, everyone. I’ll pull you out.” Eon continued as a flash of golden light swarmed over everyone and…

Reality shifted, and the Dream fell away.

A bevy of screams welcomed them back to the real world as they returned to the Inner Pavilion.

Gravity had returned to normal, but Axellion looked far, far different than it had before.

“Woah.” Shin muttered, letting go of Micheal’s arm as they landed on the ground.

Micheal sent two Life Orbs out, letting them emerge beneath his feet. He balanced on them as he floated up into the air, aiming to get a better vantage point.

From the center of the Inner Pavillion that had hosted the Founding Celebration, stretching out across the Outer Pavillion, and into Axellion proper, an entire section of reality had… changed.

Thousands of transformed Void Natives stood frozen in the now-crystallized section of the Outer Pavillion, halted in motion, sealed to a now crystalized ground. Further beyond them, outside the Pavilions, to the homes and shops, businesses and streets alike, anything within that line of sight, covering roughly 12% of Axellion, all the way to the outer walls, had been transformed.

The Founding Celebration had taken place at the exact dead center of Axellion – it was as if someone had cut the City-State into 8 slices, like a pizza, and then taken one of those slices, and turned everything caught in Kyvenval's gaze, every person, every building, every rock and every stone, into solid crystal, penetrating at least a foot thick.

‘Brutal.’ Micheal held back a wince.

It was a reminder, a keen, damning reminder, of how insanely dangerous the higher Layers became, as humanity ran into beings of great power.

In a single haphazard glance, Kyvenval had massacred tens of thousands of innocent Void Natives.

As Micheal processed this, Shin floated up quietly next to him, relying on his Neo-Levitation Bracers.

All around them, everyone that had been in the Dream also reappeared, Void Nobles and Humans alike. Micheal spotted the Commander of Rosare Knight Company, Verbon Atlas, helping a bloodied Duke Atlas to his feet. Aaron and the Round Table Knights were regrouping off to his right, while other Void Noble dignitaries and guests gathered in a large group in front of them.

“Ves didn’t make it. The Clone killed her.” Shin’s voice was thick as Micheal spun around, his attention drawn to something behind them.

“I stored her body in my Spatial Ring, but…” Shin shook his head, his eyes bloodshot. Micheal rested an arm on his shoulder, half-distracted, for…

A loud roar shook the air, making Shin spin around to see what had caught Micheal’s eye, interrupting the moment.

‘The Apexes!’

Micheal’s body was still flush with energy from his second use of the Crown of the Angel King – energy that, he noticed, had the side-effect of soothing the strain his Soul was under, cooling off his overheated Mana Circles.

The Apex Void Predators were rampaging-

Or, rather, they were trying to.

Shin’s jaw dropped as he watched an enormous 9-meters tall Tyrannosaurus Rex clamp its jaws around the shoulder of a huge Apex Void Predator and…

The dinosaur ripped a massive bite out of the Void Predator’s shoulder, in one glorious mad rush. Huge chunks of blood and gore spattered into the air as the massive creatures clashed, right beside a pair of twisting tornadoes, made up of burning red flames.

“That’s Hasoth.” Micheal named the Apex Void Predator, Hasoth the Firebringer, recognizing it instantly by its tell-tale flames. The huge monster was standing on the edge of the Outer Pavillion, several hundred meters away.

‘And is that Baron Rex?!’ The enormous dinosaur kicked its huge legs against the chest of the towering Apex, sending it stumbling down, crashing against the small outer wall that separated the Outer Pavillion from Axellion proper.

Hasoth, the Apex, was an enormous, hulking creature, roughly 34 meters tall, that had a large orange streak staining its hardened black outer skin – this Apex Void Predator was infamous on the Third Layer for its ability to create massive storms of fire, and vanish into those flames, granting it a sort of pseudo-teleportation ability.

“Kill it dead, lads! I’ve got it Spatial-Locked!” Micheal’s enhanced senses caught a distant, distinctly-British voice shout as he watched a swarm of figures rush forward, accompanied by dozens of streaks of black energy slamming into the Apex. Huge, glowing black chains appeared out of thin air, locking down the Apex Void Predator’s legs and tail.

The speaker was standing atop one of the pillars set near the edge of the Outer Pavillion, dressed in a fine black suit. They had on a fine black dark gray suit and tie, with a black vest and white shirt, and a set of fine black pants and black shoes. In their hands was an extravagant black cane, which they held at an angle, pointing at the Apex.

“Century Curse.” The figure’s voice echoed out.

A thousand huge black nails were wrought into existence, each nail around a meter long, surrounding the downed Apex Void Predator. A split second later, those nails shot forward, sinking into the flesh of the Apex at a breakneck speed, causing the creature to roar out sorrowfully as it writhed, its movements gradually slowing down.

“And that’s… Hayden Montacerry.” Micheal’s eyes narrowed.

Hayden Montacerry, Leader of the Revolutionaries, a powerful organization of humans operating on the Third Layer, and…

One of Constantine Lancaster’s Seeds.

The famous Curse Magician, whose prowess when it came to casting and manipulating Curses was well known in the first timeline.

‘So Constantine did decide to help out.’ The Revolutionaries, in the first timeline, were believed to have killed off several of the final 8 Apex Void Predators that haunted the Third Layer – they were some of the foremost experts when it came to hunting down the massive creatures.

Hasoth groaned, the Apex struggling against its chains as numerous cloaked figures spread out on top of its downed formed, stabbing dark black swords into its skin. The massive creature’s movements slowed even further, before falling completely still.

Micheal’s attention, however, was caught by the figures standing next to the pillar Hayden Montacerry was standing on.

‘Kim Jiwoon… and Jabari?!’ A good two dozen humans had setup a series of contraptions, large metal objects that reminded Micheal of what the first computers looked like, big metal boxes with tubes, levers, and bars all over. Several of these humans were dressed in white labcoats that were lined with Magic Glyphs, one of the more commonly worn outfits used by the scientists of Dark Void. A Void Noble was also present, speaking with one of the humans holding a clipboard, alongside… a floating red spirit? What?

‘Why is Dark Void working with Constantine? And is that… Allmaster arguing with them?!’

For the first time in a while, Micheal felt like he was out of the loop.

Micheal’s thoughts were interrupted, however, as-

“Vector: Lightspeed.”

The world was bathed in light.

Every corner of the Inner Pavillion, from the writhing Apex to the stone pillars, to the wall and building of Axellion in the distance, for a split second, everything in sight was highlighted in brilliant, golden light.

An eerie, high-pitched whine echoed and-

Micheal watched as Ryben, the Slaughterer, a huge, 31-meters-tall Apex Void Predator, was annihilated in a single blow.

The shockwave swept past them a moment later, setting off a storm of wind as what was left of the enormous creature collapsed, a massive gaping hole where its chest, arms, and everything above its knees used to be. The second Apex Void Predator was around 300 meters to the west of the first, with what remained of its legs sealed up in a huge mound of molten magma.

Aaron Bartram soared up into the air, his eyes glowing as several metal orbs rotated around his right hand.

Vice-Commander Yama, and several of the Knights of the Round Table, were backing away from the dead Apex, alongside one of the visiting Heroes, Kyrog – the Hero of Thunder. A platoon of Knights from Duke Atlas’ Rosare Company was also backing off, having joined in the group defense effort.

“Holy tahito.” Shin stared, and Micheal couldn’t really blame him. The sheer display of power was breathtaking.

Just like that, in a massive show of force, both Apex Void Predators had been handled.

“Shin, take us over there.” Micheal interjected, grabbing Shin’s arm and pointing at the gathering of Dark Void scientists.

“On it.” Shin replied as reality shifted.

“-readings are catastrophic, we’re looking at an Apocalypse level event!“ One of the scientists, a tan man with dark brown hair, argued loudly while pointing at the readings on the screen.

“Do you think I don’t know that, Human?! Why do you think I’m here?!” Allmaster’s words cut through the air, harsh and grating.

Allmaster was a tall Void Noble, lean and fit, with black hair and dark gray eyes. He had swapped out his formal outfit he’d worn for the Founding Celebration with a custom-made set of dark metal armor that clung to his skin like it had been shaped around him, engraved with several glowing green gems.

The Many-Faced Hero’s eyes were glowing bright red as he continued to speak, gesturing wildly. Allmaster had the ability to obtain temporary Mastery in dozens of separate Conceptual Powers, although only one at a time – this granted the Hero incredible versatility, letting him use his powers for all aspects of his life.

‘Allmaster famously hates all Foreigners – the fact that he’s cooperating with Dark Void scientists…’ It was an incredibly foreboding sign.

Micheal and Shin’s arrival didn’t go unnoticed. Several of the scientists looked up, glancing at them, before immediately looking back at their Artifact-machine hybrids. A pair of cloaked figures shifted their attention to the pair, hands going to the hilts of sheathed swords.

The rising tension was immediately dismissed, however, as Kim Jiwoon stepped forward, leaving a conversation he was having with Jabari.

“Micheal. It’s good to see you’re still kicking.” Kim Jiwoon greeted them.

“Where’s the Emperor?” Kim Jiwoon added as he looked past them, his eyes alert.

“Kyvenval is dead. What’s going on?” Micheal returned, immediately cutting to the chase.

“Already? That’s great news. And, it’s bad – like, bad, bad.” Kim Jiwoon shook his head, motioning towards the scientists arguing behind him.

Micheal took a step forward, listening in.

“…the defining gravity line that assisted all of this Plane’s floating islands in staying above the Void has been destabilized – this is a qualitative destabilization on a planetary level, the entire gravitational plane has been contrashifted down…”

The speaker, and person in charge of Dark Void’s side, wasn’t one of the scientists, but rather, the floating red spirit he had seen in the distance – a projection of some sort. Micheal’s eyes widened, however, as he recognized the voice, heard in some of Dark Void’s earliest recordings.

‘Marco Barone!’ The leader of Dark Void himself was talking, somehow, through a projection cast across space.

“What kind of countermeasures can be raised?! The Seeker says the answers I need can be found here!” Allmaster interjected, referencing the esoteric Conceptual Power of ‘The Seeker’ – one Micheal knew little about, beyond what its namesake implied.

“It’s impossible. Even here in the north, Ibari is dropping rapidly towards the Demarcation Line.” Marco’s small red spirit projection was shaped in an almost chibi-like form, of a miniature human, floating in the air – one that was also multi-tasking incredibly well, holding a conversation with Allmaster while giving orders to the Dark Void scientists.

“We think there must have been some kind of attack on the central Nexus at the center of the Empty Sea – through some sort of ongoing, reality-warping energy field, because otherwise, the force necessary should be impossible for any individual or even group to muster.” Marco continued, his voice flat.

The implications of what Marco was saying hit Micheal like a truck.

‘The Third Layer is sinking?’ Shock tried to settle into Micheal’s psyche as he processed what he’d heard.

Jay sol Arget. This was his doing.

‘He’s cutting off mankind’s access to the Third.’ Micheal blinked as the realization settled within him, his mind racing.

Without the floating islands to appear on, anyone who entered the Third Layer would spawn falling into the Void and…

No one who entered the Void was ever seen again.

‘He’s dying, and now he’s taking the entire Layer with him.’ The thought was horrifying.

‘Because of us. Because of the changes I made to the timeline.’ Micheal’s heart plummeted.

The information Shin had shared with him clicked into place, and, finally, Micheal saw the full picture.

Because of his interference, Jay sol Arget must have found that, no matter how many times he Looped, he was unable to complete all of his objectives in the same Loop.

The flap of a butterfly’s wings, altering the course of history and time.

Micheal had inadvertently forced Jay sol Arget to seek out an alternative method.

Something only a Titled Deity could do.

If he couldn’t wipe out the targets he needed dead… then why not cut off humanity’s access to the higher Layers as a whole, preventing any more of them from climbing up the Layers?

This would effectively neuter the threat humanity presented to his species, resolving Jay sol Arget’s mission.

Yet, in doing so, his actions would actively genocide not just the Void Natives, but also every other race that tried to connect to this Layer – a genocide of cosmic proportions…

But that was clearly an acceptable cost in the Titled Deity’s eyes.

Allmaster gnashed his teeth as he heard the Dark Void’s leader reply, before abruptly jerking to a halt. The Many-Faced Hero’s eyes glowed slightly brighter as he then spun around, his gaze locking onto Shin.

“You!” The Hero stepped forward, using an odd technique that let him cross the distance in an instant, attempting to get in Shin’s face.

“Back down.” Micheal’s voice was dead calm as he put himself in-between them.

Allmaster sneered and, a moment later, smirked as a huge torrent of energy flowed around him, unleashing a crushing wave of pressure that tried to force Micheal away.

Micheal didn’t flinch.

“You know something – something relevant.” Allmaster’s gaze took on an irritated gleam as he ignored Micheal, gesturing past him towards Shin.

“You interacted with the one responsible for this?” Allmaster sounded less sure of himself as he finished speaking – clearly, whatever Conceptual Power he was relying on for information wasn’t omniscient.

Micheal turned back to look at Shin, giving him a slight nod.

“Ye-yeah.” Shin stuttered slightly, before taking a deep breath, his back straightening as he continued,

“I talked to him, Jay sol Arget. To one of his Clones. He said, he said this was all a distraction.”

Shin began to relay everything he had been told by Jay sol Arget inside Eon’s Dream, from the true number of Loops that had occurred, to the fact that Jay sol Arget had been spying on them at all times up to this point, ensuring this was the perfect, final Loop.

“A distraction, the final Loop. Of course, it all makes sense…” Marco’s chibi form crossed his legs as he floated in the air, one hand tapping his chin as he thought intensely. Behind him, the scientists moved in a flurry, moving from one pseudo-machine-Artifact to another.

“What can we do to stop it?” Micheal interjected.

“Stop the sinking?” Marco’s spirit glanced at Micheal before shaking his head dismissively,

“It’s already too late. Unravelling the energy-field that’s corrupted the Nexus is possible, but it would take at least 1 hour and 31 minutes… and the Third Layer only has 21 minutes and 41 seconds left, before it sinks into the Void.” Marco’s voice was curt, undercut by a thin layer of barely suppressed rage, not directed at Micheal, but at the situation in general.

“We’ve run out of time.” The leader of Dark Void ignored Micheal as he continued, barking out commands to the scientists.

Micheal rocked back on his heels.

‘We can’t stop it?’ Those words struck him like a physical blow.

That meant humanity was doomed, destined to face a future full of death and ruin.

For a split second, dread threatened to overwhelm Micheal as a sense of hopelessness tried to crash down upon him.

However…

‘No.’

Micheal refused to give up.

‘Think.’

There had to be a way.

‘Time.’ Marco said they were out of time?

Micheal felt a sense of déjà vu as his mind raced, latching on to the only solution he could think of.

“Time. You said we need time.” Micheal tapped on his Spatial Ring.

Kyvenval’s headless corpse appeared, landing on the ground with a thud. Allmaster stepped away with a grimace as the body appeared, frowning fiercely.

Micheal’s hands moved in a blur as he reached down and ripped off two rings from Kyvenval’s hands – one that was a Spatial Ring he stored away, and the other…

“This is the Twilight Ring, an Artifact of great power that can interfere with Time.”

Marco’s chibi spirit had frozen in place the moment Micheal brought the corpse out, his eyes latching onto the ring.

The red spirit transformed into a blur as it snatched the ring out of Micheal’s hands, his chibi-spirit form holding the ring carefully with two hands.

“I’ve formed a connection to the Conceptual Power of Time, and we’re still trapped inside a Time Loop.” Micheal began, but stopped as the chibi spirit held up a hand, cutting him off.

“You want to leech onto the already established Loop structure, utilizing this Artifact and your connection to Time as a bridge, and use that to Loop backwards in Time, to preempt this?” Marco immediately guessed the plan Micheal had come up with.

“I can’t even begin to calculate how to set that up.” Micheal said slowly, his heart pounding,

“But you can.”

Standing before him was the best and brightest mankind had to offer, the greatest minds and thinkers of the entire human race, gathered together as one.

Dark Void.

Marco’s chibi form sat, frozen in the air as he thought intensively. The spirit’s hands flickered, his eyes twitching as several tense seconds passed.

“… it’s impossible. Even if we can calculate a way to latch on to the temporal structure, we don’t have primary control over the Loop - the journey back would rip your body to shreds.” Marco shook his head.

“I’m a Life Orb Master. I’ve survived worse.” Micheal raised a pair of Life Orbs up into the air.

Marco froze again, his spirit form once more calculating things at a rate Micheal couldn’t even fathom. It was incredible, in its own way, witnessing one of mankind’s greatest minds at work. As the seconds ticked past, Marco called over one of Dark Void’s scientists, ordering him to use an Ability to scan the Artifact.

Meanwhile, in the distance, Micheal saw Duke Atlas rise up into the air. Several huge Magic Circles appeared, floating in the air as the Duke began to cast several Gravity Spells, magic energy sinking into Axellion’s main island as he sought to stem its fall. Aaron Bartram flew over next to Dark Void’s scientists, descending down as he listened in and learned the bad news. Several of the cloaked Revolutionaries had also begun to return, including a grinning Baron Rex, who, for some reason, gave Shin a thumbs up.

Eon, wrapped in a strange, golden Aura, also arrived, his crippled form hovering ominously as he listened to the tirades that Dark Void’s scientists made.

Finally, the red spirit spoke.

“It’s not enough.”

Micheal frowned.

“We can use this to rig up a rudimentary temporal springboard, at the cost of shattering the Artifact, to create an outburst in Time – and this might let us latch on to the Loop’s structure but…” Marco shook his head,

“It’s close, but we need something more controlled, something to direct this force, to consign it in Time. Otherwise, the numbers won’t add up.”

Micheal’s mind raced as his head jerked to his left.

“Eon.” Micheal kept his voice as respectful as he could manage as he nodded towards the now-malformed Void Noble.

“Do you still possess the Spear of Time?” Micheal asked, his voice hoarse.

The King of Heroes gave him an odd look before replying,

“All of my treasures were destroyed, turned to crystal by this vermin.” Eon rasped as he coughed, stooping forward as if to kick Kyvenval’s corpse. He stopped, however, before completing the motion – the strange golden Aura that was wrapped around him keeping him separated from reality.

“However…” Eon shook his head,

“That doesn’t matter, because the Spear of Time was stolen from me last night.”

Eon unveiled a devastating revelation.

“So that’s why he looked so angry back at the feast…” Shin’s voice was a faint whisper Micheal just barely heard.

“It’s fortunate, in its own way.” The crippled King of Heroes let out a bloody laugh as he spat out a few shards of crystal.

“Had I still possessed it, it would’ve been turned to crystal and destroyed in the attack.”

‘It was stolen?!’ Micheal’s head snapped away, looking from face to face as he tried to find a way out, a way forward, a path for humanity to survive.

“It doesn’t matter.” Marco’s voice was cold, logic dictating the hard facts as he faced the reality of the situation.

“What’s happened, happened. If we had figured out a way to jump back, the changes would’ve already occurred – if this is the Final Loop, there should’ve been traces of that interference. Without a way to direct the jump, any attempt is meaningless.” The red chibi shook its head.

Meanwhile, Dark Void continued to work, away at their machines. Seconds slipped by as time ticked forward, the world marching on, uncaring.

‘Think.’ How could humanity still survive?

‘What’s happened, happened.’ Marco’s words settled strangely into Micheal’s gut.

“He did look red like a tomato, didn’t he, eh?” Rex’s voice was painfully cheerful, smiling obliviously as he walked up next to Shin.

“Saw the work you did with that first Apex, Barsoth. Mad respect.” Rex held out a fist.

Shin blinked before returning it, giving Rex a tight smile as they fist bumped.

‘Rex.’ Micheal looked up, his eyes latching onto the former Baron as a thought struck him.

“Rex, where is Lux?”

Just now, Micheal realized something – throughout this entire battle, from the start of the Founding Celebration to the clash inside the Dream to the fight against the Apexes outside…

Lux was nowhere to be seen.

“That’s a good question, innit?” Rex scratched his head as he turned to look at Micheal, before shrugging.

“I thought he was with you?”

Thud.

Micheal felt his heart pound in his ears.

“With me?”

Those words sent a lightning bolt through Micheal’s consciousness and…

It reminded him…

Of a message, a message left for him by Lux.

What’s happened, happened.

“Marco, wait a moment! Shin, take us to Castle Atlas. Now!”

Shin didn’t bother asking why as he jumped into action, grabbing Micheal’s shoulder and-

Reality shifted as the duo teleported away. The world around Micheal flashed several times as Shin made several precise jumps, getting a clear line of sight. It took him only a couple seconds before they arrived on the roof of Vesper’s quarters.

Micheal’s body transformed into a blur as he dashed through an opened doorway and down the hallway, sprinting through the corridors of Castle Atlas, ignoring the maids and servants who ducked aside as he rushed, until he found his way back to his guest room.

His mind, however, was focused, far away, on the message Lux had left with the Round Table yesterday, after Micheal visited, in preparation for the Founding Celebration.

Micheal ripped open his door and…

'Goodbye, I'll leave it where we met.' The message left by Lux.

Lying on the ground, at the center of his room was something that hadn’t been there when he left early this morning.

A long, thin wooden box, open at the top, revealing…

A beautiful, golden spear.

.

Chapter 47


.

“No matter what, you absolutely cannot allow yourself to be seen by the Enemy.”

Marco Barone’s voice cut through the air, his tone deep and controlled, at odds with his floating chibi spirit form. He was hovering next to a large wooden table, covered with several large maps and pieces of paper layered with calculations and data – alongside a large, metal device, about the size of a football.

Around them, not only Micheal and Shin, but also the leaders or representatives of every powerful organization present stood, listening in. This included the Round Table, the Revolutionaries, House Atlas, the Many-Faced Hero, and the Gyven Tower. Dark Void’s presence had gathered a large amount of attention, though none present made to interfere, not when they heard of their mission.

A mission that, even now, Dark Void was hard at work fulfilling – for, Micheal watched as the land around him was rapidly transformed.

The grounds of this section of the Outer Pavillion had transformed into a bustling hive of activity. There were at least 40 members of Dark Void present, robed scientists working on the construction of an enormous, painted circle. Hundreds of complex, smaller circles were being painted down in various spots inside the circle, a vast web of complex lines, each infused with Mana, making the lines glow bright blue. At the center of the main circle was, planted firmly in the ground, the golden Spear of Time. Sitting in a smaller circle next to it, was a small wooden box, upon which rested the Twilight Ring.

“We have three Relay Teams stationed along the shores of the Empty Sea, sharing their readings with us – we’ve triangulated the source of the energy field, what we’ve decided to call a Temporal Flux Field, at the exact center of the Highstorm, where it’s impacting the Nexus that holds the Third Layer together.” Marco continued, pointing down to a map, detailing where Micheal needed to go.

“We’ll only know if your mission was successful once that energy field goes down.”

In the background, Dark Void continued to construct an Empowered Ritual Circle, of gargantuan proportions.

It was a form of Magic previously unknown to the denizens of the Third Layer, separated into 3 different schools of Ritual Magic – Unempowered, Rituals that didn’t require Mana, Empowered, Ritual Circles that did require Mana, and Special type, Rituals that were unique and fell into their own category.

Humanity wasn’t supposed to learn about the existence of Rituals until they reached the Fifth Layer, not until they encountered the Cherubini, the foremost species of Ritual experts in the 7 Layers.

It was only thanks to the journals Micheal had passed on to Dark Void, passing on his knowledge of the future, that Dark Void became aware, rapidly devouring all the data he’d shared.

“This right here is a Local Field Spacetime Stabilizer, an LFS2 for short.” Marco pointed to the metal object lying on the table – the Artifact was a hodgepodge of fused metals, covered in Magic Glyphs and various metal wires. On the side of it was a large red button, covered in a glass case.

“One press of the button arms the Artifact, a second press will set it to firing.” Marco continued,

“This will, at least temporarily, stabilize the immediate surroundings for several minutes, forcibly destabilizing the Temporal Flux Field – a field our readings confirm was constructed from Paradox-derived Time Energy.” The Leader of Dark Void continued,

“Anything built from Paradox-derived Time Energy is incredibly delicate – this brief moment of destabilization will set the energy field into a slow destruction spiral, eventually restoring the Nexus to its prime state, and rescuing the Third Layer from its impending destruction.” Marco finished as he gestured with his right hand, causing the Local Field Stabilizer to float towards Micheal.

Micheal grabbed the Artifact, storing it safely within his Spatial Ring.

“However, like I mentioned earlier, the most important facet here…” Marco’s chibi form tapped on the map,

“You need to move about, avoiding Jay sol Arget’s notice, until its too late.” Dark Void’s leader went on,

“From what we now know, the Enemy has had Clones sequestered around various major and minor figures here on the Third Layer and in Axellion proper, spying on them constantly. We have no way to confirm when or where these Clones were located.” He gestured towards one of the pages of paper on the screen, where dozens of names were written out – from Micheal to Aaron Bartram to Duke Atlas, even including names like Kim Jiwoon and Jabari.

“Should this attempt be successful, you need to avoid those Clones' notice. This means no contact at all, that you haven’t already made.”

Micheal nodded back sharply.

“And how certain are we, that this will work at all?” Allmaster’s harsh voice cut in, the tall Void Noble crossing his arms as he raised his question.

Marco made several motions with his right hand, a line of instructions magically appearing on a paper that he sent out towards one of the scientists in charge of the Ritual Circle. In that same moment, he turned towards Allmaster, multi-tasking as he answered him.

“A Temporal Flux Field of this scale should be physically impossible to form, to the best of our current understanding of Time Energy. As should a Time Loop.” He spoke quickly, his voice clipped.

“We believe Jay sol Arget has fused the structure of the Loop and is utilizing it to power this Temporal Flux Field, destabilizing the Nexus. The floating islands of the Third and the Nexus have a reciprocal relationship – if the Nexus is destabilized, the islands fall.”

Micheal’s eyes widened in realization, as he offered his own reply.

“So if I destroy the energy field ahead of time…” He lead.

“You’ll stabilize the Nexus, and potentially put an end to the Loop.” Marco nodded back.

That reply received a round of murmurs from everyone around the table.

“Liu Wei! What’s our countdown?!” Marco abruptly turned away, commanding one of the Dark Void scientists, a Chinese man with black hair and tired looking eyes, who was standing by one of the large, metal machine-Artifacts.

“14 minutes and 21 seconds, sir!” The man replied, before turning away, focused on several screens filled with numbers and various energy readings.

“We have to go before that timer runs out – the destruction of the Nexus is a hard limit on the time we have to send you back.” Marco continued,

"Any questions so far?” Marco asked, as he turned back towards Micheal.

“None.” Micheal replied, memorizing every detail of the mission ahead. Marco had already gone over the timelines he needed to meet, in order to activate the LFS2 in time.

According to Marco, it was only possible to jump backwards in time here inside the current Loop - there was no way to go back to previous Loops, and start all over. It was the first question Micheal asked, once he realized Marco intended for them to stay within the current Loop. His explanation had been surprisingly concise, for such a complex topic.

All previous Loops no longer existed.

Right now, travelling to the past was akin to travelling upstream in a river whose course was already set - they weren't rewinding time, like Micheal had when he returned to the past, creating the second timeline - but rather, they were time travelling - any changes he made to this Loop would have already occurred. It was confusing, but Micheal trusted their explanation.

Travelling to a previous Loop would be akin to trying to travel up a stream that no longer existed, a section of the River of Time that had been overwritten.

Perhaps, if they possessed primary control over the Time Loop, they could alter reality and jump back to a previous Loop - but that was a power only a reality breaking Titled Deity might manage.

They were mere humans, who had to work with the reality on the ground, no matter how unideal it might be.

Marco turned away as he focused back on the construction of the massive Ritual Circle.

“To cross the Empty Sea and reach the Eye of the Highstorm, you’ll need a Void Ship worth a damn.” Veryn Aliceon, Vice-Master of the Gyven Tower, spoke up, acting as a representative of Duke Atlas' will. The speaker was a wizened Void Noble, dressed in a set of deep, red robes, with a long, bushy grey beard and a balding head.

“In this Spatial Ring is the Stormrider, a Void Ship designed for piercing through the rough winds of the Highstorm.” The 5th Circle Wizard handed it over to Micheal.

“Should you save us all, consider this a gift, from the Gyven Tower.”

Micheal returned his words with a grateful nod.

“I’ll do my utmost best.”

Allmaster grunted as he stepped forward, looking as if he’d rather be doing anything else, as he handed over a necklace with a large, square shaped amulet, made of fine silver, and carved with dozens and dozens of lines of Magic Glyphs, all written in extremely small font.

“This is a Lode Bastion. It’s an extremely expensive Defensive Artifact strong enough to deflect a direct blow from an Apex.” Every word spoken seemed like it was torn from him, unwillingly, as he tossed the Artifact onto the table in front of Micheal.

“Try not to break it.” The abrasive Void Noble turned away almost immediately.

“I’ll try.” Micheal noted back wryly. He didn’t hold Allmaster’s words against him – if anything, Micheal wanted to kill this particular Void Noble just as much as the Hero wanted him dead – Allmaster was the man responsible for the Red Line, the zone of Void Noble territories with a standing policy to massacre foreign species on sight.

“Here’s something from us.” The former Baron Rex spoke up as he walked next to Micheal, clapping him hard on the shoulder as he grinned. In his hands was an Artifact Micheal recognized instantly.

An expensive and rare Limited Artifact known as a Light Refraction Shroud

“These are pretty handy, useful for sneakin’ round.”

Micheal accepted the Artifact with a grateful nod.

Aaron Bartram walked up next, holding out a ring

“This is-“

“A Returning Ring.” Micheal muttered, recognizing this Artifact as well.

It was a rare, Limited Artifact bought out during the First Wave – and one of the extremely few Artifacts that allowed for a limited form of teleportation. It allowed one to set a ‘Home’ that they could teleport to, as long as they were within a certain distance of it – with Micheal’s current Soul stat, that range was in excess of a hundred miles.

The Artifact had a huge cooldown time, anywhere from 30 to 40 days, but was incredibly valuable despite that – the ability to teleport, even with some prior setup, was a huge boon, especially when Micheal wouldn’t have Shin with him.

“I wish we could help more directly…” The Commander of the Round Table shook his head, before resting a hand on Micheal’s shoulder.

“Try to come back in one piece, you hear me?”

Micheal responded with a tight smile,

“No promises.”

Aaron chuckled as he moved away, his attention turning to the disaster recovery efforts. The denizens of Axellion were trying to maintain a layer of normalcy, as if the world around them wasn’t currently ending.

Finally, one last figure floated forward.

Eon, the now-crippled King of Heroes.

Micheal eyed the Void Noble expectantly, staring curiously at the golden Aura that encompassed the King of Heroes.

Eon spoke, his words making Micheal blink as they resounded in the air, filled with an undertone of power.

“Do not fear the Reaper,

The March unto the End.”

A flash of golden light overtook Micheal and…

The world around him fell away as, once more, he entered the Dream.

“What?” Micheal blinked, instinctively summoning Lightshorn from his Spatial Ring. The Crown of the Angel King remained in his ring, its charges fully used, alongside one of his remaining Life Orbs.

“Easy there, young Human.” Eon raised his hand as he chuckled at Micheal’s response.

“Time is short, on the outside world. In here, however, time will stretch. Every minute inside is now but a second outside.” Eon motioned at the world around him.

It was the same familiar fields of wheat as before. The mountains in the distance had returned to normal, no lava anywhere to be seen, as had the blue sky above.

“My time in this life is short. Should you succeed in your mission, by the time you return here, I will be dead.” Eon continued, turning away from Micheal as he considered the world around him.

“My Artifacts and treasures alike were all destroyed, so I have naught to offer you, but knowledge.” The Void Noble’s words stretched out as he spoke, his deep voice echoing as a small breeze swept past them.

“Knowledge?” Micheal replied, slowly lowering Lightshorn, though he kept it in his hand still, out of an abundance of caution.

Eon turned back towards Micheal, a small smile on his face, at peace with the fact that he was dying.

“Indeed. I suppose, now that I have time to spare, I should start at the beginning.” He spoke, his words unhurried.

“I care little for this world, if I’m to speak truly. I find its practices savage and its people harsh and largely xenophobic.” He shook his head.

“A result of the environs they live in, perhaps, but I find it distasteful all the same.” He continued,

“It might sound strange to you, that I hold such an opinion – and that has to do with what I am.” Eon smiled.

“I am what’s known as a Perpetual.”

Eon went on to explain what that was, his words leaving Micheal more and more astounded.

He was a member of a supernatural race of beings that lived, died, and lived again, constantly reincarnating, while holding on to their memories, their Soul traversing space and time in an endless loop.

‘So that’s why he has such an insane Soul stat.’ The realization struck Micheal, as he recalled the extraordinary SSS- ranked Soul Eon possessed – a stat so tremendous it almost defied reason.

“My gratitude to you is not because you are saving this world, no – it is because you avenged me, striking down the attacker that sought to, and likely will, kill me.” Eon gestured to his malformed appearance.

“Let it not be said that I do not pay my debts.”

The King of Heroes, no, the Perpetual known as Eon, Micheal was starting to realize, was an incredibly prideful creature.

“And so, my gift to you.” Eon’s eyes glinted.

“It won’t help you in the immediate short term, but it’s knowledge that, should you survive, will serve you well for the future.” The Perpetual continued,

“I have lived many lives and experienced many things. I have faced off against Gods and Dragons alike, travelled across Worlds unlike any other.” He narrated, waving his hand at the world of the Dream around him.

As he spoke, the Dream began to transform, showing images of what he spoke of – from vast forest areas full of enormous mushroom trees, to a world covered in huge rivers of molten magma, to a land full of enormous, floating stone islands.

“In that time, I have learned deep and wide, of the Conceptual Powers that bind all reality.” The world around them finally came to a halt, settling upon an image of a huge, stone cliff, overlooking a forest of beautiful trees with colorful, pink leaves.

As Eon finished speaking, he waved his hand again, summoning a notebook from thin air.

The motion seemed to weigh on the Perpetual, a line of blood dripping down his nose – he had created the notebook from thin air, using the power of the Dream, an action that was incredibly costly.

“It’s a concept called Path Theory.” Eon opened the notebook, turning to a page in it.

That name sent a jolt through Micheal.

‘Path theory.’ His Divine Scan spoke of Conceptual Powers in terms of Paths.

“Mastering a Conceptual Power is akin to walking a Path, wherein the user will find various Walls that obstruct them. I’m sure you’re familiar with the concept.” Eon went on.

Micheal nodded. Achieving Mastery and Grandmastery, both times, had taken a tremendous amount of effort, much like overcoming a wall that had blocked his way.

“Every Soul is unique. Some Souls are more inclined to touch upon one Conceptual Power than others.” Eon remarked, his tone leading.

“In your case…” Eon’s eyes flashed as he looked at Micheal, as if staring through him, through his very Soul.

Once more the action seemed to cost Eon a great deal, his hands twitching as if he had been struck with a heavy blow.

“You’ve mastered the Path of the Sword to a deep level. However…” Eon continued, his free hand reaching up and wiping away the line of blood.

“Am I right in assuming you struggled, every step of the way, and now, after crossing the Second Wall, you find yourself unable to progress?”

The words struck Micheal like a physical blow, seeing true to the core of the struggle that defined part of his existence.

Mutely, he nodded back.

Eon returned his nod with a slow one of his own.

“I have seen many, many Paths across the many lives I have lived. And I can tell you this now.” His words took on an almost gentle edge.

“Your Soul is ill fit for the Path of the Sword.”

Micheal took the words calmly. It wasn’t, he found, much of a surprise – his own lived experience had told him much the same.

“If the Path of the Sword is ill matched for my Soul…” Micheal began, as a realization struck him,

“Then are you saying… there’s a Path you see, that does fit?” Eon seemed to be leading his words up to a certain conclusion, one that set Micheal’s heart racing.

“I cannot be certain, there are many aspects of Path Theory that even I lack a perfect understanding of… however.” Eon paused, his gaze considering.

“Let me ask you a question, to clarify.”

Micheal nodded his assent.

“Have you found, in your times of training, anything unusual about your ability to control and handle various types of energy? Ki, Mana, that sort of thing?”

Micheal froze, his mind set to racing as he considered Eon’s question.

‘Energy?’

As a human that broke through to the higher levels of King Tier Ki in his first life, despite only arriving during the Fourth Wave, Micheal had always felt himself a natural when it came to handling Ki. The same applied for Sword Energy,

And now, as Micheal considered this fact…

‘My Soul! I also have a talent for handling Mana!’ It was a talent he’d only learned about here in his second go at life.

“Yes, yes I have.” Micheal spoke, his voice a harsh whisper,

“Are you saying…?”

Eon nodded.

“Then there is a Path, one I believe will match the wavelength of your Soul, more than any other.” Eon tossed the notebook at Micheal, who caught it with his free hand as he stored Lightshorn in his Spatial Ring.

“I’ve transferred everything I know about this Path, and Path Theory in general.”

Micheal hefted the book in his hands, feeling the weight to it.

“And now, my debt to you is paid.” Eon turned away as another line of blood dripped down from his nose, waving his non-crystal hand at Micheal as he looked away.

“Farewell, young Human. Good luck in your journey, and may your Dreams never cease.” His final words echoed in the air as…

A flash of golden light swept over Micheal, and the Dream began to dissipate.

As the world of the Dream around Micheal fell away, he stared down at the title carved into the cover of the book, reading the words that would change the trajectory of his life.

A Dreamer's Guide to Path Theory and…

The Path of Energy.

By Eon, the Starbound Dreamer.

.

Chapter 48


.

“Try not to break em, eh?” Shin nudged Micheal with his elbow as he handed over his Neo-Levitation Bracers.

His voice imitated Allmaster’s snide tone as he joked, with only the tightness of his brow revealing his true feelings.

“I’ll be fine.” Micheal remarked as he stored the bracers in his Spatial Ring.

“You know what they say, you just can’t keep a good man down and…” Micheal elbowed Shin back,

“I like to think that I’m pretty great!” He pointed at himself, puffing his chest out slightly.

Shin snorted, before punching Micheal in the shoulder.

"You're something, that's for sure."

Shin stepped back after giving him one tense final nod. Micheal’s supernatural senses, however, caught a slight lightening of the tension between his best friend’s shoulders.

He couldn’t really blame Shin for worrying – right now, their situation was do or die.

All around them, the final preparations for the enormous Ritual Circle were taking place.

Small piles of Mana Crystals lined the ground, smashed into the complex, meandering lines that made up the Ritual Circle. Dark Void scientists had finished measuring specific amounts, making the Ritual Circle glow even brighter.

Alongside that glow came something different – the air had changed.

There was a heaviness, a presence, that hadn’t been there before.

And it was as he made this observation that he saw Marco’s spirit chibi form start floating towards him, accompanied by Jabari and two other Dark Void members he didn’t recognize. Behind Marco, the other scientists of Dark Void began to file out of the Ritual Circle.

‘This is it.’

Micheal took a deep breath, clenching his left hand around his Raidon Gauntlet, as he thought of what was to come.

‘To think, there was another me running around this whole time.’ The Ritual, Marco had explained, would send him backwards several days – it was a case of real, actual time travel, latching on to the Time Loop’s structure to travel backwards in Time.

‘I wonder if we crossed paths?’ The thought was amusing.

“We’re all set to fire the Ritual, are you ready?” Marco’s voice held a commanding edge, despite his chibi form, as he stared at Micheal, his gaze piercing.

“I am.” Micheal sent a line of Mana into his Raidon Gauntlet, pulling lightly on the Concept of Time – he embraced the Realm of Intent in that same moment, strengthening his connection. Thanks to the leftover energy in the Crown of the Angel King, his Soul had fully recovered, his Mana Circles no longer searing and painful.

“Remember.” Marco began,

“Absolutely do not let Jay sol Arget realize you’ve travelled back in Time, not until you reach the center of the Empty Sea and activated the device. Everything we do here hinges on this – avoid all contact with anyone unless absolutely necessary. If Jay sol Arget realizes someone is tampering with the Loop, there’s a chance he’ll Loop around again, making our efforts for naught.”

“Understood.” Micheal didn’t fault Marco for repeating information he’d already heard – the utter seriousness of this matter required their utmost focus.

As Marco spoke, Jabari and the two other Dark Void scientists began to strap on several long black ropes, lining up and down Micheal’s chest and legs, covered in glowing blue script, finely dusted with Mana Crystals. Micheal held his arms out, making their job marginally easier – he had switched into a set of plain black leathers for the jump, storing his gear in his Spatial Ring.

“You’ll be teleported to a location you previously travelled to while in this Loop – we aren’t exactly sure where, we can’t control that parameter.” Marco continued, while simultaneously directing the scientists.

“We’re sending you as far back up the Loop as we can, to give you as much time as possible. Again, we aren’t exactly sure when.” Marco waved a hand, motioning towards Jabari.

The Dark Void scientist stopped helping tie on the Glyph-covered straps and instead pulled out a small, metallic watch from a Spatial Ring, gingerly handing it to Micheal.

“This watch here has a record of all background energy readings we’ve taken up to the start of the Loop – it also has an Active Energy Sampler, or AES, component of its own, one that will cross-reference that data once you arrive in the past, and tell you exactly when you are.” Marco continued as Micheal stored the watch in his Spatial Ring.

“Finally.” Marco remarked as Jabari brought out an odd looking ring.

“This is a Temporal Ring Seal, a prototype, the first of its kind. It will protect your Spatial Ring from the ripping currents of Time, and keep it bound to your Soul, even if your body is torn to shreds.”

Micheal held out his hand, watching closely as Jabari looped the larger blue ring around his own Spatial Ring. The Artifact then made a ‘clicking’ noise as it locked around his finger. Micheal sent in a sliver of Mana, and instantly felt a bond form, connected to his Soul.

“I’ll try not to break it.” He remarked wryly.

Marco waved his hand dismissively.

“It’s fine, either way – I’ll take the continued existence of the Third Layer over a few Artifacts we can recreate any day of the week.” Marco continued,

"I wish we could help you more directly, but the risks of the Clones noticing..." The chibi spirit sighed, massaging its forehead, before it floated forward, looking Micheal right in the eyes,

"Godspeed. We're all counting on you."

Micheal simply nodded back.

“Get ready, Team Indigo, Team Jasper, Team Deltron! 38 seconds to launch!” The Leader of Dark Void yelled out loud as he floated away, barking out orders to different clumps of scientists. Three distinct squads moved out, pre-activating specific parts of the Ritual Circle.

“Do I get a helmet?” Micheal turned to the scientists who were currently wrapping his arms and legs in straps covered in Magic Glyphs. He felt like he was gearing up for war, covered in armored leathers.

“Uh, ah, no, sorry.” One of the scientists, a tall white man with short brown hair, replied, giving Micheal an apologetic look.

“Anything we have wouldn’t survive the trip… well. You shouldn’t survive either but…” The scientist shrugged.

“Life Orbs.”

“Life Orbs.”

Micheal and the scientist both replied at the same time.

With that, the last members of Dark Void backed off, leaving Micheal alone in the center of the massive Ritual Circle.

‘Well, alone except for you two.’ He turned his gaze to the side, eyeing the two powerful Artifacts sitting just to his left – the Twilight Ring and the Spear of Time.

‘How did Lux know to steal the spear, anyway?’ The thought struck Micheal as he stared at the beautiful golden Artifact.

“Mana Crystals are lit! The Circle is firing! 10 seconds to full activation!” Marco’s shout distracted Micheal as his head snapped forward.

There, standing across from him outside the Ritual Circle, several dozen meters away at a safe distance, were numerous figures. Micheal could make out the scientists of Dark Void, the Vice-Master of the Gyven Tower, Jessica Wiles and Felix Serrano of the Round Table, Kim Jiwoon and Jabari, Rex and Hayden Montacerry of the Revolutionaries, he even saw, to his surprise, Dunkore Salm, the eccentric disguised Dimensional Traveler, writing down notes in a journal.

'Is Hayden Montacerry waving at me?' He ignored the friendly gesture as...

Last but certainly not least…

He saw Shin, leaning with his back against one of Dark Void’s large metal contraptions, giving Micheal a thumbs up.

Micheal returned the gesture, grinning fiercely as he felt the pressure in the air around him begin to build. The blue glow of the Ritual Circle gradually grew brighter and brighter, soon becoming blindingly bright. A massive roar came out of nowhere, earsplittingly loud as energy swarmed around Micheal in a huge chaotic matrix. He felt his connection to Time strengthen and-

“Here we go!” Marco’s voice was somehow audible over the roar, as Micheal felt the world around him flex – even Time itself, through his connection, seemed to stutter.

“Hold on to your butts!”

And then-

Everything went white.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Previously…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Awareness came to Micheal abruptly, as he awoke to a world that… wasn’t quite right.

‘What?’ Micheal’s thoughts slowed as he realized something.

He was floating.

‘Ah.’ Another realization sank in.

He had died.

He was now in the strange, ethereal form he took on when his brain was destroyed before he could shatter a Life Orb to heal his injuries, losing physical consciousness. It was a strange state of being, where his Life Orbs allowed him to pick where he would respawn, though down to a limited range nearby where he’d died.

He quickly took in his surroundings – he could only maintain this form for a few brief moments, before he was forced to respawn.

He was floating above the grounds of one of the many floating islands that made up the Third Layer – this particular island was one of the smaller ones, though it had a small spring, and a bevy of trees off to his left. Clearly, he had arrived somewhere within the Inner Ringlands.

‘Is that…?’ Micheal spotted his Raidon Gauntlet, lying on the ground right below his floating, ethereal form.

A Life Orb broke as Micheal rematerialized.

“Ah.” He looked down at his body.

“I really did die.” He was completely naked – the outfit he’d donned for the jump had been completely destroyed.

“Not you, though.” He held up his hand, smiling as he saw his Spatial Ring appear, just like Dark Void had promised, still surrounded by the larger blue ring, which he quickly removed and stored away.

He quickly swapped back into his dark leather armor and cloak, donning his Cloud Stepping Shoes, Aura Nullification Necklace, Neo-Levitation Bracers. He also put on the Lode Bastion Allmaster had gifted him and the Returning Ring gifted by the Round Table.

Finally, only after he was geared properly, did he kneel down and pick up the Raidon Gauntlet lying on the stone ground.

‘It’s damaged.’ The Artifact had several dents and marks upon its surface – the journey through Time clearly had not been easy on the Artifact. Micheal stored it in his Spatial Ring, making a mental note to bring it back to Dunkore to get repaired.

He then brought out the watch given to him by Dark Void, activating its Active Energy Sampler to confirm the date.

‘Come on, come on…’ He thought, his heart pounding as he waited anxiously for the reading – everything was riding on this.

The watch let out a quiet ‘ding’ and…

“Yes!” Micheal punched the air, his composure breaking as a huge grin found its way onto his face.

Finally, some good news.

The reading on the watch made it clear – not only had he travelled back in time…

He had travelled backwards more than a week, to the early morning of the day before the Apex Void Predator, Barsoth, attacked Axellion.

“Okay.” Micheal let out a huge breath, the feeling of immense pressure that had laid upon his shoulders lightening slightly.

“I can work with that.” He grinned.

He had actually just physically time-travelled! How crazy was that?!

It was almost funny, in a way – anyone else in Micheal’s shoes would probably be a nervous wreck, knowing they had the fate of humanity resting upon their shoulders.

To Micheal, however…

That was a burden he’d borne ever since he rewound time and arrived on the First Layer, a cause he’d fought for an entire decade of his life in the first timeline.

This, now…? Well, it was just another day.

“Focus.” He shook his head as he centered himself, and then looked around his surroundings again, this time with a small frown on his face.

‘I remember this…’ His perfect memory stretched backwards, calling up a map of the landscapes he had traversed as he travelled the Third Layer.

‘This was… a few miles off from where we found the note left by Bastien?’ He’d found that note the same day they arrived in Axellion, helping fight off Barsoth – so tomorrow, for his past self.

Just as that thought struck him…

A quiet ‘ping’ noise caused him to freeze as a blue screen flashed open in front of him, distracting him.

.

— — - Titles System - — —

Your achievements have earned you a new Trait Selection.

.

Micheal stared at the screen blankly for a moment, reading its contents and then reading them again.

‘A new Trait?’

With a thought, Micheal opened the Titles System.

.

— — - Titles System - — —

Title: -

Traits: Glass Cannon, (1 unassigned)

.

Sure enough, next to the Trait he had first picked ‘Glass Cannon’ was a new selection spot, waiting for him to assign it.

Micheal reached forward and tapped on the word ‘unassigned’ in the Traits section.

Immediately, a new blue screen appeared in front of him.

.

— — - Titles System: Trait Selection - — —

Please select from the available Traits:

Iron Boned – Thick Skin – Courageous Soul

Heat Resistance – Inborn Strength – Black Veins

Alpha Restraint – Friction Resistance – Lightfoot

Mirror Soul – Steady Heart – Plasmic Blood

Curse Talent – Enhanced Lungs – Gravity Resistance

Hearty Health – Thunderous Legs – Golden Mind

Nimble Fingers – Fast Recovery – Plague Resistance

… (1/209 page)

.

‘There are more pages.’ He noticed – previously, there had been only 205 pages. This matched what he knew about the Titles System – the number of Traits you could select from grew as you experienced more, newer, or greater things in life.

In terms of raw time, it hadn’t actually been that long since Micheal first obtained the Titles System – his battle with Orion was still fresh in his mind, even now, many days later.

So much had happened, inbetween then, however, that it felt almost like a lifetime away. It was no surprise that the number of Traits he could obtain had grown so much.

Micheal scrolled through the pages, his eyes flickering from Trait to Trait. A new Trait now could prove enormously useful for his confrontation with Jay sol Arget, and his mission to stabilize the Third Layer.

‘I should pick something that also helps me in the long term.’ He needed to keep in mind the greater threats to come.

He had picked Glass Cannon as his first Trait more out of necessity – he had badly needed to increase his raw physical strength, and the downsides of Glass Cannon were easily side-stepped thanks to his Life Orbs, making it an easy decision.

This Trait, however, would take careful consideration.

‘Hmm.’

Micheal sent out his two remaining Life Orbs out as he jumped up into the air, activating his Neo-Levitation Bracers. He manipulated the Life Orbs like Kim Jiwoon had taught him, using them to grant himself the ability to fly freely. Balancing on one foot was incredibly easy when you were weightless, thanks to the Bracers Shin had lent him.

Like a rocket, Micheal began to shoot across the sky, leaving behind a flurry of blue sparks in his wake.

He wasn’t flying towards Axellion, not yet, no.

First…

He wanted to investigate something, a thought that had been bothering him – he flew towards the site where Bastien had been attacked and left a note behind.

The seconds flew by as he soared through the air, relishing in his newfound ability to fly. He made use of his ironclad control of his Life Orbs, maneuvering in the air as he practiced how he would react if he had to make evasive maneuvers.

And it was here, when he was about halfway to the location where Bastien had fought against Jay sol Arget…

Micheal decided on his new Trait.

It was one of the newer Traits, one that had only appeared recently, after his excursions here on the Third Layer – one of the powerful Traits known to the records of Dark Void from the first Timeline, back when they made great efforts to study everything about the existence of the Tribes of Deities.

.

— — - Titles System: Trait Selection - — —

You have selected the following Trait:

Fortune’s Favor

.

The appearance of this Trait in his list of available selections almost certainly had to do with his interactions with Lux – for, this was a Trait like no other – one that touched upon the Concept of Causality itself.

.

— — - Trait: Fortune’s Favor- — —

Slightly alters Causality, in your favor

.

‘Slight or not…’ Lux had proven to one and all how powerful being ‘lucky’ could be.

‘Anything that tips the scales in my favor is worthwhile.’ It was a Trait that would never not be useful.

“Fortune favors the bold.” Micheal’s eyes glinted, a hint of golden light flashing and then disappearing as he closed the screen, and returned his focus back to his flying.

He had a world to save.

.
