Chapter 49


.

Micheal wrapped the Light Refraction Shroud around himself, keeping it close as he flew through the air. Sparks of blue energy fell and dissipated as his Life Orbs grinded against each other, working in tandem with his bracers to keep him afloat.

The rare Limited Artifact was an incredible gift, the shroud granting him quasi-invisibility, as long as he kept it on. With this, he’d have no trouble sneaking around, though getting used to the distortion field was going to take a few minutes.

‘I’m here.’ He thought as he hovered in the air, his eyes scanning the nearby grounds as he stayed afloat.

Below him was an enormous, gaping hole in what once was a small-to-decent sized floating island. Large, melted blocks of rock wobbled in the air, floating dismally above the Void. A few sad trees lined the edge of this island, stripped of their leaves.

Around this island was... nothing.

No connecting islands, none big nor small – just hundreds and hundreds of meters of empty space, an unnaturally large hole isolating this central island from its surroundings.

‘Huh.’

It was exactly as he recalled – the location where Bastien had been attacked by Jay sol Arget.

Faintly, in the air, Micheal could sense remnants of the same strange energy that he had felt back when they had been ambushed.

“Odd.” Micheal whispered as he embraced the Realm of Intent, strengthening his connection to the River of Time.

Despite having just travelled across Time to the past, his connection to Time didn’t feel any different. There were no new scars on his Soul, nothing seemed to have changed at all. The Flow of Time continued, ever onward, at the same steady pace.

‘I guess there’s a difference between Time Travel and rewinding Time.’ He frowned as he released the Realm of Intent.

‘If only Tallanoran were still alive.’ He sighed. Having a Master of Time here to advise him would’ve been incredibly useful.

Despite being an incredibly taboo topic among Deities, most Titled Deities seemed all too willing to mess with Time when it served to their benefit.

It was a topic he was going to have to get used to, given the enemies and future that was to come.

Micheal kept his thoughts to himself as he hovered, leaving the grounds of what was left of this floating island undisturbed, until he found the rock that had hidden Bastien’s note and…

“Well, I’ll be.”

Micheal stared down at the rock, his perfect memory letting him confirm that this was the exact spot Bastien’s note had been under.

Except…

Micheal reached down slowly and lifted the rock up, revealing…

Nothing.

“I thought it was odd.” Micheal remarked, slowly scratching his chin. Shin had been the one to point it out.

“If he was actively being attacked by Jay sol Arget, would he really have time to write out a note in morse code?” It was technically possible, but still…

Micheal opened the Shop, moving over to the option where he could buy basic items from Earth.

It took only a moment before a piece of parchment appeared in his hand, alongside a pen.

“But wait.” Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he paused.

“If I’m the one who wrote the note… then how did I know to write a note here the first time?” He massaged his temple,

“The note was written because I wrote it. It happened because I did it.” He argued with himself,

“If I never did it, it wouldn’t have happened – but because I did it, it did happen.” He concluded.

…

“That doesn’t make any sense.” He threw up his hands in defeat.

“Whatever. Time travel.” He grumbled as he knelt down and began to write out what he’d seen on the previous note, coding it in Morse Code. He scribbled hastily, purposefully writing in a way that didn't match his own handwriting.

‘Regroup at Axellion, Wyden Inn – South Gate. Invisible Monster – do not engage. Use flour to mark – only half effective.’

“Hmm.”

‘Why didn’t future me write something more specific?’ Micheal pondered, briefly, before a realization struck him.

“Ah. The Clones.”

‘Jay sol Arget is watching.’ There was no telling when or where his past self was being spied on.

The Titled Deity had spread his Paradox Clones out across the Third Layer, with eyes and ears everywhere.

‘I need my past self to play along, unaware.’ Micheal slowly nodded.

It was the only way to be certain.

If Jay sol Arget had even the slightest suspicion that this Loop had been tampered with, there was a real risk that the Titled Deity would change the Loop, or cause it to Loop again, erasing all their efforts in one swift blow.

‘His ignorance is our only defense.’

He tapped on his Spatial Ring, about to bring out a pinch of flour when-

He froze.

On the ground, just to the side of the rock, he was now noticing, was a small clump of white powder.

‘So Bastien already knew – and that’s why I wrote a note, including a tip about flour.’ He picked up a few particles, his keen senses instantly identifying it. Flour. A handy countermeasure, to fight against an unseen opponent.

‘This note ensures that I go to Axellion, and meet up with Aaron in time, before the Founding Celebration.’ Micheal began to put the pieces together.

It was a way to guide his past self, to take the most optimal route, without Jay sol Arget suspecting interference.

Carefully, he placed the note under the stone, until it was positioned precisely like it was in his memory – folded in half and tucked beneath a fist-sized rock, with only a tiny edge of paper sticking out.

He then immediately began to float up, leaving the scene undisturbed as he crossed over the Void, until he reached a nearby floating island, settling down upon a rather oval-shaped boulder. A few Volpa grazed on some of the grasses growing on this island, the greyish black deer completely unaware of Micheal’s presence, hidden as he was by his Light Refraction Shroud.

‘Now that that’s settled.’ Micheal’s eyes narrowed as he turned his gaze in Axellion’s direction.

‘Let’s get moving.’

It was time to solve the second question that had been bothering him.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Axellion, here in the past, was a sight for sore eyes.

‘This is the first time I’ve seen the full city, before it was attacked by an Apex.’ Micheal realized as he hovered in the air, hidden from sight. He had donned a blank white face mask, further disguising his features, just in case he was spotted. Above him, a clump of clouds drifted past.

The bustling metropolis was a hive of activity. Micheal was floating near the North Gate to Axellion, an entrance that had a huge sub-section dedicated to receiving Void Ships. There, he saw dozens and dozens of vessels lining along long wooden piers, ranging from small, two-man Void Ships that reminded him of rowboats back on Earth, to fully fledged flagships of enormous size.

Micheal drifted closer to Axellion, donning a small frown as he neared the walls.

‘I can’t just fly in.’ His senses caught on to the keen invisible layers of Defensive Wards House Atlas had set, shielding the airspace of Axellion from intruders – Wards that were destined to be disturbed tomorrow, once Barsoth the Apex Void Predator invaded and began his rampage.

But that was then, and he was here in the now.

Micheal absorbed his Life Orbs as he allowed himself to slowly drift down, relying on his bracers.

There was a long line of Void Natives on foot, waiting to enter the North Gate. Some Void Nobles were accompanied by large, floating wagons, stuffed with goods to trade or sell. Others walked on foot, holding large backpacks or carrying boxes.

It wasn’t entirely Void Natives, either – Micheal saw a few of the other races that had been Chosen, waiting in line to visit Axellion.

He saw a pair of reedy female Cricken, part of an ensemble group escorting a series of floating wagons. He also spotted a solitary Raven, the bird-headed humanoid species wearing a large tan hat, resting its back against a different floating wagon as it waited for the line to move. This particular Raven had a set of fine curved blades strapped to its hip, resting a feathered hand on one of the blade’s hilts.

‘No humans, though.’ He shrugged. It was still well before the Rush. Chosen species were still a relative novelty on the Third Layer.

Micheal ignored the crowds as he dipped down, stopping a dozen meters away from the entrance, hovering just a couple meters above the ground.

“Next!” A loud voice caught his attention, one of several Guardsmen standing in front of the North Gate yelling.

“Name, purpose, and goods to be declared. Have it ready!” The Guardsmen were dressed in full metal chain mail and wielded dark black spears. The insignia of House Atlas was inscribed on their chestplates.

Micheal watched as a floating wagon, burdened with several large wooden crates, floated forward, led by a pair of Void Natives.

“Bunto, Ser, out of the Kren Township, with 24 crates of the highest quality Gorka.” The Void Native, a balding male with a bulging belly, patted the front of the wagon proudly.

One of the guards moved forward to inspect the floating wagon, while the other engaged Bunto with some small talk.

Micheal took that moment as he subtly pulled his Life Orbs out again, hovering them just below his feet, and began to fly forward.

“…excited for the Founding Celebration, did you hear the news?”

“The King o’ Heroes himself is showing up!”

“Duke Atlas truly is great!”

“…these blue-skinned Foreigners call themselves Fenn-“

Micheal ignored the wash of talk as he silently floated through the open gate, the Light Refraction Shroud shielding his presence well enough that he managed to completely avoid detection.

It took him only a few moments to clear the gate, before he zoomed away, landing atop the roof of a nearby Inn.

‘How did Lux know to steal the Spear of Time?’ It was the second question he had been pondering.

Lux was supernaturally lucky, Micheal knew, but even then – it still didn’t make any sense.

‘…Unless I asked him to.’ Micheal tapped on his Spatial Ring, bringing out a small green crystal.

It was the Kebler Crystal that Lux had given him - a communication tool that would send out a pulse of energy to its paired crystal. They had agreed on a number of predetermined locations to reconvene at, depending on the number of crystal pulses.

Micheal ran a finger along his knuckles, thinking intently.

‘But that can’t happen until a couple days from now.’ Until after his meeting with Lux had concluded.

He found himself at an impasse. He would need to wait, here in Axellion, until after Lux had made contact with his past self, and only then could he initiate a meeting between them. Otherwise, he risked messing up the timeline.

‘I also can’t risk seeing anyone my past self is going to meet.’ There was no telling where Jay sol Arget was lurking, and again, he couldn’t risk messing up the timeline. Everything needed to happen, precisely as it had already happened.

However…

‘I’m a day early.’ The realization struck him.

He couldn’t risk meeting people his past self was destined to meet…

But what about someone he had never met, someone who was about to leave this Layer entirely?

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The Purgatory Church owned several small courtyards, in the business district of Axellion. Each courtyard was enclosed by a 3 meters-tall stone wall, blocking out outside-access. Most of the courtyards also contained a pair of buildings, used by the Church for various activities, ranging from housing to bookkeeping to storage for foodstuffs to the actual main church hall.

Bastien Amiot sighed as he tried to relax, sitting cross-legged in the exact center of one of those courtyards. He was a pale middle-aged man with half-gray, half -brown hair, thin and wiry, angular face, piercing brown eyes, and thin lips drawn up in a frown.

‘At last. Peace.’ He closed his bloodshot eyes, fighting back a wave of exhaustion.

The Church appeared to be undergoing some type of schism – this normally bustling courtyard was now deserted, leaving Bastien blessedly alone, in the privacy of his mind.

Inside the Church, his disciple, Grant, was still asleep. The poor boy was utterly exhausted, as tired as Bastien was, after they were separated from his other disciple, Aiden.

Bastien wanted nothing more than to slip unto the sweet bliss of rest himself, alas…

A bloodshot eye opened as his gaze flickered, scanning the world around.

He was being hunted.

‘I will not fall.’ He would not allow himself to die here.

Not just for himself, but for Aiden, for Grant, and for all his students, both living and dead.

He owed it to them, to continue living, to keep fighting.

‘Aiden knows to rendezvous back here if we’re separated.’ Bastien had left his Soul Compass in the care of the Church, an Artifact that would let Aiden find him once he left. He had done several favors for the Church, some of the members of their research branch had been interested in how his Grandmaster Sword Energy interacted – and now was the time to call those favors in.

Bastien’s gaze drifted, his hands twitching as he slowly rested his right hand on the hilt of a single-edged slightly curved silver sword.

‘We leave as soon as Grant wakes up.’ He had already forged an agreement with a lackey for the Church that wanted out and had an exit point in the Outer Ringlands just to the west – they were going to leave this Layer, and climb up to the Fourth, today if this Frenchman had his way.

The minutes drifted by as dawn slowly slipped away.

A small breeze stirred the air in the courtyard… air that… wasn’t quite right.

If one looked closely, they might notice something odd.

The air in this courtyard all around Bastien was… strange, ever so slightly.

There was a faint tinge to it, a faint white color, staining the air…

For, almost invisible to the naked eye, tens of thousands of white particles existed, floating in the air, dispersed all around the cross-legged Swordmaster. These particles drifted ever so slightly, from left to right, but otherwise maintained their height, interspersed evenly every couple of inches.

On the ground, next to the resting human, was a small, blocky Artifact, with a glowing blue gem on top. Presumably, this was responsible for keeping these white particles afloat.

Bastien half-dozed, half-awake, always aware of his surroundings. Ever since the attack, he had been incredibly high-strung, finding it difficult to sleep at all, for – his intuition constantly screamed at him.

He was being watched.

The being that had targeted him was still hunting him.

That feeling had faded from time to time, especially now, holed up in one of the rundown courtyards not currently in use by the Purgatory Church. Nevertheless, Bastien didn’t allow himself the luxury of sleep.

‘He’s not watching now, not since I set up the flour net.’ Bastien’s lidded gaze took in his surroundings.

‘But I can’t keep this up.’ It was the main reason why he had made the decision to leave this Layer.

The exhaustion that dogged his every day was starting to catch up to him.

Several more minutes passed as Bastien rested his eyes, feeling the pulse of the city begin to take shape outside his walls. He kept his senses active, incredibly centered on the world around him, feeling the ebb and flow of the air around him, the shift of each particle of flour as a breeze stirred through the courtyard.

And then-

He was being watched.

The feeling was different from before, not the same as the one that was hunting him, yet his supernatural intuition screamed at him all the same.

Bastien opened his eyes.

Instantly, he activated his Molded Time Ability.

His perception of time dropped to a crawl as he embraced the Realm of Intent and-

He froze.

For, before his eyes, floating in the air roughly 30 meters away, beyond the border of this courtyard, was a faint, almost invisible distortion in the air – something a lesser man might’ve dismissed as nothing, failing to notice the slightly offset pattern in the clouds above.

It wasn’t this distortion that gave Bastien pause, however…

No, it was the myriad of black shadows that flickered off this distortion, dozens of vaguely man-like images overlaid upon each other, each moving in a slightly different direction.

‘What?’ He froze, dumbfounded.

Those images were spawned as a result of the Realm of Intent – the power that let him see slightly into the future – and a power that Bastien had thoroughly mastered.

That was why this was so surprising – this was something he had never seen before.

‘The Realm of Intent is… uncertain?’ How could that be? He was literally gazing at the futu-

His eyes widened as he connected the dots.

Now he was certain this wasn’t the creature that was hunting him, no…

A hint of excitement wormed its way into Bastien’s heart, a small ray of light in the harrowing haze that had been his life recently, as he realized…

Finally, it had occurred. Something he had been looking forward to, ever since he attained his current level of Sword Mastery, breaking past the barrier after Mastery.

He had finally met a fellow Grandmaster.

“Show yourself.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

‘Divine Scan.’

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Swordborn Human

Title: -

Traits: -

STR: B+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

END: A- (Growth Rate: Mythical or lower)

REG: C+ (Growth Rate: Common or higher)

SOUL: B+ (Growth Rate: Mythical or lower)

MANA: B (Growth Rate: Uncommon or lower)

Path Notes: A Swordborn Human that walks a solitary Path. Strong traces of the Path of the Sword are present.

.

Micheal read through the stats as he hovered in mid-air, staring down the courtyard with a hint of excitement, keeping the Realm of Intent open, just in case.

He had finally managed to track down one of his main goals.

‘Swordborn, just like before!’ It matched what he knew from the first timeline.

Bastien Amiot – the Sundering Swordmaster, and one of the future leaders of Humanity’s Last Army, possessed the Limited Sword God Type Ability, a Type Ability that transformed his body and Physique, into a form practically made to wield a sword. It also helped boost his Growth Rates, combined with his naturally powerful Soul Growth Rate, to become among the highest of all humanity.

Divine Scans pegged that transformation as a ‘Swordborn Human.’

And it was as he was reading through these results, however…

Micheal froze as he saw Bastien’s form transform into a blur of shifting figures and moving shadows, the overlaid future versions of Bastien warping out in a confusing mix.

“Show yourself.” Bastien Amiot’s voice’s cut through the air, holding a heavy edge.

It was a promise of violence, impending and imminent, should Micheal refuse.

‘He’s holding the Realm of Intent too!’ He had read about this, what happened when two Grandmasters clashed – the state of both warriors, tapped into the future, cancelled out each other’s advantage, rendering the Realm of Intent functionally useless, at least when it came to the other party’s immediate actions.

‘Damn.’ Micheal’s thoughts raced as he processed this, his mind moving a thousand miles a minute.

What should he do?

He had already noticed the clouds of flour scattered into the air - Jay sol Arget’s Clone didn’t appear to be present, at least not right now. This meant he had a precious opportunity here, to make contact unseen.

‘He’s already noticed me.’ Micheal frowned as he saw Bastien begin to tense up.

As he floated there, a thought struck him.

‘What would Shin do?’

With that thought in mind, Micheal made his decision.

In one smooth motion, he dropped down onto the ground of the courtyard, shedding his Light Refraction Shroud. His enhanced muscles tensed as he took the heavy multiple-storey fall, shrugging it off like it was nothing.

He then sat down on the ground, cross-legged, matching Bastien’s position.

“…”

“Ho, old man. Nice sword.”

.

Chapter 50


.

“You’re human.”

Bastien remarked, his voice holding a slightly softer edge. He wasn’t asking a question, but rather, making a statement.

“Born and raised, on the plains of Texas.” Micheal returned, resting his hands on his knees.

The tension in the air was palpable, as the two Grandmasters eyed each other.

After a few moments, Bastien chuckled.

“I always thought- in my head, the way-“

The Swordmaster’s words were cut off as he let out a series of wracking coughs. He then waved a hand in the air, shooing away a few particles of flour that were too close to his mouth.

‘…how long has it been since he’s slept?’ Micheal pondered, catching the tell-tale signs of an enhanced human forcing themselves to stay awake.

As mankind climbed the 7 Layers, gaining Abilities, energy pools from Ki or Mana, or powerful Types that modified their Physique… humanity found it possible to shrug off, to some degree, the necessity of sleep. However… just because it was possible to skip sleeping didn’t mean it was healthy. Rest, or at least, meditation, remained vitally important aspects of existence, even in the higher Layers – with the exception of a few Abilities and certain Type Abilities.

The complexities of blood/brain energy interactions were some of the most hotly debated subjects within the scientific journals of Dark Void in the first timeline.

“I always figured the first Grandmaster I’d meet would be…” Bastien began, waving his free hand vaguely in the air,

“An alien, or what have you.” He continued, shaking his head wryly,

“Didn’t think it’d be one of us.” The Frenchman smiled slightly, before giving Micheal a small nod.

Micheal returned the nod with one of his own.

“I was lucky.” In a way, it was true – of all humanity, it just so happened that Micheal was the one who happened to stumble upon the Legendary Artifact that let him reset the timeline.

Bastien scoffed, shaking his head.

“Luck has nothing to do with it.”

Bastien’s lean arms tensed as he slowly pulled out his slightly curved silver sword.

“I-“ Micheal began, but-

Bastien held out a hand, cutting him off and forestalling the conversation.

“I’m sure you’re wearing a mask for a reason – so let our blades do the talking.”

And then, all of a sudden…

An armada of stark white Grandmaster Sword Energy morphed into existence, raw Conceptual might practically oozing off the white energy as it rested on Bastien’s blade, an echo of power and a promise of death.

Micheal matched Bastien’s gaze, and slowly held out his right hand.

Lightshorn appeared in his grip, the long Blood-Refined Mithril sword gleaming as it cut through a few hovering particles of flour.

He reciprocated.

Pure, white Grandmaster Sword Energy was wrought into existence, shearing along his blade in violent spurts as it cut the air around him.

The two Grandmasters eyed each other, the powerful, deadly Sword Energies held close as they examined the other.

Both Grandmasters spoke at the same time.

“…such precision.”

“It’s beautiful.”

Micheal froze, his breath caught, as he looked, truly looked, at the Sundering Swordmaster’s Sword Energy.

For the first time in a very long time, Micheal found himself at a loss for words.

In the first timeline, Micheal had only barely managed to breakthrough the Wall that separated Mastery from Grandmastery, just a few days before his demise. He’d never had the time to sit down, as a Grandmaster, and compare notes with another Grandmaster. Sure, he’d read record after record from the works of Dark Void, journals detailing the notes left behind by other Grandmasters and even Bastien Amiot himself.

However…

Conceptual Mastery, at the higher stages, was a deeply personal thing – there was only so much the written word could convey, compared to witnessing and comprehending firsthand.

There were certain things only a Grandmaster could notice, aspects of Sword Energy that a Master was blind to, until they obtained the Body of a Grandmaster and the free time to focus.

And it was because of that, here and now, that Micheal could truly grasp what separated him from Bastien Amiot.

‘It’s beautiful.’

Brilliant white streams of alabaster, painted in a thousand shades of glory – Bastien Amiot’s Grandmaster Sword Energy was art in motion. Every line of energy, every curve of power, told a story, a menagerie of violence made manifest, the very concept of the blade empowered and emblazoned within, in spits of fury that spliced the very air itself.

To the naked eye of a casual observer, it was a torrent of white energy, ruthless and cold.

To Micheal’s gaze, however…

It was a mighty sea of energy, roaring white waves cutting forth, the ebb and flow of power shifting endlessly in an intricate dance that never ceased.

It was... wondrous.

In general, Micheal had always understood, that Bastien Amiot was a human who surpassed his limits – he had become a Worldmaster, after all, achieving a depth of Mastery few beings could match, despite wasting away for several years here on the Third Layer, when he was overcome with grief.

Bastien was one of the leaders of the Last Army – it only made sense. While he might not have ever witnessed Bastien’s achievements, apart from his final clash with the Morian Deity Kelleth, he was nevertheless aware of them.

However…

Actually observing the pure artistry that was Bastien’s Sword Mastery, even now, back when Bastien was merely a Grandmaster…

It was another thing entirely.

“Your swordsmanship is beautiful.” Micheal spoke from the heart as he gazed at the billowing waves of white energy framing Bastien’s silver sword.

Bastien paused, cocking his head before he smiled,

“Thank you.” Grandmasters could tell a great deal about their counterpart, simply by observing their Sword Energy.

Bastien continued, his eyes narrowing as he stared at Micheal.

“Yours is…” The Sundering Swordmaster paused, considering his words as he rubbed the stubble on his chin,

“Unique. A symphony of control. I can see the effort you’ve put in… such tremendous precision.” Bastien finished, his words settling deep into Micheal’s mind.

A warm sensation filled Micheal as he heard the Grandmaster’s acknowledgement, despite himself.

Indeed, as his eyes flickered from Bastien’s Sword Energy to his own, he compared them, noting the differences.

Where Bastien’s alabaster Sword Energy writhed like a work of art, Micheal’s Sword Energy held still, unerringly precise. White streaks of power, exacting in their edge, deadly in their might.

‘A symphony of control.’ Micheal tasted the words, feeling them resonate within him.

He realized that Bastien was right.

The Sundering Swordmaster had grasped the entire philosophy behind Micheal’s Sword Energy in a single glance.

Ever since he had been Chosen, in the first timeline, it was the very thing he’d sought after, bled for, fought for, in his every waking moment.

Control.

“Am I right, to presume, you have advanced just recently?” Bastien continued, unaware of Micheal’s inner contemplation.

Micheal nodded.

“Your path will be a strange one to tread.” Bastien let out a chuckle,

“I cannot fathom what it might look like at its end, a sword borne out of such exacting control.”

And it was here that Micheal realized, at least in part, why he’d struggled so far to progress, even a step beyond his current state.

‘Bastien breathes life into an entire world within his Sword Mastery.’ Micheal thought, as he gazed down at his sword, and the stark white energy borne from it.

‘Yet in mine, I see…’

Calculations. Numbers. Planning.

A labor of immense effort, relying on every trick, every facet of knowledge, combined to reach his current state.

Control.

‘Focus.’ He memorized this feeling, the sense of realization that had settled upon him, committing himself to unpack it later.

For now, however…

There were more pressing matters at hand.

“You’re leaving.” Micheal slowly let his Grandmaster Sword Energy fizzle out, the white energy fading away as he released his control of it.

“I am.” Bastien’s eyes narrowed to slits as he stared Micheal down.

Slowly, being careful to make his every motion clear and obvious, Micheal stored Lightshorn within his Spatial Ring. Then…

He brought out a small notebook.

With a flick of his wrist, he sent the notebook sliding across the courtyard, the small book slipping until it casually came to a halt, half a meter away from Bastien.

The Sundering Swordmaster raised an eyebrow.

“Read it when you get time. I can’t stay much longer, and it will explain why.” Micheal began, his voice leading as he slowly stood up.

‘Jay sol Arget’s Clone might not be here now but…’ Every second he spent here was a risk – better to leave early, now that he had made contact, and shared what needed to be shared.

‘…I’m starting to run out of notebooks.’ He would need to take a few more hours to write down a few more copies, if he wanted to keep handing them out like this.

“What can I call you?”

Bastien’s voice caught Micheal’s attention, a quiet, respectful question, from one Grandmaster to another.

Micheal’s muscles tensed as he leapt up, leaping atop the outer courtyard wall.

“Legion.” Micheal returned, his eyes placid.

Just before he turned to leave, however…

’I should say it out loud.’ It was something he’d written down in the journal, but saying it in person might help more.

“A wise man once told me.” Micheal began to recite the words he’d read, written by Bastien’s own hand, ten years from now in the future.

“A Master builds his ship, to sail the sea that is the sword.” He recited,

“A Grandmaster builds his ship, to weather the sea, no matter the storm.” He continued.

As he spoke, Bastien’s eyes locked on to Micheal’s, his focus intensifying as he listened to every word.

“A Worldmaster, a ship, he does not build – for the sea, it matters not…” Micheal finished,

“A Worldmaster is the storm.”

Micheal’s words set the air to shivering as the Sundering Swordmaster’s mouth opened, his eyes widened as he sat there, lost in thought.

His words didn’t magically induce an instant bout of Enlightenment – the Frenchman was far too alert, far too tired, pulled in many different directions at once.

However, Micheal could tell – the words had resonated with Bastien, in a way few things could. The look in the Grandmaster’s eye had changed, the cloud of depressive exhaustion vanishing from him, as inspiration took seed.

“Grow strong, old man.” Micheal muttered as he turned away,

“Mankind still needs you.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Hours had passed, the River of Time marching ever onward, as Micheal sat alone, hidden atop an empty rooftop he picked at random in one of the nicer parts of Axellion. His Light Refraction Shroud kept him hidden as he rested, finally, spending his time in meditation, after eating a quick meal or two.

He formed a new Life Orb as day slipped unto night, ignoring the world around him for the most part.

In these fateful hours, he pondered what he’d seen with Bastien, what’d he’d heard, and…

He read the book Eon had shared with him.

.

A Dreamer's Guide to Path Theory and…

The Path of Energy.

By Eon, the Starbound Dreamer.

.

‘To even touch upon the Concept of Energy, I must control 7 disparate types of energy?’

The first requirement, just to make contact with the Conceptual Power that Eon had claimed would suit him, was already quite steep.

‘Ki. Mana. Sword Energy.’ Micheal counted,

‘My Life Orbs contain Life Energy.’ He nodded – while his control over that energy wasn’t nearly as exact or precise, it definitely still counted.

‘Spatial Energy, Temporal Energy.’

Slowly, Micheal came to a realization.

‘Huh.’ It was strange.

He really did seem to have a talent for controlling energy – he was already casually capable of controlling 6 different types of energy, juggling the different powers without any hassle or issue.

‘All I need is one more.’ He needed to master one final source of energy – and in doing so, according to the notes Eon had shared, he would obtain the basic qualifications needed to touch upon the Concept of Energy.

However…

‘What should the last one be?’ Micheal had a feeling he needed to choose wisely – Eon’s writing implied that the Path of Energy, and his connection to it, would be influenced by the types of energy he controlled.

As that thought struck him, he raised a hand up, touching just below his right eye, remembering a sensation he'd felt back when he first obtained his Eyes of the Deep.

Time slipped by as Micheal caught up on his rest, energy reserves restored and his mind finally getting some much needed peace and quiet. The City-State of Axellion bustled on around him, quiet in this particular upper-class neighborhood that Micheal was hiding out in.

And so it came that day passed to night…

And night passed to day, all while Micheal sat, in quiet meditation, circulating his Ki, his energy stores growing ever closer to Lord Tier.

And then…

A loud roar shook the air.

Micheal’s eyes snapped open as…

Barsoth the Stormbringer, an Apex Void Predator, had begun its invasion of Axellion.

.

Chapter 51


.

Micheal’s form flickered, a vague shadow slipping through the air, from rooftop to rooftop, as he traversed Axellion, headed south. Rain pelted down as a furious storm began to coalesce, warbling to the growls of the Apex Void Predator that had spawned it.

‘Barsoth...’ Micheal stared at the enormous monster, frowning as he heard its roaring scream.

Below him, on the streets of Axellion, huge crowds of Void Natives poured forth, fleeing in the opposite direction. In the distance, he heard a few bells ringing out, warning the rest of Axellion about the impending attack.

‘There go the Wards.’ He felt rather then saw Barsoth shatter the Defensive Wards that protected the airspace of Axellion as it rampaged. The Apex had done something, using its wide-area control ability to manipulate the weather, somehow disrupting the Wards that shielded Axellion.

A few more well-timed leaps, and he reached the vicinity of the Apex.

“Breach! Breach! Fall back, now!” A Void Native’s voice caught Micheal’s attention, coming from the City-State’s walls.

‘Is that…?’ Micheal recognized the speaker.

It was Bellor Alten, the Guard Commander Shin and him had, briefly, interacted with during the fight.

“The Apex is through! Aim for its bloody ankles!”

Micheal watched the Guard Commander leap back off the outer wall, his eyes glowing with Mana as he charged the Apex.

“Aye, Ser!”

“Aye Ser!”

A number of Guardsmen followed the Guard Commander, forming an orderly retreat as they fell back from the damaged walls. Among these armored Void Nobles were a collection of robed figures, hastily retreating alongside them.

‘So there were Wizards fighting it down here too.’ Micheal watched as dozens of bright red fireballs and bolts of green lightning slammed into the Apex in a brilliant lightshow, attacks the Apex promptly ignored.

“Where are the bloody Knights?!” Bellor yelled as he pivoted, halting his retreat and turning to attack the Apex, two enormous blue greatswords glowing in his hands.

‘He’s brave.’ It took courage, real courage, to rush at an Apex.

Micheal frowned as he watched the Guard Commander slam two huge greatswords into the Apex’s right leg. The impact sent a wave of energy out in the middle of a small shockwave, blasting away a cloud of stone dust that had formed in the wake of the Southern Gate’s collapse. The Apex barely shifted.

‘I can’t intervene.’ If he acted now, he risked exposing himself to Jay sol Arget’s Clones.

He grimaced as he watched the Apex twitch, its head tilting as it turned its gaze upon the Guard Commander.

It was an eerie motion, showcasing the unsettling intelligence behind these monstrous entities.

“Can-“ The Guard Commander’s words were abruptly cut off as the edge of the Apex’s tail clipped him, flinging him away. Micheal just barely caught a flicker of blue energy rise to cover the Guard Commander, shielding his body as he slammed into a townhouse before tumbling down onto the stone street beyond, in a shower of bright orange sparks.

One of the younger Wizards, a Void Native who looked like a teenager, rushed up to assist the downed Guard Commander.

Micheal kept his focus on the Apex, watching as the massive creature began to move down a sidestreet. Streams of water dripped down off the behemoth, as the storm overhead began to intensify.

‘…how frustrating.’ He thought as he jumped down, moving into the street proper to get a more direct vantage point.

If there was one thing that Micheal hated, it was being put in situations where he was forced to not act. It was one thing to be helpless, laying witness to monsters attack – it was another to be capable, but forced to stand by and watch as innocent people died.

Sentience was sentience, life was life – in the grand scheme of things, it was core to Micheal’s beliefs that intelligent life inherently had value, human or not. While his overarching goal was to rescue humanity, that didn’t mean he would just stand by as innocent sentients were brutalized before his very eyes.

‘People are people.’ It was what made the 7 Layers into such a tragedy – the mass loss of life, for all people, of all kinds.

He knew that not everyone saw things that way – but so what?

He held himself to his own standard, and he’d die before he betrayed that.

And that was why…

It was all the more frustrating as he watched the Apex swat down with its tail, striking more than a dozen Guardsmen that had formed a sort of phalanx on the street, killing them all in a single blow.

‘Where is past me?!’ Micheal thought as his gaze shifted, looking beyond the walls.

This should be around the time he intervened.

“… and West Gates are sending reinforcements. The Eastern Gate is dealing with a riot, and will be delayed!” In the background, over the rain and chaos, he caught the back end of a conversation, as members of the Guard relayed information to Guard Commander Bellor.

And then…

The Apex jumped.

The enormous monstrosity leapt high into the air, its limbs splayed to the side as it jumped more than two hundred meters high.

With a loud, grinding crunch, the Apex landed atop several different houses, smashing them all beneath its feet. Micheal could just barely make out muffled screams and panicked yells, as innocent Void Natives died, crushed underneath the rubble.

And it was here the thought struck him.

Past him wasn’t going to act.

‘I didn’t want to move into Axellion because I thought this was a trap.’ He realized as he tapped his Spatial Ring. Past-Micheal had been incredibly paranoid, for good reason, in the wake of the ambush that had tried to claim their lives.

Jay sol Arget had driven Barsoth here, to damage the Defensive Wards ahead of the Founding Celebration, and to cause chaos to set up whatever plans he had in mind.

‘The only reason I moved in was because I saw a Grandmaster attack Barsoth.’ He had thought that that was Bastien attacking.

However…

Lightshorn gleamed in his hand as a small layer of precise white energy sheathed it.

‘But that must have been me.’

It was stupid – he risked exposing himself to Jay sol Arget’s Clones, and yet…

When he heard those desperate screams, as he saw children stumble past him on the street, dripping blood in the pouring rain…

He chose to act.

Lightshorn transformed into a blur as he cut forward, a brilliant slice of white Sword Energy splicing the air as it shot forward and collided with the Apex. For a brief moment, he was exposed, the Light Refraction Shroud unable to hide him while he was using such powerful energy.

A loud boom rang out as that slice of energy rammed into the Apex, sending it tumbling backwards before it could continue its rampage. A large, black gash appeared on the Apex Void Predator’s skin as it fell, the incredibly sharp energy slicing deep enough to break the Void Predator’s outer shell.

‘Past me can handle the rest.’ He thought as he spun around and dashed away, ducking behind the side of a large inn. He wrapped the Light Refraction Shroud closer around him, letting the Artifact do its work as it hid his figure.

Perhaps it was a foolish mistake, risking everything just because he couldn't sit by and ignore the injustice taking place before him... but if the only way for the human race to survive was by giving up their humanity, abandoning the pursuit of greatness and the common good, well...

Maybe that wasn't a humanity worth saving.

He fled the area, jumping up onto the rooftops and making his escape.

It was only then, as he was making his way across the city, that he heard Shin’s voice yell out…

“GIAAAANT!” Micheal turned his head and-

“PUNCH!”

He watched Shin punch the Apex in the face, Expanding his Melding Plate Arm to ridiculous proportions as he lobbed the monstrosity, sending it flying into part of the City Walls. The Apex then began to skid alongside the stone walls, leaving several long gashes and cracks in the hardened stone.

Micheal grinned.

“Thatta boy, Shin.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The Dockyards of Axellion were located in the northern region of the city, adjacent to the Northern Gate. This area was an entire sector of the City-State dedicated to receiving Void Ships.

Micheal took advantage of the chaos wrought by Barsoth’s incursion, as he traversed through the Dockyards, preparing to leave Axellion.

‘I should get some practice sailing, before I leave for the Empty Sea.’ Relying on his somewhat rudimentary method of flight to cross the Empty Sea was simply not a viable plan – the storms that plagued the Empty Sea were incredibly dangerous, and the spatial currents that underlit this section of the Third Layer were notoriously unstable – travelling using a Void Ship was almost a necessity.

For the vast majority of denizens on the Third Layer, there were only two means of travel in the Inner Ringlands – travel on foot or wagon via the Island Paths if you were close to a City-State or travel by Void Ship.

Island Paths were routes that had been constructed, linking together long strands of floating islands through a series of connections, coming in the form of wooden or rope bridges, smaller floating islands that were strung together and manually locked down, or Void Ship ferries that operated to bridge gaps too large to construct a bridge.

These pathways took a large amount of work and upkeep, and typically only existed in the immediate vicinity of a powerful or wealthy City-State.

For everywhere else, however… Void Ships were the way to go, and also the main way people crossed the Empty Sea.

The Dockyards were crowded, with thousands of Void Natives milling about. The sheer chaos of an Apex Void Predator attacking while the Duke was nowhere to be seen had caused a widespread panic.

The Northern Wall of Axellion had a large gap, several hundred meters wide, an opening that allowed for the existence of the Dockyards – this gap was sealed off at night, replaced with a large white energy barrier, a masterwork of Defensive Wards created by Duke Atlas himself, many years ago, when he first expanded the Dockyards. It was officially known as the Sea Wall.

The Sea Wall was raised, now, as Void Ship after Void Ship fled Axellion.

Micheal stuck to the rooftops of some nearby trade buildings as he watched dozens of Void Ships set course, making a hasty escape.

“I should lay low.” Micheal mumbled to himself as he ducked down, jumping to an open spot on one of the large, raised wooden docks.

Attacking the Apex had already drawn enough heat on him for one day – for now, he planned on getting out of the city, until it came time to contact Lux.

From simple skiffs to enormous schooners, the variety and quality of ship varied immensely. The docks consisted of a mix of hundreds of large, raised wooden or stone pathways, set high above the rocky ground. Countless Void Ships lay docked, though that number was rapidly dwindling as visitors and residents alike fled the city.

As he landed on an open spot of one of the wooden docks, the voices of the clamoring Void Natives and a few other Chosen sentients, washed over him, breaking through the downpour of the rain.

“The Beor Knights are still in Ador!”

“Where’s the Duke?!”

“-much for lodging and voyage down south to Kabul-“

“Black Wind is out on expedition!”

Micheal stepped carefully before jumping off the side of one of the docks, using his Cloud Stepping Shoes and his Life Orbs to hover underneath it.

The concerns of the Void Natives made sense, thanks to knowledge Micheal had learned in the days he’d spent, waiting for the Founding Celebration.

Currently, all three of House Atlas’s premier Knight Companies were away on business – the Beor Knights were helping stabilize Ador, a small City-State to the South-East that was sworn to Duke Atlas. The Head of House Braben, the rulers of Ador, had been assassinated a few weeks prior to Micheal’s arrival on the Third Layer.

The Knights of the Black Wind were out on an expedition exploring a region of floating islands near the coast of the Empty Sea – they weren’t expected back until two weeks after the Founding Celebration.

Finally, Rosare Company, and the Duke himself, alongside the main forces of the Round Table, were off on a short 2-day cooperative mission, hunting down a pack of Void Predators that had been terrorizing some of the larger hamlets that existed within House Atlas’ territory.

‘It’s the first Apex attack they’ve suffered in roughly 50 years.’ Micheal pondered as he flew forward, manipulating his Life Orbs to grant himself flight. He also activated his bracers, becoming weightless to make it easier to focus.

Like a bullet, Micheal zoomed off, soaring through the air. He passed by several other Void Ships, their crews hard at work operating them as they fled through the open Sea Wall.

‘Jay sol Arget caught them unprepared.’ It was hard to blame them, after all – there was only so much you could do when a 31-meters-tall monster invaded your city.

The storm of rain finally began to die down as Micheal exited the City-State’s premises, flying through the air like an eagle, directed and focused. He avoided the main routes taken by the fleeing Void Ships, and put the pedal to the metal as he rocketed away.

Soon, the City-State was a faint dot on the horizon, and he finally found himself some breathing room.

‘This will do.’ He thought as he descended, landing atop a mid-sized floating island.

This particular island wasn’t particularly notable and appeared deserted – there was a small patch of trees and a few large, chunky boulders, alongside a large, open stone section. Those large stone boulders, however, edged out over the Void with space in-between them, giving him the perfect place of cover, to shield himself from prying eyes.

As he shook the rain water off him, he stored his Light Refraction Shroud in his Spatial Ring.

“Alright.” He stretched his arms out, before tapping on his Spatial Ring.

“Let’s get into it.”

From his ring, he pulled out the Spatial Ring gifted to him by the Vice-Master of the Gyven Tower.

“Now that looks expensive.” He muttered as he examined the ring.

It was a custom-designed Spatial Ring, crafted from solid gold, with a large blue sapphire set on top.

Before humanity arrived on the Third Layer, Spatial Artifacts that could transport an entire Void Ship were very expensive. The ring that the Vice-Master of the Gyven Tower had gifted Micheal was the kind of gift only a wealthy Void Noble could extend, and even then, normally something only gifted to close allies or friends.

It was a Spatial Ring intentionally designed to be able to carry a Void Ship.

Even after humanity’s arrival, and the influx of Spatial Rings and Artifacts humans were capable of spawning thanks to the Shop, Spatial Artifacts still remained expensive because of their limited supply.

Micheal flicked open the Shop, checking the Artifacts section – and found himself nodding.

‘The Shop’s Spatial Rings have almost been bought out.’ At least, the lower Tiers had nearly been fully purchased, a side-effect of the mass influx of people brought by the Fourth Wave. High-Tier Spatial Rings had a larger portion still in stock, but only because they cost an insane amount – more than 800,000 Points, almost 40 times more than a Mid-Tier Spatial Ring.

Micheal closed the Shop page, focusing back on the Spatial Ring he placed on his right hand.

“Let’s get you out.” He activated the Artifact, forming a connection as he sensed its contents.

With a flick of his wrist, a large wooden ship appeared, hovering in the air above the Void.

This Void Ship was clearly custom made, on the smaller side, at roughly 42 feet (12.8 meters) in length. It was crafted from dark black wood, with a wide wooden deck and a large, central mast. Fine wooden guardrails ran alongside the sides of the deck, while a main cabin was inset at the rear.

Micheal leapt aboard the ship, his Ki-enhanced muscles carrying him as he easily cleared the sides of the boat.

‘There’s the Till.’ He nodded as he inspected the vessel. Near the entrance to the cabin was a large Crystal Till, an Artifact that was found on nearly all Void Ships, used to steer the ship between the spatial currents that flowed all across the Third Layer.

Vice-Master Veryn had included a small written manual inside the Spatial Ring, explaining the functions and giving directions on how to direct the Void Ship. Micheal intended to read that, despite already being familiar with steering a Void Ship, after he settled in.

Micheal moved into the cabin – it was as he expected, a lavish, well-designed interior clearly made with no expense spared. This vessel was clearly intended for a wealthy explorer of some kind, commissioned from the highest quality of materials.

There were several rooms below deck, including a main study, a long hallway, storage space, and two spacious cabins. There was so much room, in fact, that Micheal realized the space inside this Void Ship was actually expanded, to some small degree, making it larger on the inside than it would’ve otherwise been.

It was a true treasure, and really highlighted to Micheal how dire their situation was – no Void Noble would ever willingly part ways with so finely made a Void Ship unless their lives were literally on the line.

Micheal set up shop in the study, pulling out a folder full of charts and maps that Dark Void had gifted him. He set out the papers alongside a large wooden table, lining up the route the scientists had picked out for him. They had plotted a full course he could travel through the Empty Sea, accounting for spatial currents and weather conditions ahead of time.

“I have time.” He muttered as he traced the distance he’d have to travel.

Dark Void’s scientists had poured over the ship’s manual while Micheal was preparing for the Ritual, accounting for the speed of the Void Ship he would be using. They had also written up a plan for the worst-case scenario, on how to traverse the Empty Sea relying purely on his flight-based Abilities, should his Void Ship fail.

The journey would only take 3 days – his Void Ship was top of the line for its size, and the route planned by Dark Void took advantage of several fast-paced spatial currents found in the Empty Sea.

That left him plenty of time, now, to prepare.

“One step at a time.” He talked to himself as he leaned back in the fine plush chair set next to the table.

He closed his eyes briefly, circulating his Ki as he entered a brief, pseudo-meditative state.

‘One step at a time.’

He opened his eyes again, keeping his Ki circulating as he pulled open the Void Ship’s manual, and began to read through it.

The hours slipped by as Micheal studied, familiarizing himself with the controls for this model of Void Ship, a ‘Waverider-Class,’ and the route he would take in the coming days.

Tonight, his past-self would obtain the Body of a Grandmaster and, not long after, make contact with Lux.

‘Tomorrow morning.’ Micheal nodded. There was no reason to delay.

‘I thought he was with you.’ That was what Rex had replied, when Micheal asked him about Lux – a statement most curious.

Once dawn had passed, he would activate the Kebler Crystal, and all would be revealed.

It was time to figure out how Lux fit into all of this.

.

Chapter 52


.

In a small, off-shoot alleyway in the southern half of Axellion, two furtive figures hid in the shadows, their forms obscured and almost invisible to the occasional passerby.

“Wouldn’t want to be on the wrong end of that, eh?” Rex nudged Lux through his Light Refraction Shroud, before pointing forward, out in front of them.

For, beyond the end of the alley they were standing in lay an enormous, gaping hole, in the grounds of Axellion.

The handiwork of Aaron Bartram, Commander of the Round Table.

“Bloke packs a punch, that’s for sure.” Rex continued, his enthusiasm unabated by Lux’s lack of response.

Lux shrugged, his thoughts distracted. In his right hand, he flipped a silver coin, a knor, one of the forms of currency used on the Third Layer, in-between his knuckles. On one side of the coin was the insignia of House Atlas, a shattered globe held together by a central staff, and on the other was the visage of Duke Atlas. Each City-State issued its own coinage, though they generally held the same value, a consensus formed over the centuries.

The silver coin flipped from knuckle to knuckle, tumbling across his hand as he controlled it absentmindedly.

‘That he does.’ Aaron Bartram possessed power that defied logic, making him one of the few individuals to have earned Constantine’s personal attention.

Constantine had introduced, recently, a new threat assessment system, color coded to indicate to which degree of danger an individual posed. The information had spread throughout his Seeds, a response to threats the control freak had faced on the higher Layers.

Aaron Batram’s Threat Assessment Rating, or TAR for short, was Indigo.

The second highest possible rating, indicating a unique individual capable of acts of mass destruction on a widespread scale, wherein suppressive options were highly limited.

It was a thought Lux mused as he stepped forward, getting a better look at the massive crater.

All around the crater, the employed Wizards of House Atlas were hard at work, moving large chunks of stone into place to replace the empty space. House Atlas had spared no expense as they worked to repair the massive crater – with the Founding Celebration right around the corner, such a mar on the landscape of Axellion was considered intolerable.

This was also why they were hiding in the alleyways – several of the rooftops of buildings surrounding the crater had been commandeered, as the Wizards worked to restore Axellion to its former state.

His enslaver didn’t want him to take any action against the White Knight – observation was their limit, for now – a side-project, while they stalled out in making headway on his main mission this morning.

‘To find Jay sol Arget.’

To gain his freedom.

“Think the Duke’ll have to help out? It’s a big hole.” Rex broke through Lux’s thoughts, nudging him with his elbow again.

Lux held back a sigh.

“Perhaps. Hard to tell, really.” He casually flicked his right hand, sending the coin sailing through the air behind him without looking.

With a quiet ping, the silver coin slammed into the wall of the building to his left, a millhouse of some sort. It bounced off a small crack in the mill’s wall, flipping through the air as it shot across the alley to the neighboring building.

Once it arrived, through sheer chance, the coin just so happened to collide with the edge of a thick wooden door, hitting it and ricocheting off that door’s corner at an odd angle, which sent it falling forward back towards the duo.

All of which led to…

thunk

“Oi! Ow!”

…the coin slamming into Rex’s left elbow, the same elbow he had nudged Lux with.

That impact caused the coin to flip over one last time, tumbling through the air before landing precisely on Lux’s open palm, heads facing up.

“Wait here, I’ll get a closer look.” Lux hid a smirk as he ignored Rex’s grumbling. The former Baron shot Lux a glare, nursing his elbow as he watched him leave the alley.

The street was almost deserted, with most onlookers being shooed away by the reconstruction crews hard at work. What few Void Natives were left failed to notice the slight blur in the air, as he carefully crossed the road, until he reached the edge of the crater.

‘It really is impressive.’ He stared down the massive hole, into the dark, endless Void beyond.

‘All that power, with a flick of his finger.’ Lux mused.

He couldn’t dare imagine what Constantine would do if he controlled someone like that.

And it was here, as he watched a pair of Wizards argue over gravitational stone placement…

He felt a faint pulse of energy emerge from his Spatial Ring.

His head snapped down as he stared at his hand, immediately ducking away from the crater. The energy pulse was incredibly faint, to the point that it was impossible to detect for anyone other than Lux – but the alert itself was incredibly unexpected.

‘Already?!’ Lux walked back to the alley that hid Rex, his eyes alight with a hint of excitement.

“Come along, Rex.” Lux gestured, dragging his companion down the alleyway.

“What’s got you so cheery?” Rex chuckled as he followed, giving up his injured elbow act – his Behemoth Predator Type Ability granted him incredibly dense skin.

Lux smiled.

“We've got a date with destiny.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Lux found himself on the outskirts of Axellion, far from the main central island that housed the City-State. They had left through the North Gate, traversing the floating islands that hovered in Axellion’s immediate vicinity.

Here on the outskirts, House Atlas had long-since forbidden any sort of construction of shanty towns or out-of-wall castle towns. These lands were protected, preserved in their natural state, to better showcase the jewel of the Atlas Duchy that was Axellion.

Lux and Rex made their way off the beaten path, using their Cloud Stepping Shoes to travel from floating island to island, ignoring the official Island Paths - those roadways were crowded with traffic, an influx of traffic into Axellion as less well-off merchants and travelers alike visited the City-State, in expectation of the impending Founding Celebration.

As they finally reached the island that Micheal and himself had set up as one of their rendezvous points, Lux’s eyes scanned their surroundings.

It was a quaint, non-descript island, with a small patch of trees and a few large, chunky boulders, alongside a large, open stone section. The boulders were well positioned, however, shielding parts of the island from view – and one of the reasons why Lux had picked this particular island, out of all the others.

‘Now what do we have here.’ A Deathless Clone split off from Lux as he walked around one particular boulder, the Clone moving to set up a perimeter as Lux and Rex walked past it.

As they turned the corner, out emerged a luxurious looking Void Ship, floating between the gap formed from two of the larger boulders, hovering above the empty Void.

‘Well, aren’t you a resourceful one.’ Lux flipped the coin he was carrying, snagging it in the air before it could fall as he eyed the ship.

“Hey-ho Captain, got room aboard?” Rex’s voice was boisterous as he walked up to the edge of the island, grinning widely.

Rex’s greeting garnered a response, as from the ship’s cabin emerged a cloaked figure.

Micheal Care – the ‘Seer.’

Threat Assessment Rating: Azure*

The third highest rating, with a *, denoting this rating derived some of its scale due to abnormalities about the subject – what made Micheal so dangerous wasn’t his Abilities or Conceptual prowess, as dangerous as a Grandmaster might be…

It was his knowledge.

“You’re… different.” Lux frowned, tensing as he noticed something strange.

He couldn’t tell how, he couldn’t tell why, he couldn’t even really denote the specific difference…

But something about Micheal had… changed.

Rex noticed the change in Lux’s posture instantly, his grin growing wolfish as he stared Micheal down, his gaze shifting to that of a predator.

Slowly, Micheal reached down to his Spatial Ring, keeping his hands clear and in view of Lux and Rex at all times. From that ring, he withdrew a Kebler Crystal, the exact same one Lux had just given Micheal last night.

“I am. A lot has happened, in a very short amount of time.” Micheal activated the Kebler Crystal and…

Lux’s frown eased as he pulled out his own Kebler Crystal, matching the resonance.

‘How curious.’ He laid a hand on Rex’s shoulder, calming his companion down, as Micheal turned around.

“Come aboard. We have a lot to talk about.” Micheal’s words echoed in the early morning air as he returned to the ship’s cabin.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“You’ve travelled backwards up the Loop.”

Lux stared at Micheal, his mouth open in astonishment as he finished listening to the tale Micheal had laid out.

They were sitting inside a large study, larger than seemed possible, given the dimensions of the ship. Several bookshelves filled with books lined the walls of the room, while a large blackwood table occupied the center, surrounded by a set of fine chairs. The room was warmly lit, by a pair of well placed, glowing orange crystals, inset into the roof.

The trio sat around the table, one that was covered in charts and maps.

“That- that…” Lux stuttered before coming to a pause, his eyes narrowing as he studied Micheal.

“That does explain it.” He realized.

That faint ‘odd’ sensation, the feeling that something was wrong, was a feeling Lux had felt thanks to his Luckstrider Type.

‘His Causality is distorted.’ Lux made the connection.

His Luckstrider Type gave him a powerful connection to the Concept of Causality – however, that esoteric connection was something inherent, it wasn’t something he could actively control or utilize. In the first place, the Concept of Causality was an incredibly difficult Conceptual Power to touch upon, according to what Constantine claimed about the higher Layers.

Still, through that connection, he had a general awareness of any anomalies in Time – it was also why he was so willing to accept the explanation that they were trapped in a Time Loop. Something had always felt subtly off, at some point after arriving on the Third Layer.

“So right now, there’s another you, running around.” Lux continued, as he slowly raised his Kebler Crystal up, examining it.

“Precisely. And that’s why you need to avoid replying to me with your Kebler Crystal.” Micheal held up his own,

“Right now, yours is linked to not just this crystal, but also the crystal held by my past, or for you, present self.”

Lux slowly nodded. The signals they had hashed out last night, or well, about a week ago for this version of Micheal, could function both ways. It just so happened, in this case, that Lux had decided to show up in person, opting not to reply through his Kebler Crystal.

There wasn't any grand reason behind that decision... he just felt like showing up, unannounced, for the vibe - and yet, it seemed to have all worked out in his favor.

Lucky him.

Rex squinted his eyes as he looked between the crystals, before grunting and shrugging.

“I see.” Lux offered, flipping a coin from knuckle to knuckle.

“So now, I suppose, the question remains.” Lux leaned forward, his eyes quirking as he opined dramatically,

“Why contact us? Or, to be specific…” Lux continued,

“What do you need our help for?” He cut to the chase.

Micheal paused as he heard Lux’s response, drumming his fingers on the table.

The man was disciplined, Lux noted, not letting his emotions affect his physical state – talking to Micheal felt like talking to a brick wall, with how stoic and calm the man presented himself.

However, if there was one thing Lux had learned, in managing the Beasts of Providence, in controlling and directing so many different people – it was the small things that gave away a person’s inner beliefs.

The way Micheal held his jaw, the tightness in his eyes, the tension in his arms – it painted a portrait of a man who, very clearly, did not trust them – a man forced to do something he’d rather not.

‘Smart fella.’ Lux would’ve complimented him, if he could’ve – alas, showcasing such disunity was an action Constantine wouldn’t tolerate.

Lux had more freedom than others, able to cognize the influence of the Seed – but he never truly was free of it. It was an insidious, always present thing, invisible to him for all intents and purposes, yet always hovering, in the back of his mind and Soul.

“I need your help. Not just you, but the cooperation of those behind you as well.” Micheal finally said, as his drumming fingers fell still.

“I’ve returned to the past because we’ve discovered Jay sol Arget’s plans…” Micheal continued, his voice dour,

“…and witnessed the catastrophic consequences, should we fail to stop them.”

Those words had Lux sitting up slightly, his gaze sharpening.

“Explain.” He felt something shift within him.

‘He’s watching.’

“Jay sol Arget’s attack on the Founding Celebration is a distraction. A feint, a plan he discarded after it failed to bear fruit over countless Loops.” Micheal replied as he tapped on one particular chart, a map of the spatial currents that flowed within the Empty Sea.

“His true target is here.” Micheal’s finger landed on the center of the Empty Sea, at a place labelled ‘The Nexus.’

“He’s planning on sinking the entire Third Layer, and geocoding this entire Plane out of existence.”

You could hear a pin drop, in the stunned silence that followed Micheal’s revelation. Lux felt his adrenaline spike as he processed what he’d heard.

Before he could reply, however…

Next to him, Rex’s body stiffened. A second later, his companion’s eyes almost seemed to glaze over as he raised his right hand up and…

He began to tap on the air.

Micheal’s gaze snapped towards Rex, the tension in the air rising, as he recognized the tell-tale signs of someone accessing the Shop.

Lux held out a hand, making a beckoning motion as he turned to stare at Rex.

He tried to speak – and he failed.

He held back a flinch.

Constantine rarely made his influence so visible.

Finally, Rex finished tapping on the air, as a small, blue Artifact appeared in his hands – an Artifact Rex set down on the table. It was shaped like a block, with a large dark blue circle set on top of it.

Rex tapped that blue button, causing his eyes to glow with blue light.

And then…

A small, floating white hologram appeared, flickering into the air above the box, showing the vague figure of a human.

A man Lux recognized instantly.

Him.

“Hello, Micheal.” Constantine Lancaster’s voice was deep and controlled as he spoke, his hologram figure zooming in on a close-up of his chest and head,

“I thought it best if we talked face to face.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

It was him.

Micheal stared at the flickering image, his mind racing, as he sat face to face with none other than Constantine Lancaster, the Vile King himself.

'How is he communicating from a higher Layer?' As far as Micheal knew, it was close to impossible to pass messages down the Layers – and he didn't think Constantine would still be here on the Third.

'It has to be something he figured out through his Seeds.' He recognized the Artifact Rex had placed down, a Hologram Projector – it didn't have any communicative properties.

“You said Jay sol Arget plans on wiping out the entire Third Layer?” To his surprise, there was no posturing or threats – the Vile King dived straight into the meat of the matter.

“Yes.” Micheal replied, forcibly controlling his emotions. He would not let this intrusion get under his skin – that would only play into whatever Constantine’s intentions were.

He paused for only a moment, before he made his decision.

If there was one thing he could trust Constantine on – it was that the man, in his sick twisted way, wanted what was best for mankind.

‘The enemy of my enemy is my friend.’

“By destabilizing the Nexus, he ruptures the spatial plane that the Third Layer rests upon, sending all its floating islands cascading down into the Void.” Micheal explained.

Micheal then launched into the explanation that Marco had given him, showing Constantine the Artifact Marco had said would stabilize the Nexus, and explaining the time-frame he had to work with.

Constantine’s vague, flickering figure held still throughout the explanation, listening quietly.

Finally, when Micheal finished, the Vile King held a hand up.

“Do you have anything, here and now, you can offer as proof, to prove that you have truly travelled to the past, and that this isn’t some sort of ploy?” Constantine asked,

“Direct Time-Travel backwards has proven to be… impossible in my research… though perhaps, you would know more about that then I.” The Vile King tilted his head to the side casually as he finished.

Micheal’s eyes narrowed.

‘He suspects.’ Micheal knew his claims of being a Seer would ring hollow, at some point, as the sheer breadth of information he spread became apparent.

However…

‘Whatever.’ He would deny it all the same – there was no need to confirm such dangerous suspicions.

In the higher Layers, while there were several Titled Deities that caused havoc among mankind, there were also many Deities that did not – like Kivos and his Door Society on the Fifth Layer, or Queen Iz of the Prometheans on the Sixth Layer.

Being labelled a Time Traveler would put a huge target on his back.

Micheal redirected his thoughts to the present, pondering Constantine’s request briefly, before tapping his Spatial Ring.

With a plop, Micheal pulled out and set the head of the God-Emperor of Kalos on the table, clearing a space to avoid damaging the maps and charts.

The high density of Mana within the Kalosian’s flesh had kept his head perfectly preserved, in all its regal, very dead glory. The two black orbs that made up Kyvenval’s eyes glimmered ominously in the warm light.

“This is the head of Kyvenval, God-Emperor of Kalos.” Micheal began, but was cut off as Constantine’s flickering form raised up a hand.

“I recognize it.” The God-Emperor was a known entity, apparently, to the forces of the Vile King.

“This suffices.” Constantine’s head shifted as he glanced to the side, at something out of sight, before turning back to face Micheal.

“However.” The Vile King began, his vague figure flickering.

“I find your plan to ride into the Empty Sea and take on this Deity single-handedly…” Constantine shook his head.

“Unacceptable.”

Micheal frowned.

“I can’t risk-“ Again, he was cut off, as Constantine preempted him.

“Yes, we cannot risk making contact with your allies, not with Jay sol Arget’s Clones lurking about.” Constantine retorted, continuing,

“I trust your intentions, Micheal, but I will not leave the fate of humanity resting upon a single man’s shoulders.” He went on.

“I’m listening.” Micheal replied, forcing himself to not tap his fingers on the table as a sort of nervous tension filled him.

‘Don’t show any weakness.’ Men like Constantine respected one thing, and one thing only – competence.

Soon, their discussion broke down into a debate, a back and forth as Constantine raised questions about the future, and Micheal carefully chose his answers. He walked a fine line, telling the truth where it mattered, without necessarily revealing everything he knew.

It was fine to share what was relevant to the situation, especially information about Jay sol Arget – but the secrets of Dark Void, or the Round Table… knowledge like that, was better left in hands more trustworthy.

“If you can have your men create their own version of an Artifact to stabilize the Nexus, I’m all for it.” Micheal eventually cut in, his voice clipped.

“I trust this to work.” He held up the device created by Dark Void – while he might not fully understand how it worked, not the truly intricate details beyond what Marco had explained, he believed in their handiwork, the reputation they built in the future one more ironclad than any other.

Constantine let out a long-suffering sigh, before dropping this point of contention.

And then, of all things, the conversation drifted as the Vile King made a display of trust, revealing information that Micheal had never heard of in the first timeline, as they adjusted Micheal’s gameplan on the fly.

“An entire transportation network, hidden in the sky.” Micheal sat there, stunned for a brief moment, before he controlled his expression.

Through the use of the ‘Causeway Network,’ Constantine offered to drastically shorten the time it would take to reach the Nexus, reducing a journey of multiple days down to a single day.

More than anything else, it was this show of trust that truly caught Micheal off-guard.

‘What does he want?’ It was almost disconcerting. What was the benefit, in sharing such knowledge with him? The sheer fact that the Vile King was able to create such a massive infrastructure project on the Third Layer, and have it remain undetected in the first timeline alone was already a marvel in and of itself – sharing that knowledge with Micheal, well…

It didn’t match the image he had, of the Vile King, in his mind.

Eventually, their conversation turned, as the duo made plans and plans alike, discussing backup plans and how they would approach Jay sol Arget.

Finally, Micheal drew up the last point he had to make, and the reason he had called upon Lux in the first place.

“There’s one more thing, something that must be done, to ensure my past self can travel to the past in the first place.” Micheal began as he turned away from Constantine’s hologram, and gave Lux a small nod.

“We need to plan a heist.”

.
