Chapter 53


.

In a dimension cut off from the lower Layers there existed a shattered husk of a world once whole. The surface of this world was littered with gaping craters and enormous holes where great gouts of magma spurted, sending huge cliffs of rock cascading into an ever-widening series of mass collapses.

In this ruined world, there existed one location, one area of the planet that still stood tall – a large, black mountain, surrounded by a series of plains that had yet to collapse.

At the peak of this mountain sat a human, legs crossed as he rested upon a rocky outcropping, deep in meditation.

Constantine Lancaster sat shirtless, dressed in a pair of simple black pants, barefoot as he breathed in and out. His body was taut, packed with muscles drawn tight with tension, lean and prepared. The only ornaments he wore were the many rings adorning his fingers, each with a specific purpose of their own. Sweat dripped down his forehead as he focused, in solitude, alone.

His grand ritual to harvest the energy of an entire world had proven a resounding success.

He had undergone a qualitative transformation.

Now, running up and down his flesh were dozens of bright violet lines of energy, infused within his very skin, a part of his body as much as his arms or legs. Upon his head rested a crown of purple energy, with small spikes of power rupturing upward as he concentrated. A vast, rich violet Aura surrounded Constantine, as the excess of energy he now contained leaked outward, staining the very air.

“The game has changed.”

Slowly, Constantine let out a long exhale, his eyes opening. Two purple bursts of energy shot free from his eyes as he opened them, energy lasers that were cut short as the Vile King frowned, regaining control.

“I must find balance.” He nodded firmly. It would take time, for him to fully stabilize this transformation.

The ritual had leeched away an enormous amount of energy from this planet’s core, destabilizing the world and causing it to begin collapsing in on itself.

The results, however, spoke for themselves.

It wasn’t Ki that filled his body, nor Mana, or Chakra, or any other typical form of energy cultivated by powerful beings on the higher Layers.

No… what ran inside his flesh, transforming not just his body but also his Soul, was none other than raw Elemental Energy.

Elemental Energy made up the building blocks of reality in the 7 Layers. At its core, it served as the fundamental bedrock of all energy.

Ki itself, if broken down to its base elements, was formed from Elemental Energy.

Like breaking down an Atom to form Protons, Neutrons, and Electrons, nearly all types of energy could be broken down into complex forms of Elemental Energy.

Constantine held out his right hand, forming a mass of purple energy that hovered in the air, just a few inches above his hand.

In a blink of an eye, that purple energy shifted – in one moment, Constantine held a ball of blazing red fire, in the next, it was crackling lightning condensed into an orb, and the next, a spiked globe of twisting ice.

Almost all forms of Elemental Energy were aspected, the energy tied to one Concept or another. From the Elemental Lightning channeled by Orion Thunderfist, to Elemental Fire or Elemental Ice – further subtypes existed, thousands of different variations of Elemental Energy, from Steady Stone to Retrolightning to Subice.

If there was one rule that was constant with most forms of Elemental Energy – it was that once an aspect had been chosen, that grouping of Elemental Energy typically maintained that aspect consistently. Elemental Lightning, once formed, stayed as Elemental Lightning.

This was why more complex combinations of Elemental Energy, like Ki or Mana, never broke down into their base energies.

“Good. My control has grown.” Constantine smiled as he returned the shifting mass of energy back to its original, violet base. The orb of power writhed, sometimes appearing like a mass of purple flames, while other times appearing like a spiked ball of violet ice.

‘The modifications to my Physique has stabilized the energy within me.’ The Vile King nodded to himself as he let go of the purple energy, watching it fizzle out. He then tapped on a Spatial Ring on his right hand, bringing out and donning an emerald bracelet - a Ro Energy Band, an Artifact that could store Elemental Energy.

The Ritual Constantine had performed not only wrought into existence an extraordinary amount of Elemental Energy, but it also refined his Physique, inspired by the records and data his Seeds had gathered about the Dark Wraiths that had inhabited the Second Layer.

And now… with his genetic and physical makeup completely redefined, his body and Soul served as a conduit, letting him channel an immense amount of Elemental Energy, turning his very body into an enormous storage hold, where a veritable sea of raw power constantly circulated.

It was a rare type of Elemental Energy he now channeled, one connected to an esoteric Conceptual Power that was considered, on the higher Layers, to be among the most powerful:

Elemental Chaos.

Constantine slowly stood up, his eyes glazing slightly as he rapidly cycled through reports and viewpoints from a dozen different Seeds.

He had finally recovered from his conversation with Micheal.

Projecting his full control directly onto his Seed had proven incredibly taxing – he had managed a sort of pseudo-direct control, using a Hologram Projector to emulate a real-time conversation, but the sheer energy drain was only possible thanks to the enormous sea of Elemental Energy flowing within his veins and his transformed Physique, which allowed him to harness that energy.

“You catch more flies with honey than you do with vinegar.” Constantine smiled slightly to himself as he rubbed his eyes – he’d been left with little time to rest, in recent days.

That conversation had proven to be, in his opinion, a success.

He had thoroughly analyzed Micheal’s character profile, even assigning a small department of his Seeds to behavioral analysis, to go over their every interaction, every observation, building up a detailed breakdown just to confirm his own conclusions.

The core issue he had with Micheal, was that the man would simply never trust him, and because of that – the information he possessed would be jealously guarded, with little shared freely.

What he had shared, however, had already proven the immense value of the knowledge contained within his mind.

Jay sol Arget.

Bosmond Jingleton.

Sion Swordsoul.

Ashroth.

Navir.

Five names, descriptions, powersets, and future interactions, showcasing how they devastated humanity.

Three of which, his Seeds had already located and begun to analyze. One of which… he had already encountered.

‘He even shared information about my potential demise or disappearance, at the hands of the Titled Deity Bosmond Jingleton.’

It was this disclosure, beyond all others, that had solidified his opinion of Micheal.

He was a man who could be reasoned with.

‘What I need is not his trust.’ Constantine had decided, adapting to the reality of the situation.

‘All I need is his willing cooperation.’ And the first steps to achieve that were simple.

Prove that he was not an unreasonable monster, and show that he had mankind’s best interests at heart, even if their philosophy on how to achieve those goals might differ wildly.

The first step was easy: offer Lux, a man Micheal seemed to respect immensely, a path to freedom – and have Lux ask for Micheal’s help in achieving that.

The thought had been easy enough to plant.

Lux had a stubborn pride to him, one that made him reluctant to ask others for aid – a simple nudge was all it took, however, reframing the decision to be one borne out of necessity, for his mission - a thought Lux would assume was his own.

‘It helps that my intentions are genuine.’ He would free Lux – there was no scheme here.

His psych profile of Micheal made that very clear – any betrayal here would permanently sunder any hopes he might have for future cooperation.

The second step was even easier – show genuine intent in helping mankind, to the point of exposing his own ‘weaknesses.’

The Causeway Network had been an immense undertaking, and sharing its existence with Micheal had not been an easy decision.

Of course, Micheal had no way to know, that the moment he made that decision, Constantine had already decided to parlay the existence of the Causeway Network as a point of interaction and cooperation with the Round Table. Aaron Bartram had gathered quite the fighting force, establishing a significant human presence on the Third Layer, all entirely independent of Constantine’s influence.

It was exactly that kind of proactive human teamwork and growth that Constantine pushed for.

“The game has changed, but it’s also still the same.” The Vile King allowed himself a small smile.

‘I’ll need to reroute the Revolutionaries.’ Constantine’s eyes glowed as he activated his Empyrean Soul Root, getting to work.

“Choice is an illusion.” He muttered to himself as he directed his Seeds, sending hundreds of men and women into action.

“Freedom is a lie.” The only thing that mattered in the 7 Layers was power.

The game was afoot, and as long as Constantine Lancaster was still standing…

Humanity would keep playing.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Time.

It was a strange conundrum Micheal found himself in.

“Hurry up and wait... again.” He chuckled as he sat down, secluded in the cabin of his Void Ship, officially named ‘The Serenity’ if he went by what was painted onto its bow.

He had flown up to the sky, witnessing firsthand the massive rings of energy that formed the Causeway Network. It was an ingenious invention, taking advantage of one of the unique properties all Void Ships possessed.

Nearly all Void Ships possessed a Crystal Till, an Artifact that allowed the ships to float in space, hovering and traversing along unseen spatial currents. A side-effect of the function of these Spatial Artifacts was that every Void Ship was coated in a faint Spatial Barrier while moving – this barrier absorbed currents of wind, converting it into energy to propel the ship forward.

The Causeway Network took advantage of this Spatial Barrier, creating enormous storms of wind to propel Void Ships at absurd speeds.

Each ring was split into two corridors down the middle, one where the wind blew forward, and one where it blew in the other direction, allowing for travel either way along the network.

A few hours of practice was all it took for Micheal to knock the rust off, remastering Void Ship sailing.

The experience brought back memories, several years into the first timeline.

The Great War Between Races was still fresh in their minds when he and Shin had climbed up to the Third Layer. Even that couldn’t have prepared them, however, for what was to come.

The sheer chaos of the Rush, where billions and billions of sentients crowded into the Third Layer was a sight in its own right.

‘I suppose I shouldn’t complain too much.’ Micheal thought ruefully.

That chaos had seen Micheal make an elective decision, joining up with a mercantile human Knight Company – the Knights of the Bright Island. It was there he learned how to steer a Crystal Till, back when he was desperate for any scrap of knowledge he could find.

‘I wonder where Dmitri is now?’

Dmitri was a Ukrainian Swordmaster and the Captain of the Knights of the Bright Island. He was a hard man, a Second Waver who spent several years training with an obscure Byren Master on the Second Layer, before climbing up to the Third.

“He’s probably still training, tucked away somewhere on the Second Layer.” Micheal reasoned, chuckling.

At the start of the Great War Between Races, in the chaos that unfolded, one of Dmitri's comrades, a fellow Ukrainian he had met on the First Layer, had been murdered by a serial killer, one of the deranged humans who only saw their fellow man as Points for the Shop.

That had been the impetus for Dmitri to leave the Second Layer, as he sought to hunt down his comrade's killer. He never did find him, though that was through no fault of his own - the sheer scale and breadth of the Third Layer in the midst of the Rush was simply incomprehensible.

However…

‘With Orion out of the picture, and the Farians on our side, there won’t be a Great War.’

For all Micheal knew, Dmitri might stay on the Second Layer for several more years now.

‘He’s earned it.’ Though this timeline’s version of Dmitri might not know it, the gruff tips and advice the curt Swordmaster had offered him had proven invaluable in Micheal’s growth.

‘Better that than dying to a Void Predator.’ It was a sore point Micheal held from the first timeline – wherein he obtained Mastery just in time to save himself, but too late to save the rest of his team.

While he wouldn’t exactly call himself friends with Dmitri – there was a rough respect, an understanding between the two of them. They were companions, fighting on the same side, just to survive in this hellscape that was the 7 Layers.

‘Keep kickin’ it.’ Micheal’s smile slowly faded as he centered himself.

“A symphony of control.” Micheal uttered, repeating the phrase Bastien had used to describe his Grandmaster Sword Energy.

‘7 forms of energy, controlled all at once – that is what I need to touch upon the Concept of Energy.’ According to Eon’s writing.

Slowly, Micheal raised a hand up, to just below his right eye.

‘Eyes of the Deep.’ Micheal activated his Ability.

Within his eyes gathered a soft, pure energy, cool and relaxing.

This was a manipulated form of Divine Energy.

Divine Energy, as far as Micheal knew, acted just like Ki, for all intents and purposes. The differences between the two energies had always appeared superficial, at least to his understanding.

Ki was warm, while Divine Energy was cool – but they both functioned almost identically.

Merely, races which had Ascended and become Deities just so happened to be born with Lord-Tier Ki, or Lord-Tier Divine Energy if you were a pedant, giving them an enormous head start.

‘What’s the difference between you two?’ Micheal thought as he pondered the sensation.

‘I have access to the Titles System now, I can basically be considered a pseudo-Deity.’ Micheal once more praised whatever being it was that created the Shop, and left behind the various rewards mankind could obtain on the First Layer.

‘As long as I have this Ability, and the Titles System, theoretically… I should be able to control Divine Energy.’ He hadn’t heard of any Deities that trained both Ki and Divine Energy, but he had heard of Deities training Divine Energy and Mana.

“Reaching the Nexus is now a journey that can be measured in hours.” He spoke out loud,

“I have several days until then.” He smiled.

‘Hurry up and wait, indeed.’

And so…

Tucked away, in a corner of the world Jay sol Arget would never think to search, Micheal began his cultivation journey anew.

Day changed to night, and night unto day. Time slipped by, as preparations were made, plans plotted out, and schemes carried forth.

The river of time marched ever onward, unceasing in its flow as it carried forth the tides of the future.

And now…

For the second time…

.

1 day remained, until the Founding Celebration.

.

Chapter 54


.

Yamamura Kouko moved across the rooftops of Castle Atlas in the dead of night, her footsteps supernaturally silent.

The slim, 5 foot 4 (162.5 cm) Japanese rock climber found herself at home as she stealthily clambered alongside edged shingles and past sealed-off windows. She kept her body close to the walls, not particularly worried about being spotted, for…

Her body was entirely transparent, from her black skintight Shadow Bodysuit and Aura Nullification Necklace to her skin, bones, muscles and even blood – a power granted by the Transparent Form Ability, a superpower purchasable in the Shop for 1,870,585 Points.

It was a relatively expensive Ability, one that only granted the user the ability to turn their body and clothes transparent – it wasn’t quite full invisibility, but as long as the Ability user moved slowly, the difference was minimal.

As Kouko moved around a set of precariously placed shingles, a piece of rock debris that had been tucked under a loose shingle slipped free – some of the aftermath from Barsoth’s rampage several days ago.

Kouko froze as she watched the rock fall, and then smash against the wall, before bouncing down and landing in a pile of bushes down below.

None of this made any amount of noise whatsoever, the rock’s clattering and fall eerily silent. Not even a rustle came from the bushes as they shifted, silently shaking.

Kouko wasn’t surprised by this – after all…

Kouko was the Revolutionaries’ leading covert extraction specialist – with 5 of her 7 Abilities centered around stealth and covert operation.

She was a proud member of the Revolutionaries, fiercely loyal and devoted to their mission. They were the premier fighting force, fighting for humanity’s rights here on the Third Layer, after all – in her eyes, there was no group more worthy. In them, she had found a home.

Her Silence Field Ability muted anything that came within a certain range of her body. Her Ability also temporarily spread that Silence Field alongside anything that left her presence, lasting for several seconds. It was a perfect choice for stealth, though it was vulnerable to energy disruption.

It only took a few more minutes for her to cross across the rooftops until she reached her target’s room – the location that the Fortune Teller’s Division had pinpointed, confirmed by the Revolutionaries own on-the-ground investigation squad.

The guest quarters housing Eon, the King of Heroes.

The famous Void Noble had requested a small private room, in lieu of the grand guest quarters offered by Duke Atlas. The Revolutionaries profile had painted Eon as an eccentric, but powerful figure, who must be treated with the utmost caution.

Kouko knelt down silently above the rooftop leading to Eon’s room, her movements unnaturally still and controlled – a side effect of the Mind-Body Planner Ability, a power that let her ‘route’ her body ahead of time, moving perfectly without room for error.

And then…

Kouko’s body began to float downwards, descending through the roof itself as she phased through reality – an aspect of her Type Ability, the Ghyst Body Type, a Limited Type Ability that let her turn her body into a phantasmal form that, while not invisible, was intangible, able to move through not just physical matter, but also fields of energy, Wards, and just about anything.

It took just a few short moments before she appeared, translucent and slowly falling, within Eon’s sleeping quarters.

The room was dark, with a large grand bed, a small table with two chairs, and a set of dressers and cabinets along the walls.

Eon sat cross-legged on the bed, his eyes shut as he half-rested, half-meditated. The King of Heroes, even in his stillness, had a certain presence to him, a faint, invisible Aura of greatness that drew the eye.

Kouko ignored all of that, her eyes on the target directly below her.

A long, thin, wooden box, leaning against the wall opposite Eon’s bed. It rested alongside a cloak stand and a small cabinet, near the entrance to the door leading to the foyer of this guest suite.

She began to fall.

As she fell, she held her breath, shifting her hand slightly to line up exactly where the wooden box would be in a few split seconds.

The fifth and final stealth Ability she possessed, Null Intent, was already active. The Ability had some heavy drawbacks but the power itself was a huge complement to her toolkit – in exchange for cutting off her ability to connect with Conceptual Powers, everything about her, from her intent, to her movements, to her Aura, to her physical presence was ‘dampened.’

It was similar, in a way, to the report she had been given about the power Endwalkers possessed, though to a much lesser extent.

Those split seconds passed and she arrived, falling through the air, just a bare half-inch away from the wooden box.

For a tiny, small fraction of a second, she deactivated her Ghyst Body Type, materializing in the real world.

She was still transparent, surrounded by a field of utter silence, her body perfectly controlled as her hand reached out and grasped onto the box holding Stratos, the Spear of Time.

She didn’t make any noise, her presence so muted as to be unnoticeable to all but the most stringent of scans.

This heist had been thoroughly labbed out, with the full force of the Revolutionaries’ Research Squad and the Fortune Teller Division – detection at all should’ve been impossible, no matter how famous or powerful Eon might be.

And yet…

In that tiny moment where Kouko materialized…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The King of Heroes was deep in meditation, circulating Mana as he examined the progress of his Perfected Mana Heart – the sixth stage to Mana Heart cultivation, viewed by the denizens of the Shattered Plane as the final Mana Heart stage.

‘Ignorant.’ It was how he viewed Void Nobles – sure, their mastery of Magic was somewhat advanced, but when it came to the refinement of Mana Hearts, their warriors were sorely lacking.

Eon cultivated the Starbound Fantasy Mana Breathing Method – it was a Mana Breathing Method of his own creation, designed to perfectly refine his body and Soul to handle the impetus of the Dream.

This was a complete Mana Breathing Method that, if given enough time, would allow Eon to achieve the highest culmination of a Mana Heart that he currently possessed knowledge of:

The Eighth Stage – a Mana Throne.

In the many, many lives that he had lived, he had only ever managed to achieve that Stage four times. It was incredibly difficult, time-consuming, and the work of centuries, not decades, largely dependent on the Physique he was born with.

‘Patience, Eon. The path to power is long and arduous.’ He held back a sigh, before donning a small, relaxed smile.

Now that he was here in Axellion, the memories were nostalgic.

This was where Sylee Atlas, the first friend he made in this life, was born and raised. It brought a smile to his face, and made his time here incredibly relaxing, as he finally let loose, pleased at seeing how grand the City-State had grown under her nephew’s-

Eon noticed a shift in the currents of air.

It was an incredibly faint difference, so small, even Micheal, who possessed the enhanced Body of a Grandmaster, would barely have picked up on it – a tiny change in the currents of the otherwise still room, on the periphery of Eon’s enhanced senses.

However…

That difference was enough.

Eon’s intuition was borne from dozens of lives full of conflict, trials, and tribulations, supernaturally empowered by the single most powerful Soul present here on the Third Layer – and in that moment, even as he was caught off guard...

His intuition burned.

Eon didn’t think – he moved.

The air around him exploded into motion as he lunged forward, his eyes glowing blue as Mana gathered within him. In the same breath, he used a technique he liked to call ‘the Daydream’ – wherein he drew upon a small amount of the power of the Dream, at a time when he was unwilling to fully descend the Dream upon his surroundings.

His right fist slammed forward, utilizing the Borreal Fist, the martial arts of the Royal Guard for the Hirui Autarchy, a powerful martial-arts focused society from his 22nd life that existed on a High Energy World. This punching technique involved wrapping Mana around one’s fist in a specific way, creating an impact that would shatter the air in a localized shockwave.

In that same movement, he utilized the Dream to prevent the shockwave from spreading beyond his room.

And…

He hit nothing?

It was strange – he felt his fist collide, empowered as he utilized the Dream, sectioning off a tiny part of reality with a singular focus – that his blow would land.

However… it felt as though he was punching air, or something intransient.

“What?” Eon’s hand twitched as he ignored the sudden storm of wind that had flung the table and chairs into disarray, knocking over the dresser and nearly flipping his bed. With a casual wave and application of the Dream, he forced the world around him to return to its previous state, leaving the room just as it had been.

He then let go of the Daydream, before it burned anymore Lines. He would have to meditate for at least half an hour, just to recover from this small usage – the Daydream was an expensive technique.

Eon stared down at his fist, and then at the empty space before him.

An empty space on the wall, next to the coat stand.

The King of Heroes' pulse throbbed as he knelt down.

On the ground where he had leaned Stratos before sitting down to meditate was a small piece of black cloth, an article of clothing that dissipated, turning into nothing and vanishing as it left his hand.

The air around Eon trembled as a wave of anger crashed through him, a realization settling upon his shoulders.

For the first time in eight lives and counting...

He had been robbed.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Yamamura Kouko saw stars as she fell through the ground, her body returned to its phantasmal mode as she continued her downward journey. She phased through the floor of Eon’s room, down through a section of open hallway below, through a set of stone pillars, through a servants corridor, past the back half of the Duke’s public cellars, and finally, into the bedrock of the floating island that Castle Atlas itself rested upon.

It was supposed to be the perfect heist.

That thought kept circling through her head as she barely held on to her consciousness, forcing herself to remain focused.

Every time her mind tried to shift into panic, her thoughts were redirected.

Anywhere but towards the gaping hole that had shattered through the right side of her chest. Her mind was woozy as she floated down, the only thing keeping her alive the fact that she had suffered the injury while she was in her phantasmal state.

‘How did he hit me?’ She thought, in a stupor. In her phantasmal state, she was virtually immune to almost everything.

The answers to that question eluded her as she abseiled through the solid rock, falling through the ground at a steady rate. Time seemed to drag by as she forced herself to remain focused, her mind refusing to let her injuries get the best of her.

Until…

She emerged from the stone, finally finishing phasing through the floating island that held Axellion.

As soon as her vision cleared, she transformed out of her ghostly state and landed right into the waiting hands of a fully staffed Void Ship.

“Medical team, get on her now!”

“Wizards, use Healing Hands!”

“Healing Pills, have her swallow them!!”

The perfect heist, it was not, but Kouko smiled regardless, as blackness took her, the wooden box holding Stratos slipping free from her hands.

Mission accomplished.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Strike Team 1 and 2 will operate to support the package carrier, and shield him while he delivers the package.” A gruff, masked man, dressed in full black leather armor, stood upon the center of a large Void Ship, easily twice as big as The Serenity, floating several dozen miles away from Axellion, in the middle of a barren stretch of islands. He was a large man, with black skin visible in the gaps between his armor, heavily built, standing at least 7 feet (213 cm) tall.

He was addressing a large number of figures, various men and women, all dressed in similar getups – dark black leather armor, some armored with metal scale armor over the leather, while others stuck to simple leathers.

‘It’s an impressive show of force.’ Micheal recognized it for what it was as he leaned against the rail of the ship. Beside him was Lux, who was also watching just a few meters to his right.

There must’ve been at least 40 people present, all Seeded and under Constantine’s direct control. It was somewhat unsettling, witnessing the way the group sometimes coordinated in unison, as Constantine made no effort to hide his influence. The Vile King had a personal, overriding interest in the success of this mission.

‘I suppose that’s good.’ If nothing else, it meant he could rely on them. Hopefully.

“Strike Team 3 will cooperate with the contingent from the Research Squad, and the team dispatched from the Fortune Teller Division.”

Micheal’s eyes narrowed – Constantine was making no efforts to shield the inner workings of his Seeds from him.

It was yet another display of trust – that, or perhaps he simply didn’t care what Micheal saw. That conclusion didn’t feel like it matched Constantine’s character, however.

‘Whatever.’ He shook the thought from his mind, focusing on the present.

“We’ve obtained the Spear of Time. Lux, you’ll be carrying it.”

A new voice caught Micheal’s awareness as he saw none other than Hayden Montacerry appear on deck, emerging from a cloud of warping shadows. In his hands was a long, thin wooden box.

“The other Teams will remain behind in Axellion with me, to handle unexpected variables-” Hayden began as he walked towards Lux, but was cut off as-

“The Spear of Time is coming with us?” Micheal interrupted.

As one, the eyes of everyone present turned to look at Micheal. He didn’t flinch – if he was the type to fold to pressure like that, he wouldn’t have made it as far as he did in the 7 Layers.

“Yes.” The Curse Magician turned his gaze towards Micheal, a faint twinkle in his eyes.

He didn’t offer any explanation, which caused Micheal to take a small step forward. To show weakness here was unacceptable – men like Constantine would eat him alive at the slightest slip.

Instantly, the tension in the air shot upward.

However, before anything could happen, one of the black leather-wearing figures stepped forward. The man wasn’t masked, revealing a middle-aged white man with balding hair. There was an Aura about him, an air of vitality that belied his apparent age.

“We have no ways to confirm the authenticity of your device.” The man spoke, not introducing himself.

‘A member of the Research Squad?’ Micheal derived, using context clues.

“The Spear comes with us as a backup option, for a solution we’ve proposed, in the case your device fails.” The researcher continued,

“It’s not that we do not trust you. We simply cannot afford to take risks.” The man finished, giving Micheal a polite nod.

“The Spear needs to be placed in my guest quarters, back in Axellion, to maintain the timeline.” Micheal returned, his voice placid.

The researcher nodded.

“We’ve accounted for that. We have a method to return the Spear, with a relay network that will allow us to transport it rapidly across the Layer. Even in the worst-case scenario, we should have more than enough time to see it placed where it needs to be.”

Micheal frowned as he considered the man’s reply, his mind racing.

‘I can’t do everything.’ He held back a sigh as he slowly nodded.

“Then I’ll be relying on you.” He watched as Hayden handed Lux the wooden box.

Constantine was showing a great deal of trust in him – it was only fair, that he displayed at least some degree of trust back, when it came to working together.

The nameless commander of the mission continued to direct the three Strike teams and other forces of the Vile King. Soon, he finished his directions and the ship began to set into motion, as the men and women manning it prepared to bring it up to height, to enter the Causeway Network.

“Best of luck out there, fellas.” Hayden remarked as he gave Micheal a friendly wave,

“Kill that dodgy bloke till he’s dead for me, will ya?” There was a barely disguised hint of venom behind the Curse Magician’s cheerful tone.

Micheal blinked, before replying with a small nod. Hayden chuckled before turning around, throwing his hands out wide in dramatic fashion, and then vanishing in a storm of shadows.

There was a quiet moment as Micheal watched the shadows begin to fade away. He didn't recognize this Ability, which meant it probably came from outside the Shop.

“…he’s certainly unique.” Micheal commented dryly.

“That’s one word for it.” Lux grumbled as the duo exchanged glances. Lux quirked his lips, while Micheal held back a snort.

A few minutes passed, and finally…

It was time.

Under the cover of night, Micheal and the forces of the Vile King set off.

The culmination of his efforts from the very first step he took, here on the 7 Layers, was at hand.

As they crossed midnight, shifting from one day into the next, Micheal made a silent promise.

Today, a God would die.

.

Chapter 55


.

The Eye of the Highstorm lay still.

The towering white walls of clouds that rotated in the distance around the Nexus stood like giants, unwavering in their guard, holding up the grim, dark sky of the Shattered Plane. Flashes of lightning and the rumbles of thunder lit the air, music to the tranquil stillness that was the Eye.

“Finally. The end draws near.”

Jay sol Arget’s words were a faint whisper as he sat down, cross-legged, atop a large, floating metal platform. The platform was several hundred meters long and wide, made of Vraft metal, a special material he had encountered on the strange Vortex World that made up the 7th Layer. Its deep, dark green luster stood at odds with the dark Void below.

Vraft metal was a dense, powerful material with a singular special property – once energized, that metal would stay in place where it was set, ignoring conventional gravity as if the metal was locked into the very fabric of Space itself, immoveable.

“The Center.” That was what Ixon had called that strange world in his visions – a Vortex World of wonders, whose Nebula could connect to any Dimension.

The 7th Layer – the Center of All.

Jay wouldn’t know about any of that – he had turned around after traversing the rocky outskirts of the 7th Layer, orienting himself to climb down the Layer Path that lead to his target – the ones Ixon had sighted in his visions of the future.

‘The ones who would ruin everything for us.’ That was how Ixon sol Eden, the Titled Deity and fellow Endwalker who ruled the Endwalker Dominion, the collective forces of the independent Endwalker Tribe, and the client species that served under their protection, had described them.

“Humans.” Jay let out a long hacking cough as he felt his Soul quiver, his lips twisted in a snarl.

He was at war.

His perception of the world distorted as he trembled, his vision wavering. Thick strands of Paradox-derived Time Energy whiplashed around him as he grimaced, his body twisting as several afterimages shot out in different directions.

In some of those images, Jay stood up, admiring the huge, pulsing Nexus that hovered several dozen meters above the metal platform he had set up, at the middle of the Eye. In others, he began to wander off, walking along the edges of the Vraft metal platform he had constructed, peering down towards the Void.

‘Ignore them.’ Jay commanded himself, resisting the urge to let his mind spiral. Soon, those images faded, vanishing as they dissipated into the air.

It was the price he paid for violating the Layer Paths set up by the Architect.

That, too, was more of Ixon’s wisdom – the ‘Architect’ was the name he’d given for the entity that created the 7 Layers, dragging in countless Dimensions into a warped game, forcing countless species to climb each Layer along specific Paths, until they reached the Center. Each Dimension was sequestered with enormous walls of Paradox-derived Time Energy, staining the corridors of the In-Between and making travel down the Layers a death sentence.

Ixon believed it was all a grand experiment wrought through masterful use of an unknown Title, a sort of game where the Architect sought to discover who the superior species was, pitting all of reality against one another, forcing them through trials and tribulations, to climb up and reach the final Layer.

He who controlled the Center, would rule them all – Ixon claimed.

‘The answer was obvious.’ Of course it was – how could it not be?

The superior species was them – the Walkers of the End, Those that Dwelled Beyond, the inhabitants of the Background – the Endwalker Dominion.

“Ke-.” Jay sol Arget coughed, wiping away a trail of blood.

It was only natural that each client species they encountered came under their protection – before being dragged into the 7 Layers, the Endwalker Dominion had ruled over 31 separate garden worlds, split among 23 different Dimensions across the In-Between.

He didn’t care what the other Dominions thought – of the two Dominions that neighbored the Dimensions under Endwalker control, the Angelic Dominion couldn’t even kill off one of their own, and the Aerdu Dominion…

He saw red for a moment before he forced the thought down.

The less said about that clown the better.

Slowly, Jay sol Arget got to his feet, taking in another wracking breath.

“I’m just glad it’s finally over.” He muttered.

He didn’t always use to talk to himself like this, speaking when none were present – such a lapse of discipline would’ve been unthinkable in the past.

However…

Jay sol Arget took a moment, standing still as he looked up, at the pulsating Nexus above him.

“I’m tired.”

He was old.

With but a thought, Jay sol Arget opened the Titles System.

.

— — - Titles System - — —

Title: The Unbound

Traits: Riseheart, Great Vigor, Undying Breath, Supremely Steadfast, Steady Heart, Keen Health, Immortal’s Grasp, Stalwart Bones, Hearty Blood, Robust Organs, (…161 more)

.

He eyed his Traits, the most recent 10 he had acquired or evolved displayed in full.

All of his recent Traits held a singular focus – enhancing his health and extending his longevity.

The average lifespan of an Endwalker, with middling Traits, stood at around 200-230 years – significantly longer than most mortal species, who barely graced their garden worlds before dying off in less than a century, but the shortest average lifespan amongst the Tribes of Deities.

Jay sol Arget was close to 2,100 years old. Unfathomably ancient, by Endwalker standards, and the only Endwalker alive who had lived through the Background Rebellion that earned his people’s freedom from the clutches of that twice-cursed eldritch Jester – Bosmond Jingleton.

“They say the Heretic has north of 300 Traits.” Jay mused as he scrolled through his Traits, before closing the screen, dismissing the rogue Angel from his thoughts. His acquisition of Traits had slowed down greatly, in his latter years, as he became less adventurous.

“Yet, we all die in the end.” Jay sol Arget continued his monologue as he quietly looked up at the pulsating Nexus.

“So many Loops, so many failures.” He shook his head as he reached out with his pale right hand and…

He activated his Title.

.

– - Title: The Unbound – -

He who has Unbound that which could not be broken.

The Heavens welcome the Unbound.

.

A rush of euphoria filled Jay, a sweet, enriching sensation that never got old, as he felt the power of the world fill the palm of his hand.

He reached out towards the Nexus and…

He stole from it.

He felt reality shift again, as he subtly altered the forces at work, binding the Nexus together. The Nexus served, in this strange Dimension, as a stabilizing force, binding an array of gravitational planes together that the floating islands of the Third Layer relied upon to keep them hovering over the aberration that was the Void.

Strange indeed – Jay suspected the Void was a Plane that had been bound to a Concept – perhaps this Dimension had been subjected to some sort of catastrophic collision with a Higher Energy Dimension, shattering its garden world and leaving it in its current, fractured state. It was difficult to parse what exactly took place, given how many years had passed. Maybe Ixon could figure it out, but he wasn't here.

Slowly, the pulsating Nexus above him began to grow more unstable. The mass of energy shook back and forth, the air around it twisting as gusts of wind began to invade the calm stillness of the Eye.

“Finally.” Jay sol Arget let out a long exhale.

The world around him shifted, as several false images of Jay shot out again, moving along potential futures he might take. He ignored these false Clones, as he felt the world around him begin to destabilize.

It wasn’t easy, altering the Nexus while that horrid Void Noble, Eon, was watching it. That creature was the single most dangerous entity in this Dimension, Jay was certain. In far, far too many of his Loops, the so called King of Heroes had foiled him at every crucial moment, forcing him to take a path more subtle than he would have preferred.

‘If only I was in a better state.’ He let out a long chuckle as he coughed, wiping away a dribble of blood.

He was dying, and not even his Title could change that.

It was funny, in its own way – his Title let him Unbind that which another has, and make it his own. Conceptual Mastery, raw skill, knowledge, even power itself – he had always had a rather middling talent for Cultivation, but it had been child’s play to steal another’s God-Tier Divine Energy and make it his own, so long ago.

He flexed his Divine Energy in that moment, wincing – his powerful energy reserves had been whittled away at by his advanced age. His Title let him Unbind the life force of other sentients and make it his own, but as an Endwalker, his body itself had a natural limit to how long it could exist, before individual cells began to break down – and he had crossed that limit long ago.

Now, after forcing himself through the Paradox Barriers that prevented travel down the Layer Paths… he shook his head.

His energy reserves had fallen all the way down to King Tier.

“This should line up just right, timing wise.” He smiled as he sat back down on the ground, crossing his legs – he had sent out the last of his Paradox Clones, directing them to act exactly how he had planned across the previous Loops.

He relished in their actions - while his connection to those Clones was incredibly faint due to the distance, he could already imagine the sweet, sweet vengeance they'd dish out, on those who'd constantly troubled him throughout the Loops.

It was time to end all of this.

Now, in just a few hours, the Nexus would fully destabilize, and this world would fall apart.

As he yawned, he couldn’t help but ponder.

Everything was going just-

A portal opene-

His torso, head, and upper-body were vaporized as a massive white beam of energy blasted through the portal that had just appeared, killing Jay sol Arget’s main body on the spot.

In a spot of extraordinary bad luck, Jay sol Arget’s guard, as exhausted as he was, crippled in his injuries, relaxed in his victory, and in the middle of yawning, was down – a confluence of factors and sheer chance that just so happened to line up, leaving him vulnerable to a surprise attack that even his supernatural intuition failed to notice.

It was a spot of truly awful luck - or, from the perspective of his attackers, an incredibly unlikely lucky chance.

And so...

Just like that…

Jay sol Arget was dead.

‘…’

‘…’

‘…’

Jay sol Arget blinked, his Soul burning as he felt a reverberation through Time.

He was standing, mid-crouch, just about to sit down.

Exactly 8 seconds into the past.

‘Time?!’ A wave of shock pulsed through him as he realized, one of his fail-safes had activated.

He had just Unbound his own death from the Loop – damaging a small part of his Soul, and sending him slightly backwards up the Loop, into the past with no memories of what occurred.

“What happened?”!

With a snarl, the Endwalker flung his body backwards as he tapped into his stolen Mastery of Space, warping the air around him. That action sent a bout of agony through his crippled Soul.

An instant later…

A great beam of light melted through the air, incinerating the spot where he’d planned on sitting down, at the edge of the metal platform. The attack was blinding, incinerating the metal in a heartbeat as it shot forward before boring a hole in the side of the towering clouds that made up the Inner Wall of the Eye.

“Huh.” In the stillness that echoed following the attack, a voice rang out.

“I thought for sure that would get him.”

The speaker emerged, accompanied by dozens of figures, pouring out of portals onto the metal platform, with a beautiful, golden spear in hand - a spear Jay instantly recognized as Stratos, Eon’s Spear of Time. His senses instantly locked the presence of every individual that had appeared, his Spatial Awareness letting him track them each independently of his vision.

Jay didn’t stop to think.

He didn’t let the sheer impossibility of what he was witnessing phase him. The fact that an organization of humans had somehow subverted his final Loop and tried to ambush him was appalling, absurd, and shouldn’t have been possible.

But it didn’t matter.

This was the end.

‘I’ll do it myself.’

Space fractured as Jay sol Arget took a step forward, ignoring the agony of his crippled Soul, and…

‘Wait- that damned Seer is here?!’

The fight was on.

.

Chapter 56


.

“I thought for sure that would get him.” Lux’s words echoed in the air as he spoke, intentionally drawing the attention of the enraged Endwalker as Constantine’s forces poured out through the portals behind him.

The Nexus pulsed above them, the powerful orb of pulsating energy roaring in the background.

Curiously, unlike the Clones that the Endwalker had spread around the Third Layer, Lux found he had no issues perceiving Jay sol Arget’s main body.

‘I guess we don’t need these.’ He rubbed a bracelet that a member of the Research Squad had passed out – an Air/Energy sensor Artifact, a countermeasure drawn up to deal with Jay sol Arget’s Endwalker perception-shifting.

The Endwalker’s body was covered in a faint layer of shivering, unstable white energy, a power that made him stand out, clearly visible. The pale, brown-haired humanoid looked unsettlingly like a human, the closest to any species he’d encountered in the 7 Layers.

The Endwalker’s eyes flicked around rapidly as it registered Lux’s words, before taking a step forward.

That single step fractured the air around it, cracks spreading in the air like a mirror had shattered.

Before it could do anything else, however…

A second portal opened up behind the Endwalker’s back, courtesy of a World Room Type Ability user. Lux had to hold back a grim smile as he watched a Whitefire Beam blast forward, a concentrated energy attack created by two members of Strike Team 3 that were staged with the World Room Type Ability user.

The ambush was nearly instantaneous, struck from behind with no warning as soon as the portal opened.

The perfect sneak attack, after the first failed, wherein the other Strike Teams and Lux drew Jay sol Arget’s attention.

And…

It, too, failed.

The stark white beam of energy blasted forth and slammed into the palm of Jay sol Arget’s waiting hand.

And then…

The energy beam vanished entirely.

Lux frowned as Jay sol Arget turned to look directly at him and raised that same hand in his direction, his intuition screaming at him-

“Dodge!” The words barely left his lips as he flung himself to the side, moving just before the Deity unleashed, as…

A massive beam of white energy melted through the air where he had been standing, carving out a long, gaping trail in the floating metal platform.

“Switch to engagement plan C!” Lux yelled as the Strike Teams began to fan out, surrounding the Titled Deity.

‘Ambush tactics aren’t going to work.’ Lux thought grimly.

They would have to do this the hard way.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Parallel Thinking. Avid Senses. Golden Intuition. Calm Mind. Iron Control.

Jay sol Arget breathed in, his emotions detaching as cold logic overtook him.

The beam of energy he’d Unbound and then repurposed shot through the air, narrowly missing his intended target – the human had dived out of the way the instant before he unleashed the attack, luckily picking the only direction where the beam couldn’t reach.

‘No matter.’ He used his Mastery of Space to seal shut the portal that had opened behind him, rupturing its stability.

Despite his crippled Soul, his dying body, the fact that he had been caught off guard, unprepared…

Despite everything, Jay sol Arget knew no fear.

Because…

They didn’t understand.

Absolute Control. Swift Reflexes. Centered Mind, Centered Body. Keen Eyes. Outer Aware.

They never would.

Jay sol Arget raised his left hand up, and tilted his head exactly 23.4 degrees to the side.

A red laser beam shot through the air where his head had been, narrowly missing him – in the same moment, Jay sol Arget’s left hand landed on the head of a cloaked, invisible human, wielding two large black daggers.

‘Unbind.’ He Unbound the life force within this human and then instantly energized their body, creating a sort of corpse-energized shield that he swung to his left.

Just in time to intercept a wave of acid, pouring through yet another strange portal.

Quick Thoughts. Ordered Movements. Refined Battle Sense. Perfect Balance. Enhanced Perception.

‘Torrent.’

Jay switched Masteries, grasping ahold of his Mastery of the Sea, as from his left hand emerged a massive deluge of seawater, washing away the secondary and tertiary waves of acid that followed the first. The billowing waves of water swept across the metal platform and knocked away several of the masked humans, the surf frothing as it cascaded off the edge down into the Void below.

A split second later, his focus reverted back to his Mastery of Space, as he expertly sealed this region of Space, preventing any more of these troublesome portals from opening.

Golden Mind. Courageous Soul. Enhanced Comprehension. Wide Energy Control. Calm Body.

Without looking, without thinking – Jay sol Arget’s right hand lashed out behind his back, just in time to intercept a glowing purple arrow.

A miasma attempted to settle upon Jay as the arrow exploded in a flurry of purple light – instantly quashed as Jay flexed his Mastery of Curse, expelling the rampant energies.

In that same moment, Jay sol Arget’s left hand punched forward, Grandmaster Fist Energy rocketing through the air as he unleashed a flurry of blows.

‘Master-Tier is my limit.’ The crippled Titled Deity felt his Soul shudder as he stopped using Grandmaster Fist Energy and acknowledged the limitation, not letting it affect him on an emotional level.

The resounding white fists of energy smashed through the air, sending human bodies tumbling.

Mighty Strength. Hardened Bones. Adept Attention. Boosted Awareness. Solidity.

It was a scene he’d seen played out time and time again.

Jay sol Arget clenched his fist as he grasped ahold of his Mastery of Fire, creating an explosive bubble of flame that he expanded outward, knocking away his attackers.

Mortals could never truly grasp the sheer vastness of the gulf that existed between them and a fully realized Deity – let alone a Titled Deity.

A talented Deity aspired to complete a single Trait Cycle, typically a dedication of their entire life’s efforts – the accumulation of 30 Traits.

These Traits were chosen depending on the path that Deity planned on treading in life – there were countless different schools of thought as to which build of Traits was most optimal, varied between Deity Tribes. The Morians, in particular, had perfected the cultivation of Traits into a veritable artform, and were one of the few Dominions willing to exchange knowledge with the Endwalker Dominon.

However…

Jay sol Arget wasn’t just a talented Deity.

He was a Titled Deity.

He was the best of the best.

Jay sol Arget hadn’t just completed one Trait Cycle.

He’d conquered five, well on his way to a sixth.

He had stacked on Trait after Trait, raising his baseline so far above a mortal’s that the difference between them was simply unfathomable.

He was superior in every way that mattered.

‘I have… roughly 11 and a half minutes .’ As the walls of fire began to dissipate around him, the Endwalker made an astute judgement.

At this rate of energy expenditure, he would die in 11 minutes and 29 seconds now – after spending so many Loops careful of any expenditure, counting the hours as time passed by… it was freeing, in a way, to finally be able to go all out.

‘That’s more than enough time.’ Despite himself, Jay sol Arget smiled.

A warrior’s end.

He would quash this distraction and complete his mission.

These humans would suffer the wrath of a dying God.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“Move, move, move!” The leader of Strike Team 2, a masked woman whose name Micheal never got, directed them forward as they poured through the open portals out from the cloaked Void Ship that had snuck into the Nexus.

The journey, from Axellion to the Eye of the Highstorm, had proven uneventful – everything went exactly as Micheal and Constantine’s forces had practiced. The Causeway Network proved its usefulness, letting them cross an extraordinary amount of distance in a very short amount of time.

Even piercing through the great wall of clouds that made up the Highstorm had failed to provide a challenge – Constantine’s Void Ships had an entire suite of enchantments designed to let it pierce through hurricane-force winds.

Adrenaline spiked in Micheal’s veins as he couldn’t help but tense up, his concentration absolute as he exited the portal - simultaneously, he opened the Realm of Intent, the world diverging as a copy of reality overlaid upon itself.

Everything had led up to this moment – the final confrontation with Jay sol Arget.

The first thing Micheal did, as he touched down upon the floating metal platform, was activate his Eyes of the Deep Ability.

‘Divine Scan.’ Jay sol Arget was clear and visible, contrary to their expectations, easily found by his Divine Eyes.

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Endwalker

Title: The Unbound

Traits: Riseheart, Great Vigor, Undying Breath, Supremely Steadfast, Steady Heart, Keen Health, Immortal’s Grasp, Stalwart Bones, Hearty Blood, Robust Organs, (…161 more)

STR: S+ (Growth Rate: Mythical or higher)

END: S (Growth Rate: Mythical or lower)

REG: B- (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

SOUL: SS (Growth Rate: Mythical or higher)

MANA: S++ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

Path Notes: An Endwalker that walks a cluttered Path. Strong traces of the Path of the Sword, the Path of the Fist, the Path of Fire, the Path of Blood, and the Path of Wind exist. Traces of the Path of Space, the Path of Time, the Path of the Shield, the Path of Poison, the Path of Darkness, the Path of the Axe, the Path of Curse, the Path of the Storm, the Path of the Quake, the Path of Mirrors, the Path of the Eternal, and the Path of the Sea exist.

.

The first thing he noticed was the sheer, absurd number of connections to Conceptual Powers that Jay sol Arget possessed.

It was unreasonable to the point where it defied logic – Micheal had never heard of anyone possessing this many connections to so many disparate Conceptual Powers, especially not to the depth of Mastery that Jay sol Arget did... apart from Navir.

‘His stats aren’t as high as I worried.’ The Titled Deity had been heavily weakened by his forced climb down the Layers – likely also weakening his Growth Rates, which were still very impressive, even now.

Endwalkers were considered the ‘most frail’ among the Tribes of Deities, their unique unnamed Physique that allowed them to exist within the Background coming at a cost to their general physical prowess – that kind of logic, however, didn’t really apply to a Titled Deity.

“Stand ready to deliver the package!”

Micheal’s thoughts smoothly switched over as he stepped towards the Nexus, backed up by several members of the Revolutionaries. The team were motioning towards the giant, pulsating Nexus that glowed above them, looking at him expectantly, while the other Strike Teams distracted Jay sol Arget.

With a thought, Micheal activated the Crown of the Angel King.

He’d waited till the last reasonable moment to activate the Artifact, wanting to stretch its timer out to the absolute limit. The rush of power that filled him felt incredible, as if the world itself was bowing down to him.

Micheal tapped on his Spatial Ring, prepared to bring out the Artifact given to him by the scientists of Dark Void.

Before he took action, however…

He frowned as he watched the Strike Teams combat Jay sol Arget, his future sight giving him an even more in-depth understanding.

The battle was chaotic and fast-paced, clashes of energy and Conceptual manipulation spreading like wildfire.

‘This isn’t enough.’ It was an observation borne from the experience of a man who had seen the worst the 7 Layers could throw at someone, as he instantly grasped the flow of the ongoing fight.

Constantine’s forces acted in unison, showing incredible teamwork as they released coordinated strike after strike, a veritable entourage of violence unleashed.

And yet…

Nothing seemed to stick.

Jay sol Arget was dancing around the attacks, moving with an almost eerie, inhuman flow.

“Why haven’t you activated it?” Lux’s voice was terse as he landed on the ground next to Micheal, Stratos gleaming in his hands.

Both of them jumped up into the air as a surge of water crashed by beneath them, sweeping over the metal platform. Micheal remained floating, his Life Orbs letting him hover as he kept his focus on Jay sol Arget.

“We need to contain him first.” Lightshorn appeared in Micheal’s hand as he floated back down towards the ground, after the water had cleared past them.

“Anything we do, we should assume he can undo.” Micheal continued.

“We planned- The Strike Teams will handl-“ Lux began, but was immediately cut off.

“No time. They aren’t enough. We need to intercede.” Micheal’s words were short as he landed on the ground and knelt down, gathering his Ki. The Scythe of Chains appeared in his left hand.

“S’vol Reize.” Micheal cast the 2nd Circle Spell, Mana Blade.

The original plan had been for Micheal to activate Dark Void's device while the Revolutionaries handled Jay sol Arget. However, Micheal's instincts and general understanding of the higher Layers screamed at him.

That plan wasn't going to cut it.

It was a judgement call, but he trusted his instincts and the experience that had built them.

'I can't risk letting him undo any changes we make.' The Strike Teams weren't able to contain the Titled Deity.

Even the best-laid plan lasted only until the first blow was struck - reality on the ground took precedence.

Micheal mentally stretched his grip outward, reaching to his connection to the River of Time.

“It’s now or never. Are you with me?” Micheal turned his head slightly towards Lux, though his eyes remained focused on Jay sol Arget. His Mana Blade floated in the air behind and off to the right of his head, positioning itself.

Lux’s head snapped towards the Nexus, towards Jay sol Arget, and then back to Micheal, all in one quick motion.

In the meantime, a huge orb of fire exploded outward from Jay sol Arget’s position, knocking back several of the Strike Team members. The warriors threw up several glowing barriers as a countermeasure, slowing down the spread of the flames.

“Alright.” Lux let out a frustrated sigh, before motioning to the members of the Strike Team that had accompanied Micheal.

“Let’s do this. Shift to engagement plan Alpha 2!” Lux yelled out.

It was the last thing Micheal heard as he exploded into motion, eyes for one being and one being only.

He had a God to kill.

.
