Chapter 57


.

As the flames began to recede, Jay sol Arget’s eyes flickered.

Instinctively, he grasped ahold of his Mastery of Time – a Mastery he’d Unbound from a heretical Fulvan, a reptilian bipedal client species that served under Endwalker protection.

Reality around him slowed to a crawl as he gave himself more time to think, his enhanced brain analyzing everything he could see. In that same moment, memories arose to the forefront of Jay sol Arget’s mind, an inadvertent consequence of his crippled Soul distracting him.

Jay could still remember that moment quite clearly, where he obtained this Mastery of Time, nearly 1700 years ago – a disappointing tragedy, in truth.

Rassthor Fang, Head Shaman of the Veve Tribe, had proven a fine Governor for the southern continent of the garden world of Edor. The Lizardman, as they were commonly called, paid his tithes on time, was loyal to the then-young Endwalker Dominion, and kept the tribes under him at relative peace on Reffa, the long, skinny continent that dominated the southern hemisphere of Edor.

Alas, Rassthor’s obsession with Time led him astray.

Anything that touched upon the River of Time was a touchy subject when it came to the various Deity Dominions that ruled over more than 90% of the known Higher Dimensions. There was a reason Masters of Time were such a rare sight in these lands – any alteration of Time was heavily looked down upon, even those that stayed within the rules.

Rassthor’s Mastery, for the longest time, had kept to the rule – Temporal Forward, Never Backward.

It was the one thing nearly all Deity Dominions agreed upon, from the Citali to the Angels, the Toren to the Prometheans, the one defining rule that bound them all together, ingrained in their beliefs and culture, harshly enforced across almost all Tribes, all Dominions.

The Temporal Edict, set by Zeos himself – The First Angel, and one of the most powerful Titled Deities throughout known history.

‘The Past is inviolable. To alter the Past is the way of the Heretic.’

It was a warning all Deities learned the moment they obtained their 3rd Trait, completing the First Step of the Ten Steps to a Trait Cycle – the powerful visions were crafted by Zeos’ Title long ago, a fundamental altering of reality that every Deity experienced, a warning for all generations.

Rassthor, however, was not a Deity. He hadn’t understood.

And that was why-

‘Control.’

Jay sol Arget forced himself to not grimace, not allowing such an expression of weakness, as he regained control of his thoughts.

In slow motion, his eyes narrowed as his gaze pierced through the fading wall of fire, his keen sense latching on to every mortal present.

‘I’m not as stable as I would like.’ It was to be expected.

These mortals were no match for him, had he been in his prime… but he was far from that.

He had chosen this mission, to descend down the Layers to target these humans because of that fact – that he was dying. By the time Ixon’s visions of the future would have taken place, Jay would’ve already passed away due to his age. The only reason he was still alive now was because he’d Bound his existence to the Loop.

This was his last chance to make a difference for his Tribe.

A slice of brilliant, white Grandmaster Sword Energy interrupted his thoughts, piercing through the remnants of fire like sunlight bursting through clouds.

‘Perhaps…’ As the Titled Deity watched the raw energy cut towards him in slow motion, a sliver of doubt entered Jay sol Arget’s mind.

‘Perhaps I should plan for the worst.’

At his core, Jay sol Arget was a Deity of action, weathered by an immense amount of experience.

Superior being or not, he didn’t allow arrogance to cloud his judgement.

And so, as he raised his left hand up, activating his Title to neutralize this incoming attack…

Jay sol Arget sent out a command to his Paradox Clones, drawing upon his Mastery of Time – it was a command that would take hours to reach, given the vast distance between himself and his Clones, as distant as they were.

‘It should reach them shortly after the islands begin to fall.’

It shouldn’t be necessary, a fail-safe command given out of an abundance of caution but…

He didn’t live as long as he had by being careless.

And so his command went:

‘Kill them all.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

In the immediate aftermath of the Ritual that sent Micheal to the past…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The first one to notice something was wrong wasn’t Duke Atlas, not as busy as the Archmage was, attempting to stave off the collapse of the island housed Axellion.

Nor was it the scientists of Dark Void, as they gathered around the spent Ritual Circle, clumped in quiet, tense discussion.

It wasn’t the Curse Magician or the Revolutionaries, as they set about securing the corpse of the Apex Void Predator they had downed, claiming salvage rights.

Not the Knights of the Round Table, nor Allmaster, nor even Eon himself noticed anything astray.

No…

The first to notice that something was wrong…

Kim Jiwoon frowned as he knelt down, sifting his hands through shattered clumps of crystal. A pair of Life Orbs floated in the air next to his hand, helping him push aside larger chunks of crystal.

The aftermath of Kyvenval’s errant glance had crystalized an enormous section of Axellion – and the rampage and clash between the two Apex Void Predators had scattered a large amount of those crystals all over the Inner and Outer Pavilions.

‘How grim.’ Jiwoon’s eyes scanned his surroundings as he stood up, taking in every tiny detail.

He noticed everything.

He saw Duke Atlas hover next to a faceless man, high up in the sky, surrounded by great big Magic Circles that glowed with Mana as he cast Spell after Spell. Below the Duke, he saw contingents of House Atlas’ Knights and the Wizards in their employ work up Spells of their own, some sort of on-the-spot created Defensive Ward designed to slow their islands fall. Their Spellwork had killed the breeze that had flowed through the pavillions, stilling the air around them.

The Knights of the Round Table had split up, with several knights and Vice-Commander Yama splitting off to regroup with the remaining humans back at their main headquarters.

Nearby, Aaron Bartram hovered just above the ground, speaking intensely with the floating chibi form of Dark Void’s leader, Marco Barone. Jessica Wiles stood behind Aaron, her face pensive, next to Felix Seranno, who looked around with a bored expression on his face, as a vague figure approached them. From some simple lip-reading, the two leaders seemed to be debating about Micheal’s odds of success, and what to do if he failed.

Further away, Allmaster was talking with Eon and an unmemorable servant of some sort, pointing towards the Ritual Circle and motioning towards where the Spear of Time had been – Eon had on an amused expression, oddly at ends with his own dire situation – how the Void Noble was even alive still with half his body turned to crystal, Jiwoon couldn’t even speculate.

He saw Shin kneeling next to the body of Vesper von Atlas, one of the unfortunate to have died during the attack. Rex stood next to Shin, a comforting arm set upon his shoulder, as a nondescript man stepped towards them. Some crystals shifted next to them.

Dunkore Salm was-

The hair on the back of Kim Jiwoon’s neck stood up.

He noticed things.

And because of that…

‘Why did those crystals move?’ The world seemed to slow down as Jiwoon’s pulse spiked.

It was an incredibly small change that no one else present noticed, something that could be easily dismissed out of hand. A minor, unimportant detail, where most would assume any number of explanations.

However…

There was no breeze.

No one was there.

So why did they move?

The intuition behind one of Earth’s greatest detectives burned.

Kim Jiwoon activated his Eye of Liberation.

The world of the future played out before him, the next 27.3 seconds simulated in an instant. The stark clarity of what was to come settled into his mind, searing into his brain.

And in that future…

He saw the end.

“ATTACK!” Jiwoon screamed out loud, his voice raw as he burst into action.

“ENDWALKER ATTACK!”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“ATTACK!”

Shin reacted without thinking.

In one moment, he was coming to terms with Vesper’s death.

It was cruel – not even her own family cared enough to interrupt or see what he was doing with her body. He had pulled up the Shop, and was browsing the ‘Miscellaneous Earth Objects’ section to find a suitable coffin – anything to fill his mind while he waited for Micheal to return.

In the next…

“ENDWALKER ATTACK!”

The call to arms lit something inside Shin that he hadn’t known was waiting, a burning desire for action, to do something – and in that moment, he didn’t hesitate.

He drew upon the Conceptual Power of Strength, feeling a rush of power as his body and Soul resonated through the connection he had built. In the same moment, he stored Vesper’s corpse back in his Spatial Ring, with no time to apologize for the casual handling, and instantly shifted his focus as…

He began to teleport.

The world devolved into a million translucent lines of energy, as he activated his Warping Phaser Type Ability.

And in that transformed world…

He saw them.

The aberrations, lines of energy that stretched backwards, into the Background – a wrongness that stood out, stark in his vision.

‘They’re everywhere.’ Shin realized, to his horror.

The Paradox Clones of Jay sol Arget were visible, their very existence warping reality, all around him, surrounding various targets, human and Void Noble alike.

Shin had precious little time to think, as he chose his teleportation target. In this tense, fragile moment, the words Micheal had ironed into his brain rose to the forefront.

‘When fighting a Titled Deity…’ Micheal had made this point very clear,

‘Never, ever fight fair.’

Shin was angry. Furious, in fact. He wanted nothing more than to throw himself at the brutal killers that had brought nothing but torment and pain in their wake.

But…

He had to be better.

He had to be Stronger.

Vesper’s death had proven that.

Thus…

What was the most unfair advantage he could obtain?

With that thought in mind, Shin made his decision.

He drew upon the power of Strength, not to empower himself, but to empower his Ability to teleport, and…

The world flashed away as he vanished.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“You think the Void could expand, after the Nexus collapses?” Aaron questioned Marco, in the midst of developing countermeasures should Micheal’s ‘hail mary’ leap backwards in time fail.

“We believe it’s possible, the gravitational plane of this Dimension is regulated on a quantum-“ Marco began, but paused as…

“ATTACK!” A yell interrupted their conversation.

Aaron’s head snapped to the right, towards the speaker, a metal orb appearing above his hand as adrenaline spread through his veins. Behind him, Felix Seranno’s eyes turned red as two blood red swords began to form in his hands, while Jessica’s body began to glaciate, half of it turning into ice.

“ENDWALKER ATTACK!” Kim Jiwoon finished and-

Shin abruptly teleported into existence right next to Aaron.

It took every iota of Aaron’s willpower to not Vector-blast Shin out of existence in a knee-jerk reaction, with only the familiarity he’d gained with the teleporter in recent days, thanks to his spars with Jessica and their own chats, staving him off. He could see Jessica and Felix react in a similar manner, both of them flinching as they recognized him-

And it was here, just a split second after Shin arrived, that Aaron guessed what Shin was planning.

It was a sort of unspoken communication, borne from Aaron’s own tactical acumen, as the Commander of the Round Table, and his relatively new familiarity with Shin.

And so, as Shin’s metal left hand landed on Felix’s shoulder, as his right leg hooked around Jessica’s leg…

Aaron, for a split second, dropped the Vector barrier he kept up around his person almost 24/7 now, ever since he learned he was being hunted.

It was a show of trust, a leap of faith by the Commander of the Round Table that proved how much Micheal and Shin’s actions, and the knowledge they’d brought, had meant to him.

Shin’s right hand landed on Aaron’s chest, passing through where the barrier had been, and…

The world around them transformed as they teleported into the Background.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

The world was strange. Colors appeared less vibrant, faded, in a way Aaron couldn’t quite describe. The scents of the world felt muted, less existent, while the air felt odd, heavier, pressing down upon him.

And the wind…

It hadn’t existed a moment ago, but now it did, and it whistled, ominously, oddly, a faint, keening cry echoing in the air.

And…

Felix Seranno saw them.

Eleven Endwalker Clones, shrouded in an Aura of black, dark energy, preparing to strike.

The beast within him screamed to be unleashed – but cold logic crushed that instinct as Felix flared his Ki, rich, deep Sky Tier energy that was a hair’s breadth away from breaking into Lord Tier.

He was the first to react, faster than Jessica, faster than Aaron, faster than anyone else, even Shin, who brought them here – the young genius Vice-Commander of the Round Table – Felix Seranno.

Shin had only briefly described what this strange Background Dimension was, a world overlaid upon reality, existing in the same space. Felix knew that if he lost contact with Shin, he would automatically fall out of this strange version of existence, returning to normal reality.

That meant that even the Endwalker Clone that was 3 meters in front of him would vanish again, becoming impossible to perceive. That meant all the other Endwalker Clones Felix could now see, dotted around him, would vanish again.

And so…

Felix adapted, his mind racing as he jumped into action.

“Blood Reign.” Blood ruptured from Felix’s left hand, a mix of actual blood and Blood Energy rocketing outward in a great plume right in front of Aaron. The rough, instant nature of this activation of his High-Vampire Type would cripple his left hand for the duration of this fight, but speed was key here.

Anyone else would’ve been caught off guard by the unplanned, uncoordinated Ability activation – but Aaron Bartram regularly sparred with Felix, almost every single day. Felix had an uncanny mind about him, an intuitive and creative outlook to combat that had helped shape Aaron’s own development unlike any other.

Aaron, just like he had with Shin, looked at the situation as a whole, grasping the big picture – it was a testament to his leadership, and also a side-effect of how his Conceptual Power functioned.

Vector saw the world in numbers – and for Aaron to control that power, he had to adapt to an alien mindset, seeing the world as it was at a base level, broken down to raw data, almost like a computer.

“Vector: Scatter.” Aaron abandoned his plan of attack, instead trusting in Felix’s judgement, as he touched the great plume of blood and energy, amplifying its momentum to an extreme speed, scattering it in all directions.

It took less than a fraction of a second, an immediate action and response, teamwork built up over years of trials and tribulation climbing the 7 Layers together.

‘Blood Control.’ Felix hijacked that great burst of speed as he reasserted control. His Ki blazed within him as it fueled his Ability, every minute adjustment costing him.

Aaron’s Conceptual Power was incredibly powerful, but if there was a single weakness Felix could pick out, it was that it had a very one note nature – it lacked versatility, at least, in its present iteration.

And versatility, Felix had learned, was the difference between life and death here on the 7 Layers.

Vector granted Aaron unbelievable power in his attacks, but the complexity of his Conceptual Power came with a downside – it was extremely difficult for Aaron to multi-task with it.

Blood dripped down from Felix’s nose as he split his attention eleven ways.

Eleven ways, for the eleven Paradox Clones of Jay sol Arget, that were now visible in his Blood Senses.

The streaks of blood and Blood Energy that Felix controlled shot through the air at breakneck speed, enough particles breaking the sound barrier to create a sonic boom.

These spears of blood weren’t by any means a powerful attack, not as rushed as Felix had been. They acted more like tightly controlled streams of liquid, slamming into all eleven Paradox Clones that Felix envisioned through his Blood Sense.

‘There.’ Felix grinned, a vicious smile that revealed his sharp, vampiric teeth, as he felt his blood stain the forms of all eleven Clones.

How do you perceive something that can’t be perceived?

For a High-Vampire, the answer was simple.

His blood was a part of his being, part of his very essence, whether it was inside him or spilled on another.

Felix Seranno felt himself slip back into normal reality as he took a step forward, his right hand raised, a sword of Blood Energy held at the ready.

He could no longer perceive Jay sol Arget’s Clones.

However…

He could see the eleven giant arrows of blood that now appeared, floating in the air at his control, pointing down exactly where he sensed his blood, a part of his being, now rested, for all the world to see.

‘Got you.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Jessica Wiles blinked.

The moment she heard the words ‘Attack’ she had raised her guard, her eyes glowing blue as her body began to turn to ice.

Thus, she wasn’t caught off-guard when Shin appeared next to her. His abrupt arrival made her flinch, but the days they’d spent sparring and the fast friendship she’d formed with the blonde-haired teleporter let her push past that.

And then the world transformed, as she was brought into the Background.

And she saw-

Felix’s handiwork spread out before them in an instant, blood arrows marking the location of every Endwalker Clone.

Her world turned to ice as she immediately lead the attack.

The abrupt transversal back to normal reality almost gave her whiplash as she travelled along a small line of ice, appearing 3 meters to her right, exactly where Felix had marked.

Jessica’s hand hit ‘nothing’ as she activated her Glacial Body Ability.

A split second later, a miniature, 2 meters tall glacier formed as she hard froze the first of Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clones. The brutal nature of this quick freeze saturated every single individual cell in the entity’s body, transforming water into rigid, piercing spikes of ice.

It was a brutal attack she reserved for the worst of her enemies – a technique Felix had nicknamed ‘Ice Tomb.’

‘One down.’ The icy prison shattered as a wave of dark energy poured out of it, whatever Conceptual Power or Ability the Endwalker Clone had been prepared to use firing off as it died, its body literally falling to pieces, a pale shadow of its main body’s strength.

All of that took less than a second – and as Jessica’s gaze twisted, piercing towards the ten other targets spread out around her…

She employed a tactic she had practiced with Shin.

He called it ‘Speedblitzing.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Teleport.

Shin left the Round Table behind, trusting them to act after giving them a moment to find the Endwalkers.

The world around him transformed as he shifted his focus, entering his ‘Super Strength’ mode. His muscles swelled as he focused on his Melding Plate Arm, feeling the upgraded Artifact respond smoothly.

He appeared just to the right of the scientists of Dark Void, a group standing next to the large Ritual Circle Micheal had used, and the large machines/Artifacts that the scientists had setup.

Right in front of one of Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clones.

“Oh you-“ The Clone twisted, wiping off some of the blood staining its face, as it spun to face Shin.

“This was-“ Shin spat as his metal fist slammed into the Clone’s face, not giving it a chance to speak.

“-for all the smiles you stole from her.” He finished.

‘It’s dead.’ He noticed, intuitively – bits of light were fading off the Clone, just like the other one he had seen, but this one felt even fainter, a reflection of how weak Jay sol Arget’s main body had become.

Instantly, he teleported again, moving to yet another Clone, this one floating in the air next to Duke Atlas.

This time, the Clone was marginally more prepared, greeting Shin with a bevy of spears made of pure Darkness.

The Duke flinched as he finally noticed the attack happening right next to him, not perceiving Shin or the Endwalker Clone, but sensing the energy the Clone had fired off.

The spears of darkness rocketed into Shin, hitting him as soon as he arrived and-

They fizzled out, the energy sliding off Shin like he was a bar of soap.

.

—- Anathema Shorn —-

You are shorn, anathema to all energy.

.

Shin grunted as he felt the spears hit him and slide off – the impact felt like he got punched in the stomach, not nearly as deadly as it should be, but enough to be annoying. His Super Strength, however, bore him through it, as he barreled forward with another deadly jab.

“This was-“ Shin spat as his fist connected, caving in the Clone’s chest,

“For all the dances she’ll never get to have.”

The Clone’s corpse literally fell apart as it rocketed downward, cast from the sky.

Shin didn’t stay to watch, already teleporting on his way once more.

Meanwhile, the other Clones began dropping like flies.

Jessica bounced from Clone to Clone, freezing them as she erected miniature glaciers at will.

She wasn’t the only one to join in on the action – Rex’s dinosaur form made a reappearance as he let out a roar, chomping down on the blood-marked Clone that attempted to strike him down after Shin vanished. Allmaster and Eon joined forces as they struck down the Clone Felix marked next to them, Allmaster sending out a torrent of lightning from his bare hands, while Eon did... something, causing the Clone's body to fall apart after Allmaster's lightning clashed with the Darkness surrounding it.

The Clones were deadly powerful, able to dish out lethal attacks against any unsuspecting sentient – but their greatest weakness was their frailty. They relied on their stealth, as unstable creations crafted for observation, not combat.

“Vector: Mach 12.” Aaron’s words shattered the air. A metal orb blasted forward, sniping the farthest Clone as it pursued Vice-Commander Yama and the Knights returning to the Round Table HQ. The resulting impact obliterated the Clone's head with unerring accuracy, killing it on the spot.

Finally, Shin reappeared at the last Clone he could detect within the premises of Axellion, his Strength-boosted teleportation range letting him scan the entire City in depth.

This Clone stood in the center of the Ritual Circle, kneeling down as it observed it – it was the only Clone that wasn’t trying to attack someone, though it too was covered in an Aura of Darkness.

The Clone made as if to talk, but Shin didn’t give it a chance.

“This is for…” He announced for the last time, his emotions boiling over.

A wall of Darkness formed around the Clone as it tried to defend itself.

‘Expand.’ His Melding Plate Arm expanded smoothly, growing to enormous proportions as he punched forward with all his might.

“The life she’ll never get to live.”

‘Giant Punch!’

Like an avalanche crashing down a mountain, Shin’s enormous metal fist smashed into the wall of Darkness and obliterated the energy construct, pulverizing the Clone hiding behind it, before slamming into the rocky ground beneath, gouging out a long, ugly trail in the stone.

With a grunt, Shin teleported forward slightly, still in the Background as he pulled his arm back. The metal Artifact quickly shrank back to its original state, tingling slightly as he pulled back on his Super Strength mode.

‘Rest in peace, Vesper.’ Shin thought to himself quietly as he watched the particles of light dissolve, Jay sol Arget’s final Paradox Clone perishing.

Thanks to the early warning of Kim Jiwoon, a battle that could’ve been a tragedy was averted, and turned into a rout.

And so…

On this side of the Third Layer…

Vengeance was theirs.

.

Chapter 58


.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

On the other side of the Third Layer…

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Calm.

Micheal’s mind was serene as he stepped forward, preparing Lightshorn for another salvo.

All around him, the forces of the Revolutionaries spread out, Lux behind him, teams of men and women activating Abilities and Artifacts in an incredibly complex web of actions.

With the Nexus pulsing up above them, it was a chaotic scene, and yet…

Micheal found himself in a state of absolute calm.

In the days he spent preparing for this confrontation, Micheal had poured over the book Eon left him, meditating not just on the Divine Energy in his modified Eyes of the Deep but on all the different energies he controlled, as he reached for the Concept of Energy, trying to make a connection.

And…

He had failed.

It was hardly a surprise – the Concept of Energy was an obscure Conceptual Power and even if Eon’s words rang true, and Micheal did have a talent for it – touching upon a Conceptual Power was not a simple thing that could be done quickly, especially not one as complex as the one he was trying to reach.

Micheal had rushed to understand the Divine Energy in his Divine Eyes… but it was just that – a rush.

What he really, truly needed was a clear mind, and time – something Jay sol Arget wouldn’t give him.

The seawater had made the metal platform slick – Micheal used his Life Orbs, controlling them to make incredibly fine adjustments to his posture and balance, as he approached the flame barrier raised by Jay sol Arget.

While he may have failed to form a connection with the Concept of Energy, the days he had spent preparing had not been wasted.

He had managed to progress.

Just… not in the direction he had expected.

As the chaos unfolded around Micheal, energy clashing, Artifacts activating, Abilities firing…

Every distraction was outlined clearly in his mind’s eye, the Realm of Intent pathing the future that was yet to come.

And in that moment, Micheal dismissed the emotions that tried to distract him, casting off the fears, the worries, the anger, the rage – until all that was left was him and the world he had to face.

Everything around Micheal came into crystal clear clarity.

A vertical slice of Grandmaster Sword Energy shot back at Micheal, ripping through the fading wall of flames aimed directly at him. It was, Micheal recognized, his own attack, the Sword Energy unmistakably his own, somehow returned back towards him.

Micheal smoothly tilted his body slightly to the right, a fraction of a second before the Sword Energy arrived – in the same motion, he raised Lightshorn up again, cutting forward with another attack.

The blinding white energy sliced through the air a bare millimeter from his face, missing him by an incredibly small margin. Micheal felt, rather than saw, the cutting energy rip down into the metal floor, brutally gouging a long line into the floating platform, spilling seawater into the Void below.

It was an incredibly close dodge, the attack missing him by a hair’s breadth – and a close movement he never would’ve risked before – yet he did so now.

Emmanuel Stone called this the State of One.

The journal Micheal had passed to Bastien Amiot contained a bevy of information, data scrounged from his memories of the future – everything he could think of to help Bastien improve, copied down by him, written by hand.

And in those notes, Micheal had shared the personal observations of Emmanuel Stone, the ‘Pioneer of Moorim,’ and the Founder of the Moorim Association, a group of incredibly powerful Martial Artists that was formed on the Fifth Layer to give mankind a fighting chance at survival.

Emmanuel Stone was everything Micheal wasn’t – a natural-born martial art prodigy, the first known human Worldmaster, supremely talented in every way that mattered when it came to martial prowess.

Before he was finally killed by Sion, during their third duel on the Fifth Layer, Emmanuel had left behind a series of scrolls with Dark Void, detailing his growth, exploration, and the discoveries he made in his journey across the 7 Layers.

And among those, lay mention of what Micheal was currently experiencing.

Micheal broke through the flame barrier and-

The fight was on.

Jay sol Arget frowned the moment he saw Micheal appear, the Titled Deity’s left hand glowing white with energy. The Deity flicked his hand towards Micheal and-

Micheal cut down with Lightshorn in the same moment.

A shockwave split the air as two near-identical slices of Grandmaster Sword Energy collided, rupturing in a grand display of power.

Several of Constantine’s Seeds stumbled at the impact. Micheal didn’t flinch as he paused, letting the force wash past him, and then immediately jumped up into the air, holding Lightshorn out below him.

In that same moment, Jay sol Arget clenched his right hand, and then punched upward.

Instantly, a 37-meter-wide fist of seawater rocketed into existence, rapidly emerging from the ground surrounding the Titled Deity in a great towering spout as he knocked away several mid-air bolts of energy, at least four different explosive Artifacts thrown by members of the Revolutionaries, and several projectiles.

The waterspout splayed into the Nexus and was instantly vaporized as it hit the energy barrier that kept the Nexus’ energy self-contained, forming an enormous clump of fast-spreading fog-like clouds.

Micheal cut downward with Lightshorn, Master-Tier Sword Energy precisely parting the waters as he preserved his energy – and in the same movement, his Mana Blade shot forward, piercing through the great stream of water like it didn’t exist, imbued with Grandmaster Sword Energy.

Jay sol Arget appeared like a white, blurry figure through the walls of water that separated them – yet Micheal’s senses unerringly tracked him, even as he split the water beneath him to maintain a stable footing, hovering in the air on his Life Orbs.

Micheal felt his connection to his Mana Blade sever as it reached the Endwalker, a small explosion of energy disrupting the flow of water, before vanishing entirely.

Instinctively, Micheal ducked his head slightly to the right.

A fraction of a second later, a beam of white energy melted through the air exactly where his head had been, missing him by less than a quarter of an inch – once more, a near impossible dodge he never would’ve risked willingly.

‘He absorbed and redirected my attack, again.’

The spout of water stopped, opening a gap in the air for a brief moment, exposing Jay sol Arget’s position.

The tip of Lightshorn lowered almost to the ground in Micheal’s hand as he touched down on the metal platform before instantly cutting forward once more.

‘We’re harrying him now.’

Two beams of golden light slammed into Jay sol Arget’s waiting palms, both intercepted in the fraction of a second it took for Micheal to land. The Titled Deity sent those beams back towards their makers, his body twisted in the same moment as he noticed Micheal’s attack.

‘It’s working.’

Micheal spun to his left as a spear of darkness blitzed through where his chest had been a moment prior, his mind maintaining its unnatural state of calm as he dodged the attack by the barest movement.

His State of One was holding, and his contributions to the fight were forcing the Deity into a standstill.

‘To face a Titled Deity in combat...’

The words of Emmanuel Stone, recorded himself, in the scrolls he left behind.

‘You cannot stop.’

Emmanuel Stone was the only human to have fought Sion Swordsoul on the Fifth Layer and lived to tell the tale – surviving not just one but two separate duels against the famed Titled Deity.

‘Not for a moment, not for a second, never, at any point.’

Micheal twirled, flipping through the air as three more spears of darkness tried to pierce through where his heart had been. He relied heavily on his Cloud Stepping Shoes and his Life Orbs as he moved, every action he took made with exacting precision.

A huge, white beam of light slammed into Jay sol Arget’s right hand in the same moment Micheal was dodging, as Lux, and two of his Deathless Clones, stabbed forward while holding on to Stratos, the Spear of Time.

That energy hit Jay sol Arget’s palm and then exploded, diffusing in an enormous wall of white energy that blocked them off from the Titled Deity for a brief moment’s respite. Strange distortions in the air emerged as the Temporal Energy affected the world around them, creating random pockets of slowed and accelerated Time.

Micheal didn’t hesitate, instantly reaching out and grasping ahold of the nearest pocket of accelerated Time and-

He made it his own.

‘Time Zone.’

He created a tunnel of controlled, accelerated Time, boring through the wall of Time Energy, as he threw himself forward and-

He was greeted with Jay sol Arget’s irritated visage as Lightshorn, imbued with Grandmaster Tier Sword Energy, collided with the Endwalker's raised right arm, imbued with golden Master Tier Shield Energy.

A shockwave spread as the two energies clashed – Shield Energy, the most defensive form of Weapon Energy, resisted the cutting edge of his Grandmaster Tier Sword Energy, despite the difference in Mastery.

In a normal fight, in the clashes Micheal had experienced throughout his entire life in the 7 Layers, this was the point where there would be a pause.

There was an ebb and flow to combat, a give and take as man fought man, sentient against another sentient.

However…

‘You cannot stop.’

The Scythe of Chains appeared in Micheal’s left hand – he activated it instantly, aimed towards Jay sol Arget, even as he felt the boiling Ki in his veins flex, empowered by the Crown of the Angel King.

In that same moment, the Deity's free hand subtly sent out a fist-sized black skull of raw Curse Energy, the type of suffocating energy that would rot Micheal’s bones in their sockets.

Several black, semi-transparent chains warped their way into existence, intercepting the black skull of Curse Energy, freezing it in place.

This small interplay took less than a fraction of a second – and in the next moment, the two clashing energies, Master-Tier Shield Energy and Grandmaster Sword Energy, violently detonated, sending both combatants flying apart.

It was absurdly quick, sharp, and focused combat, complex at a speed most would fail to even notice.

This was not a normal fight.

Micheal dropped a Time Zone, accelerating his own time as he tumbled to the side, storing the Scythe of Chains, while using his Life Orbs to maintain his balance as he skidded across the surface of the slick metal platform, ducking under the flying skull of Curse Energy.

‘The State of One.’

It was, in the words of Emmanuel Stone, something he had developed on the spot in his duel with Sion Swordsoul – a counter to the absurdity that is a fully developed Titled Deity.

In a fight with a fully realized Titled Deity, there were no pauses, no ebb and flow of combat, no breaks in between attacks. It was a constant throughfare of battle that never ceased, where you had to attack, to defend, without pause, because to do anything else was to die.

Emmanuel had attributed this to the accumulation of Traits – Titled Deities, by their very nature, were the apex of their species, possessing an extreme number of Traits, accumulated over time.

They were entities enhanced to a point where it simply was not enough to be human and confront them.

The State of One was Emmanuel’s answer – it was a state of being, a focus where every emotion one had was discarded, as a warrior immersed themself within the Realm of Intent, casting aside all distractions, until the only thing present was themself, the world around them, and their target.

A state of clarity and control that only the most disciplined could grasp.

‘A symphony of control.’

Micheal’s talk with Bastien had proven enlightening, in ways he only realized later – as he took his own advice, making progress in a way he hadn’t expected.

Several explosions shook the air as Constantine’s Seeds rejoined the fight, giving Micheal a brief moment of reprieve.

Jay sol Arget’s figure was surrounded by a defensive orb of darkness as it repelled three lances of green energy, and dozens of arrows that appeared to be made of pure light.

“His energy levels are fading!” A shout from one of Constantine’s Seeds broke through the cacophony of noise.

‘We just need to stall him.’ Micheal held Lightshorn out in front of him, his eyes never leaving the orb of darkness.

For all the danger Jay sol Arget represented, there was one fact that lay in humanity’s favor – the Titled Deity was old, crippled by the actions he took to descend the Layers and hunt them.

Rain began to fall from the clouds formed by the waterspout vaporizing.

‘What-?’ Micheal felt his grasp of the State of One waver as he processed what his future sight was showing him.

“Careful! Lightni-“

43 bolts of lightning struck downward, emerging from the freshly formed clouds, the air booming as thunder rocked the world. These strikes of lightning were targeted, each aimed at striking down a member of the Revolutionaries, with three bolts in particular aimed at Micheal directly.

Micheal had managed to raise Lightshorn above his head in time to intercept one of the lightning bolts – the two others, however, blitzed around his sword, slamming directly into him.

The Lode Bastion Allmaster had gifted him glowed as it absorbed the energy attack, not quite shattering, but clearly straining as the Defensive Aritfact weathered the impact. This wasn’t regular lightning, but rather, something conjured by a Conceptual Power.

Micheal’s warning had proven useful – most of the Revolutionaries had reacted in time to defend themselves, as barriers sprang up, Defensive Artifacts activating or Abilities shielding them from the mass assault. The teams proved their elite nature, in weathering the surprise attack with minimal warning.

The simultaneous lightning strikes had lit up the area with blinding light, blasting away the orb of darkness that had protected Jay sol Arget, revealing the Titled Deity once more as he-

“A Hybrid?” Jay sol Arget froze, for the first time Micheal had seen him, his eyes going wide as he stared at Micheal, thunderstruck.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“A Hybrid?” Jay sol Arget’s eyes widened as he stared at the results.

‘Divine Scan.’

.

— - Divine Scan— -

Race: Heartflame Human

Title: -

Traits: Glass Cannon, Fortune’s Favor

STR: B+ (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

END: C+ (Growth Rate: Uncommon or higher)

REG: D+ (Growth Rate: Rare or lower)

SOUL: B+ (Growth Rate: Heroic or lower)

MANA: C (Growth Rate: Rare or higher)

Path Notes: A human that walks a cluttered Path. Strong traces of the Path of the Sword, and traces of the Path of Time, the Path of Rebirth, the Path of the Infinite, the Path of the Eternal, and the Path of Space are present.

.

He felt the burn in his Soul as he used up some more of his Divine Energy, feeling his energy stores wane. These humans, and in particular, this Hybrid, had proven more troublesome than he’d expected.

It was the first time he’d used his Divine Eyes since he started the Time Loop, always wary of burning away his limited energy stores. His Eyes had been honed over the centuries, letting him parse between this Hybrid's clearly enhanced energy state, to see their true baseline stats.

Ever since he Bound himself to the Loop, the only abilities he was free to use where those he drew from the Conceptual Powers he controlled – everything else, he had to conserve as much as possible.

‘What’s a Hybrid doing here?! To think, all this time, the Seer was a Hybrid…’ Jay sol Arget drew upon Time once more, slowing the world around him.

Hybrid – it was the term used for non-Deities that possessed the Titles System.

Most Deities were capable of procreation with non-Deities, their superior genetics capable of matching and successfully reproducing with any other sentient, no matter how inferior their genes might be.

Hybrids were the result of this procreation – a first generation breed that possessed the Titles System. Later generations possessed an extremely small, diminishing chance to also possess the Titles System, typically fading to non-existence by the 4th generation.

The existence of a Human Hybrid shocked Jay sol Arget to his core.

‘Was humanity backed by one of the other Dominions?!’ Was this all secretly a plot, targeted against the Endwalkers?!

All of a sudden, Jay sol Arget felt his worldview shift – if this was a plot by another Dominion, then everything made sense. Humanity’s strange powers, the resistance this inferior species put up, his own repeated failures.

Suddenly, his mission became all the more important, as countless questions flooded his mind.

‘This fight isn’t worth it.’ He instantly concluded.

Already, his energy stores ran low – even if the chance he lost here was incredibly low…

‘I need to nip this in the bud.’

He was dying, and resetting the Loop wouldn’t change that…

However, that didn’t mean he was out of options.

As Time reasserted itself, returning to its normal flow, Jay sol Arget raised his right hand upward and…

He activated his Title.

He drained a massive lump of energy from the Nexus and in the same motion, drew upon the full Mastery of Time, ignoring the cracks that formed in his Soul as…

He ripped a hole open in reality, a large, shivering vortex of Time, his Title drawing on the framework of the Loop, fundamentally altering reality itself. This change cost him, cost him dearly, the fractures in his Soul meaning this would be the last time he could touch upon any of his Conceptual Powers and he had mere minutes to live - but Jay sol Arget made peace with that fact.

His abrupt actions left his attackers with no time to respond as he stepped through the quivering hole and disappeared, leaving behind the pulsating vortex.

Jay sol Arget vanished, his body disappearing as…

He travelled backwards in Time, headed towards the start of the Loop.

.

Chapter 59


.

“Sto-“ The words died on Micheal’s lips.

Jay sol Arget was gone.

In his place lay a quivering, unstable vortex of white energy, a scar on reality that screamed into his senses, distorting the air around them as it pulsated. The eddies of Time diverged around the portal, in a sickening way that defied everything he knew about the Concept of Time.

The State of One came crashing down around Micheal as the world surged around him, a slew of emotions rushing back into focus.

Confusion. Worry. Horror.

‘What did he do?!’ Micheal spun around, trying to see if the Titled Deity had moved somewhere, all to no avail.

“What’s happened?!” Lux yelled over the roar of the pulsating vortex of Time Energy, several of his Deathless Clones supporting him as he stumbled over to Micheal.

There was a surreal sense of unreality that settled upon their shoulders, this close to the vortex in Time – it made the world seem off-kilter and strange.

“He’s gone!” Micheal yelled back, numbly, his senses tingling – he could feel the deep well of Time concentrated on the vortex, stretching in a way he couldn’t comprehend.

Several things happened all at once.

The lock on Space that Jay sol Arget had wrought vanished, as several portals appeared. Numerous golden barriers sprung up, partially sealing off the vortex, as Constantine’s Research Squad converged around the pulsating scar in reality. The other members of the Revolutionaries began to form a perimeter, while two Void Ships approached the floating metal platform, uncloaking as they emerged from seemingly thin air, discarding their complex Illusion Barriers.

“You need to deploy the package!” Lux shouted as he grabbed Micheal’s shoulder.

Micheal snapped back into focus.

He tapped on his Spatial Ring, bringing out the Artifact Marco had given him – the Local Field Spacetime Stabilizer, a hodgepodge of fused metals, covered in Magic Glyphs and various metal wires. On the side of it was a large red button, covered in a glass case.

To his enhanced senses, the Artifact had a strange presence in Space and Time, something Micheal couldn’t quite describe. It just felt odd.

He swiftly opened the glass case, remembering Marco’s instructions, and pressed the button a single time.

He blinked.

The Artifact, physically, didn’t look any different – but to the keen, enhanced senses of his Soul, it had just undergone a complete transformation. It now felt like an immense, gaping hole in Space and Time, a void where its presence should have been. Eerie. Unnatural. Strange.

‘One press to arm it, two to fire.’ Micheal paused as he looked up at the Nexus, and then over towards the vortex of Time Energy that Jay sol Arget had created.

‘Should I do this now? Or do I wait?’ Micheal frowned. How would the vortex affect things?!

Dark Void had accounted for-

Abruptly, in the corner of his vision, a faint, glimmer of gold flashed.

All of a sudden, Micheal knew beyond all reasonable doubt – activating the Artifact now would factor into his favor.

Micheal blinked again, almost flinching as he processed that.

‘What?!’ How did he know that? Before his mind could spiral into fears about mind control, a thought struck him and he opened the Titles System, pulling up his Traits.

.

— — - Trait: Fortune’s Favor- — —

Slightly alters Causality, in your favor

.

As soon as he focused on the Trait’s description, a sense of rightness settled onto his shoulders.

“Huh.” So that’s what it felt like?

‘A flash of gold.’ He made sure to memorize the feeling – the flash had been subtle, easily missed if he hadn’t been so high-strung in the moment.

“Micheal?” Lux was staring at him, a question in his eyes.

“Alright, I’m firing it.” Micheal made his decision as he tapped the button for a second time and…

The Artifact activated.

The world around him, for just a moment, became still.

Micheal’s connection to the Conceptual Powers of Space and Time, all of a sudden, became incredibly solid, as a small, yellow light flashed out, emitting from the various glyphs carved into the Artifact.

That moment passed and-

The Artifact half-exploded, half-fell apart in his hands, sending out several lines of glowing energy in strange patterns as the world returned to normal – well, as normal as it could be, given the circumstances.

‘Okay.’ The Artifact, at least how Marco had explained it, was a one-time use Artifact – its purpose spent, Dark Void hadn’t designed it to last beyond its first use.

Micheal stared up at the pulsating Nexus, squinting as he scanned it. Several tense seconds passed as he held his breath, studying the patterns of energy movement.

“It worked!” Micheal’s head snapped to the right as he stared down the speaker.

“Incredible… how did they manage that?”

It was one of the members of Constantine’s Research Squad – a strongly built, bearded man with short grey hair and a harsh face, holding up a large glass screen that glowed with various incandescent blue writings inscribed upon it, changing as he adjusted the strange Artifact – a sensor of some kind. Next to the speaker, several other researchers had setup two large metal poles, with a black box and an antenna aimed towards the Nexus.

“It’s still destabilizing, but the rate at which its undergoing destabilization has reversed. They’ve created a minor energy-feedback loop that shifts it to its original state… truly incredible work!” The man yelled as he stared up at the Nexus, his eyes wide,

“It’ll be cutting it close.” The man turned to one of his fellow researchers, pointing at the readings, before turning to give Micheal a nod.

“Some islands might still hit the Void before it finishes stabilizing – but the majority will fall between halfway and 2/3rds of the way down, and then recover, if this maintains. We’ll continue to monitor it in case of any further changes.” He turned away.

An immense weight seemed to lift off of Micheal’s shoulders.

‘One problem solved.’ He felt his energy boost from the Crown of the Angel King leave him in that moment, as he shattered a Life Orb to avoid dying.

The Nexus was stabilizing.

It wasn’t an instant change – the changes itself were incredibly subtle, but that had more to do with the nature of the Nexus itself – it was an absurdly dense concentration of energy. The fact that they were able to affect it at all was only possible because Jay sol Arget had tampered with it, giving Dark Void a pathway to revert his changes – and even then, only by causing the Nexus to return to its original state.

Changing it in any other way would be like attempting to strap a saddle to a raging hurricane.

As that thought crossed Micheal’s mind, the roaring noise from the scar Jay sol Arget had left audibly died down, as golden barriers fully sealed off that section of space, letting them converse at a normal level.

“Where did he go?” Micheal muttered as he stalked forward, storing Lightshorn and the Crown in his Spatial Ring.

As he walked up the barriers established by the Revolutionaries, he overheard some of the conversations taking place, as more of Constantine’s researchers set to work.

“…a paradox derived from what? Atoms aren’t functioning properly in this…”

“…got to be some kind of Claus-Fermi Temporal Object…”

“…particles are retrograding out of existence, not into, we can’t track that…”

Micheal’s presence was noted as he approached the barriers, one of the workers breaking off to intercept him. No one gave any commands to the person that broke off, and that person didn’t appear to be a leader of the Research Squad – it was yet another example of the eerie hivemind-esque influence Constantine had on his Seeds.

“What is this?” He asked, forcing down the frustration that was building within him, as he nodded towards the researcher, a man in his late 30s with bronze skin, short brown hair, and a scruffy brown beard.

He hated how out of control this situation felt – the lack of agency that came with dealing with Titled Deities was infuriating.

“Our readings are only preliminary, at this time but…”

Lux joined Micheal, his Deathless Clones dismissed, as the scientist continued,

“In layman’s terms – it’s a tear ripped through Time, an unstable portal of some kind.”

Micheal felt a pit form in the bottom of his stomach.

“Then Jay, he’s-“ Micheal forced himself to calm down,

‘We almost had him.’

“He’s travelled backwards in Time?” It was the worst case scenario.

“At this time, we believe that to be the case.” The researcher replied calmy as though his words weren’t confirming humanity’s doom, before glancing back at some of the other men and women crowding around the golden barriers.

By this point, Constantine’s Seeds had set up several large metal boxes, tables, and antenna, working away at whatever it is they were doing. The fog that had covered the area had finally begun to disperse, improving visibility.

“That’s bad.” Lux chimed in with a frown.

“Bad? It's catastrophic.” Micheal reeled back.

‘If Jay sol Arget is let loose in the past, he can change everything.’

All their struggles, all their efforts.

It would have been for nothing.

Erased, by the actions of a single entity.

A Titled Deity.

‘I cannot allow that.’ They couldn’t stop here, not now. Not after everything they’d done.

All it would take was one message making it out to one of Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clones, and everything would start tumbling down.

They knew Jay sol Arget was injured and this was supposed to be the Final Loop – but he was a Titled Deity.

It was entirely possible he could just try again.

“We can’t allow that.” Micheal spoke as conviction flooded him.

“The portal, the tear – can we use it to follow him?” Micheal grabbed the researcher’s arm as he turned to leave,

“That’s-“

“Impossible.” They were interrupted by the grey-bearded man from earlier, the researcher who had confirmed the Nexus had stabilized.

He didn’t give his name and Micheal didn’t ask for it – but from how the others reacted, he appeared to be the leader of the Revolutionaries Research Squad.

“What do you mean, impossible? We have Stratos, the Spear of Time. Surely-“ Micheal began, but was cut off.

“We don’t have the understanding to make it work.” The greybeard’s words were utterly cold as he cut in, holding up the same glass screen he’d used to scan the Nexus. He handed the screen off to another researcher after a moment, turning to face Micheal directly.

“Listen - all of this here is incredibly proprietary, powers warping reality that we’ve barely touched the surface of. With what we do know, this shouldn’t even be possible.” He shook his head,

“Controlling it is beyond us – right now, we need to focus on the downstream effects.” He turned away, his words filled with a sense of finality.

This was the work of a Titled Deity – obviously, it made sense it wasn’t something that could be comprehended by normal means, because it wasn’t something made by normal means. It was a fundamental altering of reality, something that should not be possible.

Micheal bit his lips until they bled.

Dark Void might be able to do something – but Dark Void wasn’t here.

They had run out of time.

Micheal took several steps back as he stared past the golden barrier, staring numbly at the rippling tear in reality Jay sol Arget left behind.

It felt like the world was closing in around him again.

The hopelessness that Titled Deities wrought in the first timeline, where they left desolation, destruction, and death in their wake.

‘Think. Think!’ His heart throbbed as his mind raced, his hands shaking,

‘There’s got to be something, another way, surely, I just need to think-‘

“Steady.” Lux’s voice was soft as he grabbed Micheal’s shoulder.

The physical touch shocked Micheal out of his fugue as he blinked.

‘Right.’ He shook his head, clearing his mind. It was a rare lapse in control, the circumstances getting the better of him, for the first time in a very long time.

‘Adapt.’ The thought was bitter as he felt the sting of reality hit him.

They were so close, to give up now felt unthinkable, unforgiveable – yet what could they do?

“I have an idea.”

Micheal jerked his head to the side, staring at Lux intensely.

Lux held up a hand, donning a frown.

“I don’t want to get your hopes up, but I agree with you.” He nodded towards the rippling portal, his voice filled with determination,

“We can’t just stop now.” Lux waved towards the greybeard leader of the Research Squad, commanding him over. The head researcher walked back towards them with a frown.

“I don’t know anything about time-travel, but… you travelled back once and made it. And with Stratos here, as long as I fire it properly, I think-“ Lux paused, before he shook his head,

“I know-“ He began, his words filled with a sense of certainty, “-that we can leap backwards, using the structure of that portal, just like the Ritual you said Dark Void constructed for you – we can follow the trail Jay sol Arget left behind.”

The greybeard jumped into the conversation, his voice stern.

“Even if, by some miracle-“

“I’m quite fortunate – I wouldn’t say even a miracle is beyond me at my best, and I’m feeling… lucky.” Lux interrupted, his eyes gleaming, his voice almost fanatic in its certainty.

“I’m aware.” The greybeard returned dryly before continuing,

“Even if by some miracle everything goes in your favor, the trip upstream would kill you.”

“I can survive that.” Micheal returned, a cinder of hope flaring in his heart.

“I’ve lived through worse.” Had he? The point was moot as he pressed forward.

“I still have this.” He pulled out the special ring Dark Void had given him, to protect his Spatial Ring as he travelled back in Time.

“I can survive with the tools I need to confront Jay sol Arget.”

“You’ll need my luck to aim us right.” Lux said as he took a step forward, his eyes intense.

“Both of us will make the journey back.”

Micheal frowned.

“The journey- even in the best-case scenario, the Ritual Dark Void used was enough to kill me.” He began, but paused as Lux shook his head.

“I know, Micheal.” Lux had a small smile on his face.

“That’s fine.”

The words took Micheal aback as he blinked, before the full realization settled upon his shoulders.

“Lux.” Micheal started, his heart plummeting,

“Surely there’s-“

Before he could continue, however…

“Hahaha. HAHAHA!” Lux turned away as he stared up at the sky, laughing out loud until tears formed on his eyes.

As the luckiest human to walk the 7 Layers laughed…

Black particles coalesced, rising off of Lux’s form until they formed a black orb, floating in the air above him.

Micheal recognized it instantly as he stepped back, Lightshorn appearing in his hands instinctively.

It was one of Constantine’s Seeds.

“Even he agrees, huh? Holding true to our bargain, here at the very end? And Rex as well?” Lux spun around, his eyes lit with mad light as he grinned at Micheal, his smile a fierce rictus of joy.

“Very well. It’s a choice I make of my own free will.”

As Lux spoke, two of Constantine’s men broke off, one of them raising a glass, cylindrical container, and capturing the Seed, while the other activated an Ability that covered the Seed with white light. The two men turned away immediately as they contained the Seed, breaking Micheal’s line of sight.

‘They can store them outside of someone?’ He hadn’t known that, filing that information away to share with Dark Void and the Round Table for later.

His focus returned back to Lux.

“Don’t try to dissuade me, Micheal.” Lux’s grin widened,

“It’s the first choice I’ve made, of my own true, free will, in a very long time.” He laughed out loud as he looked back up at the sky,

“I’ve made up my mind.” He looked back down, his face serene.

Micheal clenched his fists as he stored Lightshorn, before giving Lux a slow, stiff nod.

Lux broke off as he began to talk with the greybeard researcher, breaking down into an argument of technicalities as they worked out the details on how to best prepare for the journey backwards. The duo walked over to the other members of the Research Squad, as they set to work.

Micheal looked up at the sky, where Lux had stared, seeing naught but the cold, dark atmosphere of the Third Layer, before he slowly closed his eyes.

It wasn’t fair.

It never was.

Lux was a truer hero than any of them.

He shouldn’t have to die for this – not after he just gained his freedom, what he’d been fighting for all this time.

And it cut at Micheal, deep down, at his very core, because…

Because he knew he wouldn’t turn Lux down.

He would use him, his death, no matter how unfair it was to Lux.

‘For all mankind.’ The thought tasted like ash on his tongue.

No matter what he had to do, no matter what kind of monster he needed to become, the sacrifices he needed to make…

‘I’ll kill you.’ Micheal’s eyes cracked open, as he stared up at the uncaring sky, into the darkness that unfolded all around him.

He burned their names into his mind, the Titled Deities that forced him to be like this.

‘I’ll kill you all.’

Soon, the scant preparations they could make to aid them on their journey had been completed.

The golden barriers were dropped, the roaring echo of Time returning.

Lux and Micheal locked arms, chained together by a set of Artifacts Constantine’s men had provided, as they approached the portal in Time. His Spatial Ring and other Artifacts were sealed up, in the same Time Seal provided to him by Dark Void for his first journey back.

As they approached the portal in Time, the world around them began to distort. Seconds whipped back and forth as Time became strange, the world around them shifting in ways he couldn’t begin to describe.

“Thanks, Micheal, for everything!”

Lux’s words hit his ears, shouted over the roar of the world around him as Micheal looked to his right.

“I just wanted to say.” Lux smiled warmly as the world around them began to light up, the Spear of Time glowing in his hands.

“To work with a hero like you, well…” Lux gave Micheal a small nod,

“It’s been an honor!” Lux laughed out loud.

And, before Micheal could reply, the words ‘the honor was mine’ on the tip of his tongue…

“See you on the other side!” Lux smirked.

Everything went white, and-

They were gone.

.

Chapter 60


.

A blur of white.

Rassthor Fang was a genius.

It was a thought Jay sol Arget pondered every time he drew upon the Mastery of Time he Unbound from the fallen Lizardman.

The Head Shaman had been a consummate professional, commanding a coalition of Tribes that all hated each other without letting his region fall into disarray. If not for his ambitious nature, Jay could’ve seen the Lizardman reigning over the continent of Reffa for decades to come.

The Endwalker Dominion valued order above all else. Every garden world under their control was ruled by a system of Governors, assigned leaders of the client species that served under their protection, forming the resource gathering and manpower loops necessary to garrison the two crown jewels of their Dominion – Veroth, the World of the End, and Myr, the World of Blue Wonders.

Rassthor, like everyone else, wanted to change his lot in life – all client species received a basic education about the Endwalker Dominion, and naturally, as a result, would want to move to Veroth or Myr. They were the most highly developed garden worlds, a virtual paradise where Endwalker rule proved its superiority, compared to the other Dominions.

Reality stretched around Jay sol Arget, streaks of white and black whipping past him, as he tore his way through Time.

‘Your prowess is being put to good use.’

Travelling backwards through Time, altering the natural course of the River of Time, was a crime upon existence, punishable by immediate execution. To violate the Temporal Edict was to put a target upon the entire Endwalker Dominion’s back – and if they didn’t enforce it, the other Dominions would.

If Jay sol Arget was being honest – he knew he wasn’t a true believer in the Temporal Edict. Heresy, the thought was, and yet it was true nonetheless.

Jay sol Arget was a survivor. A soldier.

Once a slave – never again.

He would use any tool, any power, any card in his repertoire to protect his people.

Even the Mastery of a Heretic who violated the Temporal Edict.

The streaks of white flashing by began to grow in brightness, a heavy sensation settling upon Jay sol Arget’s crippled Soul.

‘I’m almost there.’

Rassthor had known that tampering with the past would see his doom.

And yet – a failure to contain a civil war that broke out between two Tribes under his overview had almost seen the Head Shaman removed from his position. Rassthor had obtained his position as Head Shaman from his prowess as a Master of Time, facing down and defeating all challengers – yet the crown of leadership required more than just martial prowess.

The Head Shaman sought a position on the End Senate, the highest body that governed the minutiae of the Endwalker Dominion, acting at the behest of Ixon, the official Ruler of the Dominion.

Rassthor’s obsession got the best of him, as it tended to with most Masters of Time – to ensure his record remained perfect, he researched heretical applications of Time – the ability to endlessly ‘Loop’ Time, to ensure his record remained clean.

‘One more leap.’ And he would have travelled far enough upstream.

Jay sol Arget felt his Soul strain as he reached the end of his journey, his senses whiplashing around him as reality distorted.

In the end Rassthor’s obsession blinded him – his Loops succeeded in the short term, leaving him with a near perfect record. But, as most things that tampered with Time, there was a cost, an incredible energy cost to pay - and he didn't have an almighty Title to let him cheat that cost. His Loops were imperfect, fueled with sacrifices, dark Rituals that saw the deaths of thousands of innocent Lizardmen under his purview.

An unacceptable waste of life, violating the core agreement that bound all client species to the Endwalker Dominion – and, far worse, in the eyes of the others: heresy, in its rawest form, a clear example that showed why the Temporal Edict was to be followed by all.

Reality shifted, and Jay sol Arget was freed from the thoughts of his past as the world around him came into focus.

With a faint ‘thunk’ Jay sol Arget landed on the grounds of a large, barren floating island, on the western side of the Outer Ringlands. The island was roughly 80 meters wide and a good 200 meters thick, a massive edifice of scarred rock and stone, bereft of life.

“Yes!” Victory was his!

The instant he touched down, everything came slamming back into him.

Pain, agony, power, age – his body began to fall apart almost immediately.

BIND

The activation of his Title was instinctive, as he Rebound himself to the Loop. It was a frayed thing, this connection, a strand he had abused over and over and over and over thousands of times by this point.

Yet – it would last, for the time he needed.

‘I must eliminate the threat.’ Jay sol Arget held up his hands, his mind slightly delirious.

The energy he had absorbed from the Nexus was overwhelming, now that he was present in the physical realm once more. Power, far too much power for his crippled Soul, it was too much for his state he had to-

‘Attack.’

A massive shockwave cratered the island, rupturing the earth as three enormous beams of energy melted through the air before vanishing – cast not just across Space but also Time.

The action cost Jay sol Arget – his body had been drenched in Paradox-derived Time Energy, a side-effect of how he forced himself down the Layers. All of that energy drained away, used as fuel to aim these attacks – yet in doing so, Jay sol Arget felt his connection to the Loop sever.

He was still Bound to the Loop, thanks to his Title – but this was the end. He could no longer influence or control it in any way.

A reverberation in Time hit him as the attacks finished vanishing, disappearing from his eyesight. The Titled Deity knelt down on one knee, before looking upward, a frown on his face.

‘It might not be enough.’ There was no way to confirm his attack, even here in the past.

He knew their exact coordinates, thanks to the many Loops he had suffered through.

Shin Hopefell.

Basten Amiot.

Aaron Bartram.

The three who Ixon said would prove disastrous for the Endwalker Dominion, in the far future, in the fight to claim control of the Final Layer.

And the Hybrid, the Seer, not mentioned in Ixon’s prophecies, but the one responsible for foiling so many of Jay sol Arget’s attempts.

His ambush was mighty, an energy attack that would decimate their locations, drawn from the Nexus itself…

But his enemies were like Bampfa Rats, vermin that simply refused to die, no matter what you threw at them.

‘Just to be safe…’ Jay sol Arget nodded as he took a deep breath, a shudder of relief flowing through him.

He held out his right hand. In it, his Divine Energy began to condense, careful manipulation of power forming into the shape of a bird.

In it, he would craft a message, to convey to his Paradox Clones and let his past self know-The world around Jay sol Arget stood still.

A moment later…

A roaring echo in Time burst into reality as Jay sol Arget spun around and-On the neighboring floating island, a smaller island roughly 40 meters wide and 30 meters long, dotted with large, bumpy boulders…

Two humans fell to the ground, naked and covered in blood.

Jay sol Arget saw red.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

A Life Orb shattered – 5 down to 4.

Awareness came to Micheal in mid-air.

In one moment, he was locking arms with Lux, stepping into a portal in Time.

In the next…

Micheal felt for his Spatial Ring and-

Agony.

His Soul screamed, almost causing him to convulse as he retched.

The Spatial Ring was there still, he felt – the Time Seal provided by Dark Void had worked, but his Soul felt like it was on fire. Even the thought of trying to touch upon his Sword Mastery was enough to cause him physical pain as he fell.

“Lux?” As his bare feet hit the ground, he fell down on one knee and looked to his side.

He held back a wince.

Lux looked… horrible, his clothes shredded like Micheal’s had been. Long lines of blood trailed up and down a body covered in a thousand cuts, a thousand scars. His entire body was a mess of injuries, and while the cuts didn’t look deep, the sheer number of them made him worry the man’s luck had finally run out.

The Spear of Time, Stratos, however, looked completely fine – it was unblemished, untouched by the temporal leap.

Lux’s eyes fluttered open and-

“Go!”

Micheal’s words kickstarted Lux into action, uttered the instant he saw the man was still alive.

Two Deathless Clones appeared by Lux’s side, looking far better than Lux did, clad in thin white armor. The Clones immediately picked up Lux’s main body and flung themselves away, carrying the former Seed and the Spear of Time away from their location.

It was something they had agreed prior to their trip – if Lux survived the journey, he was to prioritize his mission to return the Spear of Time – their entire journey was all predicated on the Spear of Time being exactly where it needed to be, tucked away in Micheal’s room when he searched for it.

The fact that Lux was still alive, if barely, was a testament to the man’s incredible luck – but his current state made him a liability – it sounded bad, but this was honestly the best-case scenario Micheal had envisioned and-UNBIND

Micheal died, the life force within his body ripped away as his corpse fell to the ground, a withered husk.

A Life Orb shattered – 4 down to 3.

An ethereal fogscape spread out around Micheal as he processed his death.

‘He’s here!’ Micheal snarled, in his ghostly form, as he felt the pull of his respawn call to him and-He saw, in the limited view he had of the world around him, a small energy projection of a bird begin to fly away, about 2 meters to the left of where he had died.

Without even thinking, Micheal respawned as far away as he could, in the direction the energy-bird thing was flying.

He appeared, naked and weaponless, on the ground next to a pile of stones.

One of the stones was in his hand the moment he touched down, and in the next-The rock whistled through the air as he threw it, hurtling through the grim sky and slamming directly into the energy construct with pinpoint accuracy.

He grabbed two more rocks and grunted – his Ki felt sluggish, as off-kilter as his Soul – it still responded to him, enhancing him, but he had nowhere near the level of control he was used to having. Worse, he could already tell that the side-effects of his unsanctioned Time Travel would take hours, if not days, to fully subside.

“Where are you?!” Micheal spat as his 3 Life Orbs flew out around him, circling him as he stepped backwards, ignoring the faceless man rapidly approaching him.

Jay sol Arget was nowhere to be seen.

Micheal’s gaze rapidly took in his surroundings as he continued to cautiously step backwards, his Life Orbs rotating faster and faster.

‘He needs to die.’ Any method, any plan, he would accept, no matter the process.

He was somewhere in the Outer Ringlands – the floating islands near him where all barren, rocky creations bereft of life. To his right was a large floating island with an enormous crater, a network of cracks spreading out from a singular point. Just looking at the crater made him wince – his Soul, as unstable as it felt, seemed to resonate with the energy around that crater’s location.

Energy that reminded him of something, his perfect memory letting him recall that sensation asHis Life Orb bumped into something.

Micheal threw himself to the side while, in the same motion, throwing both stones at exactly where his Life Orb had hit. The two stones exploded in mid air, hitting…

Nothing, as a figure stumbled back.

‘Dust!’ For a brief moment, Micheal saw a haze of stone dust act unnaturally in the air-The dust was gone as Micheal leapt across the gap between this island, landing on the much larger island with the large crater.

Despite his sluggish Ki, his body held strong, his Glass Cannon Trait unaffected by his weakened state.

He felt the skin of his hands break as he clawed away two chunks of rock while rolling on the ground. He then ducked forward and spun around, keeping his Life Orbs rotating around him at all times. Blood dripped down his palms as his right knee hit the ground, his body tensing in a ready stance and-Another energy projection took flight.

Another stone sailed through the air, sniping down the small bird of energy as it tried to soar away from the island Micheal had arrived on.

“Your struggle is pointless.”

The words seemed to echo, coming from nowhere and everywhere as Micheal half-crawled, half-walked several steps backwards, free hand finding another stone. The cracked grounds of this island cut at his feet as he walked, blood trailing his every step.

“So he speaks!” Micheal returned as his eyes flickered from left to right.

‘I need to keep him here.’

“You think your sacrifice here will change anything, Hybrid?” The Endwalker’s words contained barely concealed rage, once more echoing all around him, as a faceless man leapt back across to the island Micheal was on.

“I’d like to think so.” Micheal returned, shifting his Life Orbs’s rotation to be more random, as his lungs burned and the figure approached.

“Pathetic.” The words sounded uncomfortably close as-

UNBIND

Micheal’s body collapsed, life ripped away.

A Life Orb shattered – 3 down to 2.

“Every second you waste, your own life force staves off – your resistance is meaningless.”

Micheal’s Soul throbbed as he returned to his ethereal fogscape.

'He's in as bad a shape as me.'

He respawned a dozen meters away, next to a cluster of bowling ball sized rocks that were partially embedded into the cratered ground. His left hand slammed into the rocks, several small bones cracking as he wrenched free several baseball sized chunks of rock.

‘Come on, keep him talking…’ He resisted the urge to look up, his gaze focused towards where he had just died.

He felt at his Spatial Ring again – this time, he was able to fight through the pain. He could bring it out, he felt, but only if he had a few seconds to focus, undisturbed – something Jay sol Arget wasn’t keen to give him.

Micheal threw the cracked stones with enough force to shatter them, halfway between him and his last death’s spot.

A haze of stone dust clouded the air and-

Part of that cloud disappeared.

Micheal didn’t hesitate as he hurled another stone exactly where the dust was missing and-The stone vanished, disappearing entirely.

BIND

Two more stones quickly followed, flung through the air and sailing through the empty spot in the cloud of dust, hitting nothing.

“Your death will be meaningless.”

It happened so quickly, Micheal barely had time to react as-

UNBIND

The stone he’d just thrown materialized, flung through the air and smashing directly into his right knee. The crunch of bone echoed sickly as a wave of nauseating pain swept through him, acknowledged, and then ignored as-Micheal flung himself to the side, relying on his left leg to move him as he kept his Life Orbs spinning around him.

‘Nearly there!’

His hands bled freely as they scrabbled along the hard, cracked rock, pulling out chunks of stone that he threw behind him as hard as he could.

“This is your grand plan, Hybrid?” He could hear the condescending sneer in the Endwalker’s tone.

The stones Micheal threw vanished as they collided with nothing in mid-air.

BIND

“Throwing stones?”

UNBIND

Micheal’s left arm snapped, bones shattering as a rock collided with it, immediately becoming useless. In the same moment, his left knee shattered, another rock slipping through his guard – Jay sol Arget’s attacks were simply too abrupt, perceptible only at the last moment, for him to dodge in his sluggish state.

Micheal went down in a heap, as his free hand struggled to find another stone and-His Life Orb hit something-

UNBIND

And then that Life Orb was gone – vanished from Micheal’s control, its very existence Unbound as good as if it had been shattered.

1 Life Orb remained.

In the same moment, another stone shot through the air, slamming into Micheal’s head – this one, he just barely managed to pull back on, feeling his cheekbone crack as it brutally bounced off his head.

‘Stay alive! A little more!’

“Yeah, but I’ve got a secret weapon you don’t know about.” Micheal returned as he dragged himself across the ground, superhuman strength letting him fling his body into the center of the crater left behind by Jay sol Arget’s attack.

“What?” The Endwalker deigned to reply, a hint of caution appearing in its voice but-

‘It’s here!’

It was too late.

Micheal grinned, his smile a bloody rictus as his head lolled back, staring at the sky above, as he answered, “Friends in high places.”

For a split second, nothing happened, as a memory shot to the forefront of Micheal’s brain.

A conversation he had with the Commander of the Round Table – a discussion that went on for hours and hours, over the most minute of details, an entire day spent theorizing together.

A moment of trust, a leap of faith, where both sides confided everything they knew in one another, every relevant fact or detail, no matter how minor.

Everything.

That split second passed and-

The heavens cracked open.

A lance of white energy blasted forth, raw, ultra-condensed power screaming down with the rage of a dying God.

“No-“

Jay sol Arget’s last words didn’t reach Micheal’s ears, but it didn’t matter as-They, them, the floating island, and every nearby floating island were annihilated simultaneously, in a regal display of destruction at its core, shockwaves blasting through the air as even the air itself melted away.

An ambush of epic proportions…

With its Vectors reversed.

A Life Orb shattered and-

Victory was theirs.

“…”

“…”

“…”

Micheal’s mind was woozy as he respawned, falling towards the Void, before he finally managed to bring out his Spatial Ring.

Agony ripped through his Soul as his Ki activated, sluggish but still there and-A pair of Neo-Levitation Bracers appeared on his arms.

The Artifact activated and Micheal cast himself through the air, his arm wrenching as he just barely avoided falling into the Void.

There was no Points Notification, not for him, because the credit for this attack wouldn’t go to him, not based on how the Shop mechanics worked. Jay sol Arget's death had been abrupt, no epic showdown or clean clash, but Micheal couldn't care less.

Victory was all that mattered.

And of that, Micheal was certain.

Victory had been achieved, because…

As he hurtled through the sky, rapidly closing the distance on a barren floating island just far enough away to survive the blast…

A notification appeared.

.

— — - Titles System - — —

Your achievements have earned you a new Trait Selection.

.

A new Trait appearing so quickly after another required an achievement of immense proportions, something incredible, absurd, beyond all recognition.

As he reached the island and stumbled down into a rough landing…

Micheal’s vision began to blur and-

The world around him vanished as he officially completed his First Step to a Trait Cycle and...

A vision descended upon him.

.
