Chapter 61


.

This was the end.

After breaking line of sight with Micheal, Lux’s Deathless Clones carried him from island to island, making great leaps as they fled the scene. Lux could only pray, as he heard through his Clones the sounds of combat unleash behind them, that Micheal would prove victorious.

And, well…

He had faith.

Micheal, a man cursed with knowledge, had taken to every challenge in his path with the kind of fortitude and determination that Lux envied.

It was like watching a hero from a story book come to life.

The man came face to face with horrors beyond imagination and just kept on fighting.

It was inspiring, truly.

‘Ah.’ Lux felt his heart tremble.

‘This is it for me.’

Lux commanded his two Deathless Clones to stop as they landed atop a small, barren floating island, roughly 8 meters wide and 12 meters long.

He opened his weary eyes as his Clones leaned him up against a boulder on the edge of the floating island, overlooking the dark, endless Void.

‘No ring.’ His hands were bare, apart from the shreds of flesh hanging off and blood marring them.

He’d hoped his luck would let his Spatial Ring survive the journey – alas, the Artifact had shattered, turned to a useless metal husk. All the Defensive Artifacts he’d donned had been ripped apart by their trip through Time.

‘No matter.’ He hadn’t held anything particularly important in his ring. Sure, the occasional Artifact, food supplies, the usual that was just smart to keep handy – but he’d never really been a front-line fighter, not in person – powerful Artifacts were best used on keeping the men and women he had served with alive.

Lux coughed, a brutal, wheezing cough, as blood bubbled up from his lips.

He was dying.

His luck, it seemed, had finally run out.

His body was ruined beyond repair, his bones shattered, his organs shredded – the only thing keeping him alive right now was his Lord Tier Ki, and even that was slowly fading.

It was a miracle he wasn’t already dead – and yet, he knew his time was drawing near.

“You.” He commanded his first Deathless Clone.

The Clone stepped forward as it immediately grasped his intent.

The Clone walked over to the center of the floating island. It then grasped Stratos tightly in its hands and-It harshly twisted the Spear, dropping it on the ground while jumping away in one motion.

The spear skidded over the stone as it rotated, twirling about at the center of the floating island as its momentum slowly ran out.

Finally, the spear came to a halt, pointing in a specific direction, roughly opposite of where they had originally arrived, but slightly down, at an angle.

“You will travel in that direction to Axellion, and hide the Spear of Time until the time is right, to place it where it needs to be.” He commanded, implanting his desire firmly within the Clone.

The trick with the spear was one of the ways he had learned to leverage his luck – whenever he got lost, he simply spun a stick, a sword, anything really, and walked in the direction it pointed. It was a silly trick, but one that had never failed him when it came to finding places he had already travelled to once before.

His Clone silently nodded and immediately set off, fleeing from this floating island without any hesitation as it headed West.

Lux turned his gaze to his other Deathless Clone, scrutinizing it.

Deathless Clones were one of the more unique Clone Abilities purchasable in the Shop – they shared the same memory issue that many Clone Abilities had wherein, beyond a certain point, the farther away they were from Lux’s main body, the looser their memories became – something caused by the dynamic Soul aspect inherent to these types of Clones, at least that was what Constantine’s research teams had surmised. Some mumbo jumbo that never really made sense to Lux.

What he did know, however, from his own lived experience: imprinting certain commands on the Clone would allow them to complete exactly what they were ordered, no matter how weak their memories became. It was how he’d managed to leak information about Constantine’s existence to the rest of humanity.

“As for you.” Lux whispered quietly to the Clone.

Deathless Clones had another aspect unique to them, and the reason for their namesake.

“I need you to carry a message.”

Even if the Ability user had died or no longer existed on the same world, Deathless Clones would continue to exist, so long as they had energy to run. Their memories would weaken, but any commands left within them would be acted out, precisely as ordered.

Lux paused as he considered his words.

Even now – he had to be careful in his actions, to avoid alerting Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clones here in the past.

‘This one will leave a message for Micheal.’ He would send it to the Commander of the Round Table, a close confidant of the ‘Seer.’

‘We’ve travelled back far into the past. We should be close to the start of the Loop.’ It was knowledge that came inherent with his activation of the Spear of Time.

‘I’ll send it then.’ On the same day his main body and Rex visited the Round Table – he had already memorized the route to the Commander of the Round Table’s office thanks to his first visit.

His Clone would slip in and out, just a simple case of him returning to leave a message for Micheal, nothing out of the ordinary, right after his main body and Rex had left. There was a perfect window of opportunity that wouldn’t arouse suspicion as long as he timed it close enough.

‘I wonder – will my Clones’ memories be boosted since my past self’s main body is in Axellion?’ It was a question he wouldn’t have time to learn the answer to.

“As for the message…” Lux paused.

‘I'll leave it where we met'.

‘Hmm.’

He didn’t want to say anything that would interfere with the delicate order of events that had made all of this possible. The message was short and to the point, and he knew Micheal would understand what it meant, when the time came.

However…

There was a small part of Lux that couldn’t help but want to be greedy.

‘I… just this once.’

He adjusted the command for his Deathless Clone, rewriting the note: ‘Goodbye, I’ll leave it where we met.’

Lux smiled.

The Micheal that would read this note wouldn’t realize it… but this was where they would be parting ways.

His final goodbye.

‘The honor was mine.’ It was a message Micheal had yelled while they were in the midst of travelling through Time, the only memory that made it through to Lux, apart from blurred streaks of white.

“I achieved my goals.” Lux whispered as he imprinted his commands on the final Clone, sending it dashing off on its journey – the Clones were separated now, and nothing that happened to Lux would affect them.

“It’s over.”

Regrets?

Of those, Lux had not one.

He had fought for and obtained not just his own freedom, but Rex’s too.

He’d lived his life, made true friendships, and fought with heroes larger than life, for a cause he could believe in. He did what he could, with the lot he was given and…

That was okay.

“Until next time...” Lux closed his eyes with a smile on his face.

“Farewell.”

His heart slowed.

His body hunched forward and…

The silence of the world embraced him as Lux fell into the Void.

The last thought that came upon him, as he passed the Demarcation Line that trapped him inside the Void…

In the corner of his vision, he saw a sparkle of gold.

.. .. .. .. ..

beep

beep

beep

Shin sat with his fingers interlocked as his chin rested on his hands, his elbows on his knees. Around him, the world bustled with activity as Dark Void scientists adjusted various machines and Artifacts, having created a large open-air laboratory here in the Outer Pavilions.

Jay sol Arget’s Clones had been dealt with, his ambush foiled, thanks to the timely warnings of Kim Jiwoon. The abrupt ambush had sent a shockwave through those present, spurring everyone into action.

Relief efforts were underway for the damaged portions of Axellion, taking up the attention of Duke Atlas and all present Knight Companies, including the Round Table. Kyvenval’s crystallization attack had killed thousands, but not everyone affected was dead – there were those only partially glimpsed, with hands or arms partially transformed, that needed immediate medical attention.

Duke Atlas had managed to stabilize Axellion despite his injuries, in a masterful display of Magic, independent of what was causing the other islands to fall. Several enormous magic circles floated above Axellion, shifting gravity and keeping the City’s floating island stable.

So, for now, regardless of what happened to the rest of the Third Layer…

They were safe.

And…

Now all he could do was wait.

He’d offered to help with the relief efforts, but the Knights had turned him away – Axellion was placed under martial law at this point in time, and the only reason humanity was even being tolerated right now was simply due to the undeniable fact that it was Humans who defeated the attacking Apex Void Predators and the Speedster that had invaded Axellion.

beep

beep

beep

Shin breathed in and exhaled, feeling exhaustion ping at him. He flexed the fingers of his upgraded Melding Plate Arm as he stared at the monitor in front of him.

The other islands were still falling.

This monitor, a large grey machine with a green screen and several lines on it, transmitted what Marco said was the stabilization of this Layer’s ‘gravitational plane.’

Shin didn’t really understand the science of it, but apparently, this far from the center of the Empty Sea, it was impossible to tell exactly what was going on with the Nexus right now. Presumably, Micheal had gone back in time and activated the Artifact, the Local something stabilizer or whatever…

But they would only know once the floating islands stopped falling.

‘Or if they hit the Void.’ He banished the thought from his mind.

“How’re ye holding up there, Ironarm?”

Shin blinked, glancing up.

The speaker was none other than Rex, the huge man grinning as he sat down next to Shin, holding two fancy looking wine bottles, one in each hand. He held out one of the bottles, handing it to Shin.

Shin accepted it, moving almost on autopilot before he realized what he was accepting. He stared down at the bottle, and then back at Rex, bewildered.

Rex shrugged.

“Nicked it off some of the fancier tables, not like they’ll be missin’ it in all this.” Rex gestured vaguely around them as he popped off the cork sealing the bottle, before taking a swig. The powerful human was visibly intoxicated.

“That was some damn good fightin’ you did out there.” Rex remarked, giving Shin a nod.

“Just did what needed to be done.” Shin shook his head, returning his gaze to the monitor a dozen meters in front of him.

“Worried, eh? I get ya. Can’t deny I’m in the same boat, what with Lux gone en’ all.” Rex chuckled, before his gaze gradually grew somber.

Shin eyed the powerful human for a moment.

“You and Lux are… close?” He offered.

Rex nodded.

“Lux did good by me, y’know? He’s like the brother I never had.” Rex ran a hand through his shaggy black hair.

“We’ve been through thick and thin together. He’s kept me outta all sorts’a messes.” Rex chuckled, his words slightly slurring.

“I never was one for seein’ the big picture, y’know? But Lux…” Rex shook his head.

“He always had that vision. Always lookin’ forward to the future.”

Rex’s words hit Shin like a rogue wave at sea.

‘Like a brother I never had.’

That thought reminded Shin of the first time he met Micheal, and the day that spawned a friendship that would last the rest of their lives.

Back on Earth, in simpler times, when he was just a kid, going to a new public elementary school after finally being adopted. Some of the other kids had cornered Shin during recess, making fun of him because he had a weird name.

‘Shin’ – it wasn’t a normal name they said. Looking back, it was a childish, stupid fight – but kids were cruel, thoughtless, in ways they didn’t truly understand.

That was when Micheal had barged in, knocking past the other students as if he cared nothing for what they thought.

“Shin, huh?” Little Micheal had said, before giving Shin a small nod.

“I like it. S’cool name.”

His words had sparked a fist fight, Shin and him vs the other kids that saw both of them get in trouble, given the zero tolerance policy at their school. Shin had apologized profusely, but Micheal waved it off like it was nothing.

And to him, maybe it was just another day in his life.

But to Shin, it was a memory that would live in his heart for the rest of his days.

“Yeah.” Shin muttered as he snapped back to the present.

“I get that, Rex.” He really did.

After a moment, Shin looked down at the bottle, and then made a decision.

He popped the cork, and took a small swig of his own. The rich flavor of berries and spices tinged the back of his throat as he swallowed enough to feel a slight burn.

He then paused, after a moment, before holding the bottle out in front of him.

“For you, Vesper.” He poured out some of the wine on the ground in front of him, watching it spatter against the cracked stone.

‘Micheal said there was a way to resurrect people on the Sixth Layer.’ It was one of the many strange facts his best friend had seen in his visions of the future.

‘Wait for me, Ves.’ He made a quiet promise.

A few moments passed, as the duo nursed their worries and the world marched on around them.

And then…

“What?!” Rex froze, his tone one of absolute shock, to the point where it made Shin pause, turning to look at the big man.

Two other of Constantine’s Seeds had approached them, one carrying a clear cylinder container. One of those men had knelt down next to Rex, holding out the container as…

A small, black orb of energy rose from Rex’s body, flying free from his body.

Shin teleported out of instinct, Micheal’s warnings hammered into him time and time again, as he recognized what he was looking at.

‘One of HIS Seeds!’

Shin vanished and then reappeared half a dozen meters away, crouched down on the ground in a ready position. His Melding Plate Arm flexed as he held it out before him, the bottle of wine falling free as it slipped from his grasp and bounced off the stone ground.

Shin felt his adrenaline cool as the other members of the Revolutionaries ignored Shin completely, instead focusing on capturing the free Seed in the clear cylindrical container, and then turning away, leaving behind a befuddled Rex who was staring at them in shock.

And then…

beep

beep

bee-SHING

“It’s turned!”

Shin’s head whipped towards the monitor as he heard one of the scientists shout.

“The readings, it’s shifted! We have confirmation!”

For a brief moment, the world seemed to stand still.

That moment passed and…

“The islands are returning to their original positions!!”

“THEY DID IT!”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

Eon hefted Stratos in his right hand as he heard the sounds of jubilation break out around him.

A veritable wave of cheers spread, from Void Nobles to Humans, from peasant Void Natives to Knights alike, as word spread.

History had been made.

One of the greatest disasters to ever sweep across the Shattered Plane, an unprecedented assault on the way of life of all native to this Plane and travelers alike, had been defeated.

It was a tale of adventure and action, one of the greatest Eon had ever seen.

‘One for the history books.’ The Perpetual chuckled as the world warped around him, drawing upon the power of the Dream as he transported himself away, reappearing in the southern half of Axellion proper. He landed in an empty alleyway, between a closed butcher's shop and a large storehouse of some kind.

He’d noticed the looks everyone gave him when he’d picked Stratos back up, after the Ritual they’d used had spent its power. His crippled state had made him the clear target of many.

Yet – he was still Eon, the King of Heroes.

Even crippled, dying as he was – none dared make a move.

“What a story, this life has been.” Eon pondered as he took another step forward, reality shifting once more as he left Axellion, emerging out upon the outskirts of the floating island.

Eon's eyes narrowed as he gazed out towards the Void and…

He lay witness to countless islands slowly beginning to rise, regaining their lost height as they reversed their fall and flew upwards towards the sky, like great fists of light raging against the uncaring dark.

Eon took one final step, reaching the edge of Axellion’s floating island. Here, rocky outcroppings transformed into a sheer cliff-face, next to a small clump of trees.

“The life I lived, the people I met, the places I travelled…” Eon spoke quietly to himself, “What a story, indeed.”

Eon waved his hands, pulling upon the Dream one last time.

In his right hand, a journal appeared, inscribed with the number 53. The journal glowed with blue light briefly, its pages rustling as power coursed through it. Abruptly, it flapped open as line after line appeared on pages that rapidly turned over, words inscribing themselves in a great torrent.

This was his 53rd life and in this journal Eon crafted a record detailing the highlights of this life, from his very first steps all the way to what caused his end, the great, final adventure, a battle of fate between the best and brightest of humanity and the Titled Deity that tried to end them.

With a final wave of his hand, the journal vanished, disappearing as it bound itself to his Soul. The Spear of Time, Stratos, vanished in the same way, the Artifact one of the few he’d bound to his Soul, travelling with him upon every incarnation since his 23rd life wherein he’d obtained it.

“Unto the great dark, I venture forth, once more.” Eon muttered as he looked out onto the horizon, before he paused.

He was dying, without a doubt. His body was a ruin, propped up only by his use of the Daydream. The instant his attention slipped, he would fall away, passing on almost instantly.

However…

“Curiosity begets me. After all these years…” Eon murmured, his gaze dropping as he stared down at the Void below.

The Perpetual slowly nodded, the crystalline half of his face shifting slightly, “To explore the unknown is my calling…” He continued,

“For the end is never the end.”

Eon began to smile.

“The Dream lives on, in life and in death, waiting for the next great story to unfold.”

Without nary a look back, Eon stepped off the island and…

The silence of the world embraced him as the Perpetual fell into the Void.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“…”

“…”

“…”

In the Void, there was stillness.

Not life.

Not death.

A world unchanging, everything and nothing therein.

Yet in that stillness, the fading echoes of a voice once spoken traversed through space that was not space, through time that was not time.

And in the quiet stillness of the Void…

Something stirred.

.

Chapter 62


.

An angelic figure floated in the void of space, peering down upon a perfect world.

It was a beautiful biosphere, a garden world of epic proportions. The atmosphere was pure and fresh, calm energy flowing in the background like water at sea while golden clouds floated across the surface. Vast swaths of greenery covered the continents of this perfect world, wonderous forests full of towering trees, propagating a veritable menagerie of color and life.

Interspersed amongst clear river currents and bountiful forests stood grand cities of wonder, great towering marble edifices alongside tens of thousands of idyllically crafted homes, shops, and all manners of buildings alike. These shrines to civilization had been built methodically, with great care, integrating into the natural world around them, without disrupting it moreso than necessary.

The angelic figure began to descend, exiting the void of space as it began to pierce through the atmosphere. A sheen of heat surrounded the angelic figure, briefly, before a wave of the Angel's hand dissipated the gleaming corona as if it had never existed.

Zeos, the First Angel, cut a mighty image as he pierced through a set of golden clouds, the force of his arrival cutting a gaping hole into the cloud structure before he came to an abrupt halt.

A storm of wind whipped past Zeos, blasting leaves off trees as he stood, in mid-air, his gaze dispassionate. The light golden-skinned Angel stood a towering 8-feet-tall (2.4 meters), with two beautiful, feathered white wings stretching out with a wingspan almost triple his height. A lustrous Halo scintillating through the colors of a rainbow hovered above the Angel’s head, as his wings receded back, folding behind him.

“Eden has fallen.”

Zeos’ words ruffled the ornate white toga, lined with gold, that he wore, as the wind continued to stir up around him. The Angel floated through the air, before descending and landing in a large open courtyard.

Zeos knelt down, his fingers grazing the surface of the ground, running along small cracks in the stonework, as his lined face scrunched up in a deep frown.

“The True Celestials are no more.”

Micheal blinked, as he felt consciousness return to him.

‘True Celestials?’ He knew the term ‘Celestial’ thanks to Dark Void – the word was used in relation to the ‘Celestial Race’ – an ancient race of mostly extinct beings that could warp reality to mess with Time.

Silverback, one of Constantine’s Seeds that he’d fought against on the Second Layer, had possessed the Celestial Silverback Type, a Type that was almost certainly related in some way to the Celestial Race.

Before he could think further, his thoughts were cast away as Zeos moved.

The world around the Angel transformed as the Deity abruptly arrived in the center of one of the grand cities that dotted the landscape of Eden.

“What you see before you is the price of Heresy.”

The Angelic being’s words shook the air, slamming into Micheal’s consciousness like a train. There was a raw sense of shock, of awe, that enveloped the entity, the Titled Deity of yore standing before him, that could not be denied.

“An entire Tribe of Deities, and their lessers.” Zeos continued as he raised his right hand up, golden light surrounding it, “Gone.”

Suddenly the world shifted out of focus.

"Excised from Time."

Micheal felt himself whiplash as he was shown a series of visions, taken from all around this paradise-like world.

And what he saw…

Empty.

The world was empty.

Those cities of grandeur, great empires where millions of beings had made their living – those hallowed halls still stood, yet not a creature could be found, not even a mouse. No fish roamed the sea, no bugs fluttered in the air, no birds sang upon the breeze.

There was naught but the trees, in a world that once was.

“And so this duty falls to me.”

Abruptly, Micheal’s vision warped once more as he looked upon Zeos once more, in all his Angelic glory.

The Angel sat upon the edge of an exposed white marble platform, jutting off the side of the highest tower in one of the empty mega-cities that dotted Eden’s landscape. His wings were folded behind him tightly, as he gazed down at the empty world, his chin resting upon his fist, reminding Micheal briefly of ‘the thinker’ sculpture famous on Earth.

“This is the Edict I proclaim, for all Time.” Zeos’ words shook the air as he looked up, his gaze suddenly piercing through Micheal, almost as if the ancient Titled Deity was scanning him right now, seeing through to his core.

“The Past is inviolable.”

Reality shifted once more, the vision changing to gaze upon the world from the void of space.

“To alter the Past is the Way of the Heretic.”

Zeos reappeared, floating in the void of space.

“To those who will come after, let this be a warning.” The Titled Deity raised his right hand, and once more, turned to look directly at Micheal’s perspective.

For a split second, time seemed to stand still, as Micheal bore the gaze of the Angel stoically.

And then…

“Feel the consequence.”

Reality burned.

“Reject the Heretic.”

Gaping loss.

“Hate the Heretic.”

Crushing despair.

“Kill the Heretic.”

Raw nothingness.

“The Temporal Edict must never be broken.”

Tears streamed down Micheal’s face, unwillingly, as he was forced to bear witness to the death of not just a world, but the death of life itself, spread across fourteen separate garden worlds – and through whatever mechanism, he was forced to bear the emotions, the echoes left behind by this one, inescapable tragedy.

“Protect the sanctity of Time.”

The rush of emotions was crushing, overwhelming, overpowering, in ways he simply could not describe. It was a torrent, raw and uncaring, a ride he could not stop and was forced to bear until it reached its end.

.

..

…

‘No.’

‘No.’

‘No.’

He didn’t know how long it took, how far he had been trapped in the mires of emotion – but eventually, Micheal managed to fight his way free, his ironclad will overcoming.

‘This is not me.’

The blur of awareness struck Micheal as his eyes watered, reality snapping back to him.

Micheal retched, only his iron discipline keeping him from throwing up his guts as he pushed himself off the ground, resting on one knee as he regained his bearings. Several seconds passed as he heaved, his lungs burning as his hands trembled, unsteady on his feet.

“Well.” He muttered as he slowly regained control, steadying himself, “That wasn’t fun.”

A quick glance around confirmed his location – he was on the floating island he’d aimed for, after escaping the aftershocks of the attack that had killed Jay sol Arget.

‘At least, I hope.’ He turned back towards where he came from, pushing away the revelations of the vision he had just been subjected to.

All that remained of the floating island was a huge, gaping hole in space. The island, and all the surrounding islands, had been annihilated in the attack.

‘Credit for his death would go to Aaron.’ The attack that struck down both of them was the same attack Jay sol Arget had sent out towards Aaron at the start of the Loop, a massive energy beam drawn from the power of the Nexus – only, with its Vectors reversed after Aaron sent it back towards the Deity.

‘Does Aaron only get the Points after the Loop ends?’ Technically, there were other versions of the Deity that were still alive – Micheal wasn’t sure how it worked. Time travel was weird.

“Whatever.”

Micheal took a deep breath as he stumbled over towards a small, rocky outcropping on this particular floating island, ducking into a shadowy alcove.

His Soul felt like it was on fire. It was all he could manage to not pass out, as he sat down on the ground and crossed his legs.

‘It’ll take me several days to recover.’ Despite that, it wasn’t as bad as it could have been.

Launching himself blindly through Time with Lux had been a worst-case scenario forced upon them – just the fact that his injuries didn’t appear permanent was already an incredible boon that was only possible because of Lux.

“By the time I’m good to go, the Loop will have ended.” Micheal muttered with a frown, as sweat poured down his brow.

He supposed that was a good thing – trying to make contact with his past self would risk running into Jay sol Arget’s Paradox Clones.

Right now, what he needed to do was stay put and focus on recovery – he had done his part.

“But first…” Micheal turned his focus outward, to the screen that he had been ignoring.

.

— — - Titles System - — —

Your achievements have earned you a new Trait Selection.

.

“Another one so soon?” He rubbed his eyes.

Trait accumulation, for a normal Deity, was something measured in years. From what Dark Void had learned, there was an invisible ‘wall’ standing between each new Trait Selection, a level of achievement that needed to be met before a new Trait Selection could happen.

The height of that wall was something that, ever so slowly, went down over time – but in the immediate aftermath of acquiring a new Trait, would tower so high as to be nigh-impossible to acquire.

Normal Deities would spend years in-between acquiring new Traits.

Yet, here was Micheal, already on his third.

‘I guess- huh.’ The thought gave him pause as he realized what it meant.

The ramifications of his actions… they truly were having an impact, one so vast even the vaunted Titles System couldn’t deny their import, decisions and deeds he undertook changing countless lives spread across multiple worlds and numerous species.

The math didn’t lie.

Micheal smiled.

He was making a difference.

.

— — - Titles System: Trait Selection - — —

Please select from the available Traits:

Cosmic Comprehension – Planar Speed – Dividence Defiance Adaptive Form – Risen Soul – Inborn Strength Alpha Restraint – Courageous Soul – Lightfoot Mirror Soul – Steady Heart – Hafted Thought

Self-Gravity – Mire Arms – Boosted Resilience Hearty Health – Thunderous Legs – Golden Mind Swift Body – Fast Recovery – Plague Resistance … (1/217 page)

.

“My First Step.” Micheal muttered as he stared at the new selection screen, noting the changes and…

The five special Traits that glowed on the screen – ‘Cycle Traits’ as they were called, special Traits that only had a chance to show up every 3rd Trait he picked, at the end of each ‘Step’ of the ten ‘Steps’ to a Trait Cycle.

Cycle Traits were special, the strongest form of Traits a Deity could choose, available only briefly, with no guarantee they’d ever reappear again. They were something that had to be earned, at the end of each Step – some Deities never had an opportunity to even see a Cycle Trait, living plain or ordinary lives that didn’t earn them the merit, according to the words of Dark Void.

Micheal looked at the five Traits intensely, instantly knowing he’d choose from one of them.

‘Cosmic Comprehension.’ A Trait centered around comprehension, perhaps of Conceptual Powers?

‘Planar Speed.’ A Trait about… movement speed? Transport speed? It’s name wasn’t clear.

‘Dividence Defiance.’ A Trait that had to do with defying fate? Luck?

‘Adaptive Form.’ A Trait that would modify his body, making it adapt?

‘Risen Soul.’ A Trait that would enhance his Soul, or something similar.

Micheal considered each option in-depth, the vagueness of some of the Traits not making his decision any easier.

However, as he looked over them, he gradually came to a conclusion.

‘It’s not even close.’

His choice was clear.

If there was one thing that had been holding him back, what he needed most in not just this life, but also his previous life.

‘Cosmic Comprehension.’ His finger hovered over the option.

“It’s you.” All the Conceptual Powers he had struggled to connect with, from the Concept of Energy to his stalled progress in the Concept of the Sword.

What he needed most in this life…

“To understand.”

Micheal nodded stiffly, his mind set as he made his decision.

He tapped on the Trait.

And then he closed his eyes, the pseudo-sleep of meditation overtaking him as he leaned back in his stone alcove.

Exhaustion, his Soul’s unstable state, the deluge of emotions forced upon him by that strange vision… everything hit him all at once.

And yet… despite all of that…

A grim smile etched its way onto his face, as the River of Time roared ever onward, her currents shifting in their ebb and flow, the march of time relentless to all.

One Calamity down.

“…”

“…”

“…”

Four to go.

.

Epilogue – Part 1


.

Stillness.

Silence.

It was quiet, deep in the heart of the Void.

A realm of endless darkness.

Peaceful.

Calm.

There was no movement.

The Void is.

The Void was.

And…

That was enough.

Everything was still.

Everything was st-

Everything wa-

Every-

Well.

Not everything was still.

In the stranded depths of the quasi-Dimension that was the Void…

“…”

Orion Thunderfist sat alone.

The ancient warrior struck an odd sight, sitting cross-legged with one palm resting on each knee, floating amidst a sea of endless darkness. The Dark Wraith had made this Toren body his own, fully fused within it, permanently sealing himself to a life amongst the corporeal realm.

Time was an odd thing, here in the Void.

It didn’t exist – or, rather, it shouldn’t.

Everything was still.

And yet…

The Void around Orion Thunderfist acted differently, influenced by a reality-warping Title the warrior still did not truly grasp.

And so, Orion Thunderfist was left alone, with naught but his mind…

For a very long time.

‘My eyes were shut, yet I could not die.’

Time flowed strangely around the newly crowned Titled Deity.

Sometimes seconds stretched into days, while hours passed in a minute.

He…

He had lost.

In the countless days that slipped past, as Orion Thunderfist sat alone in his solitude, he began to reflect.

A lesser man would’ve railed against his circumstances, lashing out in rage and hatred at the world around him, denying reality.

Orion refused.

The man who had abandoned his wife and daughter to die was dead.

He was a coward no more.

He would never again allow himself to walk that path, no matter the difficulties he faced.

And so, no matter how painful it was, no matter how humiliating it felt, no matter the rage or irritation… he forced himself to reflect.

He pondered the chain of decisions that led to his present circumstance – the life he had lived, the actions he took, that led him to where he was now.

He thought of the battle, of the foes he fought, and the one whose clever planning and bravery saw him defeated in the end.

‘Micheal.’ He’d heard one of them shout the human’s name.

In the hours, days, weeks that slipped by, Orion eventually came to a conclusion.

His defeat was deserved.

He held no grudge.

‘I lost myself.’

It was only now, after truly losing everything, that Orion found himself a moment to look back and reassess.

What was he truly, trying to do, on the Ancient World?

Unite the realm, seizing upon the resources brought to them by these invading races, and form a mega-army to launch an assault upon the heavens, find a way to cross realms and chase after…

HIM.

Even now, Orion shook his head.

‘I was foolish.’ Frustrated by his inability to progress, trapped in a mindset that he could never overcome.

‘HE needed no army.’ Orion acknowledged.

What good would an army do, no matter how grand?

No.

All that mattered was power alone.

Power he lacked.

As that thought struck Orion…

He punched forward out of frustration.

It was just a raw expression of his anger, at the helplessness he felt facing the monstrosity that was HIM.

And yet…

That simple punch changed the trajectory of Orion’s life.

Immediately, Orion underwent a baptism of his Soul, as his connection to the Concept of the Fist broke through to the Grandmaster tier, wherein his vast comprehension was finally set upon a Dimension with a high enough background energy to support him.

In the same moment, his body, now forged as his own, was remade, undergoing an evolution as he obtained the Body of a Grandmaster.

The revelations that set upon him felt right, the wall he had run into on the Ancient World finally overcome, undergoing enlightenment based off the sheer, raw experience and skill he had accumulated.

It was a transformative moment, here in the darkness of the Void, that shifted Orion’s entire mindset.

He laughed until he cried.

‘You cannot fight fair if you want to kill a God.’

The words Micheal had shared with him, in those final moments, resonated deeply, to Orion, on a level he couldn’t explain.

As the result of his breakthrough settled upon his body and Soul, Orion shifted his body until he was kneeling down on the ground.

And then…

He bowed down, fully, deep, his back parallel to what would be the ground.

Like a student, bowing to his Master.

He didn’t know how much time had passed.

Seconds to hours, days to weeks. Perhaps even months.

And yet, now, when he looked upon the bitter defeat he had suffered…

Gratitude was all he felt.

‘My eyes are open, and now I see.’ Maria…

Orion stood up, his back straight and his head held high, gazing about the endless darkness of the Void.

His Title, the curse that had set upon him in this new body, was a powerful new tool.

And it was just that, he recognized, just a tool – like any other, a skill he could apply, no matter it’s origin.

To discard it out of hand, simply because of distaste…

Orion smiled.

He couldn’t imagine his foe, Micheal, doing such a thing.

‘You cannot fight fair if you want to kill a God.’

He only knew the Swordmaster briefly, yet their duel, their clash, had taught him much.

He could respect a warrior like that, no matter how different their origins might be.

And so…

Orion used his Title and began to explore.

The Void was an enormous, seemingly endless Dimension that went on and on, no matter how he travelled, floating through the air – yet it was not empty, not as he had initially thought.

Scattered throughout the darkness, interspersed seemingly randomly, were objects of all kinds.

Travel through the Void was measured not in steps, but in time, as his Title let him shift through the strange stillness, moving in an eerie, incomprehensible fashion.

And so it was, as he shifted from one bout of darkness to the next, the first thing he came across was a shattered hatchet, missing half its axehead as it floated in the darkness, hovering, frozen in stillness.

It was a curiosity, one he touched upon, grabbing the old axe and giving it an inquisitive look, before setting it aside after he confirmed it was just that – an old, useless broken axe.

His journey continued.

He came across object after object, from clumps of rock and dirt to old helmets, broken Artifacts, metal ores and even the bodies of alien creatures he had never seen before, from animals to bipedal corpses that were clearly once sapient beings.

Even entire islands of rock and stone, some with forests or pools of water alike weren’t spared, appearing amidst the endless darkness.

He felt no need to drink or eat, or even breathe, here in the Void – even as he travelled, everything, including his physical needs, was stilled.

And so his journey went.

Time passed him by as he pondered, moving from place to place as he sought an exit, a way out of this strange, seemingly endless Dimension.

His Title lent him the ability to move freely in this frozen Dimension, but, unfortunately for Orion, he didn’t have the expertise, the knowledge required to truly escape this mire.

Yet, he did not give up. He would not give up. Not again.

Never again.

And so his journey marched ever onward – as he travelled, he refined the magnum opus of his life – his Thunder King’s Martial Art, the storied techniques that mixed his martial prowess with his ability to manipulate Elemental Lightning, going through chapter by chapter, passage by passage, as he integrated his newfound insights as a Grandmaster into his technique.

He also finally acquired his first Trait, after learning more about the Titles System that had been gifted to him, gradually comprehending its secrets. Of the many choices he was offered, he eventually decided on the Trait that felt most apt for his current circumstances, once he realized it was offering him a power, similar to how those Humans could purchase ‘Abilities’ in their ‘Shop.’

.

— — - Trait: One Body, One Soul - — —

Strengthens the connection between one’s Body and one’s Soul.

.

This Trait’s impact had been felt immediately, his new Toren body ‘clicking’ in a way he couldn’t quite describe – no longer was it just ‘his new body’ – it was him, here and now, this was who he was, for the rest of his life.

He accepted that, like everything else that had been thrown his way.

Did it bother him, to wear the body of the same race that had ended those he loved?

The past version of himself would have said yes.

But now…

Orion shook his head.

‘You cannot fight fair if you want to kill a God.’

He made peace with it.

As he travelled, he learned more about the Void – objects that were found close to each other, he eventually concluded, entered the Void at similar frames of Time. Space seemed to function strangely here in the Void, distance not mattering as much as it would in a normal world.

The days slipped by, Time winding strangely, as his journey through this strange still Dimension continued forth.

Until…

One day…

In the corner of his vision, he saw a flash of gold.

Orion twisted, stepping through the Void once more as he drew upon his Title, letting him travel between zones and…

He came across the bodies of two strange beings.

It wasn’t a particularly uncommon sight, in his travels thus far – he’d come across hundreds if not thousands of corpses, most of them gray skinned bipedal beings, clearly an alien race he hadn’t encountered before – though he’d also come across a few other entities, from strange animals to other bipedal aliens from clearly different species than the more common gray skinned ones.

These two bodies, however…

‘Is that a Human?’ Orion paused.

It was the first human body he’d encountered in his journey through the Void.

‘And…’ His eyes narrowed as he stared at the body that was frozen, held in the stillness of the Void that none but Orion himself seemed able to resist.

‘He’s still alive!’

The Human appeared to be in terrible shape, his body a ruin, clearly the aftermath of some great battle of note – and yet, Orion’s keen senses could clearly tell, even frozen in Time as this Human was – he wasn’t yet dead.

Orion grinned.

“What luck.”

This was the first still-alive being he’d encountered in his journey, lost as he was here in the Void.

Orion paused, for a moment, as he turned to look at the other body – it was a body similar to one of those gray skinned aliens he had seen many times before, but not the same – the entire left half of this man’s body was made up of some kind of strange crystal. This figure floated somewhat far away from the Human, yet close enough to let Orion know they must’ve fallen into the Void relatively close together, at least when it came to Time.

‘An attack.’ His Title instinctively let him know, this man’s body had been ruined through the efforts of another.

And yet, despite the alien’s horrendous state…

He wasn’t dead either!

“Truly, a stroke of fortune.” Orion felt pleased.

He floated forward, first towards the Human.

As poor shape as either being was in, it just so happened to be their lucky day.

Orion flexed his Title, feeling its reality warping properties descend upon him.

Even now, he admitted to himself, he didn’t fully grasp the power of the Title he now controlled.

The Herald of Ruin.

Yet, it was a tool, like any other.

“If I’m to suffer here in this Dimension, at least I won’t be suffering alone.” Orion grumbled with a small smile on his face as he reached out his right hand.

He took a full scan of the human’s injuries and-RUIN

-he destroyed them, erasing them from existence. It was a strange sight, as the Human’s body shifted, pale, healthy flesh replacing the jagged tears in his body as his bones mended and his muscles set right.

In the same moment, Orion reached out towards the gray skinned, half crystal alien and-RUIN

Reality warped as he did the same thing again, healing the gray skinned alien, fundamentally altering reality as he undid the crystallization attack that had transformed the being’s left half.

“Odds are, you sorry lot won’t be able to help me.” Orion shrugged at the thought.

What were the odds the first living beings he’d stumble upon would be able to guide him out of this cursed Dimension?

He wasn’t that lucky.

Nevertheless…

Orion chuckled quietly to himself as he activated his Title one last time.

‘Still, you never know.’ He blamed his newfound optimism on the Human that had defeated him.

The odds might be small, but it couldn’t hurt to try.

And, somehow, if it all worked out, well…

Wouldn't that be a Dream come true?

.

Epilogue – Part 2


.

In a small, clandestine chapel built just south of the Dragon Mountains on the Second Layer, the Nirvana Saint crossed his hands together as he looked at his charge, his golden gaze pensive. In his right hand, he held a beautiful book, covered in gold leaf and intricate carvings along its back and front. Faint white light glowed out from its pages.

“An artificial species and a broken, experimental Dreamworld, shaped by the arrival of mankind’s psyche.” The Nirvana Saint’s words echoed in the small, underground room he was currently sitting in, a small office, with a table, two chairs, and a bookcase set in the wall on the side.

Across from the Nirvana Saint sat…

“Kthhh.”

A Monster Class Morenkai.

In the background, lightning faintly shook the air as a storm raged overhead.

“How cruel, to be created and then abandoned, thrust into the chaos that became the First Layer.” The Nirvana Saint shook his head sadly.

The monstrous figure sitting opposite the Leader of the Purgatory Church made for an odd sight as it shifted in its seat. It had thick, light grey skin and a large, glowing circle engraved on its forehead, gleaming with blue light. Its visage was monstrous, the stark, almost flat features of a Morenkai giving it an uneasy Aura.

Yet, the creature did not lash out in violence like other Morenkai, but instead acted with real, true intelligence.

“To have achieved sapience on your own is an incredible achievement.” The Nirvana Saint continued, giving the Morenkai a small nod, before unveiling a beatific, winning smile.

“It’s a new policy that has only recently been implemented at my command, but…” He continued,

“The Church rejects none who seek her halls, whether they be human, alien, or any mix in-between.” The Nirvana Saint’s silver hair fluttered as he held out his hands wide, his golden book vanishing.

“You are always welcome here, Dawn.”

Dawn, the Morenkai. It, or rather, she had asked for a name, and the Nirvana Saint was all too happy to comply.

“Kthhh.”

The Nirvana Saint nodded gently.

“Let us speak more, of those Inherited Memories you possess.” The man gestured, his golden eyes gleaming,

“Tell me more about your Creators, these… Celestials.”

.. .. .. .. .. ..

“I must go.”

The Lord Justiciar of the Farian Tribes stared up at the cloudy sky of the Ancient World, as a cool breeze rustled over him. A storm was coming, from the south – close now, but not yet overhead.

Gregor’s long, golden hair fluttered in the breeze. His injuries from his clash with Orion were gone, a result of both the resilience of his own powerful Bloodline and the work of several specialized Farian Bloodlines that had healing properties, members of the Shadow Guard that had attended him in the aftermath.

“The Kowalsi were right.” Gregor Mantorel’s voice was deep, his gaze somber as he turned away from the sky, landing gently on the ground. His two delicate Farian wings tucked themselves back into his back – as ill-suited for combat as Farian wings were, their recreational value was unmatched. He really did enjoy his quiet nighttime flights.

“Surely, you don’t believe that.” A sharp, cutting female voice replied.

Gregor felt his Giant blood stir within him briefly, the echoes of power just barely out of his grasp, as he turned to face the speaker.

Myla Hannis, the Wise Lady of the Farian Tribes, glared sternly at him. The wizened elderly Farian was dressed in a gray shawl and a plain, black dress, reclining softly on a raised chair of wooden roots.

The two spoke within a small, nondescript clearing in the Woolen Forest, the land occupied by the Farian Tribes on the Second Layer, through a series of brokered agreements with the Silent Sword Sect.

“When the Kinwen fell to the Dark, it was a lesson learned in blood.” The Kinwen Massacre had happened before Gregor’s time, but the ramifications from that war still pressed on even now, in the present.

“The Kowalsi, they…” Gregor paused as he considered the wayward Tribe of Farians, the only group of Farians that had climbed up the Layers ahead of everyone else.

“They were right… for the wrong reasons.” The Lord Justiciar conceded as he shook his head, holding up a hand to stifle Myla’s response,

“It’s not a choice I make glibly, Myla.” His deep voice echoed softly in the cool night air.

The Wise Lady sighed, rubbing her forehead as she looked down at the ground.

“I know, Gregor. I’ve read the reports, heard what the Humans have shared with us.” Knowledge about the higher Layers, and threats they might face…

And the opportunities they would present.

The time he'd spent in the First Gate of the Soul King's Inheritance had proved immensely useful. He'd tempered himself and fully thought out his plans for the future, the goals he wished to achieve, clearing his mind. He also couldn't deny – the break it gave him, time free of his leadership duties wrangling the Tribes together like squabbling children, was a joy to bear.

The Lord Justiciar nodded slowly, his determination ironclad as he turned his gaze to the stars above, his keen vision piercing through the clouds.

“I need to travel higher, to grow.” He shook his head,

“Even now, when I think of what could have happened… if not for the Humans…” He thought back to his battle with Orion Thunderfist, the epic duel that had decided the fate of their species on this world.

He had almost died.

He shook his head again.

Enough was enough.

He tore his gaze from the overcast sky, matching the Wise Lady’s stare with one of his own as he stepped forward.

“You know how it goes, Myla.” He knelt down next to her chair, carefully resting a hand on her thin arm.

“When everything comes to bear, when all this comes to an end, only those with power will have a voice at the table.”

It was the indisputable truth of life.

“I cannot simply wait here, and allow our people be led like lambs to a slaughter.”

The Wise Lady let out a long, weary sigh.

“Very well. I will not hold you back, Gregor.” She looked at the powerful warrior, the leader of the Farians.

“You have my blessing.”

Gregor nodded, before sharing a small smile.

“You needn’t worry overmuch. The Shadow Captains have all agreed to my proposal. They will stand by you, in acting leadership to oversee the Tribes as they prepare.”

They would begin the process, preparing all the Tribes to climb up the Layers, all the while training, taking advantage of the higher energy levels each world possessed, to progress. To evolve their Bloodlines, grow their energy reserves, to become more.

The Lord Justiciar slowly got to his feet, turning away from the Wise Lady as he gazed up at the darkness above.

In that moment, the tired, elderly Wise Lady felt herself lost for words. Gregor’s back looked huge as he stood, almost wide enough to support the whole night sky above.

“The times are changing, and…” The Lord Justiciar’s words echoed softly.

“We must change with them, or be left behind.”

The rest would stay behind to prepare, but he…

He would travel ahead – to grow stronger, to train, to become more.

Because…

He was Gregor Mantorel.

The Lord Justiciar – bearer of the Primordial Giant Bloodline, the single most powerful Farian warrior respected by all, a generational talent, a Swordmaster the likes of which no other Farian could match.

The fate of not just his people, but also those he had sworn to, new allies and friends alike, rested upon his shoulders and…

He would not fail them.

And so…

The Lord Justiciar set off, headed towards his exit point as he began a journey that would become the stuff of legends.

.. .. .. .. .. ..

BOOM!

Lightning struck, ferocious energy blasting forth as it collided with the peak of Thunderfall Mountain in a glorious display of the fury of nature.

The echoing resonance of thunder spread out across the peak as the flash of energy faded, revealing…

A woman, Human, sitting cross-legged at the highest point of the mountain peak. She had long brown hair, tied up in a pony-tail, with warm brown eyes that glowed in the stormy darkness of the night. She was dressed in a comfortable white crop top and a cozy black skirt, barefoot against the rocky stone. Strands of electricity spiked off the woman, some fizzling out in the air, while others connected with the rocky ground underfoot.

Sophia Morgan took a deep breath as she cast her senses to the world around her, deep in meditation.

BOOM!

Another mighty bolt of lightning struck her, landing directly upon her temple. The impact almost seemed to freeze time, as a web of smaller energy lines broke off from the main bolt, flowing down from her temple and through the very veins of her body itself.

“Ah.” Sophia blinked as the moment passed, exhaling a deluge of lightning energy that crackled off into the air.

‘Micheal was right.’ She thought wryly to herself as she adjusted her hair, grinning as she felt the pitter patter of rain fall against her skin.

‘I do have a talent for this.’

With but a thought…

Reality shifted around her as she was no longer just regular ol’ Sophia Morgan.

She was the Storm itself.

Great lines of lightning warped the air, the smell of burnt ozone tinging the mountain peak, as the energy snakes danced around Sophia. Huge deluges of rain ripped down, as vast swathes of wind swept across Sophia’s immediate vicinity, picking up boulders the size of a man grown like they weighed nothing, tossing them into the air.

Sophia Morgan laughed madly as the world around her bent to her will, the rush of power exhilarating in her veins.

She had progressed, stepping ever closer to Mastery as she deepened her connection to the Conceptual Power of the Storm. Her Physique, ever since it was modified by the Miracle Gem, had grown by leaps and bounds.

.

—- Stormkissed Physique - 3 Star —-

An energized body blessed by the Storm. This 3 Star Stormkissed Physique uniquely predisposes its host to the Concept of the Storm, and other related Concepts.

.

The description she’d been given was rather barebones, but that might be due to how she’d obtained it. It was, after all, something she achieved on accident, by going through enlightenment when she connected to the Concept of the Storm at the same time she underwent her Heart Trial to obtain Earth Tier Ki. Perhaps it wasn’t a ‘normal’ Physique.

Still, she couldn’t deny its effectiveness.

In less than 2 weeks, she had developed an incredible depth of control when it came to the legacy left behind by Leia, the Master of Storm – part of it was her own natural talent, like Micheal said… but the other part was simply how easy controlling the Storm felt in her new, upgraded body.

Sophia grinned, slightly lopsided, as she thought of how Shin would react once they met up again.

‘Call me Sofa one more time, and I’ll sick a rain cloud on you, permanently!’

Just as abruptly as the world had transformed, it settled again, as Sophia released her connection. Reality returned to normal, the storm that had been reborn in apocalyptic proportions now faded to what it was before.

With a smile still on her face, Sophia gathered her Earth Tier Ki and leapt off the peak of the Thunderfall Mountain. She activated her Wind Sweeper Ability as she fell, guiding currents of wind letting her sail smoothly down the mountain as she gave her Soul a break.

“I’m close.”

Her words were a quiet whisper as she danced down the mountain, stepping down only briefly every hundred meters or so, gracefully descending leap by leap.

Thunderfall Mountain was one of the easternmost mountains in the Dragon Mountains, a peak renowned for its many lightning strikes during stormy weather. Ever since the Draconic Lich that had haunted the Dragon Mountains had been defeated, the Dragon Mountains had become a far safer place for exploration and training. There were still dangerous Magic Beasts to contend with, but nothing Sophia couldn’t handle.

“I’m strong…ish.” She muttered quietly to herself.

Witnessing Orion Thunderfist fight had been a truly shocking affair. It really set the scales, for the sheer danger of the higher Layers.

Sophia clenched a fist as she felt the power of the Storm rise up within her.

‘I need to climb higher to grow faster.’ On the higher Layers, according to Micheal, not only would her Ki accumulate more swiftly, thanks to the higher background energy levels, but she would be able to grow farther and faster, when it came to her connection to the Storm.

Here on the Second Layer, it was practically impossible to breakthrough to Grandmastery, due to the relatively low background energy level.

“I hope the boys are doing okay.”

She cast her worries from her mind as she finished scaling down the mountain, before setting off in a fast-paced sprint, dodging through valleys at a blistering speed as she began to traverse the Dragon Mountains. Rain pelted against her skin, her connection to the Storm making it a comfortable, almost warm sensation.

The years she had spent, training alone, in the First Gate, weighed on her, in a way she hadn’t expected.

It made her enjoy moments like this, the quiet solitude of training and adventure, blazing a path that was her own.

And it was here, as she landed on the ground in a small clearing, pausing in thought for a brief moment-

A White-Stone Raptor, a Mid-Tier Magic Beast, launched itself at Sophia, in an ambush. The creature had been hiding in a tree near Sophia’s location, seeing her arrival as an opportunity – a chance attack during a rainstorm.

The raptor looked much like a velociraptor from Earth, but one that was covered in small white scales, with a large, hooked claw on each foot. Unlike normal raptors, this one was incredibly muscular, giving off a sense of raw, untethered strength.

Sophia moved on instinct, kicking up a small branch lying on the ground near her.

The small wooden branch flew into her hand just as the raptor reached her and-

The ruddy glow of Advanced Sword Energy enshrouded the branch as her right hand struck forward, slicing upward in a blur and-

.

—-Points Notification—-

Points Obtained: 871

.

Two halves of the raptor fell on the ground, bisected cleanly as Sophia absentmindedly dropped the blood-stained stick, discarding it now that the threat was handled.

‘Poor Serena.’

Sophia continued her train of thoughts, completely ignoring the casual exchange of violence.

It would’ve been unthinkable to her before she entered the First Gate.

But she was no longer that version of Sophia Morgan.

The years of practice she had gone through within the First Gate had transformed Sophia’s skillset, in ways she didn’t fully realize. The woman who, in the first timeline, would’ve gone on to become the S Ranked Demon Fairy of the Main Cluster had seen her talents flourish in the years she spent honing her control of Ki and her mastery of combat.

Now, even a sneak ambush attack from a Magic Beast while she was lost in thought…

Well, that was just another day in the life of Sophia Morgan.

‘I hope she recovers.’ Sophia’s thoughts remained on her new friend as she traversed the valley, nearing the southern edge of the Dragon Mountains.

Dying and coming back to life had shocked the Farian to her core.

Unbeknownst to Sophia, this was another ramification, of the changes Micheal had made to the timeline.

In the first timeline, Serena’s will was forged in the fires of her grief after Myla Hannis was assassinated and the Great War Between Races unfolded, where the survival of her species was thrust into a very violent question.

In this timeline, none of that occurred.

Thus, when confronted with the horrors of death and the dangers of the higher Layers, her will yet unforged… this version of Serena had developed and now struggled with a form of PTSD, holding her back from committing to climb up the higher Layers when Sophia posed the question.

‘Either way, I can’t afford to wait.’

The Nirvana Saint was putting together an expedition that would climb up to the Third Layer next week, seeking to reconvene with the forces of the Church on that Layer – she’d asked and he’d allowed her to join it, without any obligations, thanks to their contributions.

‘I’ll spend the rest of the week farming Points.’ Sophia decided with a small nod as she reached the edge of the Dragon Mountains.

There were a few choice Abilities she was considering picking up, to flesh out her build.

‘And then.’ She looked up at the stormy clouds above, a wide grin spreading across her face.

‘It’s a race to the top!’

She wouldn’t let her fear control her. Separated from her friends or not, she wouldn’t give up. Somewhere out there, her little sister was waiting – and that was all the motivation she needed.

The 7 Layers wouldn’t know what hit them.

“It’s a nice axe.”

Prime held up the Skysplitter Axe, feeling its metaphysical weight rest upon his Soul in a manner he couldn’t quite describe.

The duo stood atop a golden mound, the exit point to the final Tomb of the Twelve Tombs. The sun shined down brightly upon them, though by the looks of the clouds in the distance, a storm was rapidly setting in.

“Right?” Prime responded, turning towards his unruly companion with a smile.

Yvvtal grinned back, his Silverback canines showing as he matched Prime’s gaze, a question in his eyes.

“Is it time?”

Prime paused, considering the moment.

He had finished what he started – after two weeks of trial and tribulation, he had managed to secure the Legendary Artifact, the Skysplitter Axe, from the Twelve Tombs. These weeks had proven momentous, in many ways. For one, he had managed to complete his Ki Transferal – Mana now thrummed in his veins, the Nameless Mana Breathing Method used by Typhon, a Transcendent Dragon, fully activated, resonant in his body and Soul.

The Mana Breathing Method had proven a perfect match, empowering the Draconic Blood that flowed in his veins. Every day, he felt himself transform, a little at a time, as his body gradually became something… more.

Prime glanced back towards the Skysplitter Axe.

‘Makatesh’ gu Guiven Wyrn tol vn Shosh.’ He repeated the line that was inscribed into the heft of his new axe.

‘Entombed, herein lies the Heart of the Twelve.’

He glanced down at the pouch he had strapped to his person, an Artifact that kept its contents shielded from scrying eyes.

He hadn’t known what to expect, when he decided to solve the mystery left behind here in the Twelve Tombs but…

The pair of Blue Drake Eggs now resting in his Bevy Pouch were not at all what he expected.

‘Hatching them will require a High Energy World.’ Since he wasn’t truly a Dragon, the process of awakening the Eggs was more complex.

“It’s time.” Prime answered the former Toren’s question, his gaze steely.

Yvvtal grinned, his smile taking on a vicious edge.

He’d obtained what he could from this Layer.

Now…

It was time to move on.

Prime froze the world around him as he activated his World Matrix Type Ability.

Everything went still as he tapped his Spatial Ring, bringing out one of his Memory Journals. He opened to a specific page, reading over the notes he’d written down.

The List of Legends.

On the Third Layer, according to Micheal’s list – there were two Legendary Artifacts.

Rank 2 – Stratos, the Spear of Time

Rank 5 – Surrelian, the Armor of the Sun Titan

‘Eon, the King of Heroes, holds the Spear of Time, while the Armor of the Sun Titan is held by no one, yet, because it hasn’t arrived.’

Micheal’s future sight, once again, showcasing its usefulness.

‘I have no quarrel with Eon.’ The King of Heroes was incredibly powerful, but never turned his hand against humanity, according to Micheal – it was only later on that his Spear was stolen, and became an Artifact to be pursued.

‘Surrelian, however…’ Prime’s eyes narrowed.

No one knew how it arrived, presumably brought by one of the many races entering the Third Layer.

According to Micheal, the Armor of the Sun Titan wound up in the hands of a genocidal Void Noble known as Count Tusk, a leading member of the ‘Red Line’ – a group of Void Nobles whose territory actively slaughtered foreign species, including humanity, on sight.

‘One step at a time.’

Now that he knew the full scope of the enemies he was bound to face, the Gods that would set their sights upon ruining humanity…

Prime chose his every step carefully, preparing.

For a man with infinite time to think, his patience never ran dry.

‘To the Third Layer, we go.’

.. .. .. .. .. ..

If there was one thing the other Races learned to hate and fear, when it came to humanity, it was mankind’s propensity for producing individuals of great power.

As a whole, even with the Shop to boost them, humans were painfully average. Weak, reliant on Abilities they barely understood, lacking the depth of Mastery and millennia of study and practice other Races boasted.

On an individual level, however…

There were always exceptions – and mankind was full of them.

On the Third Layer, on a floating island to the far north, unbeknownst to Micheal…

Theodore Mott was alive.

If Micheal had learned this fact…

He would shrug, because why would that matter?

Theodore Mott was a name of no importance – no records of him were left with Dark Void, and the impact he had on the first timeline was negligible.

Because…

Theodore Mott was supposed to be dead.

In the first timeline, Theodore Mott died on the Third Layer, struck down by the God-Emperor of Kalos after the two crossed paths.

However… in the second timeline…

Kyvenval and Theodore Mott never crossed paths, the window in which they should have met diverted by the early intercession of Jay sol Arget, due to Micheal’s interference.

And so…

Theodore Mott still lived.

And he was livid.

“Mankind is superior in every way – how dare these lesser beings slaughter us like rats!”

The pale-skinned human muttered beneath his breath, his words a harsh hiss, as he glared at the walls blocking off the minor City-State of Sirel, home to Baron Grets – a member of the Red Line. His face was bruised and bloodied, yet there was a strange green light to his eyes, a madness that sparked, mixed with brilliance.

“You’ll learn. You all will.”

In the center of the floating island that housed Sirel… the ground began to rumble and then- an explosion.

“Or you’ll die like the rest.”

A mushroom cloud split the sky.

Theodore grinned, his mad eyes alight.

“In Nuclear fire.”

“Again, the board has changed.”

Bosmond Jingleton rubbed his chin, lost in thought as he pondered.

He was sitting in his study, a room lined with bookcases, a large couch, a desk, and a chair. Several fine works of art decorated the walls of the study. In one corner, a small bonsai tree grew, planted atop a low desk adjacent to a small window, the only window in the room.

“But why?”

Across 7 different versions of reality, Bosmond had noticed something so incredible, it gave him pause.

“Someone has begun to interfere.” Bosmond grinned, his gaze turning predatory.

Whoever they were, they were subtle – leaving behind no signs that could be traced backwards, thwarting even his Seers as he sought to discover who was interfering. Their presence was incredibly faint, minor actions taken against his agents in one timeline, traces of an investigation into others in another…

Again and again. On a mass scale.

The interactions were minor, nothing truly offensive – but.

It was clear.

Someone, in control of an organization of some scale, was aware.

Someone possessed knowledge that they should not have.

“Finally.” The Titled Deity laughed out loud,

“Some entertainment.” The ancient eldritch Jester smiled, as several versions of himself across multiple timelines began to shift their directives, intent on matching this newfound opponent.

In one timeline, the former Ruler of the Aerdu Dominion ordered his forces to creep down the Layer, beginning a genocidal massacre as he systematically went, region by region, enslaving and interrogating suspicious members of any and all races, going full scorched earth as he became the enemy of the entire world.

In another timeline, Bosmond sent his agents down quietly – investigating his new opponent while sticking to the shadows, his preferred method.

And in 5 other timelines, he completely ignored his new opponent, continuing to act on the plans he had already decided upon.

“It’s about time.” Bosmond smile widened, revealing far too many teeth,

“I was starting to get bored.”
